RE6 is the Avengers: Endgame of Resident Evil. Everyone's here and it only kinda makes sense. It's by far the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane RE campaign. We went from RE4 and 5 with mostly normal-ish zombies to fighting mutating squid men on an aircraft carrier in 6... That's how insane it is. I appreciate the amount of content, with four separate campaigns to play, each taking ~5 hours each. There's a good amount of jank, with a clunky cover system and a movement/dodge system they don't teach you how to use. There is a lot of tedium too, with too many doors being buddy doors, and the game giving me a ton of skill points in boxes instead of the ammo I need to fight the hordes of enemies they're throwing at me. I've played entirely solo, which hasn't been bad since my AI teammate cannot die and doesn't steal any of the precious ammo. Despite all this, I would recommend it if it weren't for two things:

1. The quicktime events. They happen all the time and they're really annoying keys on PC. It doesn't contribute to the 'cinematics,' it's just annoying. Didn't press space+r in time? Congrats, you're dead, and you get to start over from a checkpoint several minutes before said QTE!

2. Technical bugs. I expect some of these running on Linux, but apparently it's just as bad on Windows. Had to use a few boot commands and install RE Fusion Fix to even run the game, and even then it's not always stable. Also, running at 'variable' FPS has some quirks... sliding down ramps, invisible walls, etc. I had to get good at opening the menu and switching it quickly to 60fps or in some cases even 30fps so that I could progress. Add in the jank of action cues not always coming up and it's just enough annoyance that I felt I should write this review. Also, for me, the first chopper you have to shoot down in Chris' campaign was flying in erratic circles and clipping through buildings. Probably related to the fps thing but at least this glitch was funny.

A few more small gripes... The 'streamlined' inventory system is not my favorite. There are too few slots and most of them are for ammo for the five different guns you can keister, so when it comes time to combine herbs and stuff, there's just not enough space and I inevitably have to drop something else to make room. The controls also aren't the most intuitive but it's easy eventually I guess.
The swarm/bug enemy is perhaps the most annoying mf enemy I have encountered in a video game. ♥♥♥♥ that guy.
Leon's campaign was the closest to a traditional RE campaign and is the best I've played so far. Chris' just felt ridiculous, hitting on all the 2000/2010s action movie tropes like a Transformers movie. I've started Ada's and it seems okay so far. 

Overall, know what you're getting into and set your expectations accordingly. Even so, I can't recommend it because of the QTEs and, more importantly, the bugs. Still, not a bad pickup for $5 considering how much content there is, especially if you have someone to play through with.

Finally gathered the courage to complete RE6 after playing, and enjoying, RE Requiem and ... Damn, I can't in good conscience recommend RE6 ... Even for die-hard fans who would want to play it for the lore : It isn't even that consequential and feels like a very weird fanfic on a fan-favorite character.

For the positives of the game : The gameplay is competent and overall, it surely is a decent coop game if you're looking for one. You also get your money's worth in terms of playtime, as it is by far the longest game in the franchise with 4 distinct campaigns. The Mercenary mode is also good, as always in RE games.

However, that's pretty much all : it has the markings of the most generic and bland 2010s-era third person shooter. It's grey/beige as were most of the games then. Its score is forgettable. Its graphics did not age well and most characters are ... just cardboard cutouts of generic badasses. Gameplay has weird quirks (the cover mechanic being nigh-useless for instance), and it's not only long, it's bloated : everything takes forever, almost every contextual action require a quick time event to complete and everything has to be so unexplainably over-the-top and non-sensical (or convenient, depending on the point of view) that it end up being exhausting (For instance, a good part of the game takes place in a city that somehow manages to be an active warzone between different factions, facing a zombie outbreak ... while still retaining commuter trafic and empty public transports to act as filler for car chases and boss setpieces ?).

I played the game alone, and while I found RE5 enjoyable even in solo, here, all but the last campaign felt like chores. The last campaign was pretty enjoyable though, but as it's the campaign designed to be played solo, I might be biased.

Anyways, nearly 15 years later, I can confidently say in my opinion that RE6 is ... a pretty big letdown and not a good game.

Leon’s campaign started strong. That opening was intense, shocking, and honestly had me thinking this might be great. Leon felt like a total badass. But the more I played, the more it started to fall apart. The game feels long in a bad way. The QTEs are worse than I remembered. I kept getting stun locked, and the action scenes go from exciting to just plain ridiculous.

I finished Leon’s campaign back in 2013, and even though it is not that long, it felt like it dragged. Then I started Chris’s campaign thinking it would improve things. It didn’t. I stopped at chapter 2 and didn’t touch it again until 2020. Same issues. Constant stun locks, running out of ammo, dying over and over. I pushed a bit further that time but gave up again at the boat level.

Fast forward to 2026. I just finished Requiem and wanted more Resident Evil, so I came back to RE6. This time I finished Chris’s campaign and started Jake’s. It still isn’t good.

The action is over the top in a bad way, the camera randomly shifts on you, sometimes locking into fixed angles without warning, and the controls have aged poorly. It is honestly hard to believe this came after RE5 because it feels worse in almost every way.

The only way I can recommend this is if you have a friend to play co-op with. Otherwise it just feels like a slog. If you are solo, you are probably better off watching the story on YouTube.

Performance on Steam Deck is excellent. No surprises there. It runs max settings without any issues. But performance alone can’t save it.
Maybe back in the day it wasn't as bad, but for 2026 playing this game is a mistake. If you do want to play it, for your own sanity, play it on lower difficulties.

[h1]One of the Messiest Sequels of All Time[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 is one of the most divisive AAA games from its era. Panned by critics and most players at the time it released, the game has gained a bit of a cult following over the years who swear the game was misunderstood. It's easy to see why considering that the modern version of this game comes with a ton of content and can be purchased for a bus fare on sale. Is it the WORST Resident Evil game ever made? Probably not, but it is still a very big mess.

Resident Evil 6 goes back to what the first two games did for their story modes and features multiple campaigns to play through. Unlike in RE1 and 2 however, you now have four full campaigns to play through. You have series staples like Leon, Chris, and more all trying to stop the spread of a new virus called the C-virus. No Resident Evil game has had you globe trot as much as this one does. It feels like this is a huge series finale caliber game with characters like Leon and Chris confronting each other on screen in a game for the first time, in addition to the entire world being engulfed in war. What lets the story down though is the confusing way it’s told with you having to play all the campaigns to even understand what is going on. When you unpack it, it's basically about an Epstein class rich guy being a massive simp for Ada Wong who makes a virus that takes over the world just so he can sleep with her. I'm not joking, that's the inciting incident of the entire plot. Combine the bad dialog with the explosions that happen once per minute and yeah, this is like bargain bin Michael Bay nonsense.

Nobody cares about the story in Resident Evil right? We're here for the gameplay and it's not a pretty picture with this game. The big shift is how you can move and shoot, as well as the ability to throw out melee attacks without needing a stagger from enemies with a context sensitive prompt, though those are still here. This, combined with the broken cover system and abundance of hit scan enemies, takes all the horror out of the game and places the game firmly in the third person shooter genre. As a third person shooter, the game is flawed. The campaigns feature dumb quick time events roughly every minute, forced walking sections, gimmicks like vehicle sections that go on way too long, and tons of scripted moments where your characters get separated or stagger around and fall because of another explosion or earthquake or some ♥♥♥♥. Control is constantly stripped from you and doesn't feel good. The mechanics that allow you to roll onto your back and shoot enemies are cool and all, but the campaigns aren't designed to let you take advantage of these systems. They'd rather you repeat a bunch of dumb stealth sections or long parts where you chase a character or wait for the AI to do something for you.

One feature that completely cripples this game is the skill system. You know how RE4 and 5 had this nice weapon upgrade system? Yeah, all that is gone and replaced with this stupid COD style perk system where you equip three skills in each loadout that affect things like accuracy, view kick, weapon damage, etc. and you purchase upgrades for these perks with skill points. The game drops points in sets of 50 or 100, and the skills cost multiple tens of thousands to purchase. This means after even two levels of picking up points, you still don't have enough to buy any good upgrades. You MUST grind to get these. You can also only equip three per loadout and if you want to switch to a loadout with a different playstyle, you must pull out your characters smartphone and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cycle over to that loadout in a menu in the middle of gameplay and the UI for the smart phones are AWFUL. WHY DOES CHRIS HAVE A RADIAL UI FOR HIS PHONE WHILE THE OTHER CHARACTERS HAVE A GRID? IT MAKES SCREWING AROUND IN HIS PHONE MISERABLE. But all that would be ok, if you could ignore the system, but you can't because 80% of the things enemies drop or the things you find in chests are skill points. This game has giant arenas full of enemies shooting at you with automatic weapons, yet the game gives you far less ammo for your guns compared to RE4 or 5, possibly even some of the more survival horror focused games as well! The fact that I never ran out of ammo in the horror focused games, even on their harder difficulties, yet I constantly had less than a mag of ammo for just one gun in this game is extremely poor design. And before the From Soft bros with daddy issues come in and say "git gud", the issue isn't dying a lot. This game is baby easy when you learn how its systems work. I'm saying the campaign isn't fun because you're forced to run up to enemies SHOOTING at you and punch them in the face a few times, they drop useless skill points, and repeat till you beat the game. That just isn't a fun way to play a third person shooter with enemies firing guns at you. I understand you have save your ammo in a Resident Evil game, believe me, but even with mostly melee kills, the enemies don't drop ♥♥♥♥ in this game.

The campaigns are also horrible in single player. Routinely you'll have an AI partner that needs to do something and they will wait till literally the last second to build tension to complete an action and this will sometimes get you killed because of enemies that just refuse to stop attacking during scripted animations. Enemies will also attack you while you're forced to watch a vignette where you have no control over your character. In coop mode, you have some moments where you'll run into other players from other campaigns and sometimes you'll actually be having to compete with them to get past certain sections which is an impressive feature, but this also leads to repetition as you go through the multiple campaigns and have to repeat the same section you did in another campaign.

What saves this game from being total ass is its side modes, specifically Mercenaries mode. As before, this is an arcade style survival scoring mode where you take on waves of enemies that spawn in and rack up kills and time bonuses to keep the carnage going as long as possible. In this game though, Mercenaries is pretty much the lifeblood of the game because its just this game's fun and wacky movement tech without stupid set pieces and quick time events. Combine this with the fact that each character has just two guns in their loadout, AND the fact that skill points drop a lot less than in the campaign, you ACTUALLY have ammo for guns when you need them! Yay! You get to shoot the enemies in your third person shooter! There's also some fun multiplayer modes, arguably the best in any Resident Evil game, that allow you to do ♥♥♥♥ like invade players in their campaigns or play a competitive Mercs mode where you send enemies into another player's match. It's all fun content that Capcom probably spent too much time on where they should have focused on making the campaigns and storyline not suck ♥♥♥♥. However, the stupid skill system is still present in these modes with its own unique skills to unlock, and one of the skills in Mercs literally increases your score past a certain number of kills, so everyone uses that skill. Again, cut this dumb system from the game altogether.

So yeah, hardly a must play entry in the series. If you have a friend to play with, the campaigns become slightly more tolerable, and the coop and multiplayer modes can be fun, but otherwise, this is only worth getting on DEEP sale. There's a reason no other Resident Evil game or third person shooter plays like this or copied this game's homework. What a shame.

I have given every single RE game I've played on Steam a positive review. This is the exception. 

How do you manage to downgrade the gameplay and controls of og 4 and 5? Like seriously. That should be an IMPOSSIBLE task and yet this game manages that. The UI, camera, inventory, responsiveness and overall controls are just a steaming pile of garbage. 

This game NEEDS a remake. And when the remake comes, I hope it completely replaces this. People always complain about how remakes supposedly replaces the original (they don't), well you know what? If any game deserves that treatment, it's this game. In fact, I'll go as far as to say that Capcom can give this game the RE3 Remake treatment and the remake will still be 1000% better than this. 

And yes, I've finished at least 1.5 campaign. I did Leon's and half of Chris before getting so bored due to how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the story and gameplay is. I returned 3 years later to play coop only to realise it's somehow WORSE than when I first played it.

"It can't be that bad" was my first thought when jumping into RE6 for the first time. Well, it's worse.

Clunky controls, awkward camera angles, weird UI design and inventory system. Aside from all the aforementioned technical issues, story was weak and not up to par in comparison to the other RE games.

Gameplay was atrociously annoying as well, I don't think I've ever died so many times in a story-based game ever and 90% of my deaths were from stupid reasons (like I don't wanna talk about the amount of times I died during Jake's snowmobile section). And if you think the bullet sponge enemies in general RE games are crazy, RE6 is just hilariously worse.

However, the "bosses" in the game just take the cake for me. Feel satisfied after taking one down? Here comes 10 more rounds of that same boss you supposedly killed...like I SERIOUSLY don't wanna keep killing the same bosses over and over again (the Simmons boss fight has got to be the worst RE boss fight ever), let's just keep them to 2-3 rounds please! Introduce new bosses or something damn!

And now, I wanna finally talk about how this is obviously the worst RE game in the franchise (which a lot agree with) and also one of the worst games I've played, period. This is NOT a Resident Evil game, there is absolutely NO horror in this, just full on action, guns blazing, QTEs everywhere, with barely any breathing space. I don't know how the entirety of RE6 got approved but I'm glad we're past that and that the franchise's downfall was saved by RE7.

Let's move on to my ratings of each campaign:
Leon: 1/5. Honestly my least favourite, just straight up boring, had the weakest storyline and Simmons is a big part of why I'm giving Leon's campaign a poopoo rating

Chris: 4/5. The best out of all the campaigns. End of Chris' campaign kinda gave me chills. Hardest campaign too imo as enemies are lot tougher.

Jake: 3.5/5. Jake would've taken the top spot for me if not for that damn snowmobile section. Whoever designed, tested and approved that section needs to be sacked.

Ada: 3/5. Honestly didn't see the point in Ada's campaign in this game (same with Leon, tbh) though I enjoyed her gameplay the most, her puzzles were the most interesting.

Despite all my criticisms, I do like how the game interconnects all of the characters/campaigns together, I thought that was done pretty smoothly and it deserves a shoutout.

To anyone who suffered through the entire game and still finished it, I think that’s a life achievement in itself. And playing with a friend definitely makes the experience more bearable!

Okay, I never wanna touch this game ever again.

I haven't finished Jake or Ada's campaign yet, but I can already tell from a personal standpoint it's not going to make up for what I've experienced in Chris's campaign (at least Leon's was okay). If you can, you should play this game with a friend. At least you two might get a laugh out of this game's shortcomings. Also, this game is a good co-op experience.

Getting the pros out of the way, this game excels in its gameplay. It's satisfying, a little bit goofy at times, and does a good job at expanding on what RE5 put out. The environments and settings were also crafted with commendable effort. I did sometimes stop to look at the surroundings and admire the hard work that was given. 

With that done, if this game was called something like "Viral Outbreak: Chinese Insurgency," it might be good. This is a Resident Evil game though. It *should* be treated as a Resident Evil game, otherwise there isn't much purpose in playing it. This game leans way too much into the action to the point where there isn't really much horror to this game. Some of the set pieces, specifically in Chris's campaign are ridiculous and don't feel like Resident Evil at all. It leaves the sphere of survival horror, and becomes an action game. It's hard for me to even call it action horror when it feels about 90% action and 10% horror.

The four campaigns, while a cool idea, only worked as a concept for this game. It was clearly too big of a task as the overall story lacks depth and ends up too scrambled, resulting in a relatively shallow mess. I don't know who Helena exactly is nor who her sister is supposed to be. Piers doesn't get much backstory either outside of a flashback chapter and feels like he exists almost purely for the sake of motivating Chris. Stuff just happens throughout this game, you'll have questions, the characters will continue on because the plot says so, and the questions will never end up getting answered and the wires never connect. This leads to unfulfilling character development and a lackluster narrative which is sad because the narrative and characters are practically the heart of the Resident Evil series. 

This game tried to hit the ball out of the park, but ended up swinging and missing two times and grounding out sharply to second base on the third pitch. 
You could say it's "fun bad," sure, but I can't wholeheartedly recommend a "fun bad" game when you can play 9 other mainline games in the series and just skip this, especially since this doesn't feel like a Resident Evil game to begin with.

I'll still be finishing the other two campaigns, but I will probably attempt to suppress the function of my prefrontal cortex so I can just enjoy the gameplay and not exercise my critical thinking skills on the story and overarching narrative. If there's anything I can be thankful for in regards to this product, it forced Capcom to erase the whiteboard and start completely from scratch with RE7, remembering what made Resident Evil a video game juggernaut.

Resident Evil 6 is a major departure from what the Resident Evil series traditionally represents. Instead of leaning on the survival-horror tension that defined earlier entries, the game pivots aggressively toward bombastic action. The result is a spectacular mess.

The first thing that becomes apparent is the pacing. Even with its four campaigns, the game feels excessively long. If you cut the missions in half, it would probably still feel bloated. Entire sections drag on well past the point where they’ve delivered their mechanical or narrative value, turning large stretches of the game into a chore.

Yet despite these structural issues, the game remains strangely fascinating. At its current price, it’s still worth experiencing simply because it represents such a bold experiment. Capcom clearly decided to go all-in on the action direction, and the result often feels more over-the-top than a Michael Bay movie. Explosions, collapsing set pieces, cinematic stunts—nothing is restrained, and in that sense the developers deserve credit for fully committing to the concept.

Where the game succeeds most is its combat system. Mechanically, it’s surprisingly deep, with fluid movement, dodges, counters, and aggressive gunplay that perfectly support the game’s action-movie ambitions. When the pacing briefly aligns with the mechanics, the game delivers exactly the kind of adrenaline-fueled action spectacle it’s aiming for.

Unfortunately, the story doesn’t fare as well. The narrative is forgettable, and its major twist is easy to predict long before the game reveals it. Combined with the uneven pacing, this weak storytelling prevents the experience from maintaining momentum across its lengthy campaigns.

In the end, Resident Evil 6 is a contradiction. Its presentation is top-notch and its action systems are genuinely compelling, but it largely fails at being a Resident Evil game in the traditional sense. Ironically, it succeeds far more as a pure action title than as an entry in the survival-horror series it belongs to.

It’s messy, bloated, and often exhausting—but it’s also an ambitious and oddly compelling experiment.

In its day, RE6 was rightly criticized for being one of the worst games in an otherwise austere and cherished franchise. Time has seemingly healed that wound, and you now have people calling it a misunderstood gem. I am here to dissuade you from that rhetoric; RE6 is a bloated mess, with no identity. 
The gameplay is laughably complex, with sliding, prone position, rolling, and melee combos but there is hardly a reason to use it all. Even on professional difficulty spamming headshots gets the job done as it always has, and the game is more than happy to give you ammo to do it with. The storyline is filled with scripted "set-pieces" that feel contrived to be as explosive or creepy as possible with no regard for tone or cohesion. Each character duo goes an agonizingly long slog through set-piece after set-piece...it seems to never end. 

The shooting feels good at first, but especially by the time you get to Chris' section you will get sick of it. Where RE4 and 5 had a tactical, thoughtful pace where you need to conserve ammo and use your environment intelligently, RE6 has replaced that with a shooting gallery much more akin to The Mercenaries modes.... Until you get to the last act with Jake and Sherry where there's hardly any gameplay at all. It's so messy, I'm having trouble organizing my thoughts on it. There's just so much that's wrong with it.

It’s a bit difficult to judge this game because by 2026 it’s already quite old, so I’ll talk about how it feels to play today.

First, overall impressions. Performance is mostly fine, although even if you set the refresh rate to 240 and unlocked FPS in the settings, the game still seems to be capped at 120 FPS (In a few places it locks at 60 for a little bit). Graphically it still looks fine.

The character stories (campaigns) themselves are good, I would say it's a best part of the game, BECAUSE...

I couldn’t find a proper pause in the game. Pressing ESC opens a menu, but the game doesn’t actually pause. That means you sometimes can’t even adjust something simple like mouse sensitivity during certain moments. The menu looks stylish, but it’s not very informative, which only makes finding the right settings harder.

The interface and controls feel poorly adapted for keyboard and mouse. It's really bad...

I couldn’t figure out how to switch ammo types, for example on the grenade launcher. There’s no clear keybind for it in the controls, and I didn’t notice any tutorial explaining it. Maybe I just didn’t understand how the developers labeled that function in the settings.
UPDATE: Mentioned it in a moment playing Jake's story, somewhere in the middle.

The screen shake in some moments makes the game almost unplayable, or at the very least your eyes start to hurt and it becomes hard to understand what’s even happening.
UPDATE: It's really terrible...

Some fights feel unbalanced. There were moments where a single enemy could basically stunlock me repeatedly and I couldn’t even get up.

The aiming system feels like a joke. There is a crosshair, but you still have to aim using the laser pointer inside it, which moves around inside the crosshair after every shot.

In some sections the camera suddenly changes position on its own, which is uncomfortable. Sometimes it even becomes static, similar to the early games in the series.
UPDATE: In the last three campaigns this becomes even more annoying, often forcing you to die and retry because you don’t always have enough time to figure out where you’re supposed to go on the first attempt.

I was genuinely engaged for about one campaign (5 chapters), which is roughly 5 hours of gameplay, that was Leon's campain.

I’ve completed all the campaigns:
Leon’s campaign doesn’t feel too bad, especially while you’re still getting used to the controls. But when I started Chris’s campaign, I got bored very quickly because everything felt the same. It’s basically a copy of Leon’s gameplay, just with the “mini-games” appearing in a different order and that is all the same for other compains too. Because of that, I ended up speedrunning the last compains by just running past enemies whenever possible, since there’s little point in killing all of them anyway.

As I mentioned, the stories themselves and the way scenes are directed are actually pretty good, especially the pre-rendered cutscenes. It was really interesting in some moments.

[h2]Final verdict:[/h2]
The stories are interesting, but the gameplay is clunky, uncomfortable, and unfortunately boring. You can play it, but it’s definitely not necessary. You’re probably better off playing something else, and if you’re curious about the story, just watch a recap on YouTube or a game movie instead.

I know Resident Evil 6 gets a lot of mixed opinions, but honestly I had a great time with it—especially Leon’s campaign.

Leon’s story feels the closest to classic Resident Evil: darker atmosphere, zombies, and that tense feeling when things start going wrong. 
It has some really memorable moments and locations, and it was easily my favorite part of the game.

What I really love about RE6 is the variety. 
Each campaign feels different: Leon’s is more horror-focused, Chris’s is action-heavy, Jake’s has its own style, and Ada’s ties things together. 
Being able to jump between different perspectives of the same outbreak keeps the game fresh the whole time.

Another huge plus is the CO-OP. 
Playing the campaigns with a friend makes the experience even better. 
The game was clearly designed with cooperative play in mind, and it leads to a lot of fun and chaotic moments.

Overall, if you go into Resident Evil 6 expecting a mix of horror and action with multiple storylines, there’s a lot to enjoy here. 
Leon’s campaign alone makes it worth playing, but the whole package offers plenty of content and replay value.

Rating - 10/10 ⭐

It all goes to trash the moment you notice the stupid inventory system where nothing they did well or learned from RE5 was taken into consideration. You cannot share consumables and all loot is duplicated while inventory slots are used up by new types of ammo the more you progress making it a chore to navigate through to destroy an item just so you can pick up another one like an herb that you then have to combine and "break up" into tablets that are stored separately for quick heals. It's annoying and not very well though off.
Here, co-op is just about shooting stuff together and occasionaly giving a lif up to a ledge or healing eachother. It has some asymetrical moments where one character does something and the other has to do something else but those moments are just as rare as in RE5 and not worth mentionning really.
No, the worst offenders here are a massive amount of QTE's although they are easy, horrendous vehicle driving sections, escape sequences where you have to quickly and perfectly execute maneuvers to reach a checkpoint and frustrating bugs that prevent your friend whom you invited on , say, professional difficulty, to actually play in said difficulty and instead be on normal and not receive the completion for the harder playthrough. The only solution for that it to NOT invite but have your friend SEARCH for your lobby as by doing so he/she has to select it's own difficulty level that maches yours...
Also the last chapters almost never register as completed for them meaning they have to start it and invite you instead ... Add to that that the ONE great feature of this game has you intersect campaigns with other characters and sometimes that means other players might be there instead of bots which is a cool idea. Look, a lot of what you've heard about this game is true. The campaign is basically resident evil but micheal bay. 

That said, that's exactly part of why I love it lol. It takes the cornyness of RE 4 and whatever was present in RE 5 and just amps it up to 1000. I personally wasn't really a fan of RE 5's campaign, the main difference being that where RE 5 got kinda boring for me, this game is entertaining as all heck. The characters are fun to watch and the story being told non-linearly was fun at the very least. That said, the campaign isn't all that great.

There are some cool set pieces and action scenes which make use of the game's combat system, but then there's also too many scripted scenes and also an occasional section which isn't all that compelling. However, this game has 1 thing about it which it really excels at, and that is the combat. This is genuinely one of the most dynamic 3rd person shooters that you could ever play. It also has some very interesting enemy variety which it mixes pretty well to make constantly interesting scenarios. Every character also feels different in atleast some respect. Like how Sherry and Chris have the best throws in the game, or how Leon and Jake are the best at melee attacks, or how a character that you unlock later on is effectively a pretty perfect all-rounder.

Mind you though, that only happens in the game's mercenaries mode. The campaign is more bothered with throwing as many explosions as it possibly can in your face. Frankly it's hilarious as a result but ironically, because of how constantly over-the-top the game was, I thought some of the more serious moments of the story actually landed ( if atleast slightly ) mostly because they contrasted with the constant action. The boss fights were also surprisingly decent.

I've seen people give numerous reasons for why they think this is a bad game, and I do agree with some of them. All that said, I think this game's real failure is that it doesn't even try to teach you it's combat system. I think Capcom only realised towards the end of this game's development that they had something great here and didn't have enough time to really make proper use of it, especially since they probably already spent so much time on the set pieces.

Do yourself a favour, if you get this game then watch a few videos about how the combat works before you play it. I did the same and I frickin loved this game. Hell, I still play mercenaries. Especially the no mercy mode.

If you want a survival horror game, then stay away. 

If you want what is genuinely one of the best 3rd person shooters that you could ever play, then look no further

At the time, I thought, throw it in the fire, but maybe all this game needed was time. We were in a split direction at the time, craving the resident evil of old, but instead getting something closer to Uncharted or Gears of War set in the Resident Evil universe. I think we're all glad this is not the direction the series continued to go in, but after getting mostly great RE games since RE7 and RE2 Remake, thinking back to RE6, it's not that bad and we can put to rest the fear that RE would never be a survival horror game again.

This is not a survival horror game, but I think it can still be a GREAT Resident Evil experience in the same way the movies can be really fun to watch, even if they aren't exactly amazing either. I think the horror is more in the context of the situation instead of being scared of what's on screen, because the spread of the infection in this game is extremely tragic and this probably has the saddest moments in the RE universe. Overall, even if the blockbuster presentation is the furthest thing we really want from RE I still found most of the story and characters to be enjoyable.

Distancing from horror, I think they did nail the "Biohazard" namesake and throughout the course of the game we get to see MANY B.O.W.s, thousands of people get infected, and get to experience team missions with the BSAA. In terms of fleshing out the universe's lore and showing each character at their prime, and expanding the biohazard from a rural area to a worldwide catastrophe, I think 6 does a good job of taking Resident Evil to mach 10. The fluid combat is best felt in the mercanaries mode, which is a lot of fun. The game's bigger flaws, like poor pacing, button mashing, repetitive combat sequences, tedious gameflow, lack of puzzles and inventory management tally up after completing even just one of the 4 campaigns. I think everyone's glad Capcom veered away from this, but for what it is, RE6 is still a great action game with some of the coolest characters in RE.

RE6 is an 8/10 that mostly sets out and achieves what it wants to do.  Mostly.  There are disjointed design choices, most offensively Chris's campaign which is pure unfiltered kino, but sadly doesn't have the ammo drops to match the high-octane action and breakneck pace.

The torch is still being carried by the brilliant RE2R and RE4R, but the blemishes are there in 3R, 7, 8 and even 9 which has little to no replay value.

RE6 has gameplay at the forefront. It looks good, it feels good, it runs good, and the movement tech, cancels and enemy variety is second to none. People nowadays take it for granted, it released with four campaigns which, while crushed under their ambition, delivered tens of hours of content at $60. Mandatory action running sequences like this should be banned by international law.
-Missions are so linear I started getting FF XIII flashbacks. No exploration, no cool things to find, no puzzles, no thinking; just push forward and shoot/punch everything till the next cutscene plays. But I've played my share of CoD, so why would this bother me? I'll tell you why:

Resident Evil 6 is one of the most divisive entries in the series, and after playing through the franchise, I can see why. I am still playing this game so can update my review later.

Right from the start, the presentation feels different. The menu system is structured around separate campaigns rather than a traditional single narrative flow, which was slightly confusing at first.

The game follows multiple perspectives across four main campaigns: Leon, Chris, Jake (who even is Jake?), and Ada. Each is broken into chapters and interconnected storylines.

This is where Resident Evil 6 begins to diverge significantly from the rest of the series.

________________________________________
A Shift from Horror to Action:
________________________________________

Capcom made a major shift away from survival horror toward large-scale action.
Personally, I didn’t feel the tension or dread typically associated with Resident Evil. The emphasis on set-pieces and spectacle makes it feel closer to a cinematic action experience than a horror one.
While I don’t think Capcom was trying to imitate other action-heavy titles of the time, the result feels closer to that genre than to the roots of Resident Evil.

________________________________________
Identity Problem:
________________________________________

Because of this shift, RE6 sits in an awkward place within the franchise.

Resident Evil is built on survival horror. By leaning heavily into global-scale action and spectacle, the game moves away from what made the series distinct.

Capcom likely aimed to evolve the scope after RE5 — expanding the threat beyond isolated outbreaks into a worldwide bio-terror narrative.

Conceptually, this makes sense.

But in doing so, the series’ identity became diluted.

________________________________________
Gameplay & Interface:
________________________________________

Mechanically, the interface feels dated and overly complicated.

Examples include:
-	The transparent overlay for ammo and healing,
-	Herb combination systems,
-	Equipment navigation during high-pressure moments.

Quick-time button and toggle style reactions when grabbed or attacked also break immersion rather than enhance it.

Compared to modern titles, the systems feel less intuitive and more disruptive to pacing.

________________________________________
What Worked:
________________________________________

One positive was the skill system.

Collecting skill points and upgrading abilities added a layer of progression that I didn’t dislike. It was a new direction for Resident Evil and could have worked well within a different framework.

________________________________________
Tone & Execution
________________________________________

The campaigns lean heavily into cinematic drama.

Capcom clearly attempted something ambitious — a global, multi-perspective story.

However, the execution didn’t quite land for me.

The scale feels large, but the horror feels small.

________________________________________
Final Thoughts
________________________________________

As a Resident Evil fan, this is a frustrating entry.

It isn’t without merit, but it doesn’t feel aligned with the core of the series.

Capcom has since shown they can successfully blend action and horror in later titles, particularly in Requiem. Resident Evil 6 simply didn’t strike that balance.

Realistically, I think it’s unlikely Capcom will revisit or remake this entry in the same way they have modernised other titles, as its structure and design sit differently from the direction the series has since taken. That said, I would still welcome a full rebuild of the game from the ground up — even if it meant significantly reworking it to better fit within the franchise.

One direction that could have strengthened RE6 is leaning into a more grounded global threat structure. Instead of a sprawling but chaotic scale, the game could have explored regional bio-power blocs emerging after Umbrella’s global corporate collapse, such as:

• Former Umbrella offshoots in the Americas (as seen in Requiem).
• Plaga / parasite-based networks in parts of Europe (RE4).
• Progenitor-linked research in Africa (as hinted in RE5).
• Independent viral experimentation in Asia (potential new title).

Not as direct “Umbrella replacements”, but as decentralised power structures. The collapse didn’t remove the threat — it scattered it, with different regions inheriting pieces of its legacy.

In Requiem, an in-game video shows crates bearing both Umbrella’s logo and another agency’s — suggesting that Umbrella never operated in isolation, and that its downfall did not make the world safer. A more focused RE6 could have explored this kind of global fragmentation in a similar way, rather than relying primarily on spectacle. I think this could be a good way to bring all the other games together and could then open up more grounded, locally driven story pathways for the Resident Evil franchise.

________________________________________
How RE6 Could Be Improved
________________________________________

A rebuilt version of RE6 might work better by:

• Reducing the scale and focusing each campaign for each power bloc on tighter survival scenarios. For example:

- Europe: Cult / parasite bio-faith.
- Africa: Origin-based evolution.
- Asia: Black-market experimentation.
= Same universe. Different nightmares.
= Instead of 'Bigger threat every time', it becomes: Different threat every time.

RE7 proved a fully isolated horror works, and Requiem proved can still have a wider world hybrid but tell RE6 through localised survival spaces.

• Shifting emphasis from action set-pieces to atmosphere and tension.
• Streamlining the interface and mechanics for smoother gameplay flow.
• Grounding the global narrative in believable regional threats.

This would allow the game to retain its multi-perspective ambition which Requiem did well, while staying closer to the identity of Resident Evil.

________________________________________

Unfortunately, I do not recommend this game as it stands — even as a fan. It left me feeling more frustrated than positive. It remains an interesting experiment, but one that sits awkwardly within the Resident Evil series.

RE6 is not unsalvageable. I really think Capcom could pull this off with a rebuild.

I’m glad Capcom changed direction massively in RE7 – Back to it’s survival horror roots.

Resident Evil 6 is primarily a two‑player co‑op game that can also be played solo, but the real fun starts when you play with a buddy. The campaign is split into four main story arcs, each starring a pair of characters: Leon S. Kennedy & Helena Harper, Chris Redfield & Piers Nivans, Jake Muller & Sherry Birkin, and the unlockable Ada Wong solo campaign (with an unnamed Agent as a second player in her sections).

The atmosphere mixes horror and blockbuster action, with frequent QTEs, dramatic set‑pieces, Ada Wong’s spy‑style appearances, zombie hordes, and big boss fights. Each duo has a different feel: Leon’s story is more traditional Resident Evil with tense urban chaos, Chris’s is heavy combat and military horror, Jake’s is more over‑the‑top action, and Ada’s is a sleek, non‑linear solo‑style mission.

Overall, Resident Evil 6 is a very enjoyable, chaotic action‑packed ride that works best in co‑op perfect if you like loud, fast combat and playing through the separate campaigns with a friend.

Look, I know Resident Evil 6 gets a lot of hate from the "purists," but honestly? If you just want a game that’s pure, unadulterated fun, this is it. It’s basically a playable Michael Bay movie, and I mean that in the best way possible.

The missions are the real star here. They’re just so engaging because the game never lets you get bored. One minute you’re playing a classic survival horror segment with Leon in a dark, creepy cathedral, and the next you’re in a full-blown war zone with Chris, dodging explosions and sliding behind cover like a tactical pro. It’s got that "just one more chapter" energy because you always want to see what insane set piece they’re going to throw at you next.

Here’s the stuff people usually miss while they're complaining it "isn't scary"

The Combat is Unreal Once you figure out the movement, it’s a total game-changer. You aren't just standing there shooting you’re diving, sliding into zombies to trip them, and pulling off these brutal melee finishers. It feels more like "John Wick with zombies" than anything else.

Jake’s Campaign is a Hidden Gem Everyone talks about Leon, but Jake and Sherry’s story is a blast. Being hunted by the Ustanak feels like a modern version of the Nemesis chase, but with way more adrenaline.

Co-op is the GOAT Playing this with a friend is hands-down one of the best co-op experiences you can have. The way the stories intersect—where you’re playing your mission and suddenly bump into another player who’s playing a completely different campaign—is still such a cool, unique touch.

It’s loud, it’s chaotic, and it’s arguably the most ambitious game in the series. If you go in looking for a high-octane action thrill ride instead of a slow-burn horror game, you’re going to have a literal blast.

Tested by the Youtube channel Digital Foundry in the video "Resident Evil 4 PC: Is New DRM Impacting Game Performance?" has been found that the Enigma Protector DRM causes an average of -10% in framerate drops, with dips of -40% in certain scenarios, way more than the original Denuvo DRM.

This is not the first time that Capcom decided to put Enigma in some of their older games: RE Revelations suffered major backlash from customers because of the major dip in perfomance, so much so they had to remove Enigma from the game for good and recently they released the original Dino Crisis series on Steam, a quick scouring of the forum will reveal a lot of customers unhappy with the perfomance of said games. This is with out a doubt the worst mainline original Resident Evil game.

On the surface, the game's controls are better than 5's. This is the first game where you could move while aiming, which was novel then, as RE 4 was the major blueprint for the then current games. The shooting was snappier than 5, and you had brand new mechanics, such as dodging any direction, shooting on the ground, and rolling on the ground.

However, the kicker to that, is every enemy literally throws themselves at you, all the time, and despite using the exact same dna as 5 and 4, this game has the absolute BALLS to present itself as a nonstop action shooting game, and NOT give you any ammo to shoot with.

Despite having a larger inventory than 5, it's the most unoptimized thrown together inventory in the entire series. Everything is in one line, meaning you'll have to cycle left and right constantly through your inventory. The funniest cruel joke of this game is despite being the most hyper action focused game in the series, Ammo is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dropped like it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Resident Evil 1. You will almost always have full inventory, but it will always be a cluttered mess of grenades, herbs, or otherwise nothing items, and yet you'll never have enough ammo to complete a single level. You will constantly be whimpering through ammo reserves in EVERY single level of EVERY single campaign in this game. 

You cannot pause this game even in single player, for whatever ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason.

Defenders of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game will say "Oh there's secret button combinations you can do to avoid the insanely long falling to the ground stun animation", or to use your herbs fast, and that the combat was "misunderstood" and should be treated like a "Platinum Games" hyper action game, but what they don't mention to you is the game never teaches you these hidden mechanics, this is a THIRD PERSON SHOOTER where the AMMO is treated like a Survival HORROR game, and every campaign is filled with Michael Bay late 2000's brain dead action nonsense. There are 4 campaigns of some of the absolute WORST Third-Person action game slop you'll ever see. Let's lightly talk about them.

Chris - Feels like the campaign they wanted to make. If you are just coming off of Resident Evil 5, the enemies feel like an evolution of the Javo from that game. Although RE 5 raped the games Horror roots with literal black men with ak-47's becoming the main enemy by the end of the game, this game  brings those back but now they can mutate into different creatures. That's about it. This is the only campaign where it seems like you can last for more than 3 mins without running out of ammo, and because of that, this campaign can actually be a decent amount of fun, with a friend. Biggest problem is the Chopper boss fight, but it is def the most enjoyable.

Leon - Advertised for "classic and survival horror fans", what you get is a more relatable experience to RE 4 gameplay wise, except, You will barely have ammo, there's no merchant to upgrade your guns, You will have multiple split up from your partner moments, and about just 4 enemy types. The set pieces in Leon's campaign aren't terrible, and Helena was a great partner character for him, but once again, you will be fatigued before getting half way through it. For whatever reason, the very end of his campaign is used as the """tutorial""", which teaches you barely nothing about this game. Helena gets the ♥♥♥♥ stick all of his campaign, with the final boss literally having her just watching Leon fight the big bad while she can provide Sniper cover. Once she's out of ammo, that's it. She literally can't even participate in the fight anymore.

Jake - The absolute worst campaign out of the original 3. Jake's campaign makes you think it's going to be a throw back to RE 3's Nemesis, but what you get in this one, is non-stop quick time events, collect 3 keys in a snow level where you can't see, and some of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ driving segments you'll ever see in gameplay history. I beat this campaign once on PS3 and never touched it again, it's that bad, and anyone saying they genuinely enjoyed his campaign need to be studied, because it is the most filler based nothing gameplay of the 3 original campaigns. You will be sick and tired of mash the cranks while the Boss creature chases you by the second ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chapter.

Ada - Originally hidden, unlocked by beating the previous 3, and now just unlocked by default, Ada's is the least developed and most half-baked part of these campaigns. Her scenario feels like the demo for this game, and compounds literally everything I just said that was negative into basically the entire gimmick of the campaign. Her campaign is the shortest, but EVERY negative from the previous campaign is in this one. Corridors of dry shooting with barely any level design. Relentless nonsense QtE's Chase a monster eating a key 3 times just to pad this junk piece of ♥♥♥♥ out longer, and there's your bonus campaign. Dog with a side of ♥♥♥♥

Mercenaries is passable, but not worth paying anything other than maybe 2.99 for. An extra bonus of Left 4 Dead characters can't save it either.

You have the option of having QtE's auto complete, but you STILL have to watch those animations.

With a friend, RE 6 is still enjoyable, but no where near to the degree as RE 5. The level design is bland, the shooting is dull, the game has more QtE's than ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ RE4, the boss fights aren't even memorable either. The mode where you can invade random people as a monster, is half-baked, but an interesting concept, but, there's just not much here to warrant even 20 dollars now a days.

If there was a mod out there that actually re-balanced the drops enemies give you, and you could actually have ammo, you'd have a C- game here at best. With what was released, this game is NOT worth 20 dollars at all. If you ended up with it for 5, even that's pushing it.

There is almost no reason to replay any of these campaigns once beaten. As an interesting look, I'd say Chris and Leon's campaigns may be worth playing with a friend, but, you will really be pushing it once you get half way through either. If you beat both of those and really absolutely want to play through Jake's and Ada's, just know there is quite literally nothing but brain dead copy pasted content waiting for you in those.

Despite being pure ♥♥♥♥, this game has continued to sell well, because it ended up in the bargain bin, and used to go on sale for less than 4.99 quite a lot back in the day. If you got it in some random bundle for that amount, that's all I'd spend on the game. Anything more is throwing money into the fire.

I have to respectfully ask: How can anyone genuinely defend this game? No seriously. Even with experience playing it solo and watching someone play it in Co-op, even the power of friendship cannot defend how awfully bad this game is. But before we officially get into the very nitty gritty on why you should avoid this game at all costs let's talk the positives.

First things first, the main menu music is the best part of the entire game, I like some of the zombie designs and the genuinely horrifying nightmare fuel of it which Capcom is usually great at. And the unsung potential man that is Jake Muller himself. I know people kinda treat Jake as a joke in some corners and have every legit reason why they don't like him, but looking at him now, he's kind of hilarious and the best part of the entire game, just his quippy energy in a chaotic mess of a game and carrying it on his back, out of all the campaigns in the entire game, Jake and Sherry is the best one by far in a sea of dumb decisions and bad campaigns.

The biggest problem with RE6 is that it's a game that tries to appeal to everyone, the Survival Horrors, the COD kids and beyond that it straight up appeals to nobody. Cutscenes and campaign specific moments that tries to connect all the characters together just feels forced and bloats the game to unreasonable sizes.

Quick Time Event hell is plagued in specific moments ESPECIALLY on Leon's campaign, you know.. the SURVIVAL HORROR experience. Enemies that can instantly kill your NPC partner or you even after picking them up in the downed state and overall just a massive sensory overload of explosions and so many things going on for those with disabilities like myself.

If you play RE6 and enjoy the Mercenaries mode, fair enough you do you, it's not my place to judge you, but for any newcomer to RE6, SKIP THIS GAME AND AVOID IT LIKE THE PLAGUE, watch videos about it instead and just skip straight to RE7, you're doing yourself a favor.

To be honest? I don't entirely understand why people tend to complain about this entry in the RE series. I can see how some people aren't a fan of the genre switch per main campaign, but aside from Ada's I thought it was neat. Felt like smash bros ultimate where quite literally everyone is here!! Well, except Claire. ;-; Aside from that... 

Leon's story is obviously meant to harp more on the traditional horror part of RE, with what the main focus being on zombies rather than some big bad. I really did like the melee (for everyone, but the sideway kicks, c'mon!) and wound up using that way more than my guns lol. Helena's side story didn't leave me with any strong opinions? I didn't really know why she was there, whereas all the other partners were explained. Maybe it was explained in the trailer but I don't watch those so as to not spoil myself... either way. A solid 2nd place in terms of favorite campaigns! Played it 2nd in terms of order. Had good pacing, was likely meant to be scary if I wasn't already desensitized...

I would say Chris' story is definitely more action-based, meant to be kind of like how RE5 was. I didn't mind it- at least we had a useable partner this time- and overall it was a lot of fun! I did note the unique UI that I don't believe literally anyone else got, which is like, oookay Mr. Redfield Capcom, go off I guess? Oh. This campaign was the 3rd one I did, but unarguebly my absolute favorite! We've seen Chris grow so much since RE1 and it's always such a treat getting to play him!! Or maybe just because he's my favorite character... either way, I will miss Piers, but this one was my favorite.

As for Jake/Sherry... Eh. Obviously a mix of the horror and action. I liked it, and it was the first one I did (Come on, showing me Sherry for the first time since RE2? We're so back-) but then I didn't end up having any strong feelings about it by the very end of things. I did love seeing an adult Sherry running around, and I very much enjoyed Jake's Leon-eqsue humor. I thought they were cute together. Oh. Yeah. I guess this means that ALBERT WESKER does get some. That was... something. Either way, first I did, and my third favorite.

I don't wanna talk about Ada's. She was the last, and arguely the worst of the bunch! It was meant to be more stealth based, but much like the DLC for Relevations 2, it just didn't really work? Starting off with difficult to deal with end-game enemies and then having to fight them with starter gear made the first chapter pretty damn unfun. In the end, I've decided I'd much rather a video than play through Ada's campaign. It just... wasn't fun? She was the only one I kept having to re-do, either because I'd run out of patience or time to actually have a committed run, and at that point... what was the point meant to be? If I'm not having fun, I'm not playing it. I know her story is meant to connect all the tiny points together, but eh. Worst of the bunch >:[

Oookay. Now that THAT is over with... I don't know. I liked the game alot! The different campaigns kept things fresh, and it was an absolute treat to see everyone together in the same game!! Well. Even if I was sorely confused by the end... yeah imma go watch some lore videos to understand what it is I just played. What of it?! 

Yeah but nah, RE6 is a good game. (Much better than RE5 :sunglasses)

Bogus

• A great portion of the game is not actually gameplay. It's button-mashing, quick-time events, running sequences, vehicle sections, etc. This hurts the game so much

• Both villains are lame and suck
• A lot of guns don't feel very great to use, especially the shotguns
• The game never teaches the player crucial elements of the gameplay, such as the counter-attack, quick-shot, crouch, etc

• Controls can be wonky because there is so much, specifically the aim button also being the cover button

The story, while ambitious, is [i]incredibly[/i] out in left field. Resident Evil is at its best when it embraces the horror experience in an S-tier hub environment: mansions, police stations, villages. This game has essentially NO horror and may as well be a hallway-running-shooter. It may have the face of a RE game, but it has none of the DNA. And so for me this was a massive swing-and-miss entry.

I gradually found myself at my wit’s end with this standout, purely action-oriented entry in the franchise. Despite running out of patience fairly early on, and as divisive as Resident Evil 6 remains to this day, I can still appreciate the attempt to build upon the established frameworks of its predecessors (mainly 4th and 5th instalment) and to experiment with them further. To my genuine surprise, I am baffled that completely erasing survival or horror elements (something so dear to those who have followed this universe since its emergence in 1996) somehow still results in something like this.
 
That said, I can confidently remark that I do not intend to replay or revisit this game. Certainly not as enthusiastically as I feel towards other releases in the series. Were it not for a fun cooperative experience with a fellow Ada Wong enthusiast, I would have given up shortly after completing the first of the four available campaigns (prelude chapter excluded).
 
In recounting the storyline, the game resembles something akin to a blatant example of 2010s Hollywood-style scriptwriting with an extremely messy inclination to let the player experience the same “hits” (boss fights and entire sequences) in order to artificially prolong playtime. I cannot stress enough how blandly and rigidly the assortment of fan-favourite characters is portrayed here (including the new additions, though some are admittedly very much welcome).
 
Gameplay-wise, it is safe to say there are indeed a few interesting mechanics, in terms of movement and large-scale action set pieces. However, that doesn´t excuse the confusing camera perspective switches, exhausting QTE timed sequences, and the near-insurmountable “running from a tank” segment that needs fixing. And additionally, the whole Ada campaign second playable character patchwork implementation, which just comes across as rather ridiculous (though I am aware that this game released some fourteen years ago).

My main takeaway from this brief assessment is the same as most reviews on here:  find someone to play with in co-op, or be prepared for miserably spent 20-ish or so hours filled with relentless explosions you will soon find unbearable to the resilience of your eardrums.

While I was initially impressed at some of the improvements from RE5 in the early hours of this game (namely improved combat and a proper horror tone) I quickly grew weary of RE6. The gunplay started strong but grew repetitive before too long. I also found myself without ammo far too often for an action game (also by survival horror standards), which left me frustrated pretty often. The UI is very difficult to navigate, and paired with some unintuitive key bindings I really found myself frustrated at this game regularly. The story wasn't too engaging either, and coupled with my other issues it really made the game drag for me.

Leon's campaign was fine enough but not all that interesting by the end. Chris's was much worse frankly; it felt like it was trying to imitate Call of Duty on a surface level, with some generic body-horror enemies to try and keep it on-brand with Resident Evil. It really didn't work for me and it was pretty boring for the most part. Both campaigns had some good ideas, even a few fun sections here and there, but I was mostly apathetic towards the game as it went on. If anything I was glad when it was over. Like with RE5, this game is better when played in co-op, but that often didn't work as intended and I sometimes would be dropped from a session for no reason.

As of writing this I haven't played Jake or Ada's campaign yet. I fully intend to at some point, but honestly I'm super burnt out on RE6 so I expect it will be a while before I do. This game is far too long and far too generic to justify four separate stories, especially when they overlap as much as they do. I won't pretend like I didn't have fun in parts of this game, but I think it's a pretty telling sign that by the end of both campaigns, I was just trying to get through the game as fast as I could so I could move on. You could easily skip this one, but if you want to give it a try then go for it, just don't spend more than $5 on it.

At the time of writing this review, I've finished Leon's campaign, and I'm on the final chapter of Chris's. I don't know if I will complete it or the rest of the campaigns. Maybe I will out of a sense of completionism and morbid curiosity. I don't think it will get any better though. RE6 is such a bizarre game. Normally with game reviews, the elements that really bring it down are technical ones such as unresponsive gameplay, glitches, and bad graphics. RE6 doesn't have those. The gameplay/gunplay is actually really good and does some very interesting things in the 3rd person shooter genre. The game is in a great technical state, and you can tell that a ton of care was put into the environments. In other words, the money is on the screen with this game. It's sprawling, enormous campaigns take about 5 hours each to complete, so that's 20 hours purely of campaign, which is fully co-op. Coming from RE5, that co-op is significantly better because your companion, if AI-controlled, cannot die. Enemies still have a fair amount of health, but it isn't absurd like RE5, and the melee options really help out with finishing enemies. The campaign is basically the Resident Evil version of the Avengers as it brings in so many franchise characters and new ones in this gigantic, interconnected narrative. Why, then, the negative review?

There's a moment in Chris's campaign where you are assaulting an aircraft carrier filled with Neo-Umbrella mutated monsters. After fighting your way through the cargo deck, which involves a fight against a stationary jet whose gunner relentlessly fires at you, you learn that there is another aircraft carrier launching missiles with a virus. You then board a fighter jet, fly toward this boat and shoot down AA guns, missiles, and, eventually, a giant B.O.W. before ultimately failing in your task. Take out the horror elements, and what I just described was not a Resident Evil game but a Call of Duty mission, and that is exactly what is wrong with RE6. Somewhere along the way of developing RE6, they forgot what makes this franchise unique. In catering to the action genre and Call of Duty, the developers lost the essence of Resident Evil. There are no explorable areas in this game with locked treasures. There is no inventory or resource management. There are not even rudimentary puzzles or journals/logs lying around to spell out the more specific points of the plot. Most of the game, in fact, is just a disguised corridor that takes you from one fight to the next. There are remnants of Resident Evil's DNA there, such as the breakable boxes, herb combining, and occasional key gathering, but these feel out of place in a game that generally only want to push you toward the next combat encounter so you can snap a zombie's neck or roundhouse kick their head off. 

Resident Evil games are at their best when the narrative seems to molded specifically to fit its characters, and that is not the case here. The narrative is a confusing mess due to the 4 campaign structure. I guffawed when I rolled credits on Leon's story because I still had no clue what was happening. Who is Helena, Leon's partner? Why was her sister mutated into a nude BOW with booba? How did the United States President, who Leon kills in the beginning of the game, get infected with the virus? Why was he in a college town? Literally none of this questions are ever answered or addressed, but Leon just plows on through as the game demands that he must. 

RE6 may be flawed to its very core. Any attempt at a remake, as Capcom has been doing, would require, I think, a massive redesign from the ground-up. I don't know if it is salvageable without completing tearing it all apart. If there is one good thing about RE6, it's that its failure paved the way to RE7, which is one of the series' crowning achievements.

Survival on a Global Scale – A Review of Resident Evil 6

Overall Rating: 8.25/10

Resident Evil 6 represents the most ambitious and expansive entry in the franchise’s action era. Rather than refining a single direction, it multiplies them—offering four interconnected campaigns that span continents, characters, and tones. Where earlier titles focused on contained outbreaks and concentrated dread, Resident Evil 6 escalates the formula into a globe-spanning bio-terror crisis. The result is a game that prioritizes scale, spectacle, and mechanical freedom over tight horror pacing. It may lack the focused identity of its predecessors, but it delivers survival through momentum, variety, and sheer scope.

Visual Design and Atmosphere: 8/10

The game’s environments are diverse and cinematic, moving from urban outbreaks and war-torn streets to laboratories, catacombs, and international cities. Lighting and environmental effects emphasize chaos rather than isolation—explosions, collapsing structures, and large-scale destruction dominate the visual language. While it sacrifices the claustrophobic dread of earlier entries, Resident Evil 6 compensates with spectacle. The world feels unstable and constantly under siege. Visibility is higher, movement is faster, and encounters are larger. The atmosphere shifts from intimate horror to global catastrophe, creating tension through instability rather than confinement.

Story and Narrative: 8/10

Resident Evil 6 tells its story through intersecting campaigns led by Leon S. Kennedy, Chris Redfield, Jake Muller, and Ada Wong with each offering a distinct tone. Political conspiracy, military tragedy, viral experimentation, and personal stakes intertwine into a layered narrative about worldwide bio-terrorism. The scope is impressive, but the structure can feel fragmented. Tonal shifts between horror, action thriller, and military drama occasionally disrupt cohesion. Still, the overarching theme remains consistent: survival is no longer about escaping a mansion or a village—it is about confronting a world unraveling at scale. The story embraces cinematic ambition, even if it sometimes struggles under its own weight.

Gameplay and Survival Mechanics: 8/10

Mechanically, Resident Evil 6 is the most fluid entry of its time. Players can move while shooting, slide, dodge, counter, and chain melee attacks with stamina management. Combat is fast and flexible, offering more control than ever before. However, increased mobility shifts the survival dynamic. Vulnerability is reduced, and encounters often resemble action set pieces rather than calculated survival scenarios. Resources still matter, but the emphasis leans toward adaptability and combat proficiency rather than careful conservation. The expanded mechanics are impressive, yet they reinforce the game’s action-forward identity.

Sound Design and Music: 8/10

The sound design reinforces urgency and cinematic scale. Gunfire, environmental destruction, and enemy mutations are impactful and clear. The score leans heavily into orchestral intensity, swelling during combat and narrative climaxes. Although it lacks the subdued, haunting minimalism of earlier entries, the audio direction effectively supports the game’s high-stakes, blockbuster tone.

Replayability and Longevity: 10/10

Few entries match Resident Evil 6 in sheer content volume. Multiple campaigns, cooperative play, unlockables, skill systems, and Mercenaries mode provide extensive replay value. The refined movement system makes Mercenaries particularly engaging, rewarding mastery of mobility and crowd control. The chapter structure also allows players to revisit specific segments, encouraging experimentation and higher difficulty runs.

Conclusion: 8.25/10

Resident Evil 6 is an ambitious expansion of the franchise’s action direction. It prioritizes scope, cinematic design, and mechanical depth over concentrated horror pacing. While its tonal variety can feel uneven, it remains mechanically robust and content-rich. It may not deliver traditional survival horror in its purest form, but it offers survival through escalation, adaptability, and relentless momentum.

Final Verdict:

Resident Evil 6 transforms survival horror into a global, interconnected crisis. By embracing scale, spectacle, and player mobility, it delivers a bold and content-heavy experience that stands as the culmination of the series’ action-driven evolution—even if that evolution divides opinion.

[quote]Just saying, but I do have a curator page. If you like my remarks about games, you can find more of them here: https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44130985-TDP%27s-Gaming-Escapades [/quote]

Resident Evil 6 is quite a controversial title. It was developed and released through Capcom's dark age, when they just could not help but constantly shoot themselves in the foot with their horrible actions and decisions.
The game promised to be very big, providing three different gameplay campaigns that each offered a unique gameplay style in order to please all of Resident Evil's fans. Leon's campaign was supposed to focus on horror, Chris' campaign was designed to offer a more action-oriented experience for RE5 fans, and Jake's campaign was supposed to be a blend of two with additional ability of engaging in melee combat with enemies.
Now that looks great on paper, but is a nightmare otherwise. If you really want to do something like that, you have to basically create three different games as each of these genres use different game mechanics and design philosophies. Understandably, Capcom didn't want to do that, so they just reused the same template over all of the campaigns and tried to change it to suit their needs. As you can expect... it didn't work out.


Before we begin, I have to clarify that I have beaten Chris and Jake's campaigns a long time ago. I was playing the game again to experience Leon and Ada's campaigns, then refresh my memory on how the other two were and come up with a review to check this game off my backlog; But four hours into Leon's campaign, and I couldn't take it anymore. Now this is not to say the game is bad, it's just horribly flawed and I'll get to explain all of them soon. But do note that whatever I'm saying here is based on my fresh experience with Leon's campaign alone.


Let's address the elephant in the room first: Resident Evil 6 is designed from the ground up to be played in Co-Op; And there's a lot in the game that proves my claim is right.
All of the campaigns feature two protagonists, there are an excessive amount of rooms and actions that require both characters to be present, there is no true pause button and the gameplay still continues as you are going through the menus, the game constantly tries to connect to its online services even in the offline game mode, your inventory is dynamic and its contents persist between your playthroughs, and whatever you go through in the campaigns is downright painful without a second player on your side.
As such, Resident Evil 6 can potentially be a really fun game to go through ONLY if played in Co-Op and you have someone to laugh at and make fun of stuff with. Trust me, I played through this game solo, and while the AI partners are way more competent and reliable than Sheva, I honestly had such a miserable time that I decided quitting is far more beneficial than trying to endure whatever happens in the game. Let me explain why.


First, I must admit that the game shows actual effort has gone into making it. However, not only a whole lot of these efforts have been misguided, but the game has some glaring issues that reveal themselves more as you play it alone.
To start with the positives, the graphics and models look very good for the time [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3665055706](with the glaring exception of some zombies)[/url], the cinematics are great, the multiplayer modes (especially agent hunt) are creative, and the combat system in particular is pretty well-made as well. You have a lot of offensive and defensive options, and I would honestly not be shocked if I find out Capcom developers had used it as a basis for their future games. Admittedly, I was also very surprised and delighted to be reminded of Leon's martial arts expertise, seeing him performing roundhouse kicks and RKOs on zombies... a reminder that he should have been the Resident Evil representative in Marvel vs Capcom games and not Chris.
Then we get to the bad stuff, and there's a lot of them. There's an overwhelming hollywood-esque action feeling to the whole game and even when it's supposed to terrify you, it doesn't. The music is absent at times when it should have been used to create a proper atmosphere. Actual horror is completely gone, and has given its way to completely predictable jumpscares that are accompanied by loud sounds and usually come out of nowhere. The monster design is very lackluster in my opinion, especially compared to older titles, feeling like the devs just ripped off some of them from Left 4 Dead or similar zombie games. And then we have the overly scripted nature of the game.
Resident Evil 6 has a severe case of overscripting its events, to the point literally everything has become predictable and/or annoying. Sometimes you dump five shotgun shells into a zombie's head, just to realize it has invulnerability during its intoductory animation. A lot of times, the dead bodies that are lying around show no reaction to your interactions (basically nothing happens when you attack them), just to suddenly spring to life and lunge at you after getting to a specific point or event.


Things don't get any better when we get to the gameplay either. The game does not give you enough health items as the item drops seem to be randomly generated, forcing you to grind for them. Enemies' lunge attacks seem to be prioritized over player actions, letting them easily interrupt your in-progress melee attacks and finishers or [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3665054966]making them being able to bite you without a head[/url]. The special biohazard creatures barely react to your attacks, tanking through them to come at you, and need an absurd amount of damage to be killed. The experience is built to offer a Co-Op experience, yet the game constantly separates the players from each other while showering one or both of them with enemies that they have to deal with. And don't get me started on the overuse of QTEs and their horrible implementation on PC, because who the hell binds a split-second dodge move to the combination of "Space+R"?
I have to also mention the excessive horde survival sections through Leon's campaign in particular. For a horror focused experience, you go through way too many moments that force you to fight hordes of zombies that seemingly appear out of nowhere. And these moments are actually very destructive for the gameplay experience as they blur the line between winnable and unwinnable scenarios, causing the player to fight with a rapidly respawning crowd of zombies until explicitly told to run away.


And let me remind you that all of what you read above, is the culmination of 4 hours of fresh gameplay in one campaign. If I found this many things wrong with one campaign, I don't know how many more I would have ran into if I went through the whole thing and if I was even able to write a review without going way past the word limit.
Resident Evil 6 is... a disappointing game. It tried to satisfy everyone and has ended up satisfying no one instead, mostly due to its developers at Capcom having no concrete idea of what they wanted to do with the series after RE4's success. It's just a mishmash of ideas that are not cooked to perfection and used corrently where they belong, resulting in a game that is only fun if you have someone willing to accompany you through the whole thing.


[h2]TL;DR[/h2]
Tries to satisfy everyone, pleases no one. It's a mishmash of uncooked ideas that are not used correctly either, leading to a miserable experience that gets much more tolerable while playing Co-Op.
