When I first played this game, I was expecting an awful Resident Evil game but a pretty good action game. However, even as an action game I think this is a very flawed game and not a good one. The game is separated into four campaigns so I will briefly discuss each one

Leon’s Campaign: in my opinion this one is easily the worst. The atmosphere is not bad and the story is okay but the gameplay is really bad here. The first half is pretty bad with really boring puzzles and set pieces and all of the enemies outside of basic zombies are very boring and tedious to fight, and as well most of the guns feel very bad and unsatisfying and the quick time events are at their absolute worst here. And the final boss is just 4 or 5 very annoying and ridiculously over the top set pieces that overstay their welcome. 4.5/10

Chris’s Campaign: This one I actually think is the best one and a pretty decent story. Once you get past the dumb concept of zombies with guns I feel like the guns and combat are better here than in Leon’s story. As long as you go in expecting a dumb action story kind of like RE5, then you will like it more. Piers is also a great side character and the best new character in my opinion, and his scene at the end of the campaign is actually really well done surprisingly. 7.4/10

Jake’s Campaign: This one is just alright in my opinion. There are some really cool moments with the new stalker enemy and some other areas that are cool but other than that it’s not that great. The second chapter with the snowmobile and the stealth section is really bad however and the new melee system is kind of useless until the end. 6.3/10

Ada’s Campaign: not horrible but just really mid. The stealth is really bad in this campaign but the crossbow is one of the best weapons in the game. However almost the whole campaign is recycled stuff from the other ones, including the bad parts. And the story with the two Ada Wongs is really stupid. Thankfully it’s short. 5.2/10

There are more overall issues with the game like the dumb writing, the really long length, and the obvious lack of horror the series is known for but the mercenaries mode in this game is genuinely amazing and might be the best in the series for some. The combat works so well in this mode and it’s hilarious fun that honestly might make it worth playing just for that and a friend. And the no-mercy mode makes it so much better and chaotic with the Left 4 Dead characters. 

Overall, not a game that is awful for the most part. And the mercenaries mode and Chris campaign are good, but overall the game is just insanely mediocre when you combine it all together.

🧟 Resident Evil 6 – Over-the-Top Action With Plenty of Content

Resident Evil 6 might not be traditional survival horror, but with nearly 24 hours played, I can say it’s packed with content and delivers an exciting, action-heavy ride.

🎭 Four Campaigns, One Big Story

The game offers four different campaigns, each with its own characters, tone, and perspective. Leon’s sections bring back some of the classic eerie Resident Evil atmosphere, while Chris, Jake, and Ada deliver explosive action and unique storylines. It’s ambitious and gives players a lot of variety.

🔫 Action-Packed Gameplay

If you’re looking for nonstop action, RE6 delivers. From large-scale battles to cinematic quick-time events, the game is always throwing new challenges at you. It’s more about big set pieces and adrenaline than slow-burn horror, but it nails the “blockbuster” feel.

👥 Co-Op Fun

Playing solo is fine, but Resident Evil 6 shines brightest in co-op. Teaming up with a friend to tackle bosses, share resources, and survive together makes the game much more enjoyable.

🌍 Tons of Replay Value

Between the multiple campaigns, different characters, and cooperative play, there’s a lot of content here. Add in Mercenaries mode for extra fun, and RE6 offers hours of gameplay beyond the main story.

⭐ Final Thoughts

Four campaigns with different styles.

Fast-paced, cinematic action.

Best enjoyed with a co-op partner.

A huge package with lots of replayability.

👉 Resident Evil 6 might not be classic survival horror, but it’s a wild, action-packed ride that gives fans tons of content and co-op fun.

A lot of people hate on this game, which is sad because it's not that bad as a whole. 

I will say I wasn't quite a fan at first. I actually dropped it about a year ago and then came back to try it again. The storyline is pretty cool. The horror isn't the best, but the action was fun to me overall. Definitely gave me some Halo vibes in some ways. I disliked the gameplay for the majority of my first time playing through all campaigns, although the QTEs weren't so bad. I got frustrated even though I was just playing on Normal difficulty. Maybe my mistake was trying to jump into Chris' campaign immediately when apparently it is recommended to play Leon's first haha or maybe using keyboard and mouse didn't help either

But once I got used to it, it was more enjoyable for me. I had fun going back to find the collectibles I missed as well as doing all the campaign achievements I could, even on higher difficulties. I liked using my skill points so I could have infinite ammo. I liked seeing how the characters would cross each other's paths and have to work together. Leon's path was probably my favourite because I liked fighting zombies and there were some RE2 vibes. Ada and Chris are tied for second. I didn't like Jake's much at all and found it to be dull and boring.

I imagine it's even better and chaotic with friends, but I had no one to play with at the time so I can't vouch for any of the multiplayer modes whatsoever.

A huge con for me was that I experienced horrible issues with my first time playing Jake's campaign when I was playing as Sherry. I played as her the entire time. My inventory kept disappearing every time I'd end up in a new section in Chapter 4 I believe. It was difficult to deal with running out of ammo thanks to that dumb bug. That went away after I got to the next chapter. Throughout the campaign, I had issues with freezing, so I'd lose all my progress and get sent far back and have to restart sections... I had no issues with Chris, Leon, and Ada's campaigns, so not sure what was happening there. I had already disliked Jake's pretty fast due to how boring it was, so these issues soured my experience even more. I hope no one else has had these issues because I got so annoyed lol

But all in all, I'd say you should definitely give this game a chance, especially if you're a huge Resident Evil fan. It's different from the other games, but not a bad different. Just have some patience and maybe you'll end up having more fun with it than you thought.

Hmm a difficult question, I have put/would like to say yes but it's not a complete defo YES.
We wanted a great co-op game we could play together and enjoy as a couple.
We play this game, along with Res Evil 5/Desperate Escape which we've finished in pro with an S grade.
This game however is sadly different.
What's great about this game.
Great story/scenarios.
Great characters.
Great environments.
Coop
What lets it down badly in our opinion.
The camera in Res Evil 5 follows the characters direction automatically 
(No player input required) and works perfectly.

The camera in this doesn't, which results in the player constantly having to reposition the camera every direction they take, example turn left down a street, the camera is still facing in the direction previously set.
You can press the centre button on sticks to reposition the camera but is not really helpful when your in the middle of a load of enemies.
What would improve the game massively in our opinion, would be to add the option of whether to lock the camera to a characters direction or not. If Capcom could of only added that option, it could of been a completely different outcome to what could of been a great game, such a missed opportunity.
Conclusion I recommend if you want a good co-op and don't mind having to constantly fight the camera rather than enjoy the game, fighting the enemies ,which is what the point of playing the game should be.

Then he gets in a car that crashes. Then he hops on a bus that also crashes. Then he rides a minecart that crashes. Then he boards an airplane to China which crashes. Then he goes on a train that crashes as well. Finally he gets on an elevator which also crashes and burns. This dude went on 7 different modes of transport in the span of his 5 hour campaign that all crash and burn. 

The enemies and bosses are also unsatisfying to fight, mainly because they feel spongey and don't react much to your gunfire which makes the combat feel weightless. And it gets worse when the game doesn't tell you whether the boss you're up against is an actual boss fight or just another action set piece that you're meant to wait out for the next cutscene to play. That Simmons fight in Leon's campaign was the worst as he had like 50 different phases and I couldn't tell which one required me to actually damage him to progress.

The game is also a bloated mess. This might be the largest RE game to date clocking in at 20 hours as each of the 4 campaigns are 5 hours long and most of them recycle content from other campaigns. It just feels like every campaign went on for 2 hours longer than it needed to be (that Cathedral/Catacombs section felt like it went on forever.) That's 20 hours of near non-stop QTEs and action set pieces.

And why is the game so dark and ugly? None of the visuals or environments were pleasing to look at which is surprising considering RE5 was much more vibrant and colourful.

Also this might just be me but what's up with Ada's face? Why does she looks so plastic here? All the other characters looked fine but there's just something off about her face that I can't put my finger on it. 

But yeah, RE6 is a mess. Avoid this game unless you're idea of fun is 20 hours of recycled action set pieces.

As a third person shooter it's not terrible. It has some innovative movement and melee options that are surprisingly easy to pick up, but as a Resident Evil game it's kind of boring, honestly. The survival horror aspects are gone entirely and it plays out as a pretty linear action shlockfest with an over-reliance on 'cinematic' flourishes. Cutscenes interrupt the flow of gameplay frequently. The camera sometimes forcibly pans to 'show' you important dialogue or areas. There's entirely too many QTE moments.

Tonally as a story it doesn't really gel, either. Resident Evil has always been a bit unintentionally (or possibly intentionally) hammy with it's characters and dialogue, but RE6 never quite seems to be self-aware, playing itself with an utter seriousness that makes the absurd events and dialogue even more ridiculous by contrast. The action plays out through four separate 'chapters' focusing on two different playable characters whose missions sometimes intersect briefly with the other three. It's a neat idea, but the almost total thematic and genre shifts in each chapter make it hard to get invested or find a cohesive theme. It's almost as if the design team had four different ideas for an RE6 title and just decided to kitchen sink them all together rather than picking any one of them and developing it with more immersion and nuance.

It's not a broken game or even necessarily a terrible game. But I didn't feel it really added anything to the Resident Evil palette.

Combat is very run and gun, as much as you can do that in third person but with limited ammo as per the RE mantra. However, the enemies in this game are some of the most frustrating nonsense. You know in RE4 where the enemies would sometimes morph into the bug heads and how that got frustrating with your limited ammo reserves...well it's that turned up to 11. Almost every enemy after a certain point in the story morphs into something else when you kill it...sometimes more than once. It becomes VERY tedious after you go through it a few times, and that is for all 4 campaigns.

Yes, this is definitely an Action game, but I enjoyed every minute of it 
It continues the Resident Evil storyline with Chris, Leon, Ada Wong and even has Sherry Birkin as an adult now (The girl you save in Resident Evil 2) as a playable Character. 
The game also introduces new characters including Wesker's Son! DUN DUN DUN... But he's a good guy :)

The game is primarly designed as a co-op game just like Resident Evil 5 was, if you play solo then your ally will simply be controller by the computer AI. You can play online co-op or local splitscreen which is cool. 

I recommend playing this with a controller as this game was designed with console in mind, the keyboard layout is very weird and there are a TON of quick time events (action game) and they are MUCH easier to pull off with a controller.

I'll say it again, this is an action game, but a very fun one at that. There are a total of 4 different campaigns! Each one with a different character duo, except Ada Wong which is solo. All 4 character campaigns interact with the stories of the other character campaigns at one point or another, and sometimes you even fight bosses together which is AWESOME. In order to fully beat the game and completely understand the story then you must play all 4 campaigns. Took me nearly 30 hours on Professional difficulty so it has a lot of playtime.

RE6 is a very ambitious game with 4 simultaneous interacting storylines with many characters. It's NOT like the traditional survivor horror genre of the first 3 games, but is similar to the playstyle of RE4 and RE5 with the action turned WAY up. Highly recommend ths game to add to your Resident Evil collection.

This game is truly a masterpiece of the series. The amount of detail poured into every corner of the game is spectacular. Not only you get 4 campaign sections - Helena, Chris, Jake, Ada, but also very well executed intersections giving the stories much more meaning, suspense & realistic feel. After witnessing first intersection  I was absolutely amazed. The fact that you get to see the context of the other person being present there in their own story is absolutely mindblowing. The voice commands system is absolute top notch. The only minus in it is why can't we as players use "sorry" & "hang in there" commands when someone calls out for help. It would make more sense than saying simple "Yes" or "No". The campaign that's called Leon is actually Helena's campaign. Which you realize quickly after finishing the campaign. Leon is there to support Helena's journey. Very rarely the story steers in Leon's direction. It's just called Leon because fans have no idea who Helena is and would be less excited if it wasn't called Leon. I think the game offers so much, and a little bit of everything for everyone. You want to lean more into the classics of Resident Evil, you will definitely enjoy Helena's campaign the most. The freedom of movement, partner's company & hordes of zombies make this game much better than anything in the series ever made & still made past RE6. Chris's story shows the dark truth of Chris's journey in the BSAA - it never gets easier. He is not the scared Chris from the Mansion. He fights, he shows no mercy to enemies & tries to save the world no matter the cost. Yes, his campaign is the most action oriented, as should be expected. Chris is no rookie, he is BSAA member, let's not act surprised now. His partner who is basically nobody (to new players) at the start of the campaign and ends up being hero of Chris's story. RIP Piers, praying for prequel with my boy. Jake's story does not stop with the action, however this time you get absolute chills. The fear of getting caught by this creature called Ustanak does not stop throughout the whole story. You never know where he will be, what he will be holding, what kind of weapon he is preparing for Jake. Sherry is an excellent companion and absolute killer of a comeback following re2. Her contribution to the story is important and helps Jake grow as person. Tiny detail I love is that in chapter 1 Jake does not care enough to scream Sherry's name, instead he will just scream Nooooo. However past chapter 1 he starts to actually care & now feels some kind of need to protect her. Need Jake and Sherry comeback in spin-off game like revelations or something. Sherry, Jake need to come back! Ada is the main character of this game. Which is surprising considering how little of her we get compared to others. Though it does make sense. Ada is the last piece of puzzle that finished the story of RE6. Absolutely love her personality in this game. The voice, sass, kindness, absolute honor to have her in such amazing game. Ada is mostly puzzle oriented story, but she brings back some of the survival horror as well. People think survival horror is only dark rooms, scary soundtrack, slow movement, lighter (shading RE9, yes) But these enemies are damn scary,  you don't feel as much as fear as in tight space, but there's something terrifying about having to fight hordes of terrorists & zombies while trying to stay alive. Reminded me of ubistvo - chainsaw never disappoints in resident evil games. Absolute banger of a game. They need to make another one like this. The latest games aren't really it. This is what resident evil did the best. The action horror. And haters need to loosen up. Resident evil is not defined by RE1, it's where the series started, and it was always headed to action. They have to add new introverted characters to keep the series alive because of people like you. Now we are awaiting another Ethan Winters with RE9. Anyway, this is the best game I ever playe. Absolute 10/10. Coop is absolute yes from me. When i feel like going solo, I also got the option - this should be standard for RE games having coop option.

This game tries to be a fast-paced action shooter, but the execution is abysmal. The "shamblers" are more active than before, but your character’s movement, aim, and field of view haven’t been updated to keep up. The 3D environments are too claustrophobic for decent gunplay; aiming is awkward, and getting surrounded is far too easy. Lurker ambushes are unavoidable, even when you see them coming. Instead of shooting them first, you're forced to get jumped and lose a health bar. The zombies are bullet sponges; even headshots take multiple hits, and aiming is a chore thanks to the primitive bullet "spread" in the reticle. The lighting is awful; meant to be atmospheric, but it just makes everything dark. Constant scripted vehicle crashes kill you out of nowhere, and the tight environments and lack of peripheral vision mean you’re always getting blindsided. There’s zero horror, it's just a third-person shooter designed by a team that clearly didn’t specialize in that kind of game.

This game has so much wasted potential. 

The movement and combat system is surprisingly deep. In mercenaries it is truly incredible some things you can do - target arms to make the enemy turn around exposing an explosive fire extinguisher on its back, slide into enemies to stun them and then perform coup de graces, target legs to make them fall and then stomp their watermelon heads, dodge and roll on the floor. 

The problem comes from the overly cinematic campaign filled with QTEs and just uninteresting level designs. In Mercs the best levels are probably the Chinese overpass and outdoor ruined Castle day time levels. But they suck to play because eventually the game will spawn enemies with guns that can stagger you and make you fall on the ground. Once you are on the ground you have very little chance of getting up without a zombie falling on you and instantly killing you. Most of the weapons feel weak, there is extremely limited character selection and loadout options (who thought having 3 different costumes all have the same loadout was a good idae?) and most maps are just bland and uninteresting. The combat potential and movement are really the only redeeming qualities but they are not enough to elevate the experience of playing this game. I would love it Capcom revisit the mechanics in a new RE game or different IP because there is a lot of potential that could be capitalized upon in the right hands.

Un buen juego, me trae mucha nostalgia en particular porque lo jugué cuando era chico apenas salió. Ahora rejugándolo me di cuenta por qué me había gustado y es que la historia está buena y es interesante, la siento como si fuera similar a la del re4 pero con más "ambición" ya que en este la historia es más global y abarca también diferentes personajes. Digo que lo veo similar a re4 por esto de que (spoiler) aparece Ada y es la pieza necesaria para terminar de entender lo que realmente ocurre en la historia, ya que está presente en todas las campañas principales y al jugar su campaña es cuando se conocen detalles de la historia que antes no se pueden percibir. 

En cuanto a la jugabilidad en mi caso prefiero esta dinámica más "shooter" similar a re4 y re5 pero diferente a los anteriores que son ya survival horror, probablemente sea por esto de que me gusta ir enfrentando enemigos y usando armas además de la acción que se desencadena en el proceso. Entiendo que a mucha gente no le puede gustar porque no va con la "esencia" de lo que era Resident Evil en sí, pero yo lo prefiero por sobre esa otra forma de jugabilidad. El juego tiene una duración razonable, los capítulos de las campañas realmente no son largos y la historia sentí que esta más para disfrutarla que para otra cosa (con esto digo el tema de los puntos que no te dan tantos y apenas se llegan a adquirir algunas habilidades, comparado con lo que te dan por ejemplo en mercenarios con solo jugarlo un par de veces). La rejugabilidad que tiene también está buena ya que se pueden probar diferentes sets de habilidades y pasarse las campañas pudiendo usar a los dos personajes que las protagonizan (esto igualmente lo veo más para alguien que quiere hacerlo por mera completitud ya que la historia es la misma salvo ciertas partes donde con un personaje se hace una cosa y con el otro otra, además que esas partes por alguna razón suelen ser más complicadas con el personaje secundario) y en los diferentes modos de dificultad.

Fue una linda experiencia, siento que es mejor que el re5 o al menos a mí me gustó más pero quizá no tanto como el re4 ya que no sentí que la historia fuera muy "profunda" en sí (y con esto digo la falta de archivos que hay para leer por ejemplo, a diferencia de los anteriores juegos)

Por otro lado noté que ya en este el online estuvo mucho más presente y no me gusta tanto pero entiendo que era inevitable (al menos en mi caso no impacta mucho porque no utilizo ese modo). Cuando digo que no me gusta es que los modos extras del juego solo pueden jugarse de esa manera, salvo el de mercenarios obviamente el cual aprovecho y digo que lo noté más difícil que en juegos anteriores (más que nada por los puntos que te piden para ir desbloqueando los mapas y lo que cuesta llegar a esto en el modo de mercenarios normal, hay que rebuscársela bastante y en algunos mapas por la forma que tienen se complica más). El modo mercenarios "potenciado" fue una gran decisión, mejor para mí que el normal en este juego y con el agregado en esta versión de personajes de L4D2 que encaja bastante bien con la temática

I first picked up RE6 on release, and for some reason dropped it just a few hours in. Returning to it a dozen years later only reminded me why: it’s a bloated, ugly, mechanically confused disaster that somehow misunderstood every lesson its predecessors taught.

For starters, the game looks absolutely awful. Smudgy textures, dead lighting and stilted facial animations — the whole thing looks like a knockoff Call of Duty clone from a discount bin. It's staggering how bad this game looks when Resident Evil 5, a game that came out 3 years prior, still holds up better than this sludge. It's like CAPCOM couldn't be bothered to pay for decent 3D artists and animators, so they outsourced their assets to a Unity asset flip and called it a day.

The gameplay also regressed hard. The over-the-shoulder 3rd Person shooting was something that RE4 pioneered and RE5 iterated on to great effect, yet RE6 seems to have forgotten all the lessons its predecessor learned since then. Enemies swarm you in obnoxious hordes with no tension, no pacing, no purpose. Add in clumsy UI design, immersion-breaking pickups, and the obligatory multiplayer trappings, and I half-expected a pop-up yelling “1000 XP to Shooty McShooterpants.” It’s F.E.A.R. 3 levels of misfire.

And the story? What can I say? Sure, if you are invested in the CAPCOM soap opera that is the RE canon (which has been running for over 3 decades at this point), then I guess you'd get a kick out of the fanservice of seeing all of your favourite characters uniting in this instalment. But the narrative that's wrapped around that is equal parts dumb and also po-faced and joyless. CAPCOM was always bad in this department, but at least RE4, and RE5 to a lesser extent, still had a sense of campy fun with their ridiculous villains and body horror shenanigans. While RE6 simply turns everyone into the super-serious action hero/heroine who has no self-awareness whatsoever seen in every airport thriller ever, and its emotional beats are about as on point as Spencer's heart rate after having been visited by Wesker. It seems to desperately want to ape Call of Duty, yet having none of the latter's gravitas or Oscar Mike bravado, with second-rate action set pieces in its place that only serve to severely piss you off with their erratic QTE placements.

In short, RE6 is a title that fails on every aspect, both as a Resident Evil game, and as a 3rd Person Shooter. It doesn't have the horror atmosphere of any of its predecessors, and utterly lacks the polish or cohesive designs that made the action elements in RE4 and RE5 stood the test of time. I don't know who at CAPCOM thought this flaming wreck was worthy as a mainline entry for the series, because even released as a generic zombie shooter back then would only yield mild interest from onlookers with its shoddy quality, leave alone being served as an major instalment in one of its flagship franchise.

A Mixed Bag of Thrills and Chills  
Rating: ★★★☆☆
*Resident Evil 6* is an ambitious entry in the long-running franchise that takes the series in a new direction. With multiple campaigns featuring familiar faces like Leon, Chris, and Ada, the game attempts to blend intense action with the horror elements that fans love—but does it hit the mark?
First off, let’s talk gameplay. The action is ramped up, and the game feels less like a horror experience and more like a high-octane action flick. The combat system has evolved, allowing for smoother movements and a more dynamic range of attacks. The addition of co-op gameplay is a nice touch too, whether you choose to tackle the story with a friend or AI. However, this shift towards action does sacrifice some of the tension and atmosphere that defined earlier titles in the series.
Visually, *Resident Evil 6* looks great, with well-designed environments and detailed character models. The cinematics are cinematic in every sense, giving it a blockbuster feel. The presentation is top-notch, but sometimes it feels like the focus is more on spectacle than substance.
The story, while ambitious, tries to juggle too many plotlines at once. There are moments that shine, especially in Leon’s campaign, which harkens back to the series’ roots. Meanwhile, Chris’s story dives into more action-heavy territory, which might alienate some long-time fans. It’s a mixed bag, but there are enough thrilling moments to keep you engaged.
At its core, *Resident Evil 6* is a fun ride if you’re in the mood for over-the-top action and don’t mind that it strays from the horror formula we once loved. It’s a must-try for fans who want to see the evolution of the series, but it may leave hardcore survival horror enthusiasts feeling a bit hollow. While it may not be perfect, I had a blast with it—even if it wasn’t the *Resident Evil* experience I was hoping for.

The trend capcom has had recently with remakes has been to make them go even further to the horror, which is great! That's classic RE. That's what fans love the franchise for, but recently with comments by current RE director about not including Leon in RE9 left me thinking about this game and what it could've been in terms of how its characters behave in gameplay.

His comments were akin to saying "By this point in the story, Leon wouldn't get scared by many things if not nothing at all", and it's true! Leon, Chris, Jill, and others are veterans who have gone through hell fighting BOWs and survived countless outbreaks. I could understand Leon being a tip toeing rookie going slow and steady in the police station back in '98. But modern Leon? Gameplay: 5/10
Arcade Shooter Feel:
The game often feels like a glorified on-rails arcade shooter. Many segments rely heavily on shooting galleries, QTEs (Quick Time Events), and set-piece moments where the player’s freedom is limited. It’s reminiscent of those arcade games where you hold a plastic gun and shoot at the screen while being dragged through a linear path.

Camera Issues:
Chase scenes suffer from horrendous camera angles that you can’t adjust. This leads to disorientation, especially on a first run, where you frequently don’t know where you’re supposed to go. The controls become clunky as a result, making these moments frustrating rather than intense.

Controls and Direction:
Between the inconsistent camera and fast-paced sequences, player movement often feels jarring and imprecise. You’re left second-guessing your next move more often than not, which breaks immersion and enjoyment.

Story: 7.5/10
The intersecting campaigns of Leon, Chris, Jake, and Ada offer variety and character depth.

The global-scale bioterrorism plot is ambitious, tying together multiple strands of the Resident Evil universe.

While the writing can be cheesy and the pacing uneven, there’s enough intrigue to keep fans of the series engaged.

Co-op Experience:
Not Recommended Solo:
Playing this game alone is not advisable. The frustrating gameplay and awkward design choices are significantly harder to tolerate when you're by yourself. Having a co-op partner to share the chaos with helps soften the blow. In fact, suffering through the game together can turn into its own kind of dark comedy. Misery loves company, and in Resident Evil 6, you’ll need it.

Presentation: 8/10
Graphically solid with well-rendered environments and fluid cinematics.

Strong sound design, though the overly dramatic music during action scenes can be overbearing.

Overall Verdict: 6.5/10
Resident Evil 6 is a flashy but flawed installment in the franchise. Its compelling story and big-budget production are held back by awkward controls, terrible camera angles, and a gameplay style better suited to an arcade machine than a home console or PC. Best played with a friend, because no one should face these design atrocities alone.

Resident Evil 6 is an ambitious but uneven entry that tries to be everything at once—survival horror, action shooter, and cinematic thriller. With four intersecting campaigns, it offers a huge amount of content, but not all of it hits the mark.

Leon’s story leans into classic horror and works best, while Chris’s and Jake’s campaigns often feel like over-the-top action games, trading tension for explosions. The gameplay is fast, with an expanded melee system and co-op mechanics, but it sacrifices atmosphere and scares in the process.

Visually impressive and mechanically solid, but tonally inconsistent and bloated. Fun in bursts, especially in co-op, but far from the series’ best.

A Story-Driven, High-Stakes Evolution of the Franchise

Resident Evil 6 delivers a massive, story-rich experience that expands the series’ universe on a global scale. With four deeply interconnected campaigns, the game weaves together multiple character arcs, conspiracies, and bioterror outbreaks into one ambitious narrative.

The structure allows players to experience events from different angles — from Leon Kennedy’s suspenseful, horror-tinged investigation, to Chris Redfield’s emotionally charged mission as a hardened soldier, to Jake Muller’s intense journey of identity and survival, and finally Ada Wong’s mysterious solo operation that connects all the pieces. Each storyline has its own pacing, tone, and themes, making the full experience feel dynamic and constantly evolving.

The storytelling is a highlight. Long-time fans will appreciate the character development and lore references, while newcomers can still follow the plot thanks to strong cinematic direction and consistent writing. The game leans more into action than earlier entries, but still retains the atmosphere, tension, and darker moments the series is known for.

With its networked gameplay features, the world of Resident Evil 6 feels more alive. You may occasionally cross paths with other players during key story moments — a clever touch that enhances immersion and gives the game a sense of a broader world without breaking narrative focus.

Visually, the game is still impressive, with richly detailed environments ranging from war-torn cities to underground labs. The voice acting and soundtrack add further emotional depth, giving weight to each character’s choices and struggles.

Resident Evil 6 is a bold and story-driven installment that broadens the series' scope in both narrative and gameplay. It’s not traditional survival horror — but it’s a gripping, high-stakes ride that connects the past and future of Resident Evil in an exciting way.

I’m not an expert when it comes to ‘Resident Evil’ series, because before ‘RE6’ I played and finished only two other games from the franchise: fourth and fifth. I liked them both quite a lot and now, after spending almost 60 hours in this one and finishing it in 100% I can right away say that I enjoyed it as much as ‘RE4’ & ‘RE5’ (and in some aspects even more than them). However 'RE6' can't really be compared to previous games for very simple reason: this is truly one hell of a shooter, but NOT a survival horror. There are no horror elements whatsoever here (yup, not even jumpscares!) as it seems devs decided to drop them completely in order to create pure action game. And if that indeed is what they wanted to achieve I genuinely think they succeeded. 

But let's start with the story and as you can probably predict it's not exactly Pullitzer Prize material. Bad guys created the C-Virus that turns people into zombies, they’re planning to release it all over the world and someone needs to stop them. That's pretty much it and although the core of the story remains the same as in older parts of the franchise, there's one significant difference that separates 'RE6' and previous games and it's the fact that this game feels like Michael Bay’s work. What exactly does it mean? Well, buildings are collapsing, stuff is exploding, planes are falling down from the sky, more stuff is exploding, people are running away from avalanche on snowmobiles, even more stuff is exploding - you get the picture. On top of that writing not only blends together almost all existing action movie cliches but also is so over the top and so silly that it feels cartoony and there’s just no way in hell to take it seriously. But it's worth mentoning that if you manage to turn your brain off and treat it like nothing but a B-movie it can still be fun. Therefore I'm not going to complain here, because to be honest with you I got exactly what I expected and let's face it: for this kind of a game it's more than enough.

‘RE6’ offers four different campaigns: first one is dedicated to Leon S. Kennedy & Helena Harper, second to Chris Redfield & Piers Nievens, third to Jake Muller & Sherry Birkin and the last one to Ada Wong. You can choose the character you want to play as in every story, even solo but it’s also worth mentioning it’s possible to finish all of them in co-op with either random people or with a friend. 
All campaigns are very similar gameplay-wise and it won’t be a spoiler to say that characters from certain stories meet each others at some point and their adventures are directly connected. Full playthrough of all four campaigns takes about 16-18 hours, but it's not getting boring even for a second because when it comes to gameplay ‘RE6’ is a revolutionary part of the series. 

First and foremost, as stupid as it sounds, this is the very first game in the franchise that allows player to walk/run and shoot in the same time. Yes, you read that right – in previous games doing those things simultaneously wasn’t possible. You had to stop, aim and then shoot, but now it’s no longer the case and it really changes the pace of the game and makes it significantly faster. Combat and shooting is really good, there’s quite large pool of weapons to choose from (and each character has their own set which is cool) and design of the enemies is really well done (sometimes it's simply incredible - grasshoppers are absolutely amazing). You’ll be facing hundreds and hundreds of zombies (that’s not an exaggeration, trust me) and in order to keep it interesting all the time devs decided to offer variety in the gameplay: there are of course tons of QTEs and they are not annoying or distracting (with exception of literally 2 sequences where camera work is your biggest enemy), but there are also short sequences where you’re driving certain vehicles like humvees or snowmobiles and at one point you’ll even be flying a jet (yup!).

There are more changes to the core of the gameplay. In ‘RE4’ & ‘RE5’ you didn’t level your character in traditional meaning of the word, but after gathering enough money and resources you could upgrade your weapons. In ‘RE6’ it was dropped and instead devs introduced the brand new skill system. On paper it’s great – there’s a ton of skills to choose from (bigger damages against certain types of zombies, proficiency in certain weapons resulting in more firepower etc.) and you can use only 3 of them at the same time, so theoretically you should think carefully what to use since it can’t be changed during the mission (you can use different set of skills though). In practice however I didn’t notice any changes in gameplay so I completely stopped caring about the entire system and despite ignoring it the game still felt the same and I think it proves how pointless it is.
Changes were also made in herbs system but I didn’t care about it either because when you’re in the middle of the fight there’s no time to analyze what would be the best way to do combine them (especially considering there’s no pause. Literally – if you press 'Esc' button menu appears but the game doesn’t stop) so I was doing it randomly just to have meds ready to use. Since there are tons of herbs all over the levels it really doesn’t matter after all, so it’s another pointless change.

There’s no manual saving system, only checkpoints, but there’s a lot of them so I won’t really complain. What should be mentioned here is the fact that there are 2 types of checkpoints: when you see the pin icon it means after dying you’ll restart from there, but you’ll be moved to previous save if you close the game. However when you see the typewriter icon it means a ‘hard’ save has been made – you’ll start from this point not only after death but also after quiting 'RE6'.

Despite all the years the game still looks and sounds pretty nice and there’s not really much to say about it. I mean I know some people would probably complain about the low quality of some textures and that kind of stuff but I personally don’t care about the graphics (great if it’s good, doesn’t matter if it's not as long as the gameplay is fun). What’s important to me is the fact that game works like a charm: I didn’t experience a single crash, FPS drop or any kind of technical issues when I was playing it and ‘RE6’ has been fully adapted to PCs (it’s totally playable on K+M, even during QTEs). It’s really solid port and I can only wish all games were like this.

Now it’s time for couple of things I didn’t like.
First and foremost – lack of ammo at some levels. If this was ‘RE4’-style game I wouldn’t mind that at all. But this is 100% pure action game where you’re mowing down hundreds of zombies, so gameplay-wise it doesn’t make any sense. 
Other thing I didn’t enjoy were some of the boss fights. Most of them are fine, but there are a few that are simply way too long - sometimes in order do hit/kill the boss you’re supposed to do very specific thing 3 or 4 times in a row and it can become quite tedious. 
And last thing I want to mention is lack of any memorable moments in the game. ‘RE4’ for example had unforgettable first meeting with the Chainsaw Guy, while ‘RE6’ is quite generic and not surprising in that aspect. Considering how over the top it is I really expected there will be some ‘Wow, didn’t expect that’ moment, but there’s not. It doesn’t affect the actual gameplay in any way, but it kind of disappoints.

I don't think there's much more to say, so it's time for short summary of this review.
‘RE6’ is in my opinion one hell of a zombie shooter and it offers nothing but pure fun. I totally recommend getting it as long as you like fast paced action (especially with some oldschool vibe to it), because you shouldn’t be disappointed. However if you're looking mostly for the horror or survival aspects of the gameplay the best decision would be skipping 'RE6' and looking for something else.

First Resident Evil game that I'm skipping. The graphics are nice, but the UI and controls are some of the most bizarre in any game and there is no getting used to them. Your inventory is a bunch of scrolling blocks. You don't use healing herbs in your inventory, you load them into a capsule for later and then use them. Your health is sometimes that familiar heart beat line, sometimes squares. Various quick time events happen that use inconsistent and random buttons. And your character switches between walking and running seemingly at random times. The cut scenes seem to all be done in game so you have no idea when you have control of your character and when you don't. Even when you don't have control over your character you are still able to be attacked by zombies. I knew that the world still functioned while the cut scene played, but I was completely taken by surprise when I was shot dead at a gas station while a cut scene told me to blow the place up.

Instead of the typical story divided by chapters, RE6 is broken up into four campaigns. I managed to get to the second chapter of the first campaign, holding up in a gun store, before throwing in the towel. Due to the scrolling inventory it's difficult to pull out the weapon you need. You'll regularly find yourself scrolling past it. Why the developers thought they needed to replace the simple 1, 2, 3 for weapon select is beyond me. This makes it difficult to keep an eye on if your weapon is even loaded because weapon select and weapon info are on two different sections of the screen. Why your UI is made up of a bunch of squares that you've got no idea what they do, and the tutorial doesn't tell you what they do, is beyond me as well. Even the pause menu is just a bunch of symbols to represent the various menu options WITH THE NAME OF EACH OPTION AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SCREEN. You have to hover over the icon and then read the text at the bottom to know what the option even is instead of simply having the text BE the option. Lastly, the use of grenades is apparently a trade secret as by the time I quit I still hadn't cracked the code on how to even select the variety of explosives in my inventory.

The graphics look nice and the characters move alright, but the UI destroys this game. The fact that this game has such high ratings makes me think most of you people are more drunk on Kool-Aid than Nintendo fans are. I've heard for some time that RE5 and RE6 were the low points of the Resident Evil franchise. At least RE5 controls made sense even if they were a little clunky. At least I could complete RE5, with RE6 I could only make an attempt. I am sorry, RE5. I judged you too harshly.

Resident Evil 6 is the definition of a game trying to do everything at once. It’s bold, bloated, occasionally brilliant—and just as often baffling. Capcom’s attempt to deliver four intertwining campaigns, multiple gameplay styles, and blockbuster-level action results in a game that’s ambitious to a fault.

It’s not a total failure, nor is it the survival horror renaissance fans hoped for after the divisive RE5. Instead, it’s a chaotic experiment with flashes of greatness buried under a mountain of design compromises.

RE6 includes four separate storylines—Leon, Chris, Jake, and Ada—each offering a different flavor of gameplay. The idea is compelling in theory:

-Leon’s campaign leans into the slow-burn horror of classic RE, with creepy corridors and jump scares.

-Chris’s story feels more like a military shooter, loaded with bullets and explosions.

-Jake’s campaign is somewhere between the two, with some intense chases and martial arts.

-Ada’s campaign, unlockable at launch, adds stealth elements and narrative glue.

Unfortunately, none of them fully commit to their genre. The result is tonal whiplash: one moment you’re creeping through a zombie-infested campus, the next you’re roundhouse-kicking monsters off motorcycles. Each campaign has moments of brilliance—Leon’s opening hours are especially atmospheric—but they often stretch too long and repeat ideas.

Combat is fluid, responsive, and packed with mechanics—dodge rolls, melee counters, and even sliding while shooting. But the game often overloads the player with too many enemies and too many options, stripping tension from encounters. Inventory management and resource scarcity are minimized, a far cry from the series’ roots in survival horror.

Quick-time events (QTEs) are frequent and intrusive. Whether you're wrestling zombies or escaping collapsing buildings, the game too often takes control away from the player for the sake of cinematic flair.

There’s no shortage of spectacle in RE6’s story. Global bio-terrorism, city-wide outbreaks, shadowy conspiracies, and returning characters abound. But emotional investment is harder to come by. The narrative is convoluted, jumping between timelines and perspectives, and padded with B-movie melodrama.

Still, there are some highlights. The chemistry between Leon and Helena has its moments, and Jake—Wesker’s son—brings fresh blood (literally and figuratively) to the franchise. But overall, the plot tries too hard to be a globe-trotting epic, losing the intimate fear that defined earlier games.

Visually, Resident Evil 6 impresses with highly detailed environments, expressive character models, and bombastic effects. The lighting and cinematography can be genuinely cinematic at times. Voice acting and sound design are also solid, even when the dialogue veers into camp.

However, the HUD is cluttered, and the constant on-screen prompts can feel overwhelming. There's a lack of restraint across the board.

Resident Evil 6 is a game torn between its survival horror legacy and action blockbuster ambitions. In trying to satisfy all audiences, it ends up satisfying few. There’s fun to be had—especially in co-op—and the sheer scope of the experience is impressive. But as a cohesive Resident Evil title, it loses its identity amid the chaos.

This isn’t a bad game—but it is a confused one. And for many long-time fans, RE6 represents the moment the series lost its way... at least until Resident Evil 7 brought it back.

A massive, messy game that delivers thrills but forgets what made Resident Evil special in the first place.

Played this game with my friend. We have like 120 hours each in RE5 and we love the game to pieces. First of all, what are those completely counter-intuitive controls? The UI? Inventory management genuinely became a headache. Why can't you share items like in 5? Given, everyone gets their own items but it felt neat to have the option. 

Now for the gameplay itself. Wow, WHY. Why does kicking and elbowing do more damage than three bullets right to the noggin? On the other hand, you go and position yourself very carefully to at last get the prompt to perform a finisher, zombie puts on his troll hat and tackles you, and you instantly lose a whole bar of health. TF. Where does the troll hat go when they literally have no more head and still attack you??

The forced camera changes nearly gave me aneurysm (as did the entirety of this gift of god). The stamina thing? Maybe cool in theory. Not so much when I have to do a section of the game without guns or little ammo (see Sherry section in that Chinese base) and fail to kick after taking two enemies. Several capillaries went to an early grave due to the sheer amount of QTEs and cutscenes ("I CAN SEE THE DOOR JUST FINE BUT THANKS FOR ZOOMING IN ON IT FOR AN ENTIRELY APPROPRIATE AMOUNT OF TIME ANYWAY"). This game is actually really great in co-op. It has a lot of wild story sections, probably a few too many QTEs, and the combat is more movement and melee based than the previous two games.

An important note on this one though is that the developers leaned into the over-the-top chaos and campy vibe that the original RE4 and RE5 had parts of, which makes this game infamous. If you walk into this and try and take it as a serious Resident Evil like RE7/8, you'll likely be disappointed and maybe even a little baffled at this one.

Its also worth mentioning that while the AI co-op partner is "ok", they'll absolutely get you killed at times, which can be wildly frustrating. This is really something you'll want to play co-op just so you don't have to deal with that AI.

There are four campaigns and each one has a different "focus". Leon/Helena's campaign tries to lean into the horror/mystery, Chris/Piers try to have more action and brawling, Jake/Sherry try to have a personal thing going on, and Ada/Agent is an attempt to fully reveal all the parts of the story that the other campaigns didn't show were connected. Some of these work decently well and some feel rough. Most of them have overlapping (basically repeated) sections that feel more like a chore when you're playing campaigns all the way through.

If you do have an interest in seeing this one through, pick it up on sale and get a copy for a friend. Leave the PvP invasion stuff off because I have never seen it enhance the experience, as it usually only makes a frustrating section significantly worse with an enemy player who can exploit the AI or other game mechanics.

This game isn't for everyone, but if you got some spare time, and itching to play through a game with someone, then I'd highly recommend it. If you're looking for a more traditional RE experience, then this ain't it.

Resident Evil 6 is an action-focused third-person shooter with a strong emphasis on cooperative play similar to RE 5. The game features four campaigns with different settings, enemies, and weapons. These campaigns can be played alone or with another player. The storylines connect through multiple characters, showing events from different points of view. The game includes nice quality cutscenes and voice acting, which add depth to the story and overall experience.

One downside is the use of fixed camera angles in some parts of the game, especially during boss fights and escape scenes. These camera angles make controlling the character more difficult and often might lead to some failures in certain sections. The user interface also changes between campaigns and uses symbols instead of text, which can make it hard to manage items or change settings at first. Technically, the game runs smoothly without crashes, providing a stable gameplay experience.

In many parts of the game, anti-aliasing and textures are blurry. I do not know if it is because it is ported from console to PC and it's not done properly or it's by default, and the field of view of the character is not perfect and I have used the trainer from Nexus Mods and set the field of view to 90.

Overall, Resident Evil 6 moves away from the horror style of earlier titles and focuses more on action and story. The variety of campaigns and gameplay styles helps keep the experience engaging. I’ve seen people mentioning in some articles and forums that cooperative mode works very well, though I haven’t played it myself. The game offers a solid experience for players who prefer action over tension or resource management.

⭐️⭐️⭐☆☆ (A massive, chaotic spectacle — that runs out of steam fast)

Resident Evil 6 is the definition of quantity over quality. There’s no denying this game is packed to the brim with content — four full-length campaigns, tons of characters, skill systems, action set pieces — but after a while, it all starts to blur together. And worse, it just stops being fun.

On paper, it sounds great:

Leon’s got zombies and moody hallways.

Chris has guns and explosions every five seconds.

Jake’s punching monsters in the face.

Ada’s sneaking around with a crossbow.
Sounds like variety, right?
In practice, though, most of the gameplay boils down to endless shooting galleries, constant QTEs, and bloated set pieces that forget why people love Resident Evil in the first place. The pacing drags. The tone flips between serious bioterror drama and full-on action movie nonsense. And the horror? It’s almost nonexistent.

Mechanically, there’s a lot going on — dodges, rolls, counters, melee takedowns, cover systems — but it ends up feeling more chaotic than tactical. The gunplay is decent, but the enemy design rarely makes you think or adapt. After your 30th room of generic enemies charging at you while the game screams “PRESS X TO NOT DIE,” it starts to feel like a chore.

Even co-op, which was the saving grace of RE5, can’t carry the whole experience here. It's definitely better with a friend — you can laugh at the ridiculousness and carry each other through the slog — but that doesn't fix the fact that most of the campaigns overstay their welcome by several hours. It just keeps going, and going, and going — with diminishing returns.

This is the first time I've played the game. I remember when it came out, I went with my brothers-in-law to pick it up at the midnight launch at our local GameStop. I can't believe it's been 13 years already. It's funny that you can now play Ada's campaign from the beginning if you want. I remember before, you had to complete the other campaigns to be able to play it.

The last RE I played was RE2, when it came out... so I haven't played a RE in over 20 years, but I've seen my brothers-in-law play through 4, 6, etc. I feel comfortable talking about them; I'm not blind in knowledge.
While I understand why people hated the game SO MUCH, the truth is, it doesn't deserve the hate at all. I LOVED the game; it has by far the best "mercenaries" in the entire franchise, and that's a plus. I liked the campaigns.
Playing Ada's campaign and realizing she was EVERYWHERE from the beginning (literally, in the ventilation ducts above your head... no kidding, lmao!) was something that blew my mind for a while.
I think Ada's ending was the perfect way to close out Resident Evil, and it makes me a little sad to know we might never see her again in a game.
Of the four campaigns, in three, I found people to play with, who randomly joined my session, and that surprised me SO MUCH! I thought the game was dead.
I played 90% of the first three campaigns with people, and it was definitely enjoyable. Ada's, well, I didn't mind playing it alone. It was originally intended for single-player only, anyway.
Now it's time to play the rest. I'll go with the 4th Remake, which I haven't seen AT ALL, and I'm excited to have a new experience in an RE after so many years.
I don't plan on playing Village, or even 7, because honestly: I'm a sissy, and it scares me HORRIBLY, so I don't enjoy them. I don't get along well with real horror in games.

I think starting with the latest of that timeline and the black sheep of the franchise was the best thing I could have done. It was an excellent game, it brought back many wonderful memories and created new ones. I must admit I felt a bit nostalgic at times.
If you made it this far, I want to thank you so much for taking the time to read this. I hope you have a great day and wish you much success in life.

Me and a friend recently went through RE5 after I mentioned I had it but never actually played it before. I had only heard negative things about the game but I was surprised when the game wasn't as bad as I heard it was. Sure, it's not a great Resident Evil game but it is an excellent co-op game and only a few sections really made irritated. We beat the game, did some optional stuff afterwards and then he mentions if I would be down to play RE6. I agree, he gifts me the game and we start playing. 

My initial impressions were fairly positive, Leon's campaign starts off pretty slow but it ramps up and still feels like a Resident Evil game somewhat. We finish Leon's campaign and I'm still optimistic at this point and he makes it a point that we should play Jake's campaign next, despite my confusion, we play Jake's campaign next instead of Chris'. This is where the game starts going down hill. Any Resident Evil DNA this game has is thrown straight out of the window and it quickly becomes a COD campaign with awkward level design, annoying enemies, confusing objectives, chase segments with inconsistent controls, vehicle segments with terrible controls and last but certainly not least, QTEs. Despite all this, the campaign is still somewhat enjoyable although it got old fast. 

Unfortunately Jake's campaign was a sign of things to come and the last 2 campaigns never got better. Chris' campaign is everything I just talked about but amplified to an unbearable degree. It was incredibly frustrating nearly the entire way through and at no point did it get better. The boiling point for me was the running sequence on the water with the helicopter in chapter 3. The camera is awful, the area you have to run in is way too tight, there are enemies in the way, the climbing parts actively hinders on your time to get out of the way of the rockets on time, there were several moments where the climbing segment actually ruined my attempts because Chris kept going back down instead of going forward despite me holding the W key. Needless to say it took me and my friend several attempts. It was to my dismay to see that the final boss sequence had a running sequence as well and while it sucked it wasn't as bad as chapter 3. In practice overlapping levels on different campaigns is interesting but on repeat playthroughs or even just going through the same section on a different character knowing what's going to happen, it tends to get annoying really fast. We finally finished Chris' campaign before moving on to the last campaign, Ada's. 

Good god, I really wanted to like this campaign because Ada is my favorite Resident Evil character but I could barely stomach playing through it. The 1st chapter was enough to nearly make me Alt + F4 and uninstall right on the spot. Somehow, it's even more tight and claustrophobic, your weapons are downright terrible, your resources are incredibly limited in comparison to the other campaigns, they throw obnoxious enemies at you and on top of all that the ending sequence for the chapter is timed all while you have to fight off a couple dozen enemies, one of them able to force you into a QTE to fight for your life all while draining your health incredibly fast. There's also 2 of them in the room at the same time so if you thought your co-op partner could be able to help you, they're also probably on the floor spamming WASD. There's not really much to say about Ada's campaign past that, it's pretty forgettable and ultimately suffers from everything I mentioned with the previous 2 campaigns.

I didn't get to play the other optional gamemodes aside from Mercenaries because the online is seemingly dead other than the main campaign so I can't speak on those. Mercenaries mode is pretty fun though, but some characters get abysmal loadouts.

If you have the patience of a saint and have a friend to play with, I guess I can recommend it, otherwise, avoid this game like the plague.

The hate revolving around this game is so forced and it makes me upset to see.  Other than some janky keybindings and some very iffy camera angles sometimes this game is one of my favorites in the franchise.  As far as camera angles are, you could say the same about the RE1 game.  I appreciate them actually taking a different view of gameplay rather than being stuck double backing inside of a building the whole time like previous games doing tasks.  If you aren't a fan of quick pacing and action then it might not be for you but to claim just because of that it is "Resident Evil's worst game" is plain ignorant.  

Out of the 4 Story Co-op missions I would only actually say Ada's was both the shortest and the least entertaining in terms of gameplay.  It is worse if you're player two in the situation due to you not being able to actually interact with a single thing making it feel way less team based and more just a walking meat shield.  Ada's mission aside, I feel all the other 3 storylines were different from eachother [excluding when they meet up of course.]  Each unique scenery and layout, sometimes it even felt like a different Resident Evil game to me.  Mostly when in contrast from Chris and Leon being in completely different areas.  There are plenty of cool new movement styles unlike in any other RE games and hilarious to use inside of Co-op with friends and just in general.  

Ultimately in summary, yes it has flaws but that can be said for just about any old or new Resident Evil games.  Don't believe everything you hear from reviewers and regulars who've never picked up this game claiming it isn't worth your time.  This game is one of my favorites if not in my top 3 of them in the franchise.  Just because the new movement and overall layout isn't your thing doesn't mean it is some sloppy mess.  I would 100% recommend this game to anyone who is genuinely interested in both the lore of Resident Evil and trying out different scenes within the franchise.

This thing is rough all-round, and while looking the part it certainly doesn't feel very good. While playing with a controller the movement is stiff and downright bad: either a slow tank-like walk, or a juddery jog, it does not feel smooth or give you much control. Oftentimes it is easy to walk or move past the enemy that you are aiming at, which happens frequently because zombies spawn out of monster closets now. And if you would like to take a break and try later, expect to begin somewhere several autosaves away from where you left off. The whole thing starts to wear on you after a few hours. Where the gameplay and poor directorial decisions being made can stand aside, the experience shouldn't be constantly impeded. All that aside the field-of-view is too small, and the action is very prompt-heavy, with a definite cheapness that resembles Suda51 games....if you know, you know, it's kind of static and not smooth or flowing so it doesn't even really play well even when you are doing everything right.

I have really tried to like this game, but this is one of the worst gaming experiences I have ever had, and I have been playing video games since the 1980s. 

I am not mad at Capom that they turned Resident Evil into a third-person shooter, I am mad at Capom that they totally suck at making third-person shooters. Besides an insane amount of braindead QTEs, and weird fixed camera angles in scenarios where you are supposed to run and quickly change directions, this game gets the two basics wrong that make a good shooter:

People you shoot should be shot and the game should know when to quit. 

Here, we still have the old survival horror mechanics in place and you will see basic enemies that you just shot in the head at point-blank range scratching their heads and moving on. This is fine in a zombie survival where you are not supposed to simply blast your way through but it has no business in a shooter. 

And the other thing is that every gameplay sequence is stretched out until you hate it. You have a new situation/enemy and it's exciting. Then you learn how to overcome it, and it feels cool. But then the game continues with it until it becomes busy work. Then it goes on until it becomes boring. But the game isn't finished with that element and it becomes tedious. And then it goes on until it becomes annoying. Even then, you still have a few more ladders to climb or the same enemies to kill until you hate it. 

I think, these devs simply hated their jobs and wanted the player to suffer all the same.

Resident Evil 6 is one of the worst games I've ever played, and the worst game in the main Resident Evil series by a landslide.
In the early 2010s, corpo rat Keiji Inafune had successfully influenced Capcom to ditch any semblance of their franchises' identity in favour of chasing western gaming trends to for maximum profits, resulting in the company's dark ages and some of the worst franchise games of all time. Of the many casualties, Devil May Cry and Resident Evil were hit the worst by a landslide, and Resident Evil 6 embodies everything awful and shameless about this era.
Right from the word "go", Resident Evil 6 shows itself off as a seinen anime-inspired Gears of War ripoff that's out to destroy literally everything that makes Resident Evil... Resident Evil. Before we get any menus, we're treated to an opening level that gives us an explosion, a helicopter shoot-out, a highway battle, running away from a bigger explosion, another helicopter smashing into a building, and a collapsing tower... ALL BEFORE THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TITLE VIDEO PLAYS! Resident Evil 6 is such an actionised in-name-only sell-out, that the more it indulges in anime stunts, martial arts fights and Call of Duty setpieces, the more I expect an appearance by ALICE! 

Making matters worse (yes, it gets worse), is that not only does the game split itself up into four campaigns with a distinctive focus which ends up being drowned out by the sheer lunacy on display, but that as a third person shooter, Resident Evil 6 fails utterly with the worst controls of the entire series. Oh, sure. You can move whilst shooting, but it doesn't matter when controlling your character feels like trying to remove a tight jar-lid. The basic movement feels slippery, the aiming feels off, the inventory management is whack, the crosshair is drunk, and the keyboard and mouse controls only furthers this awful gameplay feel. Combine this with one of the worst fields of view ever and the fact that the basic enemies are zombies and zombies with guns, plus overly-railroaded level design and the fact your character gets knocked down and out after a couple of bullets from enemies and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of QTEs, and you have ultimate recipe for rage and tedium.

And graphically, it's awful. It somehow looks worse than Resident Evil 5 (which came out three years prior), and the artstyle is butt-ugly, with dreadful texture quality, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ character models, and hands down, the worst monsters in the entire franchise. I mean, just look up these enemies (I.E. the Ustanak and J'avo). They look like ♥♥♥♥! They look butt-ugly and not scary! 

Finally, the storyline is terrible. It's a series of ridiculous cliches and plot developments that, again, feels more like a terrible early 2010s seinen anime rather than Resident Evil. The plot feels overstuffed due to having four different protagonists, and the concepts are utterly dumb and make zero sense, made worse by how the game takes itself too seriously for its own good. 
In short: It's a mess. It really is a mess of a game. And before you dumb RE6 Apologists say that "it made $14 million dollars! COPE!", that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, because sales and popularity do not equal quality, and the game cost $300 MILLION US DOLLARS to make. It is honestly the worst game sequel I've ever played, tied for that spot with F.3.A.R., and I know I'm not the only one who feels this way. This is how Capcom themselves feel, as after they split people down the middle with 6, they decided to go back to the drawing board. Basically, 6 manages to offend everyone who might have an interest in the game: If you're a fan of Resident Evils 1 - 4, you'll be pissed because the horror, identity and soul is all gone. If you're a fan of Resident Evil 5, you'll be pissed because the game is inferior in every way and doesn't feel like an actionised Resident Evil like 5 did. And if you just want a good third person shooter, you'll be pissed because it's utterly terrible with some of the worst controls, gunplay and graphics in the biz.
 Avoid this game at all costs.

It took me a lot of time trying to understand what exactly wasn't enjoyable about this game. I mean, I wasn't having any fun at all, but if I tried to break the game down into pieces, each piece was okayish enough (graphics were okay, story was okay, basic mechanics seemed okay). After quite some time I understood what was lacking. The game is a shooter (with very light elements of the survival genre). As a shooter game, I don't enjoy it. It was made to play comfortably on consoles (no precise aiming, no real challenge). To make matters worse, the pace of the shooting (so the pace of the game, actually) is constantly interrupted. For instance, if I'm killing some boss, but the boss has a certain number of phases and I don't know if I'm just wasting bullets until the next phase is unlocking or I'm still doing actual damage. The pace is interrupted. There are more examples, such as interruptions for walking, quick-time events, and story that I don't really care about. There isn't free exploration (which per se isn't really a problem), and the scenery is too dark for me to bother about it.

If I ever make a game, I'll try to look back at this one as how to have many separate good things (good graphics, okayish story, etc), and still suck as game (if the game is primarily challenging you as a shooter, make sure this part fun). If you're looking for a zombie game, just go for Left 4 Dead 2.

The best combat in the series, at least at the time of the release.
You can melee attack anytime you like (as long as you have stamina). There are parries and rolls. You can run from an enemy, slide, make a 180 spin, and fire some shots without getting up.
I understand that it's a minor thing, but I really like the healing system here. The health bar is divided into sections. Instead of taking a handful of herbs, the characters compress them into tablets first. When you click the healing button the character takes a tablet which restores one section. But you can quickly tap the button a few times, and the character will take that many tablets from the case. They are even rendered on the palm correctly.
There are, unfortunately, a few quality-of-life issues that can be a bit annoying. The first one are the saves. Not sure if it works like that in a single player mode, but in co-op you may reach a checkpoint (the game also tells you that the progress is saved), end the session, return a next day and find out that you are a few checkpoints back for some reason, but with the same amount HP and ammo as you had on the checkpoint where you quit. So, I guess finish the chapter in one session? Another problem – sometimes when you sprint pass an obstacle the game interprets it as if you were trying to vault over it, so, your character vaults in the opposite direction of where you were running.
The biggest issue for me and the reason I didn't buy it on release is that RE6 is very co-op focused. The single player content are "The Mercenaries" and Ada's campaign (yes, you can play it in co-op now also, but it was added with a patch, originally it was designed for singleplayer only). Sure, you can play other campaigns with an AI-partner, but it feels um … wrong? There are other games where you are expected to interact with an NPC, like Ico, or The last guardian, or even RE4, and I had fun playing them. Probably, the difference is that those were designed for it, while RE6 was designed for co-op, and AI-partners are just a substitute.
So, if you have a pal to play this game with, be my guest and check it out. You may even have a few online players to invade your game in "agent hunt" mode, but meeting someone in story intersections is unlikely.
If you are going to play this alone, well, try it too? You can leave an online slot open, so the others could join you.

Review of Resident Evil 6
Gameplay

The gameplay of Resident Evil 6 is undoubtedly its most controversial aspect. The game strays far from the survival-horror roots of the series, opting for a more action-oriented, shooter-like approach. This results in:

    Frustrating Mechanics: The enemy "grabbing" system is one of the biggest sources of frustration. Zombies (or the new J'avo enemies) are incredibly fast and can kill you in seconds if they catch you. Combined with glitches and interactive cutscenes that lock your controls, many deaths feel unfair.

    Artificial Difficulty: The dynamic difficulty system is another issue. If you're doing well, the game becomes harder by reducing your accuracy or making enemies require more bullets to die. This, coupled with infinite enemy spawns, makes resource management tedious and sometimes impossible.

    Endless Combat: Enemies keep spawning endlessly, even in areas where it doesn’t make sense. This removes the tension and planning typical of survival games, turning it into a mindless slaughter.

    Positive Mechanics: Despite its flaws, the game introduces some improvements, like the cover system and tactical moves (rolling, dodging), but they aren’t enough to save the experience.

Graphics

The graphics of Resident Evil 6 are a strong point. The game looks good for its time (2012), with detailed environments and smooth animations. However:

    Uninspired Enemy Designs: The new enemies (J'avo) lack the visual impact of classic zombies or iconic enemies from earlier games.

    Generic Environments: While some settings are impressive (like the chaotic cities), many others feel generic and fail to leverage the series' potential.

Story

The story is one of the few redeeming aspects of the game. Resident Evil 6 offers four interconnected campaigns, each with its own protagonists:

    Well-Developed Characters: Leon, Chris, Ada, and Jake have memorable moments, and their interactions add depth to the plot.

    Entertaining but Convoluted Plot: The story tries to be too ambitious, with multiple intersecting narratives and an overemphasis on explosive action. Still, it keeps you engaged thanks to the characters and exciting moments.

    Lack of Horror: The story loses much of the series' essence, focusing more on explosions and action scenes than on tension and mystery.

Development

The development of Resident Evil 6 reflects an attempt to modernize the series, but with questionable results:

    Misguided Focus: Capcom tried to appeal to fans of action shooters but lost what made Resident Evil unique in the process.

    Design Issues: Decisions like interactive cutscenes and artificial difficulty were poorly received by players.

    Critical and Commercial Reception: While the game sold well initially (thanks to the franchise name), critics and fans were harsh, leading Capcom to rethink the series' direction.

Music and Sound

The soundtrack of Resident Evil 6 is competent but not particularly memorable:

    Generic Music: Most tracks are suitable for the action but lack the tension and atmosphere that made earlier games' scores iconic.

    Sound Effects: The sound effects are well done, especially enemy screams and environmental sounds, but they don’t add anything new to the experience.

Conclusion

Resident Evil 6 is a game that divided the fanbase. While it has some positives (like graphics and story), its design flaws and departure from the series' essence make it a frustrating experience for many players. It’s no surprise that it’s one of the least beloved entries in the franchise, and why Resident Evil 7 had to return to its roots to regain fans' trust.

Personal Score: 4/10
Technical Score: 6/10 (for its visuals and ambition, even if it didn’t fully deliver).

Resident Evil 6 is an electrifying blend of pulse-pounding action and classic survival horror, delivering an unforgettable journey through four gripping campaigns. The combat is fast-paced and satisfying, allowing for smooth transitions between intense gunfights, brutal hand-to-hand combat, and adrenaline-fueled escapes. The vast, detailed environments are varied and atmospheric, keeping you immersed in the world of terror, while the emotional stakes are elevated by memorable characters and high-stakes missions.

Resident Evil 6 might push the action to new levels, but it still pays homage to the series’ horror roots, making it a perfect evolution of the franchise. [h1]The few times this game is fun are not worth the amount of times it makes you want to pull your hair out.[/h1]

I went into this game open-minded, even though I heard it's not really good. But sadly, I gotta agree. There is a lot of content, don't get me wrong, but the thing is, none of it is really well made. I appreciate the concept of telling one huge story over the course of multiple campaigns. Sadly, none of them are really fun to play.

Leon's is by far the best since you mostly fight zombies and some B.O.W.s, and you can utilize the one thing I really like about this game: the melee combat system. That's the one thing they really made better compared to RE5. Sadly, it doesn't get used much since, in all the other three campaigns, you mostly fight enemies with guns, making melee ineffective.

The only other time the melee system is useful is in the Mercenaries mode, which I actually quite like. It almost feels like the system was designed with this game mode in mind. The last thing I find good is the ranking system with medals and titles. You get them for almost everything, and you can spend a lot of time collecting them all. I didn’t do that, though.

Now, let's move on to the things I find really unfun and bad in this game. First of all: quick-time events. So many quick-time events. And you can't even turn them off. There’s also a lot of fake gameplay where you just hold a direction key, and your character does the rest.

The chapters are way too long for the most part, each of them taking around an hour. The graphics seem almost like the most downgraded thing compared to RE5, even on PC with max settings. Speaking of settings, the in-game settings menu is just horrendous, and whoever came up with the idea of it being different for each character along with their HUD should not be designing games for a living. There are more things I really don't like, but you get the idea.

Overall, the game is not really worth it in my opinion. If you care about the story, you should just watch someone else play it, to be honest. I can see some value in the Mercenaries mode and the potential of playing it co-op with a friend. In that case, thankfully, it goes on sale quite often, so you can and should get it for no more than 5 euros.
