I went into this knowing it was a linear, cinematic action game, so you won’t hear any of that “not my resident evil” talk from me.

One of the best co op experiences I’ve had with a friend. The moment to moment zombie combat was full of satisfying head popping, heavy weaponry, and a surprisingly well made hand to hand combat system. Enemy variety was great, and I loved systematically taking down a room of enemies, so why is the game so generally panned by reviewers? It’s because the game is jank af. Most of the difficulty comes from enemies spawning on top of you or bs quick time events. Sometimes, a cutscene will trigger mid fight, but the combat doesn’t pause for it, leading you to missing any shots you were aiming or getting bit when you could’ve otherwise dodged the attack. On top of that, only half the game is fun gunplay, the other half feels like a bunch of half baked mario party mini games with jank controls that’ll cause most of your deaths. They were trying to go for cool cinematic action scenes like Uncharted, but took on too many which lead to each one being terrible. Worst feeling driving sections I’ve ever felt in a video game. I don’t want to see a snow mobile for a while.

On a story level, it’s stupid, but in a fun way. This does everything right if you enjoy ribbing into a B movie action horror flick with friends. One section has you fighting a tank in a fancy Buddha castle, another is a zombie dog chasing a train, and there’s also one where you’re a swat team taking on an underwater research monstrosity. The character’s actions don’t make sense as most events follow the logic of rule of cool over everything else. Why are we punching the zombies with kung fu moves in mustafar? Shut up nerd, that’s why.

My best advice is, either play the game with a friend or don’t play at all. There’re plenty of other games with better cinematic campaigns, but this is the highest budget campaign with coop as the focus I’ve ever seen,, and it’s worth experiencing simply for that reason alone. The budget shows with just how interactable the environment is. Putting a zombie hand in a microwave anyone? How about smacking a gong and running up a children's slide just because you can? The goofy things there’re to do combined with the expensive cutscenes that're a joy to watch make the game pure fun to riff off of. It may have been a mistake to take Resident Evil in this direction, but I’m glad something like this exists.

The good points:

1.) The campaigns are thoroughly enjoyable, each offering a unique flavor. Chris’s campaign brings intense action, Leon’s campaign delivers spine-chilling horror, and Jake and Sherry’s campaign strikes a balance between the two.

The Bad ♥♥♥♥:

3.) The AI for single-player mode is incredibly...dumb, often acting in ways that defy logic and common sense.

Resident Evil 6 is a game that tries to be everything at once—and in doing so, ends up being a mixed bag of ideas, genres, and gameplay styles. While it delivers over-the-top action, an impressive amount of content, and some genuinely fun moments, it strays so far from the Resident Evil formula that it barely feels like part of the series.

The biggest strength of Resident Evil 6 is its sheer amount of content. With four full campaigns—each with different protagonists, enemies, and playstyles—the game offers a ton of variety. The co-op experience is solid, making it fun to blast through hordes of enemies with a friend. The action sequences are bombastic, featuring cinematic set pieces, high-speed chases, and ridiculous boss fights that wouldn’t feel out of place in a Hollywood blockbuster.

However, this action-heavy approach is also one of the game’s biggest flaws. Gone are the tense, survival-horror elements that defined the series—Resident Evil 6 is more of a third-person shooter with zombies. The horror atmosphere is almost nonexistent, replaced with non-stop explosions, quick-time events, and constant enemy waves. The game tries to offer variety between campaigns (Leon’s is slightly more horror-focused, while Chris’s is a straight-up action shooter), but overall, it leans way too hard into spectacle over substance.

Another major issue is the inconsistent pacing and level design. Some sections are way too long, dragging on with repetitive combat encounters that feel like padding. The enemy AI can be frustrating, the camera occasionally works against you, and the reliance on quick-time events can be excessive to the point of being annoying.

That said, if you embrace the game as a ridiculous, over-the-top action shooter rather than a true Resident Evil experience, there’s some fun to be had. The gunplay is decent, co-op is enjoyable, and Mercenaries mode offers some replayability. But for long-time fans hoping for a return to the franchise’s survival horror roots, Resident Evil 6 feels like a messy, identity-crisis-filled detour.

Resident Evil 6 holds a special place in my heart. It was a major part of my childhood, and I have vivid memories of playing it on my Xbox 360 during cold nights, completely immersed in the experience. Even in 2025, replaying it brought back all those nostalgic feelings, and I loved every moment of it.

The game's multiple campaigns offer diverse experiences, each with its own unique appeal. My personal favorite is Leon and Helena’s campaign, which brings back the classic zombie-shooting gameplay and a compelling story. It captures the essence of survival horror while maintaining a straightforward yet enjoyable narrative.

Chris and Piers’ campaign, on the other hand, is more action-packed, focusing on high-intensity gunplay. The emotional weight of their journey hit hard, and as a child, I remember being deeply moved by the ending. It still holds up today as one of the most intense moments in the series.

Jake and Sherry’s campaign was also amazing, showcasing their growing bond throughout each chapter. Watching their relationship develop added a great layer to the story, making their journey feel personal and engaging. Then there’s Ada Wong, whose solo campaign masterfully ties all the storylines together, adding depth and intrigue to the overall narrative.

Beyond the story, the Mercenaries mode is a blast. It offers a completely different way to enjoy the game, allowing players to step into the shoes of various characters and take on waves of zombies and J’avo. The No Mercy mode featuring Left 4 Dead 2 characters is a fantastic addition, especially since L4D2 remains one of my favorite games to this day.

I honestly don’t understand the hate this game receives. Many critics claim it's too different from its predecessors, but that doesn't make it a bad game. It has an incredible story, engaging gameplay, well-developed characters, and strong emotional moments. The way all the characters connect across the timeline adds so much depth to the experience.

Capcom took a bold step with Resident Evil 6, and I hope they create another game like this in the future. It may not be the traditional survival horror that some fans wanted, but it's an amazing game in its own right. For me, it will always be one of the best in the series.

The 3rd and Final Installment of the action trilogy (RE4,RE5, and RE6). This is probably the most ambitious and bombastic RE game to date as there are 4 campaigns you can play either solo or coop (playing with a friend ofc being more fun). The overarching plotline is the threat of a new BOW known as the C virus (which is a combination of the G virus from RE2 and T-Veronica from RE Code Veronica) from the terrorist group known as Neo Umbrella. There is Leon's (voiced by Matthew Mercer) campaign where his partner is series newcomer Helena Harper(voiced by Laura Bailey) who is a secret service agent as the 2 attempt to take down national security advisor Derek C Simmons who is tied to a political conspirary, Chris's(voiced by Roger Craig Smith again from RE5) campaign as he is joined by newcomer Piers Nivans (voiced by Christopher Emerson) as they track down super spy Ada Wong who seemingly is working for Neo-Umbrella, newcomer Jake's (voiced by Troy Baker) Campaign as he teams up with RE2 veteran Sherry Birkin (voiced by Lisa Yamanaka) as they attempt to bring a sample of Jake's blood as its the key to creating a vaccine to the C virus, and finally Ada's campaign as goes solo to figure out the mysteries surrounding Neo Umbrella. In terms of gameplay it is no longer tank controls so you you free to move and shoot. You are able to jump backwards,roll around,  as well as slide this time. And the same combat features from RE4 and RE5 of shooting in the head followed by a melee follow up return. For the inventory system you are able to hold every weapon you can find in the game rather than choosing which weapons to carry like in RE4 and RE5, and the only inventory management is keeping track of how much ammo, herbs, and throwables you have. And expect way more QTE's this time around Lmao. Overall this is the most nonsensical and over the top RE game by far but if you are willing to play it for how it is rather than be disappointed by its depature from the survival horror roots like how RE5 was then you will enjoy it.

Resident Jank 6: A Rollercoaster of WTF and Roundhouse Kicks 

     Imagine a Michael Bay movie where the explosions don’t stop, ever. Car chases, plane crashes, tank battles—you name it, RE6 has it. And just when you think you’ve seen it all, a zombie pilot shows up to crash your helicopter because, apparently, the T-virus includes flight school training.

     That said, the game is a bit like a party that gets out of control. It starts with spooky vibes, escalates into a military intervention, and ends with a giant zombie kaiju battle??? By the time the credits roll, you’re not sure if you just saved the world or starred in a B-movie sequel no one asked for.

     With all that being said, Resident Evil 6 is the black sheep of the family: messy, over-the-top, but still kind of fun once you embrace the chaos. It’s not survival horror—it’s survival whoa, what just happened?! And honestly? Sometimes, that’s exactly what you need.

Resident Evil 6 is a game that tries to be everything for everyone, and in doing so, it ends up being a muddled and disappointing entry in the franchise... 
While its ambition is undeniable, the result is a bloated experience that strays far from what made the series a staple of survival horror.
The game’s biggest flaw is its identity crisis. 
Instead of focusing on a cohesive tone, Resident Evil 6 splits itself across four campaigns, each attempting to cater to a different playstyle. 
Leon’s story aims for horror but falls short, Chris’s campaign is a generic military shooter, Jake’s segments feel like an action movie gone wrong, and Ada’s stealth-focused missions feel tacked on. 
The constant shifting between these styles makes the game feel disjointed and unfocused!
The gameplay itself is overly reliant on action, with wave after wave of enemies and an overabundance of ammo. 
This shift toward bombastic set pieces and Hollywood-style explosions strips away any semblance of tension or fear. 
The result is a game that feels more like a generic third-person shooter than a Resident Evil title!
To make matters worse, the controls and mechanics often feel clunky and overcomplicated. 
The game bombards players with quick-time events, awkward cover mechanics, and cumbersome combat sequences that break immersion rather than enhance it!
The story doesn’t fare much better... 
What could have been an intriguing narrative is instead a convoluted mess of intersecting plotlines, hammy dialogue, and forgettable villains. 
While the returning characters are a nice nod to fans, their arcs are drowned in the chaos of a story that tries too hard to be epic without earning its emotional beats.
Even the visuals and environments, while technically impressive in places, feel uninspired compared to the atmosphere-rich settings of earlier games. 
It’s all flash and no substance, leaving little that feels memorable or iconic.
In trying to appeal to everyone, Resident Evil 6 ends up alienating longtime fans of the series and failing to deliver a satisfying experience for newcomers. 
It’s a case of more not always being better, and a reminder that bigger isn’t always scarier.

Resident Evil 6 is that one game that's in a weird spot within the RE franchise. It was the last RE game to be released in what I like to call the "action horror era", and the common narrative is that it strayed way too far from it's horror roots, trying to appeal to the action-packed FPS games that were huge at the time like Black Ops 2. This was in contrast to RE4 and RE5, which blended action and horror relatively well. The result was a game so disastrous that Capcom vowed to never make an action-centered RE game again, and quickly went back to making horror-based RE games starting with RE7. But what do I think about all of this? Is RE6 really the worst RE game to ever be released?

Honestly, it's pretty great.

Now, don't get me wrong, it's definitely not THE best game in the franchise (for me, it would be the RE4 remake), but for what it is, it's a pretty solid game overall. Here's some of the good things I can say about this game:
[list]
[*] I like the idea of having one plot shown though multiple perspectives. Many people will say this is confusing, but when done right, having a plot through multiple viewpoints is a great way to explore various characters' mindsets and goals, and I believe this game does a great job at showcasing that through its four campaigns
[*] Combat and gunplay is really fun, especially when playing in coop. Not only to the characters properly run now (compared to 4 and 5 where they did some weird half-sprint even in a situation where they could likely die), but the takedowns can get really creative depending on the enemy (I especially like the ones where you use an enemy's weapon against them). Weapon variety is also great, as the characters have unique guns that you can only use if you play as them
[*] It's refreshing to see a game where the US isn't portrayed as the super awesome good guys who can do no wrong, as does tend to happen with other shooter games. The villain in this game is a person who works for the US government and uses his power to manipulate those in the government (and even managed to infect the president)
[*] The game can get really emotional at times, especially if you have prior knowledge of the plots of previous games [spoiler](Piers' death, Helena losing her sister, etc.)[/spoiler]
[*] The HUD has got to be one of the coolest HUDs I've seen in any video game. Not only are they designed well, but it's also a nice touch for every character to have a different HUD to correspond with whatever communication device they have on them.
[*] Jake and Sherry's bonding throughout their campaign is adorable
[*] My boi Leon being as badass as usual (and also has one of my favorite outfits from him)
[/list]

Of course, this game isn't perfect. If I were to remaster this game, I would make these changes:
[list]
[*] Less boss encounters. After a while, they stop being scary and start being annoying
[*] Cut down on the QTEs. There are lots of moments where they simply feel unecessary, especially those where you do a simple action that could have just been part of the cutscene
[*] Change or remove the vehicle segments. These kinds of segments are very hard to get right, and if you can't do that, then don't do it at all
[*] Tone down the action. While this game is great to play through, I'll admit that the action can sometimes be a bit too much in some situations (Especially that one scene where Leon crashes a plane in the middle of a Chinese city and somehow survives)
[*] Expand the environments. Especially in Leon's campaign, there are quite a few good environments that are intertwined with some very mediocre environments. Cutting those out and expanding the actually interesting stuff can help encourage exploration and make it more enjoyable.
[/list]

Overall, while this game isn't as much of a masterpiece as RE4 and RE5, it's definitely not as bad as everyone says it is. Besides, Umbrella Corps. exists, and that game is way worse than this, since Capcom basically gave up on horror for that game and basically made a CoD clone. I'd say give this game a chance before you jump to the common consensus surrounding this game. Who knows? Maybe you can find some enjoyment out of it too.

This game is a logical evolution of RE. 
When RE2 came out, it was much more linear than RE1 and the game knew that it has enjoyable gunplay, so it gave you a ton of ammo for all these sweet shotgun headshots. 
When RE3 came out, it was even more linear and allowed you to style your enemies to death by introducing timed dodges. 
Code Veronica decided to stop playing around and straight out gave you dual weapons and AK-47 coupled with an absurd action movie plot. 
Zero started playing around with the whole "two characters at the same time" thing, and RE4 gave us over the shoulder camera and quality frame data of the enemies, allowing to quickly dodge and punish attacks by simple using backward and forward walk. 
RE5 gave us co-op and became the first game to question the tank controls dogma (some controls presets allow for sidestepping). Mercenaries 3D told us that it's OK to walk while aiming and that allowing us to put many different perks on our characters is awesome.

RE6 has all of that. 
Satisfying RE2 gunplay that doesn't starve you to death with ammo, timed parries akin to RE3, totally nuts arsenal and plot that are fully faithful to Code Veronica, camera from RE4 and multiple manual dodges, and just like RE5 did back then, RE6 went further away from classic control scheme and improved the co-op options. Mercs3D's perks received an amazing development too - RE6 allows you to build characters around different gameplay styles. I once made a Leon who was incredible at setting up melee kills with his dual pistols L2 + R2 action to the point that this specific action was his bread in butter in that play-through. Shocker centered Sherry, Chris that invests everything into his assault rifle, melee Jake, so on and so forth... This stuff is awesome.

As for the cons, this game rewards reactive playstyle way too much, especially in mercenaries. Mercs3D, RE5 and RE4 beat it at that. Also most of the alt outfits are lame...

Far from as bad as people claim it to be. It's definitely worth playing if you like action games at least. It's a rather consistent experience throughout all campaigns, but they all go through different struggles.

Leon/Helena:
Definitely the worst campaign and unfortunately the slowest of them. The beginning is a major slog due to how many sections you're forced to walk through while doing essentially nothing. It does however get pretty fun and cool once you end up in the city. The people that enjoy this campaign seem to mostly be doing it because it's the most similar to the original RE format, but I don't think it really excuses how boring it is. It really doesn't fit the more action oriented playstyle of this game either. What they did to Deborah was also unnecessary. Do they have to make everything horny? Absolutely distasteful.

Chris/Piers:
People tend to compare this one to CoD which makes sense due to it leaning more into the military fantasy. It's not so much about the monsters in this campaign, but rather the internal struggles of Chris who keeps getting his teammates picked off one by one while trying to pursue his goal. It's pretty fun and probably the best campaign in this game.

Jake/Sherry:
A bit of a mixed bag, but overall a pretty solid experience. It feels like this campaign makes the least sense, at least chronologically since it spans over at least 6 months while taking place at the same time as the other campaigns which seem to take place in less than a week. I don't really like the dynamic between Jake and Sherry since it feels like they were there just to force a couple into the game and have somewhat of a return of the fan favorite from the previous two mainline games Wesker. As their own characters I like them however. The snow area was way too large and there wasn't really any point in actually fighting anything there. Somewhat comparable to RE3 due to the giant monster that follows you throughout the game, but RE3 is more fo a horror game.

Ada:
Both the easiest and the hardest campaign. The difficulty comes from being a solo player experience (you can coop, but it's meant to be played solo) that crams you into tight spaces in a game where mobility is a big factor. This is however mostly just an issue in the first chapter since everything is such a breeze throughout the rest of the game. For the most part you'll be acting like somewhat of a sniper that helps the other characters out. They can however not die so for the most part you can just wait for the AI to do its job. Whenever you're truly playing alone however, stealth is possible and there aren't that many enemies so it's not that difficult anyway. Her campaign is what ties everything together, kind of. It's just not that interesting though and feels more like a bonus mode.

This may not be a good RE game, but it's a good action game. The controls can feel a little clunky when you want to do tighter movement and the aiming feels a bit off at times. It feels like they added a bunch of fan service for no reason which at best was pointless or distracting and at worst distasteful. It's however not that big of a deal unless you play it around your parents or something. This game is probably better as a coop experience, but it's not bad alone either. I'd recommend getting it one sale, but it's relatively cheap normally.

There are a lot of reasons why Resident Evil 6 is bad, but chief among them to me is that this is four short games shoved into one package, and all four of those games individually suck! The story is an incoherent, impenetrable mess, the character writing and direction (especially for Chris and Leon, the supposed headliners of this game) is tragically bad, and even though it's one of the rare games with a full co-op campaign, that co-op has several game-breaking bugs that make it extremely frustrating to finish in the only mode that makes it tolerable. God this game is awful!

To take it campaign by campaign: Chris's campaign is essentially poor man's Gears of War, with zombies that shoot back with machine guns (insane), cover mechanics that often simply do not work, and an asinine, backwards story that's told in as muddled a manner as possible, blunting the early-game stakes and lessening the impact of the inevitable sacrifice at the end. Leon's campaign is touted as "classic survival horror," but the puzzles are messy and vague, some of the zombies STILL have guns, and Helena's contributions to the story are irritating at best and unbearable at worst. It's Capcom's worst instincts in survival horror all wrapped up into one terrible campaign. And Jake's campaign...yeah, sure, he's Leon lite and his quips are funny, but his campaign feels like a dumping ground for ideas that didn't or couldn't fit into the other two, and is where the game-breaking bugs really, truly start to ruin sessions. The novelty of seeing Sherry again is not nearly enough to make up for it. And Ada's campaign, finally, is a waste of time, with an absolutely horrible co-op experience because the mode was clumsily bolted onto it post-release.

People always cite RE6 as the nadir of this franchise, where it was clearer than ever that Capcom had no clue where to take the series, and those people are absolutely right. This game is only tolerable when you don't take it seriously at all and laugh your way through co-op, and even then, it makes absolutely certain to irritate and confuse you anyway. This game is not worth it unless you really, really want to say that you've played every mainline game, and where do those bragging rights get you? Nowhere at all. Don't play this, just read the Wikipedia summary if you're that curious.

Resident Evil 6 is known as the 'black sheep' of the series for a good reason; it is a rough hewn diamond. - It is a hard recommend, it is fun but that fun does come with a lot of caveats and unless you are a big fan of the series it might be simply better to skip this one.
The best way I can describe it is that someone was playing the entire Resident Evil franchise whilst watching Michael Bay films in the background and had the misguided idea of trying to combine the two. Every level is full of spectacle moments that require the camera to pull away from the thing you are actually fighting so you can watch the pretty visuals whilst getting massacred somewhere off camera.
.
This could have been a really good game; Three campaigns that intertwine telling portions of the overall story. Characters from past games getting another chance to shine and interact for the first time with each other and a new virus which brings brand new monsters and mechanics.
.
The problem is the story requires you to play in a particular order, if you dont then you will be left very confused about certain characters complete lack of reference to prior events that they absolutely should be discussing. I also find that the end of each campaign feels very rushed, and without going into too much spoiler territory there is a major event in China at the end of the game that doesnt seem to get resolved by the main characters. One could assume the BSAA finish off the situation but to be honest nothing short of a nuke would seemingly solve the issue - but the game never talks about so its left to you as a player to wonder just how it all ended.
.
There are also plot threads that dont seem to actually go anywhere but are just there for lore, such as Sherry's connection with the G-virus in her body. Its a neat detail but ultimately plays no role in the game, sherry has no special abilities related to it (such as Jake's melee attacks being much better than the regular knife or pistol whip attacks).
.
The game is also riddled with cutscene after cutscene. Some you can skip, but others you are forced to watch and it becomes very infuriating on replays of the game.
.
The inventory system is also frustrating to work with especially in the middle of a fight
There are also mechanics that the game simply does not mention - for example, the 'combat gauge' or stamina as most people would call it. its an important mechanic because you use it when you use close combat attacks or slide attacks, and once depleted you are in a weakened state that allows enemies to one-shot you. This is a really important mechanic and there is NO tutorial about it.
.
There are also opportunities I feel the developers missed out on with certain mechanics. Enemies have the ability to mutate into several additional forms. Certain zombies can transform into fleshless berserkers that take a lot to kill, and J'avo can grow shield like arms, armoured legs, long tentacles or extra strong claws. The issue is there seems to be no consistency when these mutations occur, I'v run numerous tests and they dont appear to be part of any script and shooting the arm of one J'avo sometimes will trigger a mutation when on the next playthrough shooting the exact same J'avo in the same way yields no mutation. If there was a consistency to the mechanic it could lead to some very cool tactical decision making about how to deal with certain enemies in groups. There could even be detrimental mutations that cause enemies to swing wildly hurting or killing their comrades nearby.
.
And then there is a pet peeve of mine - online only achievements. I hate games that can only be 100% completed if you play online too. This is often tricky with older games as the community has moved on and those that remain are probably pretty good at the game to the point it will make noobs never want to play online. There is also the constant threat that eventually the servers will be shut down and then these achievements will be beyond anyone's ability to reach
-
sigh, overall the game had promise, its a 6/10 in my books but it could have been so much more. I want to love it which is why I kept playing it but there are so many frustrations it brings the overall experience down . I'm really glad I managed to beat another Resident Evil game. This time supposedly one of the fans' least favorites and the one considered the lowest point of the franchise. It did however surprise me in a good way. So here are my thoughts on it.

I'm going to start off with the gameplay. The game plays a bit differently from the remakes 2-4. It's a lot more action-packed, less focused on horror and inventory management, and more centered on action. It's honestly a really nice action game with cool set pieces that kept me entertained for the 29 hours I spent playing it. I played through most of it in co-op, which was really fun, up until the Ada campaign. Its co-op felt like an afterthought, not very enjoyable for the person playing as the soldier who can't open doors or do anything except walk and shoot. The enemy variety was decent... However, some of the enemies felt basically like what you get in an FPS game, with guns and stuff, which honestly wasn't what you'd expect from a Resident Evil game, and I'd understand if people hated it. The boss battles were good, they had some cool designs, especially in the Ada campaign.

The game is divided into four campaigns, which means there is so much content to get through, and all of the campaigns were equally good in my opinion, and they're all worth playing in order as the last one ties up everything nicely.

The story is okay, it's a bit silly at times, and the voice acting is cringy, but it honestly didn't hurt my enjoyment of the game. The technical performance was pretty good. I mean it's a 2012 game at this point, so you should be able to run it no problem, and it honestly still looks great even in 2024.

[b]TL;DR: The game is really fun. It's not like the RE remakes, it's its own version of RE. It's not scary, it's action-heavy if that's what you're looking for. Pick this up for cheap on sale.[/b]

PROS:
- Bosses (The Ustanak and Simmons)
- Playing on hard difficulty can give you a sort of survival horror gameplay
- Skills (although these are disabled on No Hope)
- Co-Op
- Wonderfully voice acted

CONS
- You will be mainly getting skill points in drops
- Physics are too realistic in this game.
- There are no in game costumes
- Some sections are rage quitting at times

FINAL VERDICT: Whilst Resident Evil 6 is a flawed experience, I overall had fun. My favorite campaign has to be Leon's, followed by Jake. Chris comes in third place since some of the Javo enemies can be outright infuriating to deal with. Ada comes in last place and this is where my main concern comes in. Ada's campaign does not work in Co-Op. From what I understand, it was originally supposed to be a singleplayer experience, with co-op being added later. This messes some of the balance up in the campaign, there was one boss that was more or less annoying to deal with since it was obviously designed for one player (i.e. the chainsaw guy on the bus). 

8/10, Play this game if you want to have a good time with your friend, but maybe avoid this game if you're looking for a survival horror experience.

Leon's campaign was a classic horror thriller that kept me on edge the entire time. Chris' campaign was more intense and action-packed, with huge battles that had me glued to the screen. Jake's story was a perfect mix of high-energy combat and emotional depth, while Ada’s campaign gave me a real sense of mystery and intrigue. Each one kept me hooked, and it felt like I was playing a completely new game with every change of character. 🎮🔥

💀 Action-Packed Combat: Honestly, the combat in RE6 was a game-changer. The moment I jumped into the action, I was amazed at how fluid and satisfying the controls were. Switching between intense gunfights and brutal hand-to-hand combat felt seamless. Whether I was executing a brutal melee move to take down a B.O.W. or unloading a clip into a horde of zombies, everything felt smooth and impactful. The variety of weapons, from shotguns to grenade launchers, kept me excited to try out new strategies, and the QTEs (Quick Time Events) had me on the edge of my seat, especially during boss fights! 🤜🤛

👾 Stunning Graphics & Environments: One of my most memorable experiences with RE6 was just exploring its world. The graphics were so detailed, I found myself stopping just to admire the environment! From the gritty, dark streets of Tall Oaks to the lush forests in China, every location felt real and immersive. The lighting, textures, and level design kept me hooked and made each area feel unique. Some sequences, like escaping a collapsing building or fighting off waves of enemies in tight corridors, were pure cinematic magic. 🌆🌲

💬 Great Multiplayer: The multiplayer aspect of RE6 is a highlight, and my time with it was a blast! I spent hours playing co-op with a friend, and it was so much fun. The mechanics were easy to get into, and we could strategize and tackle enemies together. Whether we were navigating the tense, tight spaces or fighting off massive boss monsters, the teamwork aspect made it all the more rewarding. The ability to play both locally and online also meant that I could dive into some epic sessions with friends no matter where they were. 👫

🎶 Epic Soundtrack & Sound Design: The sound design in RE6 blew me away. The soundtrack was perfectly timed, with tense music building up during fights, giving me an adrenaline rush before a big battle. The sound effects—whether it was the groans of zombies or the thundering footsteps of massive enemies—were so immersive, I found myself truly on edge. After finishing each campaign, I couldn’t wait to jump into a higher difficulty or explore the hidden secrets scattered around the maps. Unlocking new costumes, weapons, and even bonus modes like Mercenaries kept me coming back for more. I also loved unlocking extra content that made me see the story in a new light—RE6 doesn’t just end after you finish the main campaign; there’s so much to uncover. 🔄

In conclusion, Resident Evil 6 exceeded all my expectations and delivered an experience that was both thrilling and unforgettable. Whether you’re a longtime RE fan or new to the series, this game has something for everyone. Oh dear god how do you screw up a game this bad. Saw the game on sale for 5€, thought to myself "how bad can the game actually be, might as well buy and check it out" and now I have regrets. Finished one out of four campaigns and I can't wait to be done with the rest.

Let's start with what's good. Combat. It's hard to learn the intricacies, but it's clear that there's actual depth to it. In my opinion, the combat is enjoyable and really high quality even by today's standards. Unfortunately the game treats its combat like an unwanted stepchild and kicks it into a corner.

On to the negatives. Zombies are bullet sponges. You're so much better off meleeing enemies most of the time that I feel like the game actively hates gunplay and discourages players from using it. In addition, way too often you find yourself in areas where you're essentially getting a permanent horde spawn à la Left 4 Dead, so not only does the game discourage gunplay, it also often discourages combating enemies at all and rather just have you run through areas.

All the areas in first story are pretty much corridors, so I don't expect the other three to differentiate from that. There's practically no exploration in this game, and every area is either tight or small so the possibilities of the excellent combat system can never be fully explored. You're borderline forced to use the most efficient methods at hand rather than tackle enemies the way you want.

Story. The four stories are interweaving which is interesting but also leaves the stories as standalone experiences, lackluster. I also feel like they tried to make this "something greater than a game", almost like a game/movie hybrid. The characters do not react to important revelations like real people, almost like the revelations aren't meant to have an effect on them but only on the viewer/player as if they're one of the participants rather than an independent observer of the story and characters.

Quicktime events. The game is full of them.


Even if the game was free, I couldn't recommend wasting time on it. RE5 at least had some merit as an action game, but due to RE6 trying to be a bit of everything it ends up being universally dislikeable.


---Edit---
Finished the whole game. Sticking with all the criticism above, and could add plenty of cons... but that would be beating a dead horse. Instead, I'll add some of the pros I encountered:
- In campaign 3, there was one instance of being rewarded for exploration. The fact that I'm adding a single instance of rewarding exploration to the pros-list should say everything that needs to be said.
- Piers Nivans. I really disliked most of the character depictions (Helena and Ada Wong being neutral), and while Piers isn't winning any awards, he's still miles ahead of the rest of the cast.
I'm trying really hard to not just say "the whole game is ♥♥♥♥", but other than the criminally neglected combat system and the two points above, I can't think of anything positive to say.

Resident Evil 6 : By Triple F

"Resident Evil 6" stands out as a unique and highly ambitious chapter in Capcom’s acclaimed franchise, aiming to provide a blend of action and survival horror. Released in 2012, the game takes an unorthodox approach by dividing its story across four distinct campaigns, each featuring different protagonists and gameplay styles. By casting players as franchise veterans Leon Kennedy and Chris Redfield, alongside newcomers Jake Muller and Ada Wong, "Resident Evil 6" offers a rich, intertwining narrative with varied experiences that shift from classic survival horror to intense action and even stealth. However, while this diversity adds replay value, it also leaves the game feeling disjointed at times, with each campaign pulling the player in vastly different directions.

The Leon campaign is the closest "Resident Evil 6" comes to delivering traditional survival horror, with dimly lit hallways, tense exploration, and an ominous atmosphere that hearkens back to earlier series entries. Players find themselves battling slow-moving zombies in settings that feel eerie and claustrophobic, from a zombie-infested university to creepy subterranean catacombs. Although the horror elements are palpable, they’re often disrupted by quick-time events (QTEs) and cinematic set-pieces that prioritize spectacle over sustained tension. The campaign does manage to satisfy fans nostalgic for Resident Evil’s early atmosphere, but these interruptions sometimes break the immersion, preventing it from fully achieving its horror potential.

In stark contrast, the Chris campaign is a full-fledged action experience, placing Chris in the role of a military squad leader fighting bio-organic weapons (B.O.W.s) in Eastern Europe and China. This campaign is heavily combat-oriented, with cover-based shooting mechanics and large-scale battles that feel akin to modern military shooters. It delivers non-stop action but distances itself from the suspense and fear traditionally associated with the franchise. The change in tone may appeal to players who enjoy fast-paced firefights, but fans of Resident Evil’s horror roots may find it lacking in atmosphere and suspense. Chris’s campaign highlights the game’s identity crisis, as it’s torn between pleasing action fans and remaining true to the series’ horror roots.

Jake’s campaign adds another layer of variety by blending action with an emphasis on evasion and boss encounters, reminiscent of Resident Evil 3’s Nemesis gameplay. Jake, the son of long-time antagonist Albert Wesker, is paired with Sherry Birkin, creating a unique dynamic as they face the relentless Ustanak, a powerful enemy that stalks them throughout their journey. The Ustanak provides a good dose of tension, and the campaign’s globetrotting locations offer diverse settings. However, Jake’s over-the-top combat skills and confidence often downplay the horror, and the campaign occasionally feels like an action-adventure romp more than a horror experience, catering more to fans of escapism than fear.

The Ada campaign, available after completing the main story, serves as a stealth-focused, puzzle-solving chapter that ties together plot elements from the other campaigns. Ada’s storyline unfolds from an almost espionage-like perspective, with quieter, slower-paced sections and a focus on exploration over combat. It’s an attempt to introduce classic Resident Evil elements with an added twist, but the game’s mechanics don’t fully support true stealth gameplay, often defaulting back to action. While Ada’s campaign contributes significantly to the story, filling in gaps and providing a bird’s-eye view of events, it ultimately feels like a missed opportunity to deliver a stealth experience that might have complemented the series’ focus on suspense.

Mechanically, "Resident Evil 6" introduces a range of new moves, including sliding, dodging, and shooting while moving, all of which modernize its gameplay and add fluidity to combat. The melee combat system has also been expanded, with characters now able to perform a variety of melee attacks, adding depth to close encounters. A stamina meter limits these melee moves, adding a bit of strategy, but the game still offers a surplus of ammo and health resources that lessen the challenge, making survival feel less daunting than in past titles. The abundance of resources shifts the focus further from horror to action, a move that divided fans and critics alike.

Visually, "Resident Evil 6" is quite impressive, especially considering its time of release. Each campaign boasts distinct, richly detailed environments, from eerie graveyards to bustling urban streets, making the game a visual treat. Character models and animations are well-crafted, and the game’s sound design contributes significantly to building atmosphere, with unsettling sounds and tense music that heighten the immersion. Yet, the constant shifts between horror and action tones can make it challenging for players to fully immerse themselves in any one mood, as the game often leans too heavily into bombastic set-pieces over quiet, suspenseful moments.

In conclusion, "Resident Evil 6" represents Capcom’s desire to broaden the franchise by exploring different genres, blending horror, action, and even a bit of espionage. While the game is commendable for its scope and ambition, this attempt at diversity creates an identity crisis, leaving it struggling to fully satisfy any one audience. Fans looking for traditional survival horror may feel disappointed by the action-heavy approach, while new players may find the pacing inconsistent. Though "Resident Evil 6" may not stand as a fan-favorite, it serves as an intriguing, albeit polarizing, experiment that paved the way for future installments to revisit and refine the series' roots, ultimately bridging the gap between horror and action in Resident Evil’s evolving legacy.

The best resident evil in my opinion. Why?... 

Although it is the least survival horror of the series (outside of O.R.C, U.C., Resistance, and Re: Verse) and leans more into action/adventure, it has THE BEST GAMEPLAY in my opinion, with the Revelations series coming in close second. Characters that actually RUN! Can you believe it!!?? No more stupid ass half sprinting. I mean... would you only use a light jog in a bio-terror situation or zombie apocalypse? I dont think so~!!!! You'd be running your ass off. Being as tactical, fast, and agile as possible. Sneaky and stealthy when needed but when ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan its go time!!!!  I mean.... movement so bad in the 2 and 3 remakes you have to spam dodge and hobble around like an idiot in order to speedrun! None of that here! 

This game was pre-adaptive damage as well, meaning if youre actually a good shot it doesnt take six or eight headshots to down a zombie and you arent penalized for accuracy and skill. It has great dodge mechanics as well! AND A RUNNING SLIDE! Which is not only useful for evasion but also to stun enemies. You really feel like you have control of your character and not just limited for the sake of artificial difficulty. 

On top of all of that, the skill system is pretty neat and adds a reason to replay the game more than once, collecting points to unlock skills such as the weapon master skills that increase your damage, and shooting wild which removes your laser / reticle / cursor but gives you a massive damage boost, rewarding you greatly for accurate shots.  There are other great skills as well like pickup frequency enhancements, infinite ammo if youre into that, piercing (bullet penetration), crit damage, enemy type damage, etc. 

And if all of that wasnt enough, the game includes what is essentially 7.5 campaigns. There are 4 actual campaigns, and you can play through each as two different characters which both have their own unique experiences / roles during gameplay. Ada's campaign has Hunk as the second character which has somewhat a limited experience hence the 7.5 campaigns instead of 8.

Yes, there are a few mechanics that some players feel are annoying or frustrating like a couple of instances that rely on button timing, a couple of wonky vehicle sections,  and some instances where you dont have equipment and may have to hide, solve a puzzle, or use stealth/melee. 

ANNNNND!!! The game has multiplayer co-op that you can join in at any time (or be joined), you can turn on/off the ability for players to join in as enemy monsters when you start a campaign (or play that mode yourself, joining in and trying to kill players). You can play with players all over the world, or set it to regional, and it shows their connectivity strength. 

ANNNNNDDD!! The game has mercenaries. 

The RE Games frequently go on sale from 30% to 75% off. If youre a fan of the series and like games with good character control mechanics, dont mind that its not super spooky and leans into action, want a ton of content for a very reasonable price, then grab this game. ESPECIALLY if its on sale.

Resident Evil 6 sees the zombie apocalypse take a truly global stage, as outbreaks happen internationally from the United States to Eastern Europe to China and beyond. Following four separate campaigns exploring the latest virus's origin and destruction, you the player will follow what is *supposedly* the most intense and dangerous bio-organic weapon outbreak to date.

RE6's campaigns follow main characters Leon, Chris, new character Jake, and Ada, along with side AI/co-op characters Helena, Piers, and Sherry. Each campaign covers five missions which can take anywhere from 30-120 minutes depending on the story. RE6 takes the action-focused gameplay introduced in RE4 and amplified in RE5 and turns that dial up even further. RE6 has absolutely zero brakes with the action, for better or for worse, constantly sending you into high-octane scenarios of explosion-filled, slow-motion QTE martial arts nonsense. While at first the action feels fun to experience, like watching a late-night movie with a bowl of popcorn in hand and not a care in the world, but when it doesn't really stop whatsoever to take a break for significant plot or dialogue or emotion or other such, it can get overwhelming quickly, or worse simply boring. And for better or for worse yet again, there is so, damn, much, videogame, to, play, in RE6. You really can't get away with just playing say Leon's campaign and then nothing else, as the story doesn't truly wrap together and make sense until completing all four campaigns, meaning you're going to spend 20 hours *if you RUSH* in RE6, and by the end of it if you're not memeing your way through it with a friend you're going to be downright exhausted. At the very least, the weapons feel satisfying to use, and using the melee smartly in combination with your weapons can feel rewarding when done correctly, saving you ammo and letting you see Leon suplex a zombie which always ends up being funny. The health system in this game is absurd though, where instead of consuming herbs and sprays raw you have to assemble these pills which only heal small portions of your health bar at a time. And while I'm on the topic, the inventory system/UI is a NIGHTMARE to navigate, with the most ridiculous layout to switch weapons, craft items, and equip consumables.

With a story that lacks cohesion, absurd dialogue, action-packed gameplay that loses its charm after just three hours, RE6 is rarely a joy to play, and more often a chore that I would have a hard time recommending to even the most dedicated Resident Evil fan. RE6 is unfortunately a product of its release era, where turning intense horror-focused series into explosive action was the norm; at the time it wasn't a great idea, and even nowadays I can't say it's really worth your money.

RE6 decided one story wasn’t enough. No, we needed four. Leon’s here doing his best Night of the Living Dead impression while Chris is busy starring in his own Call of Duty: Zombies spin-off.

Resident Evil 6 is like trying to read a book with four different endings, except you can’t remember where you left off. "Wait, why is Leon here? And who’s this new guy Jake?" Imagine walking into four action movies that started before you arrived, and everyone’s shouting “Bioterrorism!” while you try to grab your popcorn.

Leon’s campaign teases us with classic survival horror for about five minutes before you’re blasting zombies in the face. Chris, on the other hand, is full-on military action, yelling at every mutant in sight. Jake punches a mutant to death because apparently being the son of Albert Wesker makes you part Terminator. Ada Wong, always 10 steps ahead of the plot, spends most of her campaign in a solo stealth mission, and honestly? It’s like she’s playing a completely different game.

Remember the days when Resident Evil made you fear every bullet you wasted? Not here! In RE6, guns are a formality. Why waste ammo when you can perform a flying karate kick into a zombie’s skull? And if you’re tired of suplexing the undead, don’t worry: there are driving sections! Yup, in RE6, you’re not just battling zombies, you’re also somehow behind the wheel of a car. Or a boat. Or a jet ski. Because Resident Evil is now also Fast & Furious.

Graphically, the game looks great, for 2012. It’s got all the high-octane visuals you could want: fireballs, crumbling buildings, and grotesque monsters galore. But the best part is the dramatic slo-mo during action scenes. Because when Leon Kennedy is kicking a zombie off a speeding train, you better believe you’re going to see that from five different angles, all in slow motion. 

Resident Evil 6 is the game you play when you want pure, unfiltered action. If you’re looking for the slow-paced, nerve-wracking horror of earlier titles, you’ll find glimpses of it in Leon’s campaign.

Altough you'll see many people hating on this game, and ignoring it's existence, I've really enjoyed it. I feel like any RE fan will enjoy this experience. This game is a bit more action packed than the previous ones, just like RE5 is, but RE6 did everything far better. 

In this game you'll have 4 different campaigns, with 3 of them being coop campaigns. You can either play with your friend or an AI companion and this time you don't have to worry about your AI companion dying or anything like that, so that's a huge improvement from RE5. 

3 coop campaigns are: Leon & Helen, Chris & Piers, Sherry & Jake.
While in the last campaign you play as Ada Wong, she's got no partner there, so no coop there.

'Each Campaign' has '5 Chapters', and each chapter is about an hour or an hour and a half long. 

Everything that you hate about RE5 has been drastically improved in RE6. 

Note each campaign will tell you parts of the same story + some original parts that you've had no idea about in your other Campaigns. So let's say out of 5 chapters 1 maybe 2 will make you replay the same mission that you've already played in your previous campaign, while the other 3 chapters will be completely new missions that you haven't played trough yet.

Should You Play Trough Every Characters Campaign Then?
You don't have to. You'll understand the story just right even if you play trough 1 coop campaign with your friend or an AI companion, but trust me when I tell you, you're probably missing out on a lot if you don't play trough all of the coop campaigns, there are so many cool missions and locations in each campaign that you'd miss out on if you don't play trough them.

However you should definitely play trough Ada Wong's solo campaign, because it's the most important one. In my opinion her campaign was maybe even the best one in RE6.
Ada is and very much feels like a main character in this game, altough other campaigns were interesting aswell. Each one was unique in some way.

Graphics are fine, but  new games have much better graphics, then again for a game that came out in 2012, they did a good job. Controls aren't the best ones out there, but they're good enough, unlike in RE5 where it was a really big problem, you can shoot while moving, you can actually turn around normally unlike in RE5.

Agent Hunt - 
you can join random players campaign and play as the monster, your aim is to kill him, you can respawn as many times as you want. Personally I didn't like this mode I feel like controls for monsters are not very responsive + they suck, you know that it's bad when AI controlled monsters feel stronger than player controlled ones.

Mercenarys -
play as any of your favorite characters from RE6, each character has a different loadout, kill as many monsters as you can in a short amount of time, and survive for as long as you can. Also by doing finisher moves and collecting certain things you can earn some more time.
I've really enjoyed this gamemode, and many people are saying that this game's got the best Mercenarys mode out there, so if that's your thing, this game's got a lot of reasons for you to try it.

The start of the game is bonkers-go-nuts. It throws you in the middle of a terrorist/zombie attack with no instructions on where to go or how to play or why you’re there. It’s been a while since I played Resident Evil 5 and I just finished Resident Evil 2, so I’m used to the slower pace. But all of a sudden I’m falling out of a helicopter and climbing up skyscrapers. What kind of tutorial is this? Can you not give me at least a little context? Mise en Scene is for movies, not video games.

Plus I hate when they throw you in without a chance to adjust the controller or the video settings. I thought I’d have to save at some point before even getting to setup. How do I get health? How do I deal with inventory? What’s new and different in this game compared to RE5?

Not much it turns out. It seems like the big draw is that there are four interconnected campaigns, each about five hours long. But each story is so fragmented that it makes no sense, and playing each campaign does nothing to fill in the gaps.

How about some background on these characters? Who is this Nemesis-knockoff Ustanak chasing Jake Muller? What’s the deal with him being Albert Wesker’s son? (Jake, not Ustanak). When did Sherry collect Jake’s blood after they crash in the helicopter? They’ve been running around crazy the past hour (video game time). It sounded like you needed a lab for that. And now they’ve got a fetch quest to find three data chips that fell out? Plus, you’ve still got him next to you. Just collect the data again!

Half of Chris’s story takes place in flashback. What is it, five years ago? So that makes it all pointless–I know Chris survives because I talk to him in Leon’s story. Playable flashbacks in video games are as pointless as sesame seeds on a hamburger bun. I should be invincible because, by laws of temporal mechanics, I have to live in order to do the actions which are already cemented in time.

And then the final boss is a giant housefly.

Resident Evil 6 is a blend of adventure and horror, where the story unfolds from four different perspectives. You can choose between four stories: Leon, Chris, Sherry, and Ada. The four main characters meet and assist each other throughout the game, providing a unique experience where you have to piece together the narrative by playing through each storyline. Each story offers about four hours of gameplay.

Story Rating:
1. Sherry & Jake
2. Chris & Piers
3. Ada
4. Leon & Helena

Let's start with the cons:
The game is very clunky. The inventory system is a mess, requiring you to press hotkeys to access healing items, grenades, and weapons, which makes it unnecessarily complicated. I like the sneaking and sprinting attacks, but they’re difficult to execute due to how bad the controls are. You can't adjust the mouse sensitivity, and even if you could, the sensitivity fluctuates. Sometimes it's too low, other times it's too high. The graphics are fine, but compared to other games from the same year, they fall short, especially for a big company like Capcom.

Now for the pros:
I love the game’s story. The way all four stories intersect, requiring you to play them all to get the full picture, is an amazing concept. Even if some bosses repeat and the gameplay can feel a bit repetitive at times, it's all worth it in the end. I also adore the new characters—Sherry, Jake, Helena, and Piers are a great addition to the already exciting cast. Plus, having a campaign focused solely on Sherry and Jake, giving us a new Resident Evil duo, is a chef's kiss moment.

My review:
Overall, I have to admit Resident Evil 6 ranks among my favorite Resident Evil games. If it ever gets a remake, I hope they address the criticisms but keep the four-story structure. Some people think it would be too much work, but I disagree. The average playtime of the game is 16 hours, which is normal for a AAA title. I am still torn on the koop since I personally enjoy it but also understand that, if executed wrong, it can be killing the atmosphere. Capcoms remakes were all very strong, so I trust them and their ability to uplift this oldie!

Resident Evil 6 is like sonic adventure with a less cohesive plot. 

RE6 is the black sheep of the main franchise and is often considered the worst game in the series (excluding all the spin-off games.) Whilst many considered RE4 as the starting point of action resi it at least tried being a horror game, the same can be said about re5, re6 however is just pure action porn, a game that from start to finish is just non-stop set pieces. I used to absolutely despise this game but as I've gotten older I think I've come to enjoy it for what it is, now that we've had 5 'pure' resi games since the release of 6 it's easier to go back and play this game without any preconceived notions that capcom has destroyed the franchise. 

So with that said let's talk resi 6, you must temper your expectations, this is not a horror game, this is a 3rd person shooter and a damn fine one at that, you play as a multitude of different resi protagonist both old and new and they all have their own flair, they feel so good to control and shooting is tight. I'm quite a big fan of 3rd person shooters but I find it tricky find a solid tps from a Japanese dev, this might be the best one. The amount of content this game has is staggering and all the extra modes can keep you playing for hours, if you like action resi that is.

The story is a massive cluster ♥♥♥♥ of characters and nonsense. You pick a character and then you see the story from their perspective and they then overlap with the other characters. Thus the sonic adventure comparison but at least in sonic adventure I cared more and the stakes were higher. My biggest complaint is the utterly nonsense story. 

Coop makes a return and is a much smoother experience than resi 5, ai is ruthless in this game and I very rarely if at all got annoyed at them, with the exception of Helena who seemed utterly useless and would often just break in situations in which it was vital she acted by herself with the fire trap and plane sections being the biggest offenders as she'd often just stand around doing nothing when she needed to either go off and pull a switch or defend me.

Now we know the redi franchise is back on course and has been from some time I can't hate this game anymore. For me when it initially released it was at capcoms worst and I feared for the future of resi. If this has been a spinoff game all the memes and backlash would've been less, though in hindsight that might have meant less sales, this is the highest grossing resi after all.

Overall, this is a very decent game.  The 2 player co-op aspect to this game is a welcome addition to the gameplay, which is already good.  I wouldn't say that the controls are an improvement over previous installments (RE4, RE5), but they work well.  Definitely different.

The storyline's pretty much seemingly no different than other RE installments - big evil bio-weapons corporation starts an outbreak, leaving you to fight hordes of zombies and other genetic monstrosities through a variety of settings that range from urban environments, to factories/laboratories, to weird tombs and castles.  It is definitely a departure from the original installments (RE1, RE2), in that it's less 'survival/horror' and more of an action/adventure game. 
 It's kinda cliche, but I won't rag on that because by the sixth installment of this franchise (not counting the other related titles), it's safe to say this one's for the fans of RE4 and 5.  

That said, it's not a bad game to play if this is your first time playing an RE title.

Resident Evil 6 is a fun and engaging game, especially if you enjoy action-packed horror experiences. One of its most interesting aspects is how it combines four different storylines, creating a kind of crossover that keeps the game fresh and varied. Despite having multiple campaigns, the game doesn’t feel overly long or tedious, and the intertwining stories make it easy to stay engaged.

The difficulty is generally moderate. One of the few challenges I encountered was a shortage of ammunition at certain points, which added tension to the action sequences. Combat and gameplay mechanics are solid, but I personally found the controls a bit cumbersome at times, especially when using a controller (I played with a PS4 controller). Keyboard controls work well too, but the game is definitely more comfortable for players used to controllers, even if some aspects feel a bit clunky.

Graphically, the game shows its age a bit, even for its 2012 release. Character models, lighting, and textures are decent, but some environments lack the polish and detail seen in other games of the era. Despite this, the atmosphere of tension and horror is effective, and the cinematic camera angles and dramatic set pieces keep the action exciting.

The music and sound design are strong points. The soundtrack heightens suspense and adds intensity to combat, while sound effects, like gunfire, explosions, and monster growls, contribute to an immersive experience. The voice acting is also solid, giving each character personality and helping make the story more engaging.

Overall, Resident Evil 6 is an enjoyable experience for fans of the series or action-horror games in general. While it has a few flaws in graphics and controls, the multiple storylines, tense combat, and cinematic presentation make it worth playing.

A solid action title, even if it falls short as a Resident Evil game. 

Resident Evil 6, released in 2012, is the third action-heavy title in the longrunning Resident Evil franchise. Like RE5, it features two-player co-op spread across a new episodic format of four separate campaigns. It tells four different events happening at around the same time; gov. agent Leon S. Kennedy uncovering the truth about the death of his close friend, the current US president and the mysterious new virus spreading in the States, freelance spy Ada Wong investigating a setup plotted against her by an overly attached business partner, BSAA operative Chris Redfield coping with the losses he's suffered throughout his career and tracking down an Ada lookalike after she massacred his strike team and finally an escaped test subject, Jake Mueller, being scouted out by Sherry Birkin so his blood can be synthesized into a cure for a virus outbreak running rampant internationally, as well as explore his origins and whether or not they define him as a person. 

Gameplay once again takes heavy notes from past action RE titles, like 4, 5 and Revelations 1, with your usual weakpoint shooting, melee finisher and kiting loop present that had become so addicting the past few years. New additions include a handy, omni-directional dodge, the ability to perform melee combat on command, letting you initiate entire combos against enemies, which becomes a tad bit overpowered against your more regular enemies, as well as many new context-based melee techniques and counters that I can't name here all at once. The game has arguably the most combat depth in the entire franchise, and it isn't even close. Enemy variety is delightful here, some of the strongest monster design I've seen, thanks to the new C-virus (chrysalid) which transforms its victims into a multitude of grotesque and specialized bioweapons, coming in all shapes, sizes and functions, from being able to split and recombine their own body parts, to creating hardened armor and projectile spines, to repurposed limbs into clubs, glaives and wings. Levels and puzzles are relatively fun, split into a couple stages (usually four) per each of the four campaigns, and the runtime is the longest out of any game in the series, clocking in at at least a casual 20 hours, if not more. RE6 also introduces a perk and tally point system at the end of each level, letting you equip perks that upgrade your character's stats like rate of fire, health, recovery speed, etc. Not unlike Revelations 1's weapon part kit system, but for your entire character. Several additional gamemodes are added ontop of the main campaign, the most exciting of which being the ever delightful Mercenaries mode, packaged with a sick main theme this time.

The most common complaints about the game, some that I agree with, are the story that gets a bit too over-the-top at times (but otherwise does fit regular RE shenanigans), annoying QTE's and the focus on action over horror. Other minor complaints would be janky setpieces, but they were never too bad. 

I think this game is overhated even with its flaws, and can offer a decent experience if you have a pal to play it with. The game isn't expensive, but it gets criminally cheap during Capcom's frequent publisher sales, so just get it there, probably even in the triple action pack bundled with OG RE4 and 5.

Resident Evil 6 is probably the most confused game I have ever experienced. While Resident Evil is known best when it does survival horror, RE6 is known as the survival horror... action, blockbuster, military shooter, etc, etc, this game can't really be described better than just a huge mess that attempts to please everyone, but instead pleases nobody.

Story
While most games would go the route of telling one, strong story, RE6 takes the brave route of telling 4, separate (but same storyline), weaker storylines. The main storylines are from Chris, Leon, Jake, and last but probably worst, Ada. Quite honestly they vary greatly in quality, as Chris probably has the least amount of story, but a simple goal. Jake's storyline focuses on the Nemesis like enemy and the relation between Jake and Sherry, almost like a love story. Leon's Campaign probably has the most attempts to do storytelling, but falls flat with many moments of just forced walking sections. They vary a ton in tone, but at the same time share the same (big explosions go boom). Probably the most disappointing was Leon's campaign, as it was obvious that they wanted to focus on horror, but then realized that they might bore the player, so reminds us that we are playing RE6 and throws an explosion I swear, more times than Chris' Campaign. Jake was the surprisingly stronger campaign, which isn't saying much, but thanks to its love story. Chris' was also a strong potential, but had less times to flesh out the story and instead focus on the action. Ada's campaign... sucked, and the story was just so one note that it got really stale real quick. The worst aspect of this story however was how they tried to connect everyone's story together, which on paper sounds really sick, but ends up with many segments of corny one-liners, standing still watching someone else have fun, or terrible, terrible writing moments that just makes me face palm more than take seriously.

Characters
While Resident Evil never had SUPER fleshed out characters, they always had more interesting characters. RE6 decides that the best way to flesh out a character is to force them to have terrible one liners, especially leon and jake oh my GOD man. They still do hold interest, as like said before, their relations between one another were interesting, and whlie I still complained about the storyline interconnecting was its biggest fault, it was still kinda cool to see them bump into each other and how they contributed... even if it lead to some fights just having you watch them have fun. Jake and Sherry's love story was the most interesting storyline, with Leon and Helena's was the 2nd most interesting. Chris' and his partner was probably the least interesting, and Ada... tried. I do think Jake trying to act the most badass in front of everyone was a bit corny, but I did like his development at the end... but man it sucks how much Leon's campaign storywise and gameplay wise was disappointing, even if they made it to appeal to horror fans... just to make it more action than the rest of the campaigns.

Gameplay
RE6's magnum opus... is super conflicted. Quite honestly the combat and core gameplay they made was pretty good, and was easily the most engaging of the RE games... if only they made the gameplay around a good game. RE6's gameplay is what happens when you have a good system, and do all the wrong things to make that system shine. They have a RE core gameplay with mechanics that focus around dodges, dive rolls, leaping around, and a melee system that encourages stuns into a almost wrestling game? Now instead of having that shine, they instead force you to fight goons with guns, annoying big monsters, and barely give you enough ammo to even flop around and experiment with the system they made. Or better yet, segments of just walking around, watching your 500th explosion, quick time event to just climb a rope? I feel like if they took this exact same combat system and made it around a better game, it would be a different tune. They instead shoved it into a game that didn't know what it wanted to be, action? Horror? RE3 fan? stealth? ♥♥♥♥ it lets have EVERYTHING. The one thing that does save this game is how much fun it is for COOP, which is where this game shines the brightest. I can't fatham playing this game by yourself and having the best time of your life. Compared to RE5's more streamlined, but still fun coop, RE6's coop tends to throw everything at the wall and hope you both enjoy it. While some segments are pretty fun, overall they get stale REAL fast, and especially Ada's campaign which had the most obviously tacked on coop to the point where the partner doesn't even seem to exist, yeah its a mixed bag.

Music
Generic, Generic, Generic. They really tried to replicate the "hollywood feel" a bit too much, and most songs in this ost was just really forgettable.

Last Positives/ Nitpicks
- a ♥♥♥♥ ton of skill points, which were worthless as we played no mercy.
- not the best pc port, but not the worst.
- The Inventory system sucks balls, and the last of coop partner trading and upgrading does hurt a ton on working together and such.

Conclusion
Even though I dog on this game, I still do think its worth a try... on coop only. Solo you might as well play any of the other RE games, as not only will you have a more enjoyable experience, but actually play a game that knows what tf it wants to be. I am glad this was when capcom realized to turn a complete 180 with the direction they were going and finally steer towards Survival Horror again, as I truly believe if they kept going this route, we would be singing a different tune about the RE franchise compared to how we talk about it today.

Resident Evil 6, as the name suggests, is the sixth episode of the main RE saga. It takes place after the events that characterized the previous episodes and continues on the path of the transition from a traditional slow paced survival horror to a fast paced action game.
The game is set in different locations and covers, depending the character you choose, a quite short temporal timeline. Continuing the tradition of the fifth episode, in RE 6 you will tag with another character all along your adventure.
The game expands the concept introduced the first time with the original RE2 where you have to play all the characters stories to have a comprehensive view on the plot.
With a roster of 4 playable main characters (Leon, Chris, Jake and Ada) and, for each character the possibility of selecting the main character or the teammate (the only exception is Ada who is a solo campaign), you will play four different histories to play through the full game.
The four characters are not just a different point of view of the same thing but, in RE6, they mean playing different timelines, different stories and different areas that make each run enjoyable and full of “ah-ha” moments, especially if we already have played with another character another story.
There is a preferential order to play the stories, but I have found that plots are sufficiently well crafted that can be played in whatever order with good satisfaction. The only exception is Ada one, which is better to play at the end even if not mandatory (if you play it first it won't ruin your game).
From a gameplay point of view RE6 is a third-person shooter. You will therefore face hordes of enemies and you will have to kill without too much hesitation. Compared to RE5, battles are more matures and the game is now worth of playing. The plot is also logical for an action shooter which gives you a context where the action approach is also justified and not just a gameplay choice.
Scenario is also better organized and environmental killings become something necessary and not just a fancy different way of get rid of enemies.
Each character has a slightly different set of moves which leads to a different combat experience, especially at higher difficulty level. 
An interesting element is the ability slot. During each run we will collect some ability points that can be used to unlock special abilities like, increased damages, better resistance, more ammunitions, etc. Abilities, once unlocked, are available for all the characters of all story lines, which means that we benefit from the results of our previous run. Abilities become key at higher difficulty level where a hit can easily end your game.
From a general perspective RE6 is a good game that improves the limitations of RE5 and reunites 7 characters in the same game. Combat is nice and the pace is good.
Characters' differences in term of gameplay and attitudes are unfortunately not so marked to make the difference. You can easily use the same tactical approach with all the characters with good results. It would have been nice to have more marked differences to have four different experiences.
Plot is also very minimal. I think that Capcom could have worked a little better in developing the story, creating more intrigue and giving more details to the player as done in previous episodes.
In summary I think that RE6 can be recommended to all players that are willing to play another RE game. The game fits also those who do not know the series but are just looking for a fast paced, with a good amount of environmental destruction, action game.
Final note: for those who remember the coin op House Of The Dead, you will find in some scenes some potential references to that game.

Resident Evil 6 is the video game equivalent of a summer blockbuster: it’s loud, it’s flashy, and it occasionally makes you wonder if the writers were high on caffeine and nostalgia. It’s like they took every action movie trope, threw it in a blender, and added a dash of zombies for flavor.

First off, the game has more plot twists than a daytime soap opera. There are so many storylines and characters, it feels like a family reunion where everyone’s a secret agent or has a dark past. One minute you’re playing as Leon Kennedy, the hair gel poster boy, and the next you’re Chris Redfield, whose biceps have biceps.

The combat is a mixed bag of awesome and awkward. Shooting zombies is satisfying, but the melee moves are so over-the-top, you half expect to see WWE logos. I once roundhouse-kicked a zombie so hard it flew into the next room. Take that, undead scum!

The quick-time events are a thing of nightmares. One moment you’re running from a giant monster, and the next you’re mashing buttons like your life depends on it—which it kind of does. Miss one prompt, and you’re treated to a death scene that’s both gruesome and slightly comical.

Speaking of monsters, the enemies in this game are ridiculous. There are zombies, sure, but also mutant Jell-O molds, zombie T-Rexes, and whatever that thing with all the eyeballs is supposed to be. It’s like the developers had a contest to see who could come up with the weirdest creature.

Co-op mode is where the game shines and/or falls apart, depending on your partner. Playing with a friend can turn the most frustrating moments into laugh riots. Trying to coordinate with an AI partner, however, is like herding cats. They’ll either save your butt or stand there while you get mauled. Thanks for nothing, AI.

The graphics are a highlight, even if the characters’ hair physics occasionally defy the laws of nature. The environments are beautifully rendered, from creepy, foggy graveyards to exploding aircraft carriers. It’s a visual feast for the eyes, provided you can see past the horde of zombies trying to eat your face.

Despite its flaws, Resident Evil 6 has a certain charm. It’s like that cheesy action movie you can’t help but love, even though you know it’s ridiculous. It’s a rollercoaster of adrenaline, absurdity, and a lot of “WTF” moments.

So, if you’re looking for a game that’s part horror, part action, and all kinds of crazy, give Resident Evil 6 a shot. Just remember to bring a friend, a sense of humor, and a lot of patience for those quick-time events. Happy zombie hunting!
