Visually, Resident Evil 6 impresses with its detailed environments and character models. The game's graphics showcase a high level of polish, capturing the eerie atmosphere of various global settings ravaged by bioterrorism and viral outbreaks. From urban streets to decaying interiors, each location is meticulously crafted to immerse players in a world on the brink of catastrophe.

Gameplay in Resident Evil 6 introduces a mix of over-the-top action sequences and survival horror elements. Players can choose between multiple protagonists, each with their own storyline and gameplay mechanics. While this diversity offers replayability, the execution often feels disjointed, with gameplay styles ranging from intense shootouts to tense encounters with grotesque mutations.

One of the game's notable features is its emphasis on cooperative gameplay, allowing players to team up with friends or AI-controlled partners in split-screen or online modes. Cooperative play adds depth to combat strategies and encourages teamwork, which can be rewarding when navigating through chaotic encounters and solving puzzles together.

However, where Resident Evil 6 falters is in its narrative coherence and pacing. The storylines of different protagonists intersect in convoluted ways, sometimes at the expense of character development and plot cohesion. The narrative lacks the psychological tension and suspenseful pacing that defined earlier Resident Evil titles, opting instead for bombastic set pieces and cinematic spectacle.

Sound design in Resident Evil 6 is competent, with atmospheric sound effects and a moody soundtrack that enhance the game's horror elements. Voice acting is generally solid, although some dialogue exchanges can feel melodramatic or clichéd, detracting from the immersion.

In conclusion, Resident Evil 6 represents a departure from the series' survival horror roots, aiming to appeal to a broader audience with its action-packed gameplay and cooperative features. While it boasts impressive visuals and moments of adrenaline-pumping excitement, the game's narrative inconsistencies and departure from traditional Resident Evil elements may disappoint longtime fans seeking a more cohesive and atmospheric horror experience. For players open to a more action-driven approach to survival horror, Resident Evil 6 offers an ambitious yet uneven entry in the iconic franchise.

I only played through this to fulfill my desire of getting through all the mainline games... idk why I did it. So here's the pros and cons if you're wondering about this horrible experience.
Pros: 
- I like how the stories intertwine. 
- Ada's campaign was decent (Not as good as 1-5 but decent nonetheless). 
- The finishers were amazing and I hope they make a comeback. 
- Sneaking around the discount Mr X in the snow in Jake's campaign was fun.
- Chris holds up a whole ass hydraulic door, amazing.

Cons: 
- The plot was horrible, like bad soap opera horrible and it drags on for far too long.
- The movement had you staggering or falling over from losing a block of health. 
- The QTE's omg the QTE's they just stack one QTE on top of the other over and over again, granted this was made during the time where devs thought QTE's were a beautiful thing, but this has the worst QTE's in both amount and application I've ever seen in a game.
- The boss fights drag on and on. I get the meme that RE bosses don't die, but this is just stupid. There's a whole chapter dedicated to fighting a boss and it goes on for almost an hour.
- This game throws a lot of enemies at you, but barely any ammo. Top this with the fact that a lot of enemies are bullet sponges and the bosses take everything you have and then some. Luckily you can run past most encounters with enemies.
- The levels are just a series of corridors or narrow paths, there are almost no open spaces save for a handful.

TL;DR The story is bad, the level design is bad, aggressive QTE's, the encounter designs are bad, the bosses are bad, the staggering and movement isn't very good, Ada's campaign is a small silver lining, the finishers are beautiful, the intertwining stories are neat, and one part of Jake's campaign is good. Unless you're forcing yourself into doing all the mainline RE games, do not bother with 6.

Edit: I went through it on co-op and it was still awful, not as awful as single player, but everything that is wrong with the game is still present.
EditEdit: Got forced through it with another friend because he really badly wanted to try it but in co-op only, it was still a horrible experience, any remake of this even if it was given the re3 remake treatment would be an improvement.

Resident Evil 6 is a bad game. To say it is "so bad it's good" would be mostly inaccurate. It can be hilariously bad sometimes, but most of the time it is just boring and frustrating.

Compared to RE 5, a game I would say is "so bad it's good", UI, UX, combat, writing (somehow), art direction (somehow), inventory management, item economy, progression, enemy design, and the controls especially are all massive downgrades. Leon's campaign is the only one with zombies (Ada's has some too, but they were not the primary enemy). They were somewhat fun to fight because you could easily suplex them, but they weren't particularly challenging or engaging. Unfortunately, every other campaign has enemies known as "J'avo". Many of them have machine guns that stagger the player on hit, causing the player to be stunlocked if they are shot even once. Because crate and enemy drops are randomized, I often found myself with little ammo. Skill points were vastly more common than ammo in my experience. The issue here is that I did not need skill points, because by the end of the first campaign I had all of the perks I wanted. What I did need is ammo, because without it I had to engage the J'avo in melee combat. Doing so was excruciating because of the aforementioned machine gunners, who would often come back to life after death to extend the duration of the tedious and miserable game that is Resident Evil 6. 

The UX changes with each character, which is an interesting idea, except for the fact that the UX for the settings menu also changes, which led to some needless confusion. 
Inventory space is another minor annoyance. The player has limited inventory space, though how much you have isn't communicated. I also found the inventory annoying to navigate, but it wasn't too much of an issue.

To RE 6's credit, the game does a good job of making the second player feel involved, with the exception of Ada's campaign, where I had to wait for player 1 in order to do anything that didn't involve shooting. I understand not being in the cutscenes, but waiting around was pretty boring.

The cutscenes are funny and nonsensical at the very least, but my friends who didn't play the game found them just as funny as I did, so you might as well just watch them on youtube. 

One issue that I had with the game that may not bother other people as much was the "fan service" that the second player is subjected to. I don't mind sexy characters in media, but here it just felt gross and exploitative.

I have many other issues with the game, but I am sure that another review has covered them sufficiently. 
If you are looking something "so bad it's good" just play Resident Evil 5. RE 6 isn't worth the money. At least in RE 5 you can punch boulders.

Do not play this game if you have even a shred of self respect. It's a terrible game period. It has so many flaws, and was so close to being average but every design decision holds it back. The following is a loosely structured review as I ramble my thoughts about all the negative aspects of the game (which is most of the game).

STORY
The story is boring and predictable. It would be better if you didn't have to play four different campaigns rehashing the same story four times but the game is too long, and too repetitive. Otherwise the story is serviceable.

UI
The UI was designed by someone who has never seen a video game before, or probably any piece of graphic design. It tried so hard to be modern and cool but in doing so obfuscated everything that mattered and made things more tedious. Want to switch weapons? (of which the game gives you an absurd amount), well you have to scroll through a wheel of weapons until you get to the right one unlike the previous game where you decide the slot and that's it.  The menu radial wheel is also obnoxious to use, having to rotate through it to find the settings or exit button etc. The health system being changed from the old system of health states to health bars was also strange, and kind of complicates this mechanic just for the sake of adding more.

ENEMY DESIGN
Enemies lack uniqueness or interesting variety. It's just mostly the same thing across all four campaigns. Jake and Sherry's even copied enemy designs from Revelations. There isn't much to say here, though some boss designs were semi interesting. 

GAMEPLAY
You play through four different campaigns with 8 different characters all rehashing the same story and areas with a decent amount of overlap. This is absurd. It is too long, and results in chapters feeling like they drag on. It gets boring fairly quickly which isn't helped by the fact that after you finish the first campaign, you've basically played half of all of the other campaigns. I am overestimating this but the issue is that gameplay feels very samey. 

They should have cut the characters in half at minimum, and made one campaign. 

Level design is also terrible, they give you a GPS system so you can find your way around. That is indicative of poor design. The actual layout and structure itself is just bad also.

COMBAT
Guns have no real impact. There is no recoil, there is no staggers. You shoot an enemy in the head with a pistol 14 times until they die and fall over. They don't stagger backwards, their heads don't pop. Nothing gives you positive feedback except them just falling over. This issue is most prevalent with the shotgun. Look at 4 and 5, where a shotgun blast sends an enemy flying backwards. In 6, they just keep walking forwards like nothing ever happened. 

Weapons in this game just have no significance or impact. They fill your inventory with 15 different weapons and ammo types, and with nothing feeling special the gameplay is reduced to shoot enemy until you run out of ammo, swap weapon, shoot enemy and repeat. There is no reason to use any one weapon over another. The Elephant Killer weapon (traditionally strong weapon that in an earlier entry, would one shot enemies and massively damage stronger enemies) does not really do so, so there is no reason to conserve ammo and use it accordingly. Though part of that may be because of the total lack of visual feedback. 

This extends into melee combat, which is kind of overpowered, or at least would be if not for the obnoxious stamina system that adds no value. You can punch any enemy to death with ease and Capcoms way of balancing this is making it so you tire out after about 3 hits, slowing you down massively. This is just annoying. It adds no value and is just there because they realised they screwed up with how strong they made punching people. 

One thing I will give them credit for is the slide/dodge system which is interesting and adds a layer to combat, so that is definitely an improvement from previous games.

SUMMARY
Resident Evil 6 is a significant downgrade from 5 and Revelations in almost every way possible. They tried to be too different to play into the action focus instead of survival horror. And they didn't know what they were doing. They didn't realise they still needed to make a good, fun game. It's too long and nothing has any impact. Go play 5 if you want coop, or Revelations if you want a pre RE7 game without tank controls and more modern mechanics. It's so close to being a mid game, but it falls short.

[h1] Resident Evil 6 – The Last Action RE Game [/h1]

After completing Resident Evil 5 last October, here I am again reviewing the next numbered Resident Evil title. This part is widely considered to be the weakest Resident Evil game, even though this was Capcom’s largest production. This will also turn out to be the last action third person shooter RE game, after switching back to survival horror in Resident Evil 7, but this time in first person.


There are several changes and innovations in this game, but its core and formula are pretty much that of previous two parts – RE4 and RE5. For the first time ever, there are 4 campaigns to play in total, which makes this title the longest Resident Evil game. The 4 main characters are Leon Kennedy, Chris Redfield, Jake Muller and Ada Wong. Of course, every campaign can be played in co-op mode, which I did, and so along with our main characters there’s a choice of playing their partners – Helena Harper, Piers Nivans and Sherry Birkin, respectively. Ada’s part was meant to be played solo, but there’s also an option to play co-op with the unnamed agent. She won’t have any interactions with him and will act as if he isn’t there.

I can understand the hate that came from Resident Evil fans when this got released – but as one YouTube reviewer of RE games (AvalancheReviews) said, those same fans are the reason for the way Resident Evil 6 turned out to be. Capcom saw immense success in Resident Evil 4, therefore they wanted to please their fans and thus RE5 and RE6 were created. Of course, gradually there was more and more action involved, which completely abolished the survival horror aspect of the game. This is and always will be a con for me for all three of these games, as I am a huge fan of the early RE games. [b]BUT[/b], even with this in mind I would say that Resident Evil 6 is a good game.

Even though the game is pretty long, especially for a RE title, every campaign had its “style”. Leon’s campaign is reminiscent of RE2 and RE4, with somewhat slower pace  and after a long time we have a zombie invasion, like the one that happened in Racoon City. Chris’ campaign is more shooting-oriented and more brutal, which is logical especially if you take RE5 in consideration. When playing Jake’s campaign, you are able to use his physical strength for some powerful melee attacks while also being able to jump over long gaps which other characters couldn’t do. And finally, in Ada’s campaign you will be using a more stealthy approach, which is also reminiscent of Separate Ways from RE4.

The main con for me was that I need 22 hours to complete the game. After the first two campaigns I felt full, and when I realized that it’s only the first half, I started to feel tired. It’s always a double-edged sword when making such long games, especially for a RE title. It can really get repetitive and you just want to finish it as soon as possible. The other flaw is, as I already mentioned, the absence of survival horror and no presence of scare factor whatsoever.

Graphics - this title was the newest one, released 3 years after the previous part and obviously it’s the best-looking one. The cutscenes are as good as in RE5, only more polished.

Storywise, the game reconnects with Racoon City disaster from original RE2 and reconnects the individuals from different RE titles. Sadly some of the characters won’t be seen again, the same was done with Sheva from RE5. Personally I really liked the character of Piers Nivans, and playing him was really cool.

And here we are at the end; Resident Evil 6 is a good game, if you are a die-hard fan of old RE titles, you may not like this one too much, but if you played previous two parts, you’re going to be alright. If you like third-person shooter and enjoyed RE4 and RE5, you are in the right place – play this game. If you have a friend for co-op, even better, because it’s so much fun to play together with someone.

Tier list update until I finish all the Resident Evil titles (the main titles):
RE2 (1998) > RE4 > RE5 > RE (1996) > RE3 (1999) > RE6 > RE: Code Veronica > RE0

[b]Yo, fellow survivors! Strap in and get ready for a wild ride through the apocalypse with Resident Evil 6, a game that's as action-packed as it is cheesy. Let's break it down and see if this zombie-slaying extravaganza is worth your time.

First things first, let's talk about the gameplay. It's like a buffet of destruction, with three different campaigns to sink your teeth into. Whether you're blasting zombies as Leon Kennedy, kicking ass as Chris Redfield, or doing ninja moves as Ada Wong, there's something here for everyone. And let me tell ya, the action is as fast and furious as Vin Diesel on a caffeine bender.

But it ain't all sunshine and rainbows, my dudes. Resident Evil 6 is about as over-the-top as a Hollywood blockbuster, with more explosions than a Michael Bay movie and more melodrama than a soap opera. And let me tell ya, the story is about as coherent as my grandma after one too many glasses of wine. But hey, when you're mowing down zombies with a rocket launcher, who cares about plot holes, am I right?

Now, let's talk about the graphics. They're like a double-edged sword, my dudes. On one hand, you got some pretty sweet visuals that'll make you feel like you're right in the middle of a zombie apocalypse. On the other hand, you got some wonky animations and character models that'll make you wonder if the developers ran out of budget halfway through.

But the real star of the show is the co-op. Whether you're teaming up with your buddies online or going old-school with split-screen, there's nothing quite like taking down hordes of zombies with your best buds by your side. And let me tell ya, the camaraderie that comes from surviving the apocalypse together is something special.

Now, I gotta keep it real with you, Resident Evil 6 ain't perfect. The controls can be about as clunky as a three-legged horse, and the QTEs will make you wanna throw your controller out the window. But hey, when you're knee-deep in zombie guts and saving the world from certain doom, those issues seem minor in comparison.

So, if you're looking for a game that's equal parts cheesy action and zombie-slaying goodness, then Resident Evil 6 is the game for you. Grab your weapons, grab your buddies, and get ready for a wild ride through the apocalypse. Just don't forget to bring plenty of snacks and ammo, 'cause you're gonna need 'em both.[/b]

A big, clumsy mixed bag of an experience. It's clear that Capcom were shooting for the stars with this one and I guess in some ways they succeeded. The game is relentless, always moving forward and mixing things up. The issue is that what it does to give that variety varies.

Leon's campaign is the strongest, but it doesn't put its best foot forward. The school is a dull slog, and the underground segment isn't much better. However, the destruction of Tall Oaks and the Chinese city is well done, and moving through the destruction has a certain kind of fun to it. It's big and flashy, and there are segments that drag, but I really enjoyed the emphasis on both disaster and combat this one had.

Chris's campaign is okay, mainly taking place in China. Like Leon's campaign, there's a lot of novelty in seeing the apocalyptic scenario unfold right in front of you, and the perspective of special forces containing it is cool in that distinctly 2010s way. It's also fairly generic, ESPECIALLY given the time period it came out. I think this one peters out a bit towards the end but at the very least the final boss is a really neat design.

Jake's scenario is by far the worst in the game, throwing in every 2010s action trope it can think of; almost every chapter has a vehicle segments; sometimes these are fun, more often than not they suck due to the ease by which you can fail them. The Ustanak, a sort of Nemesis type character, is kind of a lame villain, with him just teleporting to wherever the game demands he be. RE has a history of enemies with ludicrous levels of resilience, and this guy is probably the dumbest of them all. While the writing in the game in general is B movie junk, the writing here is especially egregious; Jake is such a try hard edge lord that he's comical in all the wrong ways. Meanwhile, Sherry is treated as eye candy half the time, and the fact that they would do that when her only previous appearance is as a kid in 2 is more than a little creepy. The romance between them is about as forced as it gets considering just how dumb the script is, and this has the honor of having possibly the most cringe credits song I've ever heard. 

The final campaign is a bit shorter than the others, and supposedly sheds some light on the plot. All it actually does is show just how dumb the story really is, with some revelations that feel like they were written by a 13 year old boy whose only idea of romance is offering a dead rat to your crush as a form of tribute. There's a bit more emphasis on sneaking around, but you're largely retreading similar ground as the other campaigns.

This is a gigantic, dumb mess of a title, a very far cry from what the series has been before or since. For every cool part (and there are definitely some enjoyable moments of spectacle in just how destructive things can get) there are segments that are a total slog. The writing is insultingly bad across the board, and trying to follow the increasingly convoluted series of events is a waste of time. But the combat is perhaps the most fluid in the entire series, making this game's Mercenary mode quite fun, and it's tough not to smile like a dumb kid at just how ridiculous the destruction and spectacle can get.

This game is very much of itself. If you're in the mood for what it's selling, it hits the spot. It gets the series completely wrong, but as a biohorror themed blockbuster that puts spectacle and flashiness above all else, there is fun to be had.

If, by any chance, you find yourself wanting to play this game, don’t. Just don’t. Turn around, leave, don’t look back. I think this was hands down one of the single most annoying games I’ve ever completed. Why you may ask. Where do I even begin?!

The gameplay is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I’ve played a lot of games. I’ve played a lot of “older” games that were released years ago, so I think I have a good frame of reference of what I can and cannot expect from a game that came out in 2012. This game has aged so spectacularly badly that I am convinced it can’t even have been fun on initial release.

The inventory management is annoying with super unbalanced drops. You end up picking up a lot of items like grenades that are really uncomfortable to use, so they just end up taking up inventory space. The amount of times I ended up throwing those away just so I could pick up healing items is beyond count. As I said the drops are very unbalanced so you will run out of ammo for some of your weapons and just not ever see any again for ages. And it’s not like there are vendors where you can buy more.

At the end of each level, you can get some perks. They feel super pointless because they don’t do much to begin with and there are so many, there is no way to level all of those up. You would have to replay the game a ridiculous amount of time to put a somewhat useful amount of points into any of those which will not happen because this game has zero replay appeal.

There are many games that like to give you cinematic cutscenes, or rather those bits where you, say, enter an area and it pans around to show you everything for a few seconds. I’m pretty sure we’ve all seen this in other games, right? So, RE6 does this too. It takes control from you and points the camera wherever. The only problem is, contrary to other games, things keep going here. So, you might be in the middle of a fight, you are getting attacked and the game decides that you need to see that corner over there. Congratulations, you are now dead. This happened so many times throughout the game, it made me legitimately angry. Oh, and did I mention that you will get insta-killed numerous times just because you were standing in the wrong spot? No indication, no time to react, nothing. You stand somewhere, out of nowhere a car flips, a wall crumbles, etc., and poof you are dead. If this would happen once, okay, whatever. But it was a constant occurrence and, as I said, you couldn’t do anything about it. There were no giveaways that a spot might be dangerous to stand in, and you had zero chance to dodge, or even to take damage and survive instead of dying in any of those situations.

At several points in the game, you get levels where you have to use vehicles/escape on vehicles/run away. All of those were so bad I wanted to tear my hair out. Again, the random camera pans that are no help whatsoever coupled with even worse controls than you get in a regular level make these bits nigh on unplayable. Normally I would assume that I am the problem here, that I’m just not good at something. However, I played this in co-op (more on that in a moment) and the person I played with had the exact same issues I’ve discussed so far. In fact, when I discussed the game with other people, they all reported the same things.

Let’s talk about the co-op stuff a bit. To be honest, the only reason I even completed RE6 is because I was playing it with a friend. Otherwise, I would have binned it off at some point along the way. First of all, the game would occasionally kick you out but keep running. So, you are in a mission but somehow the online part disconnects. We’ve had that happen and neither one of us realized that we weren’t in the level together anymore, because as I said, the game continues just fine. Seriously, what the ♥♥♥♥?

At several points on different levels, you have to split up with each person having to do different things. However, sometimes one person literally only needs to stand about and wait, while the other, say, opens a door. Sometimes both need to do something. The game gives you literally no indication of which of these options it might be. So many times, it was completely unclear what you were supposed to do. And I don’t mean this in a “it was a puzzle, you had to think about it for a bit” kind of way. Just ♥♥♥♥ game design, nothing else. Oh, and mind you, certain bits are unplayable if the person who hosts the game plays a certain character. The game just breaks then. We spent way too much time trying to figure out what we were doing wrong until a Google search revealed that it was not us that was the problem, it was the game.

Let’s talk about the thing that absolutely takes the cake though. I guess this involves a few spoilers, so you have been warned. [spoiler] So, in this game, there are different story lines that converge at the end. These storylines take place simultaneously. You play the different parts of the story, always two main characters you and a friend will take control of. The first story was okay. Leon and Helena go through their stuff just fine. It’s not the best thing I’ve ever played by a long shot, but it was alright. It was all downhill from there on out. While we got some semblance of story there, the next bit is mainly just mindless shooting with the absolute barest minimum of even trying to add a story in there. But you know what, that’s fine. Whatever. And then you make it to the final bit with Ada. Let me reiterate. Everything else so far had been designed for two players. TWO. That bit was not. Sure, you can play with two people, but that definitely was meant to be single-player. While the other storylines all get two proper characters, that one has Ada and disposable soldier #584. Calling the second player in that an afterthought is even giving them too much credit. The person who is not playing Ada can but tag along. Literally, you can’t even do most of the things, like opening certain stuff or completing objectives. When Ada goes somewhere you might literally just get transported there. I just don’t understand why. The entire thing clearly was meant to be played with two people, so why on earth would you decide to do the final bit like that?[/spoiler]

All in all, there was pretty much nothing I liked about this game. It started out decently enough but turned to ♥♥♥♥ very quickly with just all aspects of it making you miserable. Seriously, just don’t play it.

[h1]Resident Evil 6: A Mixed Bag of Survival Horror and Action[/h1]

Resident Evil 6 is a game that elicits a range of emotions. As a longtime fan of the series, I approached it with both excitement and trepidation, unsure of what to expect after the divisive reception of its predecessor. What I found was a game that attempts to cater to a wide audience with varying degrees of success.

First and foremost, Resident Evil 6 is an action-packed thrill ride. The game is filled to the brim with intense set pieces, explosive action sequences, and a variety of gameplay styles that keep you on your toes. From shooting hordes of zombies in the streets of Tall Oaks to engaging in high-octane boss battles, there's no shortage of adrenaline-pumping moments.

However, where Resident Evil 6 falters is in its departure from the series' survival horror roots. While previous titles instilled a sense of dread and tension with limited resources and strategic gameplay, this installment often feels more like a third-person shooter than a survival horror game. The abundance of ammo and health items, along with the emphasis on action over atmosphere, may leave some longtime fans feeling disappointed.

It's worth noting that there is nothing quite like Resident Evil 4, which successfully blended action and survival horror elements to create a truly unforgettable experience. Resident Evil 6, while ambitious in its scope, struggles to capture the same magic.

That said, the game does have its strengths. The story is ambitious, intertwining multiple narratives that converge in unexpected ways. Playing through the perspectives of different characters, each with their own motivations and backstories, adds depth to the overall experience. The production values are top-notch, with impressive graphics and sound design that immerse you in the chaotic world of Resident Evil.

The co-op multiplayer deserves special mention, as it adds a new layer of enjoyment to the game. Joining forces with a friend to take on the horrors of Resident Evil is undeniably fun, and the game is designed to accommodate both solo and cooperative play seamlessly.

Ultimately, Resident Evil 6 is a game of contrasts. It's a rollercoaster of action and excitement, but at the cost of sacrificing some of the series' signature survival horror elements. For fans who enjoy intense, fast-paced gameplay and don't mind a departure from tradition, Resident Evil 6 offers plenty of entertainment. However, those seeking a return to the franchise's roots may find themselves longing for the tense atmosphere and strategic gameplay of earlier titles.

DISCLAIMER: All Campaigns were completed on No Hope difficulty, which I find provides a different experience than playing on lower difficulties.

I can only recommend this game for people who plan on playing it co-op with a partner. Otherwise, to be frank, I do not believe the single-player experience is worth it at all. I'm not just talking about A.I problems; i'm talking about overall enjoyment of this product. 

Let's get one thing out of the way: Resident Evil 6 is perhaps one of the dumbest RE games in terms of narrative and writing and that's saying something given the track record of the series. This is something you have to come to terms with very early on. It is important to mention because the narrative is an important aspect of the game. Unfortunately, it is simply not up to par to any standard that can be deemed good. Perhaps it is through this terrible narrative that is split across four different campaigns that the game shines in co-op though. I would argue that the game would not have been entertaining to go through with my co-op partner if the story was good or straight-forward. The shameless fan-service, corny one-liners, forced romance and disjointed out-of-character moments make this game's story hilarious in an unexpected manner. Think of it as deliberately watching a bad movie with a partner just to make fun of it.

The great surprise here is how the combat system of the game has aged tremendously well. The thing that stands out the most to me is the lack of regenerating health on No Hope difficulty. Not only does that challenge force you to consider when to use healing items, but it also adds a feeling of satisfaction when you complete a chapter without using a single healing item. Instead, it is your stamina that regenerates throughout the game. Your stamina also depletes fairly quickly. This allows the player to think about when to engage in melee combat versus when to use your gun. While the different campaigns are very similar, there are small but distinct differences that make each one play different from one another gameplay-wise. This can come in the form of what weapons each character has access to or the subtle differences in melee combat. They're definitely marginal, but they're different enough to make each campaign feel like a fairly unique experience.

While the narrative is incredibly weak, the action set-pieces are not. There are a lot of varied opinions about which campaign is the best. Personally, I find that Chris Redfield's campaign is superior because it adheres to the principles of an action game, which is what Resident Evil 6 ultimately excels at. There are so many action-packed moments that'll leave you sitting straight. The overabundant usage of sudden quick-time events will make sure of that. When the great combat mixes with the entertaining action set-pieces and the terrible narrative, you are left with a sporadic mess of a game that is horrible to experience alone, but incredible to play with a co-op partner. I highly suggest playing on No Hope difficulty as it will leave you feeling miserable, happy, engaged and frustrated at different intervals. Going through these emotions together with a partner is what made this experience so special to me. 

If I was forced to summarize everything I mentioned here, I would write that Resident Evil 6 is a game that is shockingly ahead of its time in certain aspects such as combat, but incredibly behind in others such as narrative design. There is a lot to love here, but a lot to hate; doing so with a co-op partner will turn that hate into an enjoyable laughing session. So again, only buy this game if you have someone to play with. You will not regret it if you enjoy action-adventure games.

Let's kick things off with Resident Evil 6 – now, before we dive in, let's make one thing crystal clear: this isn't your grandpa's survival horror. Nope, this is a full-throttle, adrenaline-pumping third-person shooter extravaganza, packed with zombies, monsters, and more bio-weapons than you can shake a stick at. And hey, I get it – if you're a fan of the classics, this might not feel like a trip down memory lane.

But let's give credit where it's due. RE6 throws some surprises our way, like the "shoot-while-flat-on-your-back" move – seriously, who doesn't love that bit of innovation? And let's not overlook the satisfaction of throwing some proper melee punches instead of just flailing around with a knife like a mime gone mad.

Sure, there are some quirks to adjust to. Like waiting for zombies to awkwardly shuffle into range before you can take 'em down, or dealing with those pesky assault rifle-wielding undead (seriously, aim lower, guys). And don't even get me started on the J'Avo – these aren't your average zombies; they're like zombies on steroids, causing chaos left and right.

Now, if you're a die-hard purist, you might raise an eyebrow at the addition of Wesker's son, Jake. I get it, it sounds a bit like a soap opera twist. But let's face it – the Resident Evil series has always been a little out there. And can we just appreciate the delightfully cheesy dialogue and voice acting? It's part of the charm!

But here's the thing – RE6 isn't afraid to mix things up. You want puzzles? They've got 'em. And okay, maybe they hold your hand through them a bit like you're a kid learning to tie your shoes, but hey, just turn off the HUD and immerse yourself in the experience.

To all you die-hard RE fans clinging to your original copies like they're relics – I hear you. Change can be tough. But let me drop some truth bombs: Resident Evil ain't what it used to be. It's evolved, for better or for worse. If you're longing for the days of pure survival horror, you won't find 'em here. And if you're hoping for a blast from the past, well, keep on hoping.

But if you're in the mood for a top-tier third-person shooter with a side of horror, a sprinkle of gore, and enough action to get your heart pounding faster than a cheetah on caffeine, then my friend, Resident Evil 6 might just be your ticket to gaming paradise.

My experience with Resident Evil 6 largely leans positive. However there's one Achilles Heel that will either make or break RE6 for you. How much content there is on offer here in terms of the story. 

Resident Evil 6 can either be a bloated mess or a welcomed jam packed game depending on what you're looking for. Resident Evil 6 is longer than any RE game prior to it has been with 4 campaigns, all of which being at least 5 hours. I'm on the fence with my stance as I largely enjoyed the game as a whole, but after awhile this game was tiring to play for me due to the game not offering enough variety and being non-stop action 24-7, some things such as in Jake's campaign you have to climb up an icy hill and if you get shot and fall on the ice you slide all the way down hill, and for me the first 2 and a half chapters of Ada's campaign was miserable. But I did greatly enjoy the combat of RE6, I found that by and large gunplay felt really good and you can do some cool stuff in this game, more than in any RE game before it. Although I did say (and stand by) that RE6 can be very tiring in part to its non-stop action, I can't deny there are some really fun and memorable set-pieces such as Chris and Piers chasing Ada on the free-way, or getting to pilot the helicopter as Ada. There are moments where certain characters from one campaign cross over with another and you have to play the same segments over again, which I can see why someone might find that frustrating, but for me since I already knew what to do replaying those wasn't the worst since I could complete them much more easily.

Another element in the room I have to address is Resident Evil 6's huge focus on action and basically abandoning its survival horror roots almost entirely. This is always going to come down to a matter of opinion, but as somebody who's been playing all the RE games in a row and has gotten so see how this series evolved overtime in a post RE7 world, I personally don't mind. I completely understand why many were miffed by the drastic change in direction at the time seeing as RE4 and even (to a much lesser degree) RE5 could still be considered survival horror because even if they were more focused on action there was a nice balance of tense atmosphere and resource management. In RE6 resource managment is practically non-existent and it's just crazy action all the time. Again, I don't really mind this because RE6 is still (mostly) fun to play and does what it set out to do really well. I'll also argue this game was more tense for me at points than RE5 was in its entirety such as when Sherry and Jake have to hide from that monster that chases them throughout the campaign. 

To be completely honest, Resident Evil 6 is not even close to being a favorite RE game for me, it's closer to the bottom of the totem pole in terms of RE greatness but having said that I still had a mostly good time with RE6. There were points where I got frustrated with the game but I can't really say I was ever bored. I personally think there are worse RE games such as Code Veronica and RE0. If you're willing to look past the drastic change in direction, and judge RE6 as an action third person shooter I think there's a good time to be had here. The game is really cheap when it goes on sale too so I'd say at least give it a try. At the very least you can play this game co-op with a buddy so that's gotta count for something right?

Resident Evil 6 is often cited as the weakest mainline entry in the series, and the PC port only reinforces that reputation. To begin with, the game was already poorly received because Capcom had largely lost sight of what defined Resident Evil. It no longer felt like a survival horror experience. At the time, Call of Duty and Battlefield were in their prime, and instead of making a true Resident Evil game, Capcom appeared to design a title meant to compete with those franchises, simply branding it as Resident Evil and featuring the series’ iconic characters.

Beyond this, the PC port itself is extremely unpolished. It is immediately apparent that the game was designed primarily for controller use and later translated to keyboard and mouse. This results in some of the most convoluted keybindings in the series, along with a camera that is difficult to control. The camera is consistently either too fast or too slow, with no comfortable middle ground. The most obvious solution is to use a controller, which is easy enough, but it feels like a slap in the face to players who prefer keyboard and mouse controls. While keyboard controls are not unusable, they are undeniably frustrating.

That said, as a pure action game, Resident Evil 6 can still be enjoyable. It retains some elements of the classic Resident Evil formula, including challenging boss fights, generous ammo availability, and nearly limitless replayability. If you are unsure whether you would enjoy it, I would not recommend purchasing it. However, if you are looking to complete your Resident Evil collection, it may be worth picking up—just be sure to keep your expectations low.

Yes it may be one of the worst Resident Evil's to be released but in my opinion it should be viewed as something different. Even if i'm a big fan of the whole RE saga and have played countless games i went into this with a different perspective without trying to put it in the same category as the other masterpieces.

Me and a friend were just looking for a co-op game to play that has decent mechanics and the one basic thing that one looks for when playing a game with a friend, FUN.
Needles to say that this game delivered, yes the mechanics are weird, yes some things that happen are way too over the top and janky to be considered realistic but guess what? That makes it 100 times funnier.

The fact that the game is janky and too over the top is really the highlight of it, if you have a friend to play it with you actually should consider buying it.

One of the things i don't see people talking about is how good some of the stories are, if you're a fan of the saga you may just really enjoy them. Some of the campaigns have really good moments and some really good plots, not to mention that all campaign intersect each other so the more you play them, the more you notice all characters some way or another have a brief interaction.

All in all the jankiness of the game filled with the good campaign stories and the fun factor of everything really makes it a good experience with friends.
My final advice? If you plan on playing it with a friend, get it; But if you plan on getting it because you like the RE saga and want a good story focused serious game, then don't even bother.

Duuude.. this game is a literal hate love(for me personally) and if there would be a third option to vote for reviews like a neutral(“—“) vote, I would do it because I cannot really down- or upvote this game.
Some situations/parts and certain things(which seem to be only bad programmed) I just hate in that game and don't even want to proceed further in the game and then there are some situations and certain things where I absolutely like that game.
And to be fully honest, I got so pissed off during a certain part in the game that I not only was about to rage quit, uninstall that game and never play it again, but also give that game definitely a thumbs down..
[h3]AI Character[/h3]
There’s one super annoying thing I really hate about the AI in this game and that’s the fact that you have to play babysitter but what does that mean?
If you are at a certain spot where you have to press “V”(on PC) to perform an action like opening doors or to boost the AI onto something and as soon as you pressed “V”, you’re stuck in this action until the AI is with you to perform this action but what makes this so annoying? 
It’s simply the fact that you cannot cancel this action by yourself which means that if the AI is miles away from you, it takes forever for the AI to come to you.
The only way this action will be cancelled is if you’re attacked by an enemy which is imo the most dumbest thing I have ever seen.
I mean there are other spots where you have to perform QTE(Quick-Time-Events) in the game where you have to spin a Valve Wheel by quickly pressing “WASD”(on PC) and this action you can cancel by pressing “Space”(on PC), why the hell isn’t that possible with the other actions where you have to wait for the AI?
[h3]Inventory[/h3]
I cannot tell how long it took me to understand and get used to this inventory system.
(This is a little “Guide” to demonstrate this “special” inventory system) 
Combining herbs and selecting any utility is so stupid weird..
For combining herbs you have to press “E” to open the main inventory, scroll to the green herb, press “Space” to select it, press again “Space” to select the second green or red herb and then press again “Space” to combine it – if you want to store the combined herb, you have press again “Space” to select the herb and then press again “Space to store it in the “tablet case”.
See, absolutely dumb and super laborious…
To select any utility you have to press “Shift” to open the “sub-inventory” and then you have all your utilities.
… just don’t ask me, why, ok x) 
I have never seen a more dumb and laborious inventory system in any other game!
[h3]Tutorial[/h3]
Yep, this Resident Evil Part does have a Tutorial which you have to play first before playing the actual game but spoiler alert; [spoiler]the entire tutorial is also a Part in the final Chapter of the Leon Campaign.[/spoiler]
[h3]Controls[/h3]
This game has a completely different controls compared to all other Resident Evil Part’s!
Usually you press and hold “Shift” to sprint in almost every game but in this game you have to press and hold “Space” to sprint..
For example; there was a Part in Chris' Campaign - Chapter 3, where I got so pissed off, that I not only was about to rage quit and uninstall the game, but also definitely would've given that game a thumbs down because there was a Part in this Chapter where I thought to be stuck(I died 44 times in this Part) and only a comment in a other f*cking Steam discussion(from 10 years ago) helped me to proceed because the game itself didn't tell me anything, during the entire play through and at first I thought it was a bug but it wasn't, it was only the very first time in the game where I had to use “Space” to sprint which I apparently didn’t needed before.
As I already have written in my Resident Evil 4 2005 Review, the QTE happen at least on PC sooo stupid fast where you have literally a time window of max 1 second to react with a weird combination of keys on the keyboard whereas you have all buttons on the controller directly ready to hand – as much as I have seen in videos on YouTube, you have a react time window of about 3 seconds with controller, like?? x)
[h3]Ada[/h3]
There’s nothing to complain about her, she’s the real boss in the entire Resident Evil Franchise(you can say what you want) and she knows exactly what she is doing – oh and her love for Leon(and vice versa of course) is so special, especially the scene of those two on the Quad Tower in Lanshiang!
[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
The way the gameplay is in this Resident Evil Part is how I imagine it as a typical Resident Evil gameplay. 
But this game had also it’s few situations again where too much happen at ones - my biggest complaign especially in this game would be that it's quite unnecessary to fight besides the boss also the regular zombies as it was already in Resident Evil 3 Remake(penultimate Nemesis Boss fight).
[h3]Bosse[/h3]
A few bosses were really easy whereas other bosses where just annoying and kinda hard to beat.
Those who have played Resident Evil 7 before this Resident Evil here, will definitely recognize a certain boss fight again ;)
[h3]Game Length[/h3]
For my personal taste, this game has a wayyy too long story length and honestly it felt like I was playing 4 Resident Evil Parts because each Campaign took me about 9 hours to beat, only the Ada Campaign took me about 6 hours.
[h3]Graphics[/h3]
Honestly? For a Game which was released back in 2012, this game looks really good!
[h3]Rating[/h3]
As I have said at the beginning of this review, I was about to give this game definitely a thumbs down but later on I really began to enjoy and like this game. I'd give that game a 7/10!

I love RE games, but I usually just play them once and am done with them. Like most solo story base games.
This one though, despite being the fan least favorite, kept me hooked and I still play it regularly. Joining a random coop session or whatever.
If you are looking solely for a RE game, you'll be disappointed indeed, as it is far different from the holy trinity (RE1/2/3).
I think what I really like about the game is the rythm, and the balance between action/shooting/QTE/escape scenes, etc...
Maybe if you have an ADHD brain like mine, you'll like it, as you never linger too much in one thing and everything is so various and flashy. The game is also linear and straightforward, there is no frustrating labyrinth or anything to waste your time. Pure packed action, little time to get bored, nothing too difficult or nerve-wracking. A frustration free game.
The story is often criticized, however I did find it interesting. We always love to see the ever stoic Ada and her character being explored in more depth, Leon is still himself, altruistic with his peculiar sense of humor. Chris is also himself, and we can see some interesting character development in his campaign. Finally, it is nice to see grown up Sherry and her dynamic with Jake is interesting.
It is all very subjective of course, but RE6 became one of my favorite game, one that I can play multiple times without being bored.
PS: If you play it in the highest difficulty setting, you'll actually get that Survival Horror experience, lacking ammo and all that jazz...

Resident Evil 6 is a divisive entry in the iconic survival horror franchise, and my experience with it has been nothing short of a rollercoaster ride. Capcom's ambitious attempt to blend various gameplay styles results in a game that's both exhilarating and occasionally bewildering.

From a technical standpoint, Resident Evil 6 is a visual spectacle. The environments are detailed, character models are lifelike, and the sound design is top-notch. The action sequences are intense, and the game's scope is undeniably grand. The variety of locales, ranging from urban landscapes to dark, eerie caverns, keeps the visuals engaging throughout.

However, the departure from the series' survival horror roots might leave purists feeling a bit disoriented. Resident Evil 6 leans heavily into the action genre, with fast-paced combat, spectacular set pieces, and a relentless onslaught of enemies. The inclusion of multiple playable characters (each with their own unique campaign) adds replay value but contributes to a somewhat disjointed narrative.

One standout feature is the cooperative gameplay, which allows you to team up with a friend for a more enjoyable experience. The synergy between characters can lead to some epic moments, and the shared sense of dread amplifies the horror elements.

The game's biggest flaw lies in its occasionally convoluted plot and an overabundance of quick-time events (QTEs). The narrative jumps between different characters and locations, making it challenging to fully immerse yourself in the unfolding story. The QTEs, while adding cinematic flair, can sometimes feel like a distraction from the core gameplay.

Despite its flaws, Resident Evil 6 delivers a satisfying action experience for those willing to embrace the departure from the series' roots. It's a game that's best enjoyed with a friend, where the chaos becomes part of the fun. If you can overlook the narrative hiccups and embrace the change in direction, Resident Evil 6 offers an intense and visually stunning journey through the darker corners of the Resident Evil universe.

If you see this as an action packed game with plenty of explosions, quick time events and some bullet sponges bosses then you will enjoy Resident Evil 6. If you forgive (and forget) about what made Resident Evil past games so tense and unique, you can even grab a friend and play the entire game in co-op sharing all the action paced chapters. However, even if you get past all these nostalgia things you can't avoid to feel of how the little things that made these games what they are today are gone. You will miss the calming music when entering a safe room, you will miss the risk-reward in getting a slot in your inventory filled with herbs instead of more ammo. If you're just in for the action, then the game will deliver plenty to shoot, plenty ammo to find and plenty ways of how you want to upgrade yourself. Looking to find more items and ammo? I've played through several Resident Evil games and I really loved the earlier ones. I didn't know much about RE6 when I picked it up for 5€ on this Winter sale.
Resident Evil 6 lets you choose out of four available campaigns, each accompanied by a different pair of protagonists. The story was meant to intertwine between these campaigns, but sadly the result is pretty confusing. Apparently story isn't that important in RE6 - you find yourself in a city overrun by zombies and that's basically all you need to know.
In contrast to its survival horror predecessors, Resident Evil 6 is a full-bloodied shooter. You have unlimited inventory space, the game is automatically saved on checkpoints, there is no map and puzzles are reduced to zero. Along with these "improvements", the game is now insanely linear - most of the times you can't even return to the room you visited just moments ago. If that wasn't bad enough, real-time events are sure to put the nail in the coffin. Every now and then, the gameplay is chopped by a real-time event in which you are forced to press a certain button combination or do something quickly (otherwise you'll die in most cases). This literally happens around every other corner and it's really irritating. The only good thing about RE6 is the presentation. Despite the game being rather dark, the interiors are full of details and look very realistic. Zombies have been animated excellently and voice acting in cut-scenes is top-notch. Thanks to that, the creepy atmosphere characteristic to Resident Evil games is still present in RE6.

If you're thinking about buying Resident Evil 6, just don't. You won't miss out on anything, story-related or otherwise. This game is just another horror shooter and there are lots of better horror shooters out there.

Nonsensical story even by Resident Evil standard. Who the hell are half of these people? Don't tell me. I don't care.

 Abysmal inventory management. I feel it's pretty bad over Resident Evil games overall really, but this one takes the biscuit. It's this weird mess of basic scrolling, but it scrolls both ways and you can fast swap weapons, but when you have a lot of weapons it make it so you're back and forth. The game also decided to pack your inventory out by giving you way too many throwables, but makes them a chore to use. Every so often you're best off just stopping and clearing them from your inventory.

 Controls are garbage. It has this weird cover system that's a mix of something like Gears and Army of Two, but instead of copying one or the other and improving them, it takes the worst aspects from both of them. Dreadful.

Vehicle sections are uniformly terrible. They even know this themselves because when you die it gives you full health from the check point.

Game constantly has points where it wrestles the camera from you, or even anchors your view to something while you are in the action. The action doesn't pause. You will die because of this. It also has a weird habit of not letting you see what you need to see.

Some parts are impossible if you are playing as a specific character in some hosting situations. You can become soft locked.

When a player gets downed, the game takes control away from you while it stun grenades your eyes with a negative flash. You can receive damage during this time, just like when it does the cinematic pans or focuses your camera on whatever it's doing.

FOV feels like it's inside my eyeballs. Why does it have to be like this?

No auto reloads when a magazine is empty meaning that you're often caught with your pants down.

Terrible AI. Even in co-op you're stuck with AI doing stuff that will just get hung up and cause you fails.

 "Puzzles". Generally you're only going to get stuck because the geography of the level is horrendous in parts. In fact there's a part in every single campaign where you have to do three of whatever in an area and these parts suck so much.

Health system is garbage. Damaged received is inconsistent across the game. You can get stunlocked in certain areas of the game.

The item drop rates are skewed as to be a bit of a headache. This is tied to the bad inventory I think, because you can get 100's of pistol bullets and can't use them fast enough to negate more pistol bullets dropping, but not getting anything for other weapons or vice versa. My co-op partner regularly has run completely out of ammo, sometimes through her own gung-ho nature, but sometimes just because the game insist on giving you xp. I hate it.

XP is pointless. The perks are pointless. I feel like some of them might as well be a placebo effect they aid you so little. There's so many situational ones that provide so little value there's no point in them existing. So many of them require you to kill 1000 enemies or whatever with a specific weapon. No thanks. Only someone with brain damage would want to play this game more than once. 

It's never 100% clear what an area wants from you in some instances. Is it to survive? Is it to get the keys and escape? Do I need to do a puzzle to stop the waves? Is it a combination of all of the above?

In instances of where the players get split up and must do something to progress the parts, it's barely clear on what needs doing, especially when you are at a whim of the co-op partner. Like, do I just stand and defend? Do I have urgency to do the objective to get them out of trouble? Also these parts are utterly awful to play when its you waiting on them.

On said parts, holding to view what they are doing so you can see what they see only works part of the time. Why. Because they don't care about this awful game.

The characters are terrible. Leon and his sidekick are fine in isolation, but the rest of them are truly the worst of the worst. Jake in particular is to Resident Evil 6 as to what Poochie was to the Itchy and Scratchy show. They make the people on Love Island seem like fantastic filled out people with something to give the world.

The running away sections are a travesty. All of them. All of them are hampered with spinning the camera around and generally making them as unpleasant to experience as possible. 

Boss fights are atrocious. Boss fights in RE games have never been it strong suite, but they somehow managed to make them at best tedious and at worst agonising. Rubbish design throughout, such as bosses getting toppled out of reach where you cannot continue the attack that is needed to finish them.

Constant QTE's. All the time. I'm surprised I'm not asked to complete a QTE to post this review.

Ada campaign is for one player only, making it so that the co-op player is just there to be dragged along. Why make a game that's intended for 2 players and then do this? Baffling.

Instances of where you can be instakilled through no fault of your own by standing in the wrong position are too frequent. You could argue once is enough, but this game does it a lot. Ambulances, cars, trains, helicopters, floors collapsing, you name it, there's probably some nonsense there that will cause a kill screen before you even knew it was going to be there. I will honestly never understand most of the reviews for this title. I find them so disingenious and unreasonable - "I started playing this game and it got boring after the first half an hour (which is literally a tutorial action sequence) so I will just leave this negative review".

Most of the negative reviews come from this game being such an over-the-top action title - and the RE franchise probably strayed the furthest from being a survival horror title. But what I don't understand is why should that mean it's the franchise's "downfall". I am very happy Capcom chose to experiment down this path, most probably because I saw too many flaws in Resident Evil 5 and I really hoped for a higher value production than that, and I think they absolutely did that with RE6.

I understand that this is not what Resident Evil usually stands for. It's a "bombastic extravaganza", very Hollywood-like, but how could this ever be rated lower than Resident Evil 5? Because they share a lot of the same ideas and overall direction choices, I will further compare it to RE5 and make my point as to why I think it's better than its predecessor.

Here you get to play 20 chapters from 4 different perspectives (or rather 7, because even the duo co-op chapters differ to an extent), with many intersections between all these characters. The characters here are not written perfectly, but some of them actually make some sense. I liked Sheva in RE5 but I found her to be such an uninteresting character. In RE6 you actually see the reasoning behind the character's actions. Piers, for example, I find to be a really strong character. He was given a task to complete no matter what, and he was willing to do so all the way through, you really get to see how he views Chris as his idol and following his steps. And you also get a glimpse of their backstory and the losses they went through together. It's a shame they killed him off, as I could definitely see him having a story of his own, but at least they pulled off a decent ending to Chris' campaign, it really hits you in the guts.
What also shines compared to RE5 are the choices and different playstyles you're given with these 4 campaigns, but at the same time it's the game's failing point as most people weren't even aware of this. Leon's campaign is slow-paced, but if you want fast-paced action you get to choose from Chris' or Jake's campaign, or if you want a stealthier campaign with more puzzles, you go for Ada's campaign. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3102206744
The same goes for the difficulty between these campaigns. I would say it gets harder by this same order, and I found Ada's campaign specifically really tough to beat on higher difficulties. There are a lot of different enemy types, and even though most of them share a lot of the same ideas, some are tougher to beat - I found Rasklapanje to be a really annoying enemy, especially during Jake's campaign, just like those swarms of insects, specifically during Ada's campaign.

Every campaign has both boss fights where you work together with players from other campaigns in co-op play and boss fights that are specific to the campaign you're playing, and I absolutely loved that idea. The bad side of this is that now there are so many different villains you're bound to forget most of them. However, I found villains like Ustanak and Simmons really decent, and I'd say the other boss fights were entertaining too.

Now, when I say this is an upgrade from RE5, I mean it in a technical way as well. You're not stuck with those awful movement mechanics and that camera. What I did find irritating at times are these specific camera angles during a chase where they switch through a lot of different angles in a short span of time and it's really easy to clip on a wall and die, but I usually found them really enjoyable and reminiscent of the older RE games. Also, you're not stuck with that god awful co-op AI. Here it actually functions independently, your playthrough is not about babysitting them anymore, but rather about the game itself as it should be. Yes, I do miss the ability to trade inventories between them, but I would rather have an AI that does not die on me every minute and is actually useful for once. The online co-op is equally good, where up to 6 people can play together, and there is actually a decent number of players online. I was able to find a teammate for most of the chapters I played through. Compared to RE5, you now have a voice chat and it's even more enjoyable to play with others. Where I do see this fall short compared to RE5 is that the market and the upgrading system for the weapons is gone, but I really liked the new skill point system and the ability to make different loadouts depending on the run you're going for or if you're playing solo or online.

One of the things I do agree with the negative reviews, to a certain extent, are the QTEs. I wouldn't say the game is over-reliant on them, I'd say they're well placed, but some of them I found excessively hard or unrealistic. I can't even count the number of times I've died to a QTE that literally lasts for a split second. You simply don't have the time to react as there are so many different keys used and the game forces you to remember these specific QTE by replaying the same part a sh*t ton of times.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3099130146

And for the final mention - the graphics look okay, and the character models look great, but the textures often seem low-resolution.

This game isn’t good. I do not recommend it. As someone who has played through the Resident Evil franchise in 2023 I found Resident Evil 6 to be the worst mainline entry.

I don’t like how it completely shreds its roots in the survival horror. The prior games were all fun to play. But starting with Resident Evil 5 the franchise was at a low point that relied on action over horror because it was during the “decline of survival horror”  that occurred towards the end of the Xbox 360/PS3 era.

This reliance on action, insane story events, and online co-op is not synonymous with Resident Evil. The strong environments, puzzles, and interesting characters associated with the prior games is not present in any way in Resident Evil 6, and the intertwining narratives it is trying to tell get lost in the terrible writing and story. We get a shell of its former self. One that tries to cater to broad appeal and one that tries to jump the shark in numerous ways, but it ends up being a game that doesn’t really excel in anything and one that doesn’t really appeal to anyone.

If its gameplay was good I could be a bit more positive but Resident Evil 6 is also a poorly designed game as well. I was thrown around during gameplay, the enemy AI is inconsistent, and your partner AI is awful (I often saw both my partner and enemies just chilling out together before shooting at each when I catch them). The cover based shooting is awful, there is an overreliance on unfair QTEs, and enemies soak up a lot of bullets. Every combat encounter was a joyless slog and combined with being thrown around, the overwhelming action set pieces, and QTEs it made me feel unwell whilst I was playing it. I really tried to finish it and I really tried to find the positives in it, but I can’t find anything good to say about it.

I don’t personally agree with the idea that this is a good game if you take away the fact that it’s a Resident Evil entry. That sounds like copium, because even if it wasn’t a Resident Evil game it would still be terrible and no-one would remember it. This game was a dead end and Capcom knew this as well. It would have killed the franchise if they didn’t reboot it with RE7. 

Resident Evil 6 is not Resident Evil in the slightest. It’s a game that chases trends and high levels of action, but also one that disregards its legacy and franchise history in the worst way possible. As such I do not recommend it, not even during a sale. Please play any of the other mainline games instead.

You know what? No. This game isn't ass. This game isn't ass at all, and I want to give a sincere "screw you" to everyone who told me it was and stopped me from playing this game earlier. This is one of the best third-person shooters I've ever played bar none. 

RE6's gameplay is very in-depth, though almost to a fault. Those who go in blind will likely struggle a lot with it, but after learning the game and how its mechanics work, I can say with full certainty that it has some of the smoothest, most understated gameplay I've seen in a game like this. Quick shots allow you to quickly put an enemy in a daze if they're getting a little too close, dash attacks allow you to quickly take a small group out, sliding allows you to get through large groups relatively unscathed, and diving basically replaces the QTEs of RE4 and 5 with a mechanic that makes you feel much more in control of what your player character does. The game didn't tell you "press X to dodge", you had to input the dodge [i]yourself[/i]. It makes for a game where you feel much more in control of what your player character is doing. If the game had explained these mechanics better, a lot of the "enemies don't react to my shots" comments would go away. They don't react to your shots because you're [i]not supposed to just be shooting them blindly[/i]. It puts great focus on choosing what method of attacking is best for the given situation, be it shooting, quick shooting, meleeing, sliding, whatever it may be, and once you get used to it, it's extremely fun to play with. 

My main issues with the game lie with other problems. Some smaller, like I'm not a big fan of Leon's VA around this time. Others larger; for example, the Nintendo Switch version added support for gyro aiming, while the PC version is still missing this feature. They split the game into [i]four[/i] campaigns, each of which is a self-contained story, is five chapters long, and gets its own credits roll. The campaigns cross paths with each other, so there will be brief scenes where you're battling a monster alongside some of the other characters before the plot forces you to go your separate ways again.

It's definitely continuing the trend that started in RE4 of gravitating toward action and away from survival horror, but I feel like the execution is much better than RE4 and RE5.

It's a nice effect having the different aspects of the plot revealed by the characters' different perspectives on the same events, much like RE: Revelations 2.

There was a wide variety of environments: most of the RE standards (city in crisis, crypt, sewer, research facility, mansion, …) and some more. There was [i]not[/i], however, a wide variety of enemies: there were zombies, J'avo (basically dudes), and two kinds of mutated J'avo.

Special note: [i]I [b]love[/b] the melee attacks![/i] They're actually effective! And so satisfying! And you can even use them on bosses!

Overall, I really enjoyed Resident Evil 6: the plot was engaging and typically byzantine, the gameplay was dynamic, the typical RE jank was … [i]there[/i], but tolerable. I'd say this is maybe my third favorite so far, behind Revelations 2 and RE3 remake.

This allows players to experience the story from various angles, providing a comprehensive understanding of the game's universe.

The game's combat system is more refined compared to its predecessors, with improved shooting mechanics and an advanced cover system, offering a satisfying action-oriented experience. Graphically, "Resident Evil 6" presents detailed environments and impressive character models, with a high level of polish that immerses players in its world. The game also boasts a cinematic presentation, with dramatic set pieces and intense boss fights that keep the adrenaline pumping.

The game has received criticism for straying from its survival horror roots, but it compensates by offering a substantial amount of content and a variety of experiences. It's a game that's not afraid to evolve and try new things, which can be seen as a positive aspect for the franchise and the genre.

In summary, "Resident Evil 6" should be played for its action-packed gameplay, cooperative features, polished graphics, and its bold approach to storytelling across multiple campaigns. The DLC section, meant for online play, is virtually deserted, and I haven't come across a single player there, at least not in my experience. But within the game itself, you can still find people to team up with for co-op play.

In my opinion, I'd rate it a 7 out of 10.

This game is the most over hated game I've played in a long while. 

Much like RE4 and 5, 6 is an action game and not a survival horror like the older entries. Going in after enjoying 4 and 5, I was expecting a game that was "so bad it's good" and that's pretty much what I got. What I didn't get was a game so bad that it deserves the title of "a game that killed the franchise." Because honestly? 6 is the natural evolution of everything 4 and 5 had to offer, and I am baffled that people like those two games (or at least 4), but hate this one. And after the success of 4 and 5, I really don't know what people were expecting, and I say this as someone who very much prefers the classic RE titles. 

Now that I've played it, I can confirm people overreacted to this game an absurd amount. "It isn't survival horror!" Neither was 4 or 5, and 4 is practically worshiped as the best RE game to the point where its influence can be found in every subsequent RE title. "It has too much action and it can't be taken seriously." Again, such was the case with 4 and 5 - Leon roundhouse kicked BOWs in 4 and was a one man army, while in 5 Chris punches a boulder. Even in the older entries, RE always had an element of ridiculousness and being over the top, and this game is no exception. So in all honesty, I find the vast majority of complaints people have with this game to be, frankly, invalid.

That said, it does have some issues, but one glaring one in particular: Holding space bar is your run key and your "action" key most of the time. What this means is that you'll be running, and without meaning to, you'll vault over an object, which gets pretty annoying pretty quickly. This problem is further highlighted during the game's chase sequences, where you'll be running away from something, only to be slowed down because your character vaulted over an object unintentionally, and because of that, you fail the sequence and die. Changing the key won't make a difference either as you'll still encounter the same problems. Additionally, there's also a "skill system" with skill points, which is just...not needed and feels really out of place. Oh, and there's also QTEs and a bad cover system, but that's just peak early 2010s gaming, and for the QTEs in particular, again: 4 and 5 did that too.

Aside from all that though, this game is a fun time, especially if you bring a friend to sit back and laugh at it with. I personally find it fun and I'd say it has the smoother gameplay compared to the original RE4 and 5, although it still is a bit jank, mostly for what I just mentioned. I think at the very least, this game deserves praise for making knife/close quarters combat feel good, as you can now execute special moves after knifing enemies or just punch them a lot and doing the same. Close combat/the knife feels like an alternative to your guns, instead of something to fall back on as a last resort. It's definitely worth it on sale, even if you're just playing solo like I was. If you like 4 and 5, this game is more of the same, albeit turned up to 11.
