I know this is going to tick a lot of people off but Resident Evil 6 is actually my favorite RE title, with 4 close behind.  This game is a vast improvement over its predecessor, Resident Evil 5, with better controls, smoother gameplay, smarter AI, wider enemy variety and enough content to make its rather steep price, shared with RE7, worth it.

This is the most maligned RE game out there but I think most of the hate is unwarranted.  Is it a bad game?  Absolutely not.  Is it a bad survival horror game?  Yes, but so are 4 and 5, 4 less so but still not great.  Is it a bad Resident Evil game?  Yes, but only by old Resident Evil rules.  The thing is, those rules don't apply to all Resident Evil games forever.  RE4 did not jump the shark by going for action over horror: it evolved the series into something new for the new generation.  RE6 is the culmination of that evolution, the ultimate outbreak/disaster that every player of the original Resident Evil envisioned when they saw the horrific monstrosities infesting the Spencer mansion.

I played through all four campaigns without being too frustrated or quitting for ages at a time as I did with the previous game.  And, I have to say, they're all good in their own ways.  Leon's reeks of classic Resident Evil horror, Chris' feels more like a typical action monster movie, Jake's brings back the terror of having Mr. X hunting you in RE2 with the fearsome Ustanak on your tail, and Ada's campaign, while the least fun, does tie all of them together quite nicely.

The AI is much smarter and more useful than Sheva was in RE5 and is less of a liability.  I've had my skin saved far more times by Piers, Helena or Sherry than I ever was by Sheva.  Weapons and commands are better and the AI just seems more coordinated.  However, this game is also a blast with a friend.

The story is a little confusing, but it's not hard to piece together if you've played the game enough.  The J'avo seen here are far more threatening than the Ganado of RE4 or the Majini of RE5 with their ability to spontaneously mutate into terrifying new forms, and the C-Virus Zombies, while slower and less intelligent, are no joke either.  The only reason they're not as dangerous in-game is because you're stronger, with the ability to melee without shooting enemies and perform dodges and dives.

And the Mercenaries mode... OH MY GOD, the Mercenaries mode... easily the best in the series, tied with the RE4 Remake of 2023.  I have almost 100 hours in this game from this mode alone with how astoundingly entertaining it is.  I never thought just cracking zombie skulls and disintegrating J'avo for a few minutes could be so damn fun!  Not to mention, RE5's Mercenaries has to be unlocked by playing the main game through to the end, while the Mercenaries mode in this game is unlocked from the get-go.

People say RE6 is bad, but I say nay nay, not unless you were looking for an old-school Resident Evil game, because this is new school Resident Evil and that honestly makes it more fun.  I played this after playing RE5 for a while, and had so much fun with it that I actually beat it before coming back to RE5.  Would I recommend it?  Yes, definitely.  For a game that's over 10 years old, it's still quite fresh and a helluva good time!

Edit:  I think the story could have been a little better if Albert Wesker had survived RE5 and been the villain again, then he could have faced off against Jake in his campaign and have Jake call him out for being a bad father and an all-round psycho.  I also think the QTEs are a little excessive but at least the game added a counterattack option, which this series has needed for a while.  I really love how each encounter with the enemies is like its own mini-puzzle and how each B.O.W. you face has their own way of taking them down, which is pretty good for pretty much all of them.  Except the Lepoticas.  (Le-Poh-Tits-Ah)  Those things can just f*** right off.

I also understand the lack of an upgrade screen or Merchant and just starting with fully upgraded weapons because the campaigns take place over multiple countries in a short span of time, so I think Capcom can get a bit of leeway there.  I really love that this game has a sprint mechanic that actually lets you sprint, instead of the lame-as-hell jogging from Resident Evil 5, and even lets you perform some kick-ass sprinting melees so you can pull off devastating combos.

I think most of this game's horror comes not from how the B.O.W.s seen in it affect you, the protagonist, but knowing how they must be affecting the populace, who aren't trained or equipped to deal with them at all.  This is a horror game if you think about it, just not in the direct or traditional sense.

So after more time with the game I still feel it is awful, but it can be quite fun at times. The combat system can definitely be quite entertaining with all the options in mobility and melee combat, but the game communicates so many mechanics so poorly that learning all the ins and outs of it that it somehow makes all the gameplay feel half baked. The game has some of the worst scripted sequences I’ve ever played in a game, they somehow feel more akin to a low budget game, there is one in particular when you drive on some snowmobile and my god is just awful. Also, the amount of QTEs are horrid, most of them with terrible timing and foreshadowing, but thankfully, you can turn them off, which I highly recommend. Also, while the game doesn’t look bad for its age, the quality of the assets, geometry, texture and lighting is inferior to the one in Resident Evil 5, the main character models look decent, but the environments can be incredibly dull and on close up just straight up ugly. 

I will now say some more positive things. As previously stated, combat can be fun, and there are some places where this element shines and as a consequence of this, there are some truly fun boss fights here and there. The game also runs smoothly as hell, aside from a weird bug that would tab out of the game, I had no problem with running the game. The story is also a highlight, it’s insane and stupid in all the right ways and I loved it. Also, if you have a friend who is willing to turn off their brain a little and not take the game too seriously it can be a blast in certain parts and you can laugh at everything wrong and dumb about the game.

In general is a game with ups and downs, but the issue is that the downs are by far the worst the mainline series has seen. If you have someone to play it with and go with the mentality that you will play a dump game and then turn off the QTEs, maybe I would be able to recommend it, otherwise, just don’t. While fun at times it’s a miserable experience for the most of it, especially playing alone and I consider it to be the worst of the numbered RE games.

Can't believe I'm saying this but after 30 hours on Steam and another 40+ on Switch I have to say that despite what this game would have you believe, it is actually a lot of fun. Characters and plot alike are shallow if not entirely flat, environments seem to have the bare minimum of detail as you charge through your 50th generic asian urban street or eastern european town. HOWEVER. Despite everything, despite almost no tutorial, despite having sometimes asinine enemy design, despite having clashing tones of pure action and a thought of survival horror, despite having the worst inventory/crafting/quickswap system in the series, the actual core gameplay is, against all odds, fun. This game could have been another MT Framework cashgrab, perhaps tacking on some features to RE5 the way that game had taken after RE4. But the new gameplay, featuring a free camera devoid of tank controls, far more dynamic interactions with enemies (as opposed to 4 and 5's routine kick/suplex/punch), a wealth of interesting dodges, counters, slides, and rolls, weapons that have a distinct punch to them (personal note, it was a good idea to remove weapon upgrades for an action-focused game), seriously does offer something that the rest of the franchise had never offered before. The biggest criticism I had was that it took 2 full 30 hour playthroughs to finally get a feel for the gameplay. The game does not make the slightest effort to teach you about any of the cool things it does, and that is its greatest mistake.

Resident Evil 6 definitely gets the most hate out of the franchise, some undeserved and most deserved in my opinion, 
When I played this game I was going through a Resident Evil marathon and I almost dreaded getting to this game because of its reputation but when I got to it I tried to keep an open mind as I am somewhat of an unwilling contrarian and Resident Evil 5 (the closes game to this) is one of my favorite games in the franchise. However I just can't bring myself to like this game.
Defenders of this game will often bring up the mechanics of the game such as the movement, the gunplay and the melee moves (which have been greatly expanded upon since 5) and I agree that the mechanics in this game are really good, the big problem is that the game is often more interested in showing you its lackluster setpieces, drowning you in qte or waiting for something to happen in the game so you can progress and when the game isn't doing this you have to bear its less than stellar level design. 
The enemies is in this game are also much less fun to fight against than the enemies in 4 and 5. Enemies in general feel more tanky and are less responsive to your attacks when compared to 4 and 5 which I feel is a great flaw in this game as the most fun part in those games was settting the enemies up for a melee follow through. Another gripe I have with the enemies in this game is that infected with guns are much more common and they are particularly unfun to go up against. 
Finally, a lot of the boss fights in this game are quite unbereable. To me Resident Evil as a franchise has never had outstanding bossfights but they feel like more of a nuissance here than in other entries as they tend to be very drawn and are particularly bad when it comes to the aforementioned setpieces and quick time events. 
Overall I can't really recommend this game unless you play it with a friend or are a big fan of RE and want to follow the story threads between this and following entries.

RE6 is basically your average summer blockbuster action movie, but in the worst way possible. There's no substance to any of it, it's just dumb set piece after dumb set piece. It's a trial in seeing just how crazy it can get and what kind of situations it can push the characters into to have them try to survive. It has some good ideas here and there and they clearly PACKED this thing full of content but most agree that the content you get here isn't quite up to par with any of the previous games in the series. RE6 killed the franchise for a reason.

As said before, this game has tons of content. It's easily the longest RE game even now with 4 different campaigns and one of the most extensive Mercenaries modes in the series. Each campaign revolves around different characters and they usually intertwine at certain moments. This sounds pretty awesome on paper but it doesn't feel as developed as say when Leon and Claire meet in RE2 at various points in the campaign. Usually you run into the other characters during a segment and they are just kinda there to help you fight then leave right after. I think Leon and Chris's campaign clearly had the most work done with them with Jake's being slightly worse and Ada being by far the worst of the four. Not all campaigns have the same amount of effort put into them unfortunately.

RE6 doesn't have much in the way of story. Sure there's plenty of cutscenes and attempts at a story but a lot of it feels like rehashes of previous games, there's this dude called Ustanak who is literally a carbon copy of Nemesis in Jake's campaign for example. I think Chris and Piers had a lot of potential though, and Jake as a concept is pretty cool but I think they could have been executed better.

Now there is one thing that RE6 does pretty well, and that's the gameplay. It's definitely a far cry from the Resident Evil that everyone knows but it's a very well made combat system focused around action, doing dodge rolls and performing take downs that feel like something out of a John Wick movie. I find the Mercenaries mode to be especially fun because of this, mainly because it's just pure gameplay without any boring story/annoying set pieces to get in the way.

I don't think RE6 is terrible but by the franchise's standards it's definitely the worst numbered title in the series. If you're looking for some dumb fun with a buddy, RE5 is a lot better for that but this is here as a backup option as well.

Resident Evil 6 is often called the worst of the main series, and that is probably true. Although, I personally believe this game gets more hate than it deserves.

Resident Evil 6 places you in the usual apocalyptic situation our protagonists somehow find themselves in. Unlike previous games, you have four separate stories to play through, all of which are intertwined in some way with each other.

I'll start with the negatives, as there are quite a few. First, the game's story is completely ridiculous at times. It has its good moments every now and then (especially at the end of Chris' campaign), but most of the time it feels confusing and really weird. It can get hard to follow as well. This is most likely because the game attempted to lean on action instead of horror while also trying to do horror, leaving it a muddled mess.

Second, the actual campaign flow for each campaign is horrendous. Large quiet sections often drag the game on while action sections come one after another, never really letting up (this is actually a positive which I will get into later). This is probably because they focused on making four separate campaigns instead of just one really good one, making each campaign feel half-baked in a sense (this is not the fault of the developers, more the fault of the people who actually set the deadlines).

Finally going back to the story, it doesn't really end on a single note. Thanks to it being split into multiple campaigns, the game relies on the final one to tie everything together. This results in the final campaign feeling really awkward and ending on a "okay, so what?" kind of note.

Okay so me saying all of this and still giving it a positive review must tell you that there's something else this game has going for it. And there is.

The gameplay.

Of any Resident Evil game, RE6 has the most engaging combat I've seen. From RE4 and RE5, the characters can still shoot enemies in their weakpoints and use melee attacks to deal extra damage. However there are so many more controls in RE6. You can dash and ram into enemies to stagger them. You can melee enemies to deliver a second blow with a powerful melee attack. You can slide into enemies to stagger them. You can dodge-roll to the side or backwards to evade attacks. You can even counter enemy attacks to deal heavy damage, often out-right killing the enemy. And there are far more controls than that that would take a long time to list out. There's a reason this game is said to have the best mercenaries mode. In fact, the game is best played foregoing your gun in favour of melee attacks against regular enemies (even on the highest difficulty and with infinite ammo).

This is why I believe the best way to play this game is not treat it as a Resident Evil game at all. Sure, as one it's terrible. But as a stand-alone game, it is a fantastic action game with a decent action-based story to go with it. There are still those really slow moments, sure, but when the game gets going, it gets going.

This is especially true on the highest difficulty, where the game pulls no punches. On Professional or No Hope, you are expected to display constant mastery of the game's controls or else you WILL be annihilated. It's an exhilarating experience to complete a chapter on one of the highest difficulties, especially with someone else helping out.

All in all, Resident Evil 6 fails hard as a Resident Evil game. It lacks the horror, resource management, and good story-telling that made the foundations of far better Resident Evil games like RE4 and RE7. However as its own thing, RE6 is a brilliant action game which shows you that when there's a zombie ahead and you have a gun, the best solution is to punch it in the face and break its spine. The game has a semi-decent story, and the difficulties allow both casual and experienced players to have a challenge to measure themselves up to.

Resident Evil 6, a game that's been unfairly maligned by some, but one that I think deserves more credit than it gets. Let's grab a drink and dive into why this game is worth your time.

First off, let's talk about the gameplay. Yes, it's true that Resident Evil 6 is more action-oriented than previous entries in the franchise, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. The combat is fast-paced and satisfying, with a wide variety of weapons and moves at your disposal. Each of the three campaigns has its own unique gameplay style, which keeps things fresh and interesting throughout the game. Now, let's talk about the story. I'll admit, it's not the most coherent or well-written story out there, but it's still a fun ride. The game ties together multiple plotlines and characters in a way that's ambitious and impressive, even if it doesn't always make complete sense. And let's not forget about the iconic Resident Evil villains, who make their return in memorable ways.

[h1]Resident Evil 6[/h1]

Compared to other RE titles, Resident Evil 6 is the one I have the most mixed feelings with. While RE6 is a [b]highly[/b] entertaining action-based game with high replay value, it is plagued by a mediocre plot, aggravating UI + set pieces, and an overly action-saturated atmosphere with meek attempts at horror in which I would find it hard-pressed to call this game the "dramatic horror experience of 2013."

[u]Story + Characters (Possible Spoilers!)[/u]

Oh man, the story. Resident Evil plots aren't known for being the best, but this has be one of the most convoluted and ridiculous plots I have ever seen.

The entire plotline of RE6 can be described as follows: [spoiler]A leader of an Illuminati-like organization becomes a simp for Ada after a brief business relationship and clones her using one of his staff. Fake Ada is created and gets pissed at him for using her as an experiment, seeking revenge and setting the world on fire as a bonus.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]This entire story is not only generic but it is irrelevant to the entire storyline of Resident Evil. None of the villains, Carla and Simmons, are really mentioned at all before this game and after. They just show up as if we're supposed to know them and care. Regarding the separate campaigns, it's a mixed bag. Leon's campaign is irrelevant, Chris' campaign is okay, Jake's campaign is pretty good, and Ada's campaign feels like it's there to just point out why all this insanity happens. If you wanna understand the whole plot, Ada's story does the best at telling it.[/spoiler]

[u]Gameplay[/u]

RE6's strongest point is definitely the gameplay. Compared to other action titles, RE6 is almost always fun thanks to the amount of fluidity you're given with your movement. Sprinting, dashing, sliding, countering, melee attacks, quick shooting - there are an insane amount of ways to move about and play this game. Capcom really went all out with making as many possible mechanics with how the player can move and attack. It can take a good amount of time to master RE6's movement system, but it's a joy to feel in absolute control when you do. 

Among the three action-era RE games, I would say I have the most fun playing RE6. It's also the best one to play Co-op online or split-screen.

Each character has a unique mechanic they have so none of them feel the same even if it's pretty minor. Leon can dual wield, Helena has a unique shotgun which has unique quick shot animations, Chris has ample firepower at the beginning despite being among the most generic, Piers has the best starting weapon set among everyone with his MP-AF and Anti-Material Rifle, Jake's Hand-to-Hand is among the most fun to use, Sherry has access to a Stun Rod and a burst-fire pistol, and Ada can use her crossbow along with unique dashing and quick shot animations.

There are still some serious problems here though: first, the camera is atrociously bad because not only is it slow and hampered by terrible angles, the game will sometimes wring control of the camera to hyperfocus on an event happening which gets tiring really quick. These moments are most prominent in the Chris and Jake campaigns. Second, the QTEs. It's already been said, but there really are too many of them in this game; it feels like 40% of the game is just QTEs, some of which aren't even deadly if you fail. Third, the design of the set pieces; for some reason, there are so many parts in this game where all you do is run/sprint forward or you die - it happens so often, you will die more from these than actual enemies taking your health down. Again, these are found most in either Chris' or Jake's campaign. Lastly, the UI is not that great since it feels like you're supposed to use the interface while multitasking on the move which adds more burden to the lightning fast pace at which this game makes you play at.

[u]Graphics & Sound[/u]

I found the music in RE6 to be serviceable, but not groundbreaking. It is just there and the differences in music between the campaigns is trivial. They tried to get some kind of horror-like feeling from the main theme but that sort of contradicts with the action-saturated environment of the game. All in all, mildly average.

Comparing this with RE5, it seems like RE6 downgraded in graphics compared to past titles and it's a shame that some of the details of this game are average at best even for a 2013 game. Outside of cutscenes, much of the graphics of the game feel second-rate.

[u]Conclusion[/u]

When it comes to any game, the most important part for me is that it's fun to play. If it's not, what's the point? In that area, RE6 succeeds. It's among the most entertaining Resident Evil games I've played and even more so when you play it with a friend. That being said, the mishmash of problems from the story to some of the gameplay properties mark it as a "black sheep" among Resident Evil major titles.

I would only recommend this game if you're the kind of RE fan who prefers action horror over survival horror and can enjoy the fast-paced gameplay without being ticked off by its flaws.

[h1]Forgiveness in Motion and Witness to Redemption[/h1]

When I read and heard what [i]Resident Evil 6[/i] was — amid grievances and backlash — I asked myself: why not attempt to inhabit it? I find it compelling that this world is one in which the characters’ voices permeate every city. They provide a warmth that the C-virus seeks to eradicate. What unfolds is a fragmented world, akin to reading scattered fragments of letters that must be pieced together to uncover something genuinely poignant.

I played it with friends, and with my sister. Yet it was my sister who gave me pause, compelling me to look with greater attention. We embodied these characters, and one feels the ballast of guilt they carry. It is heavy, aching — like a long wait for pardon. It is fair to laugh at me; and yet, if they seek forgiveness, why not grant it? As we asked ourselves: can one forgive an action once time has passed, or when the person is no longer the same — or when they are merely kin to one who has done us wrong?

The city becomes a kind of purgatory, where each strives to shed the weight of guilt. Every character confronts the phantom of their past: Helena, haunted by her sister; Chris, by the loss of his squad; Jake and Sherry, by the transgressions of their fathers; and Ada, by her role as a detached spy, perceived as one without allegiance.

We must confront our own Nemeses in order to free ourselves from guilt. To ask for forgiveness, one must first behold what one is capable of, and acknowledge the projections of fear. Here, however, therapy does not take the form of speech. It consists instead in facing seemingly invincible enemies through action — through who we truly are. This is true of Simmons for Leon and Helena, or of Ustanak for Sherry and Jake. The greater the guilt, the greater the challenge. More effort is demanded, pushing us to the limit; yet this does not extinguish us. It fosters sovereignty — and friendship — as we endure it together.

We exorcise our ghosts. The battlefield becomes a stage upon which purification may take place. It is not merely an action game; rather, the greater the guilt, the greater the exertion required to overcome one’s phantoms. Nor is this a superhuman feat, but one grounded in capacities we already possess — as agents, as companions, as those who endure.

And yet, this path cannot be walked alone. My sister and I noticed this: forgiveness directed towards another becomes, in turn, forgiveness of oneself. Am I capable of forgiving myself? This question is devastating when one realises that the person who might grant such pardon is no longer here. This is the weight that burdens our struggle. And still, it is shared. I am moved when Helena declares that they will stop Simmons together; when Jake steadies Sherry’s Magnum through action rather than words; when Piers sacrifices himself for the team; or when Ada watches over them all in silence.

Without my sister’s witness and protection, I would be left alone — merely attempting to clear my own name. The noblest act is not to erase blame, but to cleanse the whole being: the soul, burdened with sorrow, and the body, dragged through mire. Without her, I would be fighting only a psychological monster. Without witnesses, without the act of cleansing together, sovereignty would remain unattainable.

This first forgiveness is the power to heal — for my sister and for myself — within our shared sovereignty, so that we may continue to aid others, reciprocating in their sorrows. This is seen most clearly in Ada, who assists others before proceeding with her “mission”.

Guilt binds both sight and heart. We begin to perceive only darkness, and it slowly consumes us. Once stripped of guilt — with forgiveness restoring our power to choose what is good and sustaining — clarity returns. Helena accepts her responsibility, and together with Leon, seeks justice rather than revenge. Their gaze is transformed. So it is with the others.

We clear ourselves of the past in order to endure the present.
And thus, redemption is achieved — always together, one supporting the other — for the other becomes our moral compass, ensuring that we do not harm, but protect, with our lives, or until our strength is spent.

[i]Past weighs on the eyes,
forgiveness flows like a river —
we walk it, together[/i].

So me and my friend have pushed ourselves to finish the entirety of the game at the hardest difficulty, we did not play any of the dlc missions or stuff like that just the basic story modes. 

The mechanics of this game is more or less identical to re5, but worse. We had encountered so many problems with doors and the game just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ itself that we had to reinstall 3 times. There were times when the player hosting had to be the one that opened and interacted with all the objects or else the game would soft lock. An absolutely horrendous experience and these problems caused us to take a month break before completing the game.

Other problems include the default key mapping and the controls. Who in the right mind would put interact and sprint on the same key? The mouse and character movement was also horrible. The overall movement felt clunky even with a controller, mostly due to insanely wide turning radius and extremely slow character movement. And when using mouse there were times where the cursor would snap behind you after an interaction and cause a death.

Next is the story and how fast paced and boring it was. The characters were so flat and predictable and the action sequences was something my 14 year old sister would be able to think up. Me and my friend started betting on what action sequence would happen next and we would get it right every single time. The story was so repetitive and stereotypical that it showcases what little thought was put into these multiple story modes.

The Leon campaign wasn't that bad but it felt especially slow, and the Chris campaign (honestly the best one) started off slow and ended way too fast.

Castlevania Legends is the third Castlevania title released for the original Game Boy. It was released in Japan on November 27, 1997 and in Europe and North America on March 11, 1998.

The game was conceived as a prequel to all other games in the Castlevania series; however, it later became recognized as non-canon. The story follows Sonia Belmont, a vampire hunter battling the first incarnation of Count Dracula.  Castlevania Legends is a side-scrolling platformer where the protagonist, Sonia Belmont, armed with a whip, charges through five stages of Count Dracula's castle, filled with various enemies and candles containing items. Each stage ends in a mini-boss fight which rewards a "Soul Weapon", which Sonia can cast, consuming varying amounts of hearts.

The game implements two difficulty levels and password based save states. Should the timer run out, Sonia fall off the screen, or either her life bar or time counter fall to zero, she will lose all of her hearts and one life, and will restart at the beginning of the current screen with the basic whip. If she loses all of her lives, the player is presented with the Game over screen, where they may exit or choose to continue from the beginning of the current stage. Once per stage, Sonia can activate her inborn ability to enter "Burning Mode", where she becomes invincible, moves faster, and has more powerful attacks for ten seconds.  The story begins in an unspecified year in the Middle Ages in Transylvania, during the incarnation of the original Count Dracula. Sonia Belmont, the first vampire hunter of her clan, develops mystical powers in her 17th year, and ventures out to challenge Dracula, meeting Alucard who seeks revenge against his father. After Dracula's defeat, he swears to Sonia that as long as there is evil in the world, he will be resurrected, and in response she swears her family will always defeat him. The game was designed as the first game in the series timeline, but later declared non-canon after the release of Lament of Innocence.  IGN called the game one of the Game Boy's cult classics despite the portable system's limitations. GameSpy called the music "disappointing", as the previous two Game Boy Castlevania games were highly praised for their music.[ Game Informer's Tim Turi felt that the game was lacking especially compared to Castlevania: Symphony of the Night.

Longtime Castlevania producer Koji Igarashi removed the game from the series timeline, claiming that in his opinion it conflicted with the plotline of the main games. He has stated that "Legends remains something of an embarrassment for the series. If only that development team had the guidance of the original team of the series." 
Sonia was one of the confirmed leads in the Dreamcast game Castlevania: Resurrection, up until that game's cancellation. Known in Japan as Akumajō Dracula: Dark Night Prelude (悪魔城ドラキュラ 漆黒たる前奏曲, Akumajō Dorakyura Dāku Naito Pureryūdo, lit. Demon Castle Dracula: Dark Night Prelude)

Columbo (/kəˈlʌmboʊ/) is an American crime drama television series starring Peter Falk as Lieutenant Columbo, a homicide detective with the Los Angeles Police Department.[2][3] After two pilot episodes in 1968 and 1971, the show originally aired on NBC from 1971 to 1978 as one of the rotating programs of The NBC Mystery Movie. Columbo then aired less frequently on ABC from 1989 to 2003.

Columbo is a shrewd but inelegant blue-collar homicide detective whose trademarks include his rumpled beige raincoat, unassuming demeanor, cigar, old Peugeot 403 car,[4][5][6] love of chili con carne, and unseen wife (whom he mentions frequently). He often leaves a room only to return with the catchphrase "Just one more thing" to ask a critical question.

The character and show, created by Richard Levinson and William Link, popularized the inverted detective story format (sometimes referred to as a "howcatchem"). This genre begins by showing the commission of the crime and its perpetrator; the plot therefore usually has no "whodunit" element of determining which of several suspects committed the crime. It instead revolves around how a perpetrator known to the audience will finally be caught and exposed.

The series' homicide suspects are often affluent members of high society; it has led some critics to see class conflict as an element of each story.[7] Suspects carefully cover their tracks and are initially dismissive of Columbo's circumstantial speech and apparent ineptitude. They become increasingly unsettled as his superficially pestering behavior teases out incriminating evidence.[7] His relentless approach often leads to self-incrimination or outright confession.

Episodes of Columbo are between 70 and 98 minutes long, and have been broadcast in 44 countries. The show has been described by the BBC as "timeless" and remains popular today.[8]

[h1]Resident Evil's Lowest Point[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 is a 2012 third-person shooter video game developed and published by Capcom. A major installment in the Resident Evil series, Players control Leon S. Kennedy, Chris Redfield, Jake Muller and Ada Wong as they confront the force behind a worldwide bio-terrorist attack. The story is centered around their four interwoven campaigns, and every campaign features a unique style in both tone and gameplay.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ATReviews]Follow My Review Group Here![/url]

💾Graphics - Resident Evil 6 has such a mix set of graphics. First I have to say that the UI is actual torture. Whoever made the UI in this game hates you and wants you to truly suffer. Wanna pause the game and change settings? F*ck you, basically. You can pause the game with a big PAUSE in the middle of the screen, but changing audio settings or controls while playing is a nightmare. Having to navigate through your game phone “no joke” is comical at best. I guess it’s cool that every character’s story has a different style UI? It would have been better if the UI was easy to navigate. Also switching weapons is a huge pain too so have fun with that. The lighting is pretty good in some sections (especially Leon’s campaign), while others look so washed out and depressing. The world textures are disgusting if you get close to them. The character models and cinematics do look really good though.

🎮Gameplay - Okay the gameplay is pretty average on a good day. Now the movement is the best in the franchise. Being able to roll and dive around during some cool dodges is pretty addicting. I really enjoyed the movement in this game. The shooting not so much. I can’t put my finger on it but the shooting feels so stiff and hard to aim. Playing RE4 and RE5 was day and night different in terms of gunplay compared to RE6. It’s not good here I will say, the gunplay is pretty awful. Speaking of awful, for a game that focuses on actions and a ton of enemies, sure hates giving you ammo. Breaking a grate or killing an enemy sometimes gives you ammo, but most of the time you will get skill points. The skills in this game don’t really make a huge deal here from my experience. Only a few are worth using, so most are just filler. The drop rates are horrible, most of the time you will get skill points and no ammo so good luck. I don’t see why they added the skills in this game, they don’t play a big role here. Honestly you can play without them and your gameplay will barely change at all. The map design is trash. Jakes snow mission is torture, chris’s helicopter chase section is a pain at best, and much more. Also this game feels like an action flick with a taste of michael bay. I swear they have a love for explosions here. It's pretty comical. Oh and if you enjoy QTE’s, this is the game for you. Literally you will be doing QTE’s for the most pointless reason, like finding keys in a car for example. It’s hard to find something good here. I guess the Co-op is fun, if you don’t crash a lot. Oh and the enemy design is heartbreaking (they have half human/half grasshopper enemies). That says enough.

📜Story - The story is actually pretty interesting I will say. Playing through it, not so much. I just didn’t have a good time with some sections of the game. Chris was fun, Leon was good, Jake was meh, and Ada’s was the worst. This game is canon so if you are wanting to dive deeper into the Resident Evil Universe, you will learn a lot here from the story. It just felt kinda weak and forgettable from my experience.

🎭Multiplayer - In terms of co-op, it’s pretty fun. As fun as it gets for this game I guess. I would totally prefer company while playing this game since the co-op is actually really well implemented here (well kinda). I have experienced crashes on co-op and lost of connection sadly. It’s not rapid, but it can happen. The PVP is trash. Just get a friend and get the achievements since it’s so bland and a bore fest (also no one plays it).

🕛Playtime - To beat all the stories it takes around 20+ hours (depending on difficulty). If you focus on getting 100% it will take you around 60-70+ hours.

🎧Sound - I will say that the voice acting is actually pretty good. I really enjoyed the cutscenes a lot here. The music is a no no sadly. The soundtrack feels like an afterthought. Prepare to hear a lot of generic action music, also has the weakest safe theme in the franchise (from my experience).

❗Bugs❗- I didn’t notice any game breaking bugs or weird glitches from my experience. Besides the loss of connection while playing co-op at times.

🔅Performance - RE6 runs really well on my system. Being able to play max settings with a solid 60fps, it looked really smooth with no stutters or glitches.

This game gets a lot of hate from die-hard fans for a good reason. no, it doesn't feel like a resident evil game. It's supposed to be dark, a lingering fear of what's around the corner, anxiety inducing from lack of ammunition, and music that makes you feel eerie.

Resident Evil 6 has none of that. The game has 4 total campaigns and Leon's story is the closest you get to that feeling.

However, it's one of my most favorite Co-op experiences that you're gonna make great memories with a friend.

Each story offers a different flavor but ultimately tie into each other:
Leon's campaign: The darkest of the bunch. Offers a great story of finding the cause of the bio-terrorist attack.
Chris's Campaign: Your typical run & gun 3rd-person military shooter. Chris is tasked with eliminating the BOW's of the attack. If you want action, this is it!
Jake's Campaign: This mode is meant for people with Scopophobia (The fear of being stalked). Jake's story takes him on a mission to cure the virus, but is relentlessly hunted by a HULK looking brute monster that's been tasked with killing him.
Ada's Campaign: Unlocked after completing all the campaigns. This story just a filler that ties up unanswered questions gives more back story.

I also wanna mention how awesome the boss fights are in this game. Very intense and cinematic.

The developers tried to satisfy old fans, bring in new fans, and appeal to shooter fanatics. It didn't make a true resident evil game. But if you can get past the RE mindset, your gonna have a fantastic time playing this game with a friend.

Highly recommend. :)

If you’re wondering, like I was, as a fan of the series but a person who doesn’t like the action heavy entries as much, is this game worth playing? This review is for you.

I think the worst Resident Evil game is 5, hands down. If you got through that one, I think this one is better in every way. Better story, better gameplay, and better set pieces for sure.

I played it on Easy to minimize deaths because I hate having to repeat parts in shooters, and for me at least that ended up being a good call.

Pros
- 4 ~5 hour long campaigns that play like self contained stories
- Story is not amazing, but I found it pretty interesting
- Really cool set pieces
- Sections with different styles of gameplay (vehicles, for example)

Cons
- The default FOV made me motion sick (I have only felt this way in playing VR games with low frame rates and don’t normally get motion sick in any other games) and it can only be changed at the main menu, not in-game
- Even with “fixing” the FOV, the camera jerks around quite a bit through each campaign and at times I found myself still feeling a little dizzy
- Some fights feel really long
- Lots of quick time events that will end up killing you if you miss them
- Some segments where you die if you don’t move fast enough, and you end up dying excessively trying to memorize these parts
- Little to know horror or atmospheric stuff
- Very few puzzles (maybe 1 or 2 good ones in 20 hours)

While there is a lot to forgive, and this game doesn’t provide the survival horror that I love about the series, it really has a lot of fun moments. The four campaigns overlap some, which leads to the story being told in fragments which is kind of fun to piece together. It may not be the best Resident Evil game, but it is a good game, and it is definitely fun.

Overall Score: 7.5/10

Resident Evil 6 is the definition of a mixed bag.

At the time of development, RE6 was aimed to be the biggest game in the series with the largest group of devs working on it at one time. The hype for it was pretty palpable, especially after the gained interest in the series thanks to RE5 and its co-op.

RE6 gives you four campaigns to choose from and out of all four, only two are worth your time. The plot of RE6 is told from a collection of perspectives. You have Leon S. Kennedy paired with Helena Harper, a emotionally driven hot shot driven by desire for revenge. You have Chris making a return alongside new partner Piers Nivans who I think is one of the most boring characters in the series. Next to that, you have the McGuffin Jake Muller, son of Albert Wesker teamed up with a grown up Sherry Birkin from RE2, both of whom understandable have daddy issues and finally we have Ada Wong, she does have a partner; Agent but he was added as an afterthought after the initial games release in 2012 to make her campaign viable for co-op and only shows up should you play the co-op, solo, it is just Ada.

Leon and Helena's campaign takes the slow burn route, offering a take on horror more than any other. It certainly tries but it's not scary in the slightest, there will be no part where you are tense or scared to move forward, especially not when Leon can bust out dual pistols or Helena can run up to an enemy to do a flying kick.
Chris and Piers campaign is 100% action and 200% boring. I can't even pretend to like it and I struggle to get through it, please, do not play that one. Ever.
I can also say the same for Jake and Sherry, it tries to be a hybrid of action and horror with the scripted segments with Ustanak, which is like a knock off Nemesis. In the end it is just as boring as the Chris and Piers campaign.
Ada's campaign also tries for the hybrid route but does a slightly better job of it but since Ada is essential to the plot, seeing it from her POV makes her's instantly the most interesting and her weapon load out is easily most fun to play with too.

All of these characters and campaigns tell the grand story about one man who got friendzoned. I'm not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ joking, the reason for all the horrible events taking place in RE6 can be traced back to a villain who got friendzoned years ago by Ada...

Still with me? Good. The gameplay is definitely one of a kind for Resident Evil, they went all out on the action orientation for RE6. You have the ability to run, slide, run-180 slide-shoot, engage in melee combat at will, no need to stun an enemy to set up a round house kick or set up a melee combo like in RE5 but to stop the endless spamming of melee combat, Capcom introduces a stamina system and a new herb system in the form of pills that when taken can also instantly restore all stamina. It's crazy honestly and this robust system only really comes into it's own when you play the Mercenaries mode. Like any RE game, there are of course "puzzles" but I say it in such a way because they are hardly puzzles, they require next to no problem solving and are just a form of padding more than anything. Depending on the campaign will dictate the level of "puzzle difficulty" also. You still have limited inventory space but you burn through ammo so fast that you hardly have to do any inventory management and that system itself from an aesthetic point of view changes with each campaign. Gold is now replaced by points in the form of chess pieces that are used to purchase an extensive list of perks, of which maybe only five, not counting infinite ammo guns are of any use to you.
QTE's also return and with a vengeance. I swear, there are certain people on development teams who have never played with a keyboard before or just hate PC gamers because some of the QTE's combos are just insane, who's bright idea was it to make 'i + space' a viable QTE prompt?! If you don't like dealing with QTE's in games then you are going to have the worst time with them in RE6 because they are everywhere...

Graphically, I think RE6 is a small step back next to RE5. Granted this game has more enemies on screen at once with some more complex environments but there are times where character models look like they are just made of gel or some of the assets are low poly and low textured. It's not too much a distraction though.

RE6 boasts a decent soundtrack with a mix of great action pieces and slower, more ambient pieces. It's worth listening to the unique themes for each character duo on the main menu and I highly recommend you check out the Mercenaries theme; Heat on Beat 2012 and the track used in Agent Hunt mode.

The campaigns are not the only thing in the game to pass the time, there is also a wide selection of different modes. The Mercenaries mode makes a return and is probably the best thing about RE6 since that is where all the mechanics seem to work at their best. There is also the return of the No Mercy variant which get's absolutely nuts and highly suggest you play that mode with a friend. Agent Hunt mode allows you to invade another players main campaign run as certain enemies which is a neat concept but at the time I think it was a bit too ambitious to include such a thing, especially in Resident Evil and even more so when the main characters can be easily over powered against a basic zombie,
Next you have Survivor mode which is you against other main characters in the game, with some zombies on the field too, it shakes things up but the novelty wears off fast.
Predator mode is a 5v1 game mode where one player controls Ustanak and you have to take him down before he takes you out. Funny how this concept is now a common place, full fledged game in the form of DBD or even later down the line with RE: Resistance.
Finally there is Onslaught mode which I think is the best out of the extra game modes, it is like a blend of Mercenaries and Survivors, you and another player have to take down waves of enemies but each enemy killed is sent to the other player, so the more efficient you are, the more deadly you are to the other player, it is definitely worth checking out.

Honestly, there is more things wrong with Resident Evil 6 than there is right but it does just enough right for me personally to just barely recommend it. I don't think it is fair to just brush off RE6 as the black sheep of the main series because there is stuff in there worth experiencing but you will also have to deal with a lot of crap along the way, I'd suggest slogging through it with a friend too if possible to make it more fun.

RESIDENT EVIL 6 is not only a bad game, I consider it a disgrace to the name of Resident Evil, and an absolute spit in the face to fans of this beloved franchise.

RE6 returns absolutely iconic characters Leon S. Kennedy, Chris Redfield, and Ada Wong. It also introduces one new main character, Jake Muller, and 2 partner characters to Leon & Chris!

RE6 does an absolutely great job with the characters themselves, which is an amazing thing in this game considering every other thing this game suffers from immensely.

If you've played any other mainline Resident Evil game, you should know the charm & feel that RE Environments give off. They just feel like Resident Evil, y'know? Yeah, well, throw all of that charm out because RE6 does that for you already. Not a single environment in this game gives off that great feel that other entries always do. This game mainly takes place in 2 cities, and it feels as if they dropped Leon or Chris into the environment of an action-zombie movie with tons of neon lights & random explosions. Not only are the environments themselves bad, you ever like that environmental storytelling in other entries? Y'know, the notes and stuff you find lying around when you explore? Yeah, well, say goodbye to that amazing thing too. RE6 rips it away from you. "Hope you're okay with that!", I'm sure Capcom was saying.

RE6 contains 4 campaigns which all round out to about 5 hours long each, and I only played 2. Leon & Chris'. I could not allow myself to play the other 2 (Jake, Ada) as I seriously feel like I would go insane. This game is horrific to play with it's weird obsession of sending unnecessarily long hordes at you that seem like they are never going to end. They send random hordes that last so extremely long you don't think you will see the end of them, and when you finally do reach the end of one, you might as well prepare because another one is right around the corner.

Leon's hordes consist of casual zombies, similar to the Raccoon City Incident of RE2, but also zombies that regenerate into a new form after their death. This wouldn't be so bad, if they weren't constantly in hordes that seem to never end. Oh, yeah, try body-armored zombies too. So you're going against constant hordes with casual zombies, some of which regen into a stronger, new body, and also body-armored zombies. Sick, right?

And if that doesn't sound super bad to you, then I'm sorry if your a Chris Redfield fan who chose to play him first, because instead of that already annoying stuff Leon goes against, Chris is put in literal shootouts. Any encounter you find yourself in, it consists of you firing a gun at your enemy who is also firing a gun. They put that in hordes, too! So, you'll find yourself in a horde but instead of dealing with regeneration or body-armor, you are literally getting hit with gunfire. Fun, right? No. It's not. It sucks.

The stories themselves (atleast Leon & Chris) aren't ... that bad. Leon's is extremely forgettable, I barely remember what his plot even was, to be honest. Chris' on the other hand though, it's not forgettable. It's actually really sad, and it really shows that he has been through some bad stuff, and that doesn't stop as he's constantly going through more stuff during his campaign. It's sad and really gives you a new outlook on the "Great Chris Redfield!".

Other games in RE, such as 5, or even the side-series Revelations are really action-heavy, but somehow managed to hold onto that flare that Resident Evil always gives off. RE6 is action-heavy as well, but on a completely different level and shows no flare of Resident Evil. Such a disappointment.

You like good performance in your games, right? You know, smooth framerates, but also with some good looking graphics. Sorry to tell ya, this game isn't great in that category. Throughout both Leon & Chris' campaigns, I was dealing with constant stutters, and even full-on freezes at times. This game is from 2013.
This means: RE6 is a 2013 game running on a high-end PC from 2020(being mine, of course) and still stuttering to all hell with some actual freezes at times, and the game isn't even graphically insane. It looks okay of course, but it's not anything groundbreaking. Even the games made in RE Engine in recent years don't have this issue, so 6 must have really bad optimization.

The overall events of RE6 aren't very memorable, and it seems Capcom agrees as (atleast afaik) neither 7 or Village mention any of the events that occur in 6, which is a little odd as 6 does have some big events.

It's clear Capcom was trying to go for a big action-zombie movie type feel, and while they may have hit that mark a little bit, it completely ruins Resident Evil and had the franchise continued down this route, I am sure it would have met it's end. Thankfully, RESIDENT EVIL 7 biohazard came and fixed this whole mess and brought the franchise back to it's horror roots.

Capcom made an attempt at making Resident Evil something it's not, and they seem to have succeeded in that with RE6. As a newcomer to RE who has been playing thru all the games in a row, I have enjoyed them all up until this, and I feel this is a big spit in the face to the fans. Whatever this monstrosity was, never do it again Capcom. Thanks.

Resident Evil 6 is a highly action focused title in the series, attempting to expand itself in all directions with multiple inter-weaving stories, locations, and characters. While the game can be fun, it strays far from the series' survival horror origins, while most other aspects of the game remain, sadly, average. Like with the previous few titles, the game features third-person gunplay combat, peppered with quick time events, mutant creatures, and monster infested locales. While the gameplay appears to be like other third-person entries in the series, it diverges in tone and design. I struggled with whether to give it a thumbs up or down, which is perhaps the most telling.

As a game on its own, RE6 is not terrible. While it has its frustrating aspects, it is not devoid of interesting moments, and entertaining gameplay. However, as a Resident Evil game, RE6 is demonstrably poor, forgetting almost entirely the aspects which made former titles great, and which typified the series as a whole. Resident Evil itself coined the term 'Survival Horror' to describe the nature of its first title in 1996. This game focused on horror, limited resources, fight or flight choices, and a foreboding and mysterious atmosphere which came while investigating. RE6 is a plain action title, with the horror aspect relegated to set dressing. While the series has always had its cheezy moments, with B-movie schlock, RE6 instead feels like it is trying to be like every other action title that came out around the same time.

This trend in the series was already present in RE5, which in turn was responding to the success of RE4, which first introduced the third-person gameplay used in proceeding titles. RE6 triples down on this action aspect, expanding the 'partners co-op' style gameplay of RE5 into an absurd, convoluted, quasi-multiplayer experience. Not only do players have the option of co-op, but they will encounter other teams where missions 'cross'. While interesting theoretically, it further kills much of the horror survival vibe. Further, players can also opt to control a zombie, invading another player's game. If this all seems redolent of Left 4 Dead, you are right, as RE6 had cross over content with that franchise, and obviously took cues from it.

As a long time fan of the series, RE6 is a disappointment to me for all these reasons. But, I feel it would be unfair to wholly damn RE6 simply for being different. Indeed, L4D and the other action style games RE6 draws influence from are not bad games. For those considering playing RE6, just be aware that if you are looking for a survival horror experience or are a returning fan, you will be far better served with any title in the series other than this.

Resident Evil 6 (A Post Rant Review):
Resident Evil 6, it also has a number of smaller changes differentiating it from RE4 and 5. Firstly, all weapons are found in the game world. Weapons cannot be upgraded as in other games, but instead the player buys and equips 'skills'. These range from general damage, to increases drop rates, to more health or stammina.

Skills are bought with 'experience' which is dropped from enemies or found. This is, in esscence, the same as money in 4 & 5, though with more limited uses. With this being the case, I would have preferred if exp was acquired more like other games, given on defeating enemies or completing missions, as opposed to a pick-up. This would also insentivise players to beat levels with speed and flair. This seems to mostly be used to maintain a certain level of player power at all times through out the game.

For those players who do wish to upgrade their skills, they can replay previous missions taking their weapons along with them. There are a total of 4 main stories to play through featuring different characters fighting through a worldwide plot to infect the planet with the C-Virus. Stories 1-3 are done in pairs, each featuring a returning character from previous games. These are Leon, Chris, a grown-up Sherry Birkin, and Ada Wong. Jill is presumably on sabbatical.

Leon, Chris, and Sherry also have a new character to act as their partner. Leon gets Helena, a fellow government Agent who knows more about the outbreak than she lets on. Chris gets Piers, BSAA super sniper, and in some ways a reflection of Chris's early incarnation in STARS. Sherry gets Jake, a mercenary, whose unique genetic origin grants him immunity to the C-Virus. A reasonable effort is made to make each pair have some contrast.

Leon is earnest, but tired of the horror. Helena is desperate and fueled by a need for vengeance. Chris, having fallen into a amnesiac depression, has forgotten that he's a hero, a fact which Piers will try to correct with his own selfless devotion to the cause and to the BSAA. Sherry Birkin takes after Claire, being caring, brave, and determined. She and Jake develop a quick chemistry as Jakes devil-may-care attitude and mercenary position clash against her sincerity. They may honestly be the best pair, if only because they have been given the most space to be individuals, unhindered by previous games. Ada is her usual aloof self.

Each campaign is 5 missions, with each taking just over an hour, rounding out to just over 20 hours total. While some have praised the game's increased length compared to RE5, the split in stories and the multitude of characters makes much of the game a mess. Indeed, everything seems to be a hurry in RE5. The disaster is always in progress, with players desperately trying to act as quickly as possible. While this is not always true, the tone is present, and on many occasions it seems enemies continue to drizzle into the area, preventing the player form feeling safe enough to full explore.

The enemies themselves have some good designs, though I would have like to see more consistency for the C-Virus mutations. While most enemies have fairly solid designs, they feel somewhat inconsistent. Sometimes the C-Virus makes regular zombies, sometimes L4D style mutant infected, sometimes lizards, and sometimes bug mutants. The insectoid mutations really should have been the most prevalent. The game's frequent use of cocoons and other insect imagery would have fit a lot more. But sadly the game want to show you as many designs as it can with little thought, further preventing any consistent design through line.

The stories themselves are half-way self contained. Playing in order, Leo and Helena know the least, with Ada knowing the most about the whole incident. While an interesting concept, I often felt like I was re-treading old ground, and by the second campaign had already guessed one or two of the major secrets revealed in Ada's campaign. Overall, the stories are individually ok, and could even serve as decent RE plotlines on their own, but are ultimately made weaker by placing them interconnectedly in one game.

What remains, after all this, is the gameplay itself which is serviceable. Gun play is fun and fast. Melee is functions while the stamina bar keeps you from simply pounding the enemies into dust. Where it fails, it fails in the details. Small moments where the greater 'coolness' of the moment never gave way to player's perspective. This is where its impossible to tell if your damaging a boss, or where a camera angle gets in the way of the player. I found one of the most frustrating early examples of this was the fact that I could shoot or stab zombies prior to them re-animating, only for them to lunge at me when I passed.

These moments, while small, can add up over 20 or-so hours. Overall the gameplay is serviceable fun, and the plot can be entertaining. In fact, if RE6 were its own game, not part of the series, I would probably have praised it for its ambition. As it stands it is an ok game, and a bad Resident Evil game. It has my recommendation only for the former, and with a heavy grain of salt.

Resident Evil 6 is an excellent game marred by a terrible first impression.

The combat system is genuinely deep, with a firearm-melee combination that flows well together once you get used to it. It's a solid evolution of 4 and 5's, as melee can be used anytime instead of exclusively through contextual button prompts. And there are lots of different kill animations depending on the character, the weapon equipped, the type of attack, and the location of the enemy.

The problem is that the game is very light on tutorials and doesn't teach you about the mechanics much at all. I think the idea was that players could discover the combat system for themselves, but what ends up happening is first-timers just get knocked down a hundred times (quite literally because of the new stagger system) before anything seems to click. And even the inventory interface takes some getting used to.

But once it clicks, it's beautiful. I'm glad I stayed with it til the end. Even now, I'm still mastering the counter system, which I discovered by accident only after I completed the story.

This game made me feel dumber after playing it.  I have to say, to each their own if you like this game but there are fundamentally too many things holding it back for it to be enjoyable.

The camera is an absolute mess.  You'd think that'd be standard for the RE games, but the camera in this game shakes and moves around so much I was legitimately getting sick.

The weapons feel even more limp than RE5.  RE5's weapons were pretty limp in terms of feel, but RE6 takes it to a whole new level.  The skill system basically removes the weapon upgrades from 4 and 5 and makes it so that it lets you *think* there are multiple playstyles.  There aren't.  The game was designed in a way that's so...7th gen.

There's tons of quick time events, tons of walking segments, tons of interruptions, and the gameplay that is there is so unsatisfying outside of a few melee quick kills.

Let's go over the campaigns real quick:

Leon's campaign: If this campaign is supposed to be the best this game has to offer, then I genuinely feel bad for the people defending this game.  Even the Evil Within 1 is more scary, more balanced, smarter, and more fun than Leon's campaign.  This is supposed to be the horror chapter.
Chris's campaign: This is the real reason I played this game.  I wanted to know why he's the way he is in RE7 and 8.  To my lack of surprise, it's never explained.  His campaign is bloated, boring, and very "Gears of War"-lite.  It has the worst final boss of the bunch too.
Jake's campaign: This legitimately should have been a different game.  Jake would also work better if he wasn't a resident evil character and his whole "twist" was predictable since he teams up with barely lega-I mean Sherry.  This is basically the melee part and at times it works fine, but it's wrapped up with enemies that aren't designed very well, don't have interesting or cool designs, boring levels, and and awful QTE's/driving segments.
Ada's campaign: By this point, I was done.  She's the stealth character.  This pales in comparison to the RE4 chapter.  Again, it's bloated and boring.  The "twist" is again predictable.  It's also poorly explained.

I can't with this game.  I gave it a chance in the end after 10 years since it came out.  I figured I might have a different view on it.  Nope.  Not even close.  It's not even fun with Co-Op.  If you want a fun co-op game, there's tons of other options out there.

This game saved my life.

I am 27.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.

After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.

Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.

After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.

Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.

I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.

Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

When this game released, it was polarizing to a lot of people.

A group of people wanted Resident Evil to go back to the puzzle aspect it originally was, in the same vein as Resident Evil 1, 2, and 3.

Another group wanted it to be more action oriented, blazing through the trail that Resident Evil 4, and 5.

Then there was the new group of people whose first experience with the juggernaut franchise was this particular entry.

In a vacuum, RE6 is balls to the wall action, making you feel like you're in a typical Hollywood blockbuster film, filled with explosions, guns, charming if a bit corny dialogue at times, and witty one-liners that only Leon Kennedy can serve up and make you smile. This is the biggest the RE series has gone in terms of scope, both in story and gameplay. 

Gameplay is more responsive than ever before. No longer are you burdened by the tank controls. You can now run, shoot, dash, slide, melee, roll, take cover, and kick ass while doing it. The counter system is one of the most satisfying mechanics ever introduced into the series and mastering it makes you feel like one of the most badass people out there in the world. You've got turret segments, driving sequences, classic RE puzzles, QTEs, it's like a mish-mash of past and then-present gaming trends all blended together to make an action game that others should be compared to.

Story-wise, it's classic RE-schlock and if you haven't checked out by RE5, then RE6 should be a no brainer for you. But much like majority of the franchise, the devil is in the details. Playing through the game lets you get a cursory glance at the plot: a bioterrorist attack that results in zombies, orchestrated by a maniacal villain. But in reality, it's shockingly more fleshed out than the game presents itself to be. It's all in the files, which is a shame because it's a collectible that majority of the people would miss and not bother to collect except for the most diehard of fans.

When I first played this game way back in 2013 on my Xbox 360, I was admittedly confused at what in the world was going on, much like majority of the people that played it. I could follow along, but I could never understand why some characters did what they did, and what happened in between the moments of transition. Only through reading the files did I actually get the whole picture.

RE6's story is surprisingly well though out, though that is my opinion and others may disagree. If anything, the only thing I'm genuinely disappointed about is how some of the interesting developments presented in this mainline entry (Jake being who he is and what he's doing after, Sherry being present, Leon at the aftermath of it all, Ada's next gig) aren't really touched upon in RE7. The only "mainline character" we've seen thus far after RE6's outing is Chris. Hopefully Capcom revisits these interesting characters in a future entry--possible RE9 as of this review's writing.

All in all, Resident Evil 6 is a masterclass on how to make an amazing, responsive, and satisfying action game that was unfortunately marred with the baggage of its extensive franchise history. It had the unfortunate burden of satisfying different demographics that wanted vastly different things from it, 

Some would say it failed to satisfy any of those groups of people. I would have said the same thing. But looking back it now, I think it was alright. It's one of my favorite games in the franchise's every evolving history. No other game comes as close to the action that was presented here in RE6, and it really is a shame that no one else had tried since.

Resident Evil 6 is a game that can be very fun in short bursts, but the more you play it, the more its poor design and repetition start to show. While I still enjoyed getting back to killing zombies, especially in Leon and Ada’s campaigns, which came closest to the horror tone of the older Resident Evil games—the experience is weighed down by excessive action and constant repetition.

The gameplay is easily one of the game’s strongest aspects. The melee system, in particular, is genuinely fun and well-designed, adding variety and purpose to combat. Movement and combat feel smooth, and in isolation, the mechanics can be satisfying. However, that fun doesn’t last long because the game constantly throws the same encounters, enemies, and scenarios at you with very little room to breathe.

The story, while ambitious, is poorly structured. Telling it across four separate campaigns sounds interesting on paper, but in practice it makes the game feel bloated and repetitive. Seeing the same locations and cutscenes from different perspectives quickly becomes exhausting rather than engaging. While I do appreciate seeing how each character arrives at certain events, the execution drags the experience down instead of enhancing it.

Overall, Resident Evil 6 has moments of genuine fun and solid gameplay ideas, but they’re trapped inside a badly designed, overly long, action-heavy game that loses sight of what made Resident Evil special in the first place. It’s not a terrible game, but it’s a deeply flawed one, and far from the strong entry I once thought it was.

(For my non-British folk, people either love or hate marmite) 

The reason the game is both loved and hated leans on how you play the game and what you are looking for with a resident evil game. Most of the game falls into being more of a Third Person Action Game rather than a puzzley survival horror. .

What also makes a difference is the campaigns that you play. All the campaigns range from around 4-6 hours and all can be played with a friend or an AI if you hate people.  The campaigns also all intertwine so you'll play some areas a couple of times if you play through each campaign. 

In order from best to worst 

Leon's campaign - This campaign feels more like classic RE. You have more urban settings, a gothic church and a whole lot of zombies. There's some puzzle elements, some big mutated creatures including a literal T-Rex. Overall this campaign feels right. 

Jakes Campaign - This campaign features a new character whom is resistent to the C virus (One day we'll run out of letters) and Sherry from RE2. You travel the world dealing with a good mix of enemies from the other campaigns. Whilst a little disjointed at times, this campaign doesn't feel too out of place and there are some really fun areas and set pieces. 

Adas Campaign - This one should be played last as it generally ties everything together from the other campaigns with a kind of behind the scenes sort of story. This campaign is similar to Jakes in that you get a nice variety but the transitions between each chapter feel quite jarring as Ada just pops up wherever the story needs to be. You also get a lovely co-op partner in this that is incapable of doing anything outside of shooting. For some reason this hasn't been patched or changed so playing this one co-op is a bit lacklustre. 

Chris' campaign - You play as Chris the boulder punching machine as you take down mutant humanoid enemies for practically all of the story. This feels way more actiony and is the least fitting of the game. It's more like Gears of War than anything. This campaign feels like a slog overall. Definitely the least fun for me personally. 
 
Something worth noting is that the movement in this game is actually top notch and makes for some really fun gameplay. You can counter melee attacks, slider, roll and have a lot of manoeuvrability compared to other games in the franchise. The moment to moment gameplay is solid and there's plenty of enemy variety to take this into account. In fact the game overall has quite a bit of content from four campaigns to secrets hidden within the levels to levelling up skills and gunning for the highest ranks. There's a lot of replay value if completionism is your thing. 

Overall the game runs well, co-op works well (Aside from Ada's useless no nmed co-op buddy) and there's a lot of stuff to like here. It's wacky and it's tacky but if you're looking for a competent horror co-op shooter, RE6 is actually quite fun despite it being a bit of a mess.
