I'll preface this review by saying I didn't play mercenaries and I played all four campaigns in co-op with a friend of mine. I'll review each campaign individually since my thoughts vary wildly on each one. 

Leon's Campaign: Leon probably has the best campaign in my opinion (which isn't saying much). In Leon's campaign, you and secret service agent Helena Harper go on a journey to expose national security advisor Derek Simmons for his role in the assassination of the U.S. president. The story and writing in general isn't very good in this campaign (just like with most of the campaigns) but in terms of positives this campaign actually has a few. The opening outbreak in Tall Oaks is very reminiscent of Resident Evil 2/3 and the outbreak in Raccoon city, which was really cool to see back in 2012 when this game first came out. However, we now have modern, much better done, versions of said outbreak in the form of Resident Evil 2 and 3 Remake. The zombies, while not as fun to fight as the zombies in re2/3r, are definitely the best enemies to fight in this game, if only for the reason you don't have to worry about them shooting you mid-melee animation. This campaign also didn't have any terrible vehicle sections to pad out time. The set pieces in this campaign didn't feel as ridiculous as the set pieces in the other campaigns either. Finally, this campaign is definitely the most polished. In terms of things that drag this campaign down, the boss fights are pretty bad for the most part, the UI and inventory system in general is the worst in the series (you can't even give your partner items which is really strange since you could in re5). The quick time events are really in your face and annoying, even compared to re5 and especially compared to re4. Overall, I'd probably give this campaign a 6/10 as it wasn't horrible but there isn't really a reason to play it now. If you want to play a modern resident evil with zombies, just play resident evil 2 remake or even resident evil 3 remake. 

Chris' Campaign: When it comes to positives, the only one I can really think of is the writing in this campaign is slightly better than the others. In this campaign, Chris is working for the BSAA (once again) with his partner Piers Nivans trying to stop bioterriorst operations in Edonia and later China. While in Edonia, Chris' entire team is killed by "Ada Wong" and he gets PTSD and tries to drink his feelings away. Piers picks Chris up in a bar and convinces him to come back to the BSAA to help stop a bioterrorist group known as Neo-Umbrella from completely destroying a Chinese city (which later turns out to be a world ending threat). It is also revealed that "Ada Wong" is in charge of said group and Chris has to overcome his need for revenge in order to save the world. Overall, the story of this campaign wasn't great, but it was a lot better than the stories in the other campaigns. The story is also a lot better than the gameplay. Chris' campaign is basically that last 45 minutes of re5 stretched over 6.5 hours. It's basically a glorified cover shooter where you fight j'avo (some of the least fun enemies to fight in any resident evil game) in a bunch of poorly designed arenas for most of the game. Unlike the zombies, j'avo have guns so you'll often be shot down before you can even run up and punch the ever-living ♥♥♥♥ out of them. Chris' campaign also has one of the worst driving and flying sequence I've ever had the misfortune of playing. Overall, I'd give Chris' campaign a 4/10.

Jake's Campaign: In Jake's campaign, you basically run around and punch j'avo with a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ combo system. His story is that he's a Mercenary fighting in Edonia, but for some reason, he's unaffected by the C-virus (the virus that turns people in j'avo). Sherry Birkin shows up and basically says he's the key to making a vaccine for the virus and he needs to come with her. While trying to get out of Edonia, they encounter Ustanak, a tyrant like monster whose goal is to capture Jake for Neo-Umbrella. They end up getting captured by neo-umbrella and sent to China so the rest of the game can happen. The only other thing worth mentioning about Jake is he's apparently the son of Albert Wesker, which feels really stupid and tacked on. In terms of gameplay, this campaign is really bad. The level design, particularly the level where you're escaping the mountain is absolutely atrocious and Jake just isn't fun to play as. Ustanak isn't nearly as memorable as Mr.X or Nemesis and just serves as a quick time event generator for most of this campaign. The vehicle sections in this aren't as bad as Chris' but they're basically on rails and control really poorly. Overall, I'd give this campaign a 3/10.

Ada's Campaign: Finally we get to Ada's campaign. This campaign only really exists to tie up loose ends left over from the other three campaigns and the only positive I can say about it is it's really short, not even three hours long. In terms of polish, it's pretty clear this campaign was basically an afterthought. Ada doesn't even canonically have a co-op partner with her. If you play this campaign in co-op, you play as Ada while the 2nd player gets to play as some generic soldier guy who can't do a damn thing except kill enemies. He can't even open doors or progress through the game really. Just about every single one of Ada's levels is reused from previous campaigns, she has a helicopter flying sequence at the end which is easily the worst vehicle section in the entire game, and this campaign is by far the glitchiest of the four. Overall I'd probably give this campaign a 2/10. 

In conclusion, Re6 isn't nearly as bad as people claimed it was when it launched. This game isn't even as bad as a lot of the later silent hill games. But the I can't help but feel that people who think this game is secretly a masterpiece and always was are just wrong. The amount of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and jank you have to ignore to come to such a conclusion is just way too much in my eyes. This is definitely one of the weakest mainline resident evil games, only beating Re0 and Code Veronica in my eyes. I guess if you're really bored and have nothing else to play you could try this game, for anyone else I'd recommend steering clear.

After three years of playing this game on and off, I finally finished all four campaigns — almost 40 hours total. Each campaign delivers a unique storyline, and together they fuse into a surprisingly coherent narrative. The story here is one of the best I’ve played in a long time, and paired with the combat system, it made this Resident Evil title extremely enjoyable.

Leon’s campaign is incredibly cinematic, Chris’s ending genuinely brought tears to my eyes, Jake’s story adds a romantic angle, and Ada is the perfect thread that ties everything together. This game pulls the action feel of RE4 and RE5 into a more modern take on a classic Resident Evil plot.

If you don’t pay attention, it can be easy to lose the thread — especially when you’re playing with someone who won’t stop talking during cutscenes. I swear I could barely follow Ada’s and Chris’s campaigns because of this.

I like the serpent emblem collectibles and the inclusion of Mercenaries, but I’ll admit I miss the small, isolated environments from RE0 through RE4. I’m playing all of these as a tribute before RE9 releases, and so far, Resident Evil 6 sits at a solid 8/10 for me.

My Breakdown

Gameplay – 27/30
This is the most fun I’ve had with gameplay in a Resident Evil title. Herbs being turned into tablets and instantly usable is great, the weapon modes are fun, and the level structure flows well. Getting separated from your partner at times really helped immerse me in the world.

Story – 24/30
The characters are written well, and the campaigns weave together nicely into one overarching story.

Audio – 4/10
The audio design itself is fantastic — Capcom always nails this — but in multiple points across the four campaigns, the audio randomly cut out. I missed chunks of dialogue and story because of it. The gunshots, though, are the best in the series.

Visuals – 8/10
Great cinematics, and I like how HUD elements change between campaigns. The purple aesthetic of the main menu pairs well with the orange-and-blue hues used throughout the story.

Voice Acting – 10/10
Matthew Mercer, Roger Craig Smith, Troy Baker, Laura Bailey — and that’s just the obvious ones. The performances and line delivery sell the emotional beats extremely well.

Music – 7/10
The opening track will probably be stuck in my head until the day I die. Suspenseful and memorable.

Final Score: 80%

Do I recommend this game?
Yes.
Do I recommend playing it with a friend?
Also yes — though if you’re trying to rush through the story, maybe play solo… otherwise it becomes too funny.

This is one of the most discussed games in the Resident Evil series and I understand why.
It´s a common fact that this game is the most action-filled main title in the series. But that doesn´t necessarily make it a bad game, as long as the action is fun. Which it is, because it´s ridiculous non-sense you can laugh about. Watching the cutscenes of the game is the same experience as watching the RE movies starring Milla Jovovich. It´s trash, but it´s enjoyable trash. The storylines of the the campaigns are held together by coincidences combined with explosions, crashing helicopters and the extreme mutations of your enemies. 
And while we´re at it, let´s talk about the four campaigns, wich can all be played in co-op.
Each campaign revolves around two heroes, following their own orders and motivations. However, you don´t play four seperate stories, because the storylines of the four campaigns all merge into one. While playing one campaign, you can meet the protagonists of the other campaigns, doing the things you do in their story. This can lead to a bunch of "Oh now I understand"-moments while you puzzle the story of RE VI together. You even have a timeline including all cutscenes from all four campaigns, where you can look up which events happened at the same time or are connected to another. The only downside of this concept is that you sometimes have to do the same battles or boss fights again, but with another character. 
But of course, RE VI has some other problems, too. The savepoints can be very unfriendly, some enemies are very annoying, some death animations are waaayyy to long and some boss fights leave you clueless what you have to do. While the graphics are overall ok, there are points where the game looks like straight from PS1 era, including blurred textures on 2D-houses. Another problem of the game is its action. I know, I´ve said earlier that it´s fun because it´s ridiculous, but sometimes it´s TOO ridiculous, to a point where it destroys immersion and creates plotholes. 
The co-op works very well most of the time, except the last campaign, where the player not hosting the session has to play a nameless agent, who can´t interact with most objects and riddles. So my friend and I decided to play this campaign alone.

Overall, RE VI is a good Resident Evil game to have fun with, and it´s definitely not as bad as its reputation. 
To conclude my review of this game, I once again have to compare it to the Resident Evil movies starring Milla Jovovich. They are fun to watch, but they won´t win an Oscar.

Another issue is the lack of a comprehensible menu. It seems that the standard wheel menu is an invention of 2018 or so. Old games haave incomprehensible, complicated menus. I simply fail it figuring out to even find a menu screen of what weapons I have. Sure, I could google that on reddit, but at some point I have to consider whether I want to make the effort.

Lastly, and related again to poor menu design, I simply fail at configuring mouse sensitivity, and that is SUPER ANNOYING.
We know from the RE8 Demo that Capcom magically sucks at offering a menu option where you can set mouse sensitivity: If I move the mouse 1cm to the right, how much does my character rotate? Now, in RE6 there is no clue how to set that factor, and it is faaaaaaar too large! You tip the mouse and rotate like five times. Man kann mit dem Spiel Spaß haben, aber es gibt viele Sachen die stören. Erstmal überhaupt das ich das Spiel nie im ersten Versuch starten kann, es ist immer  nur ein Blackscreen da und dann muss ich das Spiel neustarten. Selbst RE5 hat das Problem und da muss man sich etwas herunterladen das es dann funktioniert. Es ist ein Resident Evil Spiel aber es fühlt sich nicht wie ein echtes Resi an, es ist viel zu action reich. In allen Resi Spielen davor musste man immer Abstand von  Zombies halten, selbst in den action reichen RE 4 und Re5 musste man Abstand halten. Aber hier kann man die Zombies einfach mit den Fäusten schlagen und so ist das Gefühl der Angst gegenüber den Zombies komplett weg. Es gab mehrere Orte mit Dunkelheit die einem ein gruseliges Gefühl vermitteln sollte, aber weil es so action reich ist fühlt man es einfach nicht. Desweiteren hat man viele unnötige und schlechte Veränderungen unternommen. Statt normal die Kräuter zur Heilung zu nehmen, nimmt man jetzt einzeln Tic Tacs. Der Multiplayer hat sich auch verschlechtert im Vergleich zu RE5. In Re5 gab es immer nur ein Item und man konnte sich die Waffen geben. Aber hier in Re6 hat jeder seine eigenen Items. Desweiteren sind die Räume enger gestaltet als in RE5 und so bleibt man oft mit dem anderen Teammate stecken. Und die Bosse kommen viel zu oft zurück. Die meisten Bosse kommen immer wieder zurück und so nimmt es einem das Gefühl der Befriedigung weg, wenn der Boss eh wieder kommt.
Kommen wir nun zur Story also Spoiler. Leons Kampagne hat mir am wenigsten gefallen. Nicht nur der Fakt das Leon nun einen anderen Synchronsprecher hat als in RE4, sein Charakter hat mir hier nicht gefallen. Am Anfang von RE6 wollte er noch eine Person retten, die er in einer Überwachungskamera gesehen hat, aber später im Game, überall wo er hin geht bringt er nur Tod und verderben. In der Kirche, wo all die anderen Überlebenden sind bringt er ein Monster raus und viele sterben aber nachdem er das Monster besiegt hat, geht Leon einfach weiter und erkennt nicht mal an das er für die Tode verantwortlich ist. Helena mochte ich auch nicht so sehr. Sie hat die ganze Zeit etwas verheimlicht, aber sie hatte immer die Zeit es zu erklären und was interessiert mich was mit ihrer Schwester passiert. Chris und Pears Kampagne mochte ich am meisten und die duo dynamik war auch sehr gut. Chery und Jake ist ein interessantes Konzept, weil deren beiden Väter ja acuh mal zusammen gearbeitet haben. Bei Ada Wong fragt man sich wieso ausgerechnet sie ein double hatte. Warum hat man sie ausgewählt hat. Generell hat man auch den Virus kaum erklärt. In  all den anderen Teilen wurde es sonst immer gut erklärt egal ob das T-Virus, G-Virus, Las Plagas, etc. Aber hier gibt es kaum Erklärungen zum Virus.
Kommen wir hier aber zu den Paar Vorteilen. Es gibt hier 20h Spiel content, die man alle im Multiplayer spielen kann. Die Grafik sieht sehr gut aus, auch für ein 10 jahre altes Spiel.

A lot of people hate on RE6 because it tries to carry on the cheesy action shooter trope that Capcom was pushing the series in since the success of RE4, some will say "It's not Resident Evil!" because you just run around through 4 guided storylines, except 4, 5, 7 and 8 all follow the same formula.

As a action cover-shooter it's probably one of the best I've played despite the cover system being almost completely pointless. The movement system, CQB and gameplay mechanics all seem alien at first but once you begin to understand them they all perfectly blend together to make the game into a crazy gun-fu simulator, like how the RE: Vendetta movie portrays the series. There's always new tech to learn and you feel like a badass every time you play if you're willing to learn.

The interconnected campaign system is really cool, you can tell they really focused on multiplayer and co-operative play with this entry. There are 4 campaigns and all of them have points where they cross over into the other's campaign. Leon's campaign has large fights where Ada shows up to help him and Helena, if another player is at that section of Ada's campaign at the same time you are they'll actually join into your lobby as Ada temporarily before splitting off again. All of the campaigns seem to overlap story-wise too and there are little tellers to the other campaigns as you play through them. There's a point in Leon's campaign where you take a plane to China, if you look at the TVs on the plane you can see live news feed of an attack in China going on with members of the BSAA fighting them. When you play Chris' campaign you'll actually push aside the guy who was recording that live news feed and experience that fight. There's a couple other points where this happens and if you're a big RE fan you'll love the cross-overs and character reunions, otherwise this system doesn't really work anymore because people are all playing with the feature turned off or more likely you wont be able to find anyone playing at the exact same time as you which sucks because it's a really cool feature that I imagine felt amazing when the game was released.

The game has so much extra-content and honestly most of my hours on the game come from playing through the extra-content. I would go through it all but it's got your standard RE Mercs mode where you have a set limit of enemies and you kill for time and score etc, as well as a handful of other modes that are super fun to play as a group.

HOWEVER, this game does have some pitfalls...
Mainly, I would've liked more DLC that included characters from other RE games, for example RE5 included Rebecca despite her not being in the story. This is just my personal problem I guess because the game does already come with 8 (9 but Carla is just a reskin of Ada) unique characters all with different weapons and take-downs, I just sort of exhausted them and would've liked getting characters like Wesker, Rebecca, Carlos, Jill & HUNK for example.

On the topic of HUNK, Ada's campaign is honestly the worst campaign in the game and Co-Op functionality was clearly implemented last minute, you're better off playing the campaign completely solo because the campaign features Ada and a character added in a free update called "Agent" who serves no purpose other than allowing another player to tag along during Ada's campaign. The worst part about him is that he can't even interact with things and it completely ruins all immersion when Ada grapples somewhere and Agent just pops in out of nowhere because he's not actually supposed to be there. Why didn't they just make HUNK Ada's partner? At this point in the story Umbrella has collapsed and HUNK is supposedly a 'Legendary Merc-for-hire', both of them have had ties with Umbrella and have very notable reputations. Could've done a whole lot more with Ada's campaign instead of making it only about her relationship with Derek Simmons. Would've even allowed for a cool cliche moment where [spoiler] Ada and Carla get into a melee fight and HUNK doesn't know which Ada to shoot [/spoiler] ! Instead it's just about a government official being creepy and stalking Ada because she's hot and destroying most of the world for no real explained reason other than him having an obsession with someone who he's only met in person like twice. Frankly this makes for a terrible villain and highlights how they ran out of ideas on how to continue the story after killing Wesker off. If we had HUNK, the game would've definitely more attractive to a lot of people and we'd have another unique character to play around with in the extra-content.

They've also done the RE Character thing where they introduce these amazing characters only to just make them disappear from existence from every other title in the franchise. Jake Muller, the biological son of Wesker - A pretty big title and name to live up to hasn't been heard from in RE7 or RE8, he just flirts with Sherry and it implies they become close and then he just goes around the world helping people. That's it. Despite him being near superhuman and a carrier of Project W (<- Uncertain but for some reason he has antibodies to the C-Virus so this is the only logical explanation) he just disappears...
Same with his partner Sherry who actually still has the G-Virus in her blood which shows how it allows her to regenerate wounds also disappears throughout RE7 and 8 with no explanation.

Piers Nivans was the Sheva replacement and he was an amazing character, arguably he was a better squadmate for Chris than Jill was in terms of their compatibility and dynamic, Chris being a teacher who fell from grace and Piers being there to pull him back to reality and remember his core values, amazing. Unfortunately Capcom gave us the finger and [spoiler] Killed him as well as gave him an off-screen death [/spoiler] which is such a waste of a great character.

Jill also isn't mentioned at all, she just vanished too.

As someone who's really invested in the lore and story of Resident Evil, for a continuation of the series it adds literally nothing because everything that happens wraps its-self up in the story and writes its-self out. It could've not been made and would've had no effect on the story of RE7 & RE8.

Pitfalls aside, if you're new to Resident Evil I recommend this title as an entry title into the series, it's so dummy simple and entertaining.

The base line premise of Resident Evil 6 is an over arching story told over the course of 4 seperate campagins that overlap with each other at various points. With each campagin having its own feel and own enemies that match the overal tone of each setting with the downside being you may run into the same foes over various campagins. For the good this means lots of shooting and even some melee combat mixed in with the overall gameplay mentality. The bad on other hand is that some may see this as a departure from the traditional survival horror style of gameplay that Resident Evil was originaly founded on and not a true Resident Evil game. As there less of a focus on the moment to moment tension and having to conserve resources while balancing out the need to move forward. 

If you are looking for an accesible action oriented Resident Evil game this is it right here. Good value for money and on sale totally worth it with the extra modes included. If however you are looking for more of a traditional survival horror game then you won't find it here and if anything you should pass on this.  As the overall theme here is action. [hr][/hr]

Sure, the game often wrestles the camera control away from you in nauseating ways even in the middle of fights to go "Look at that thing! It's important! Are you looking? Are you looking?", often for a double-digits amount of seconds.

But your characters can do unnecesarily flashy, flippy wrestling moves that end up exploding the heads of the enemies.

And, sure, one of the campaigns starts with an unskippable, +15 minutes, infuriatingly slow forced walk segment that pointlessly tries to create atmosphere in an action game that 5 minutes earlier had you escaping from an exploding jet that turned a main street into lava.

But you can grab a plastic explosive, sprint slide into the middle of a horde of zombies, place it mid slide, turn around and detonate it in one fluid move, all while your partner spams a dedicated "That was awesome bro" button.

And yeah, it is true that the story is a bunch of nonsensical impossible to follow ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with characters that you won't care about.

But there are bossfights that span entire hour-long chapters with so many over-the-top transformations that they break the scale of the ridiculous and go back to being awesome.

For every frustrating QTE there is a fight with ancient skeletons with dynamite strapped to their chests. For every excessive, ridiculous slow-mo scene, there is another set-piece in which you and your partner protect a guy that is setting C4 on something, while being attacked by giant mutants and guys whose bottom halves have turned into insect legs. Yeah there is a forced stealth section in an environment that is entirely built of white textures, but oh my god, [b] [i] your partner just jumped over a helicopter with a motorcycle! [/i] [/b]

[hr][/hr]

Some will say something along the lines of, "It's not true Resident Evil".

But Resident Evil has been a top down portable game with "stop-the-bar-in-the-right-place" combat. Resident Evil has been a coop survival horror game based around short levels. Resident Evil has been a lightgun shooter. Resident Evil has been an action coop game with tactical elements agaisnt human enemies. Resident Evil has been... Whatever the hell Umbrella Corps was.

At this point, Resident Evil has mutated more than any of the monsters featured on it! Why can't a game where you use a 50 cal sniper rifle as a shotgun with the quickfire mechanic be a Resident Evil game, huh?!

This is a Resident Evil game, alright. It's a Resident Evil game for those whose favorite part of RE and RE2 were shooting the tyrants with the rocket launcher. It's a Resident Evil game for those who thought that taking down the helicopter in RE3 was kickass. It's a Resident Evil game for the true conoisseurs that know, deep down, that the island was the best part of Resident Evil 4.

I now understand why RE6 is often considered "the bad one". 

Gameplay: For a game that leans into being an action game it feels clunky to actually play. The experience of using the menus is clunky, the game-feel is off, the action feels worse than its predecessor, and there is little positive to say. If you DO like the feels of the combat and movement, it will be CONSTANTLY interupted by QTEs and cutscenes. QTEs aren't inherently bad, and Capcom themselves made Asura's Wrath the same year where the QTEs feel right at home and I can't imagine the game without them, but in RE6 they are constant and feel out of place. If you are playing the the game single-player like I did, you'll have even more to complain about as you wait for your AI partner so you can open every other door. RE6 loves repeating itself by constantly splitting the 2 players up and doing the "player 1 has to do something so player 2 can progress forward to use something that allows player 1 to progress" thing which isn't bad in itself, but in one 5 hour campaign it happened at least 3 times, which means I'm just waiting for the AI to do what it has to do. Even more often it's a case where one player has to lift the other to a spot to open the way, which, playing single player with an AI meant lifting up the AI and waiting every time. Riveting.

Story: I only did the Leon campaign, but boy oh boy is the story contrived. So many moments feel like they are only there so the campaigns can all meet up. You can have mulitple campaigns meet up, that's cool, but its often enough that I FEEL that design choice being made. At so many of the points where Leon ran into/interacted with the other groups it didn't feel like "oh wow it's one interconnected story" it felt like "oh wow they shoehorned this in here to try and give this some sense of cohesion." On top of things feeling somewhat slopped together, so often the presentation was just the weridest choices of when to jump to in-engine cutscene, or pre-rendered cutscene.  There were quite a few moments where I had to wonder "why wasn't this just a voice line?" because it was just the camera cutting away from gameplay to point to a sign. You have two characters who talk to each other a lot, having one of them say "hey this is our train to [wherever]" would be a lot better than hard stopping the game for 10 seconds to zoom over to a sign that says that. In the last chapter there is a moment where you jump from in-engine cutscene to a pre-rendered cutscene to  like a frame of gameplay perspective right back to an in-engine cutscene. WHY? Top that all off with an incredibly inconsistent  tone and you have RE6. Why does driving over a single zombie spin out a bus or be a threat in a cutscene but walking down a road Leon can roundhouse kick their heads and pop them like damn balloons? Tonally jumping around isn't always bad but I'm more likely to forgive it when I'm actually enjoying the rest of the experience.

What did I like? Well it looked nice for a 2012 game and the aesthetic in general was a better fit for the series than RE5's brighter areas. Unlike RE5 I didn't have a lot of problems with my AI actively making bosses harder/impossible but I feel like that's less because they improved them and more because they don't have enemies and bosses with any special weakpoints that require coordination to hit. 

Overall RE6 is poor. I've played games that are worse at a technical level but there is usually at least something redeeming that makes the experience good, RE6 is just bland.

As far as "survival horror", this is not it. You're given plenty of ammo to shoot through enemies and recovery items at easier difficulties in a way that's more akin to action games. That's not a bad thing as it's a very fun action game particularly if you want to go the co-op route. The AI is also solid enough that you won't be playing guardian to your partner. If you somehow do run out of ammo, then there's an okay melee option built-in so you can literally beat up zombies with your bare hands while the AI covers you! It's a little ridiculous but really fun to just launch yourself at your enemies.

Fair notice: There are QTEs, and the button-mashing did not necessarily endear me. Furthermore, certain sections switch to fixed camera angles that definitely threw me for a loop.

Verdict: Particularly on sale, this has good playtime-to-price value. If you're looking for something more on the survival horror spectrum, this isn't it, but it still manages to be a fun action game if you're into shooters.

[h1]Resident Evil 6[/h1]
*****************
If you go into this game having played basically any other Resident Evil game (even 5) you'll probably be disappointed.


Straight out the gate you'll notice how over the top the game is. City wide zombie infection, explosions everywhere, helicopters flying into buildings, an overwhelming arsenal of weapons and items, obnoxious skill-check QTEs, "grimy" and now militaristic main characters submerged in this layer of forced edginess. And that's just in the first 10 minutes, maybe less.

I'm all for a bit of fun and absurdity, but as opposed to just being chaotically too much like the beloved [spoiler]Chris v. boulder[/spoiler] boss fight of RE5, this game seems to try to take itself seriously. Every level is like an hour to two hours depending on your pacing as a player and it very quickly becomes a chore to try and play through the game. If they had even split each level into 3 parts (as it almost feels that it was intended) it would play smoother. Events refuse to defuse tension, ever-constantly building and sustaining climactic events, and as a result it feels draining to play. Even completing one level can sap the energy out of me to play any more of the game for the day.  Which is rough, because I am a fan of the story, as stupid as it feels to say that in regards to such a busy and messy game.

I like the idea of four campaigns intertwining. I like the concept of each campaign being themed and playing slightly differently. I like the idea of each duo of main characters facing their own dilemmas and moral stressors. I like a lot of the ideas presented actually, but God d*mn are there far too many. It seems as if no idea was scrapped, filtered, questioned. It feels bloated. Sorta messy. Really, really busy.

The controls are a nightmare. Sure you get used to the movement and dodging and the mechanics upon mechanics upon mechanics eventually, but I genuinely think that I'll never get used to the God awful menus. The game has basically no horror, and the inventory in turn feels cramped in a "welp, guess I'm discarding grenades again" way, as opposed to the tight and in turn tense management of previous and future RE instalments.


I think that I have so much to say and even more that I won't say (as to limit review size) because of how much potential I see in the game. Please don't get me wrong, I've enjoyed the game so far. I've disregarded it as Resident Evil and now I'm having fun just trying to navigate all the sensory overload this clusterf*ck presents while playing a fairly decent shooter. But I'm also spending most of the game in co-op with a friend laughing about the bucket-loads of poor executive decisions made. 

If you go into RE6 with expectations, you'll be let down. Even without expectations you might be let down. But if you manage to stick with it you might find a bewildering gem of batsh*t crazy that could tickle your funny bone. Yet I would not recommend attempting to do so lightly....

I'm not going to lie: this was an incredible game for me and my older brother, and it was one of the best co-op games we bonded over in my childhood that I'll never forget since it was the game that made me feel close to him despite his detachment from me when I was younger.

We are in good terms now and as I purchased this game when it was on sale, it brought back so many memories for my brother and me when we booted it up and saw the title screen. We genuinely spent a couple of days together playing the various campaigns and enjoying it immensely together as we really felt nostalgic with it.

The storyline was engaging and interesting to play through. It took me some time to get used to the controls again, but after I figured out how everything worked, it wasn't too difficult. Although there were some parts that were so difficult to manage that they required too many tries and attempts to get them right, I'm not sure if I should blame the controls, the game section, or us (I'm more or less specifically talking about Jake's campaign snowmobile section, which has always been annoying to get through and was honestly our hated section together).

People have criticized the game for not being scary enough or being too action-packed, which I respect and understand. After all for almost everyone the main idea behind Resident Evil is that you must survive against dangerous and challenging enemies while dealing with the horror of it all, through various scenarios and locations that are terrifying to traverse, but this game was more or less different from that, and I could say it focused more on the story aspect, which was action-packed rather than the series' actual horror.

For the most part, I was completely enamored with this game. It was enjoyable to play with my brother, and we had an absolute blast with just really going through with one of my favorite childhood classics. We might even play it again in a few years simply to relive the nostalgia.

If you're looking for a game to play with a loved one or a friend, I highly recommend this; it'll be a great bonding experience for even casual players and fans of the franchise.

If you're looking for a game that "should embody the Resident Evil horror experience," look elsewhere because this is certainly not it.

Resident Evil 6 - just like Resident Evil 4 and 5, is taking the franchise into a completely new direction.
Resident Evil 4 tried to combine atmospheric horror with action and absolutely succeeded in doing so.
Resident Evil 5 removed the atmospheric horror with more action and COOP, but absolutely succeeded in making a story-rich, fun COOP experience, proving that Resident Evil didn't need to be scary all the time.

Resident Evil 6 kind of tried to do everything. Horror, Action, COOP, Puzzles and cheesy lines. It sucks.
Straight up. The gameplay and story of Resident Evil 6 are complete garbage.

Now you're wondering why my review is positive, right? Is it because the COOP is fun? No it's not. The game is buggy and clunky to the point where it's not fun to play. Now why is my review positive!?

One very simple reason: Not all of the campaigns in the game are bad.

Chris' and Piers' campaign just feels like a generic, trashy, clunky third person shooter HOWEVER it has good story points and following Chris' PTSD ridden rampage is just interesting.

Leon's and Helena's campaign is BY FAR the best one of the three. It kinda feels as if you're playing Resident Evil 4 with a pinch of Resident Evil 2, but in COOP. Lots of horror, classic zombies and puzzles. Helena as a character however is annoying and ruins the whole experience most of the time because the entire story is Leon carrying her useless, whiny butt through the campaign. It's almost a CRIME from Capcom's side that it wasn't Claire they gave Leon as a COOP partner.

Sherry's and Jake's campaign is the absolute worst pile of retconning trash I've ever seen. Adult Sherry is cool and I loved the cutscenes where her G-Virus infection actually gave her some smaller superhuman abilities and all, but Jake? Jake is just like a piece of cardboard with the personality of [insert every 90s high school jock/bully here]. He literally feels like bootleg Shadow the Hedgehog. My biggest gripe is how Sherry in cutscenes has superhuman abilities and Jake does too, however Jake also has his during gameplay meanwhile Sherry has nothing except for a badly made hitbox. That and their story is literally only plot relevant in one part of the game, which makes you ask yourself in the end: "Why did I play this then?".

Overall...Just sit through this game and enjoy it as much as you can by making fun of how clunky and buggy it is. It's kinda "The Room" of the Resident Evil franchise. SO bad that it's good.

This is a tricky game to recommend. I would only say that if you're a huge fan of the Resident Evil series that you should give this game a try. But tbh, you're not missing much since a lot of people consider this as one of the dumbest/worst resident evil games in the series. 

This is NOT a horror game as much as it tries to advertise it. There is nothing scary and it's just filled with over the top ridiculousness. It doesn't have a theme or identity. It tries to do everything in one package. Which at first sounds good, but it doesn't work. You end getting a subpar experience in the horror, action, story and etc. 

You get 4 campaigns:
- Leon is "horror" focused. 
- Chris is action focused
- Jake is over the top action. 
- and Ada (that ties it all together)  

It tries to please everyone and it doesn't work. Myself who enjoys horror, never felt scared or tense throughout the Leon scenario. Then when came to the other campaigns, I slogged through them and didn't really have a memorable experience. When it came to end of the game and pieced together the plot. I just didn't care. 

For example. In the Chris Campaign. [spoiler] I never felt a connection to him. In the game, he suffers from PTSD when his entire squad gets wiped out. So he goes on this need for revenge. But for me, it never made any sense from his character because of the previous games. He has lost very close S.T.A.R.S team members in the original game. He didn't have this mental breakdown or stop fighting monsters when his closest friend and partner, Jill Valentine was assumed dead in Resident Evil 5. So it feels out of character, or does he care more about strangers than his friends?  [/spoiler] 

In Jake campaign. You will literally not give a toss about anything. Even when they bring characters and plot pieces relating to the previous games. I got this impression that it was poorly tagged in just to have any relevance to Resident Evil timeline. Like, these characters could've been anything or anyone else. But one writer just went; "Oh yeah, he/she is X long-lost family relative that wasn't mentioned or hinted in the past". It makes Sonic fan fiction writing look more appealing than whatever the writers did this.

They didn't keep it simple and tries tackle a lot of elements. But it ruins the flow and again, just get tacky and has a terrible structure in the story.  

The controls is great. I enjoy being able to move and shoot, melee, dive and sprint. But it somewhat backfires even during Leon horror segments. It's okay for an action sequence, but not so great when it's trying build tension. It's fun, but it's far from a resident evil game. What I also noticed is that the character interface is different for each campaign. So after playing several hours on Leon. You'll have get used to the new interface for Chris, Jake and Ada. While it's not a big issue, it can be distracting. 

There is ZERO puzzles, and focuses entirely on the action. Which if you're looking for that experience with a friend. It can be a good experience. It can get comical in a lot of places where the game will get even more ridiculous every chapter. Which if you're with a friend, can be a good laugh. If you felt like the planning and tension in the previous games wasn't your cup of tea. Then you can strap yourself in and enjoy the ride for this fast-faced game. 

The theory behind this is because of the Resident Evil 5. Sadly, despite people saying that the previous titles are miles better. Resident Evil 5 focused more on the action and sold vastly more than any of the other games. I think this made Capcom believe that Resident Evil 6 should be taken in this direction. 

There is only a few good elements in this game. But I can't honestly recommend it even if you pay the discounted price. I can say you should play this if you have friend who is also interested and enjoys Resident Evil...for just one weekend. If you're buying this on a sale and want to play it yourself. You might be able to enjoy some elements. This is not the worst thing or even a terrible game, but it fails to be gripping compared to other games. 

It offers a massive variety and the game gives over +20 hours playtime. But in this game case, more doesn't mean better. I'd say skip it and go play something else.

Graphics are good for a game that came out in 2012. Voice acting is good. Music is pretty decent. Even though the game is dated, for the amount of content, the asking price seems far.  	[*] Unpolished gameplay sections
	[*] Most bad design tropes from the 2010’s
 [/list]
[h1]My Score: [/h1]
[b]D[/b]

 [h1]Quick Summary[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 starts with a combat system I love, throwing in a wide variety of enemies that couldn’t keep up with my already high power level, but that’s nothing new to the series. Then, as the game went on, it felt like they forgot what made the game fun. So, they piled on a mixture of shallow and repetitive spectacle bosses, the most QTE’s ever, a lot of varied yet unpolished gameplay “additions”, with a story so long and convoluted that seemed to go nowhere. After 12 hours, we rang the bell and tapped out.

[h1][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/31495025/] My Personal Curator List [/url] [/h1]

[h1]Promising Premise[/h1]
RE 6 offers four total campaigns focusing on a single character's perspective of the story, with Leon and Chris being the two I played. Jake’s and Ada’s are the ones I did not attempt, as you hopefully will understand why later. On paper, this idea of a massive interconnected plot, with each one being different, sounds amazing, but in execution not so. Let me start from the beginning and see how I grew to dislike RE 6.

You start with Leon’s campaign mid-story in an odd prologue to tease what is to come later; here, it is mostly QTE prompts to escape a helicopter, open a door, and shoot a zombie. Yes, that should have been a warning of things to come. Once you get past that prologue, which you will replay when it comes up hours later, the game finally lets you enjoy some actually great shooting and improved melee combat.

[h1]The Best Action in the Series[/h1]
The gameplay has changed to allow moving and shooting at the same time, which is nice, even if it’s sad to see the previously unique style gone. Your melee move-sets have been expanded with stamina to manage now, to prevent spamming these new martial art moves to disarm or kill enemies. The best addition is a prone move that allows diving into, sliding, dodging, and shooting enemies like a tactical god. There is an instance with saw blades that you can prone under that is the crowning moment of this new move.

These great new additions are carried into each campaign, with every character having different melee hit combos, stealth, throws, and counter animations that are truly amazing and offer depth for a series that was just simple shooting. These new additions bring RE into its best action feeling, even after RE 8. It’s just a shame the enemy AI and difficulty are not brought up to match this newfound power, think of RE 5 but you are Neo.

This praise and actual enjoyment are mostly from the first 3 chapters of Leon’s campaign. Up to this point, it contains one fun boss(that is just a beefed-up zombie) with cannon fodder helping showcase how fun the combat is when it’s simple. The brisk pace of new zombies, locations, weapons, and the ratio of gameplay to non-gameplay is nicely balanced. This is about the halfway mark, as each campaign is six hours long with five chapters each. So three out of the total ten I played were enjoyable. Then the game takes a slow descent into disaster until we get to Chris’s campaign where it plummets.

[h1]Just Give up on writing, Resident Evil[/h1]
Before that, I need to explain the story: in order to have a story, stuff needs to happen, right? RE 6 has a lot of stuff happen and yet nothing really does. Characters will go places, get betrayed, the villains will die, and then come back to life half a dozen times. They will kill your comrades or entire cities and then you let them go because you don’t have time to explain why and never get any answers. It’s so circular that it felt like after 12 hours nothing happened, you might as well skip the cutscenes, and you will basically get the same idea of what’s happening.

A huge problem that happens here, is that in all the previous games each had a relatively low amount of story and therefore cutscenes, and let you just play the game. Here, it feels like you can’t go five minutes without something to interrupt the core reason you play RE, to the point that it feels like half of the game is non-gameplay.

[h1]A lot but Shallow[/h1]
The game takes you around the globe from a city similar to Raccoon, then to China, and lastly to Europe, in some well-crafted levels that you will revisit with other characters later. Probably the coolest moment was a laser hallway of death leading to explosive Roombas that you had to get rid of. For the most part, I feel the game is afraid to have you just move through a level without something outside of normal combat breaking it up, which rears its ugly head towards the end of Leon’s campaign.

[u]A short list of stuff that breaks the flow of fun[/u]:
[list][*]Boss fights where one person does literally nothing
[*]Turret sections
[*]Bosses that feel like cutscenes instead of playing 
[*]A car chase 
[*]Flying a jet 
[*]The worst and most amount of QTEs in the series
[*]Chris’s clear Call of Duty inspired sections
[*]Sequences that are unskippable gameplay cutscenes
[*]Puzzles that aren’t puzzles
[/list]

With Leon’s main villain, you barely fight him and your co-op partner during one literally can’t. He will transform from a dog to a T-rex, then a fly. These over-the-top boss fights might sound or look cool in a trailer but is terribly boring and tedious when the more simple bosses where you just shoot big zombies were more fun. You “kill” him each time in some explosion or fire to the point that you just give up caring as it overstayed its welcome the first time he wasn’t killed.

The 3rd campaign's character, Jake, who is Wesker’s son, so it’s further tied to the series’ lore. The reason they need him is to end the virus. Just imagine if RE 5 had a separate campaign centered around Sheeva, especially after how bad Chris’s campaign was. 

[h1]The Descent into Despair[/h1]
I can stomach the story because you can skip it, or not pay attention if it’s too long. The same can not be done while playing. You have those “gameplay” sections I mentioned above, which feel like 70% of Chris’s campaign if you also include the cutscenes. They went with an insane amount of variety and yet none of it was enjoyable at all. I would rather have QTE running sections from RE 4 and 5 over actually having to do it. I now understand why they overused them so much, as they have to be inept to screw up running, and yet they did, as platforms are wide and yet so narrow that if one of us made the slightest movement off the path, it resulted in death, so would jumping, or looking around. Also, the car chase and jet flying felt more like a proof of concept that was thrown in, as they sound cooler than they actually play.

Further proof of these half-baked ideas, the inventory is now expanded to allow more items,  an improvement from RE 5, but now it has a carousel format so scrolling takes longer, and removing and managing items is now a pain. The real kicker here is that every new gun takes up a slot and you can’t drop them. Even with the triple inventory space, it somehow feels like less as you will be constantly swapping weapons with how few bullets you will have with grenades and health taking up any free slots as well, fumbling the flow of the fun combat that they seemed to forget they had.

The final change from a system that everyone loved and worked perfectly from RE 4 and 5, the weapon upgrades are gone. Now you get poorly described perks from the score you get after each mission to basically do the same thing but they aren’t needed, as again you are a god with your newfound power.

It is tough to give a recommendation for RE6. As a fan of the series since it's inception, RE6 is one of the worst RE games, definitely the worst mainline title in the series. However, the game isn't that terrible if you view it as a 3rd person action shooter and NOT a Resident Evil game.

The game has it's fun moments but it is unpolished and mechanically messy, many of the mechanics available to the player are cool but poorly thought out and unreliable. Running in this game will often result in your character snapping around instantaneously in the opposite direction and leaping over something, it gets frustrating. Melee attacks are cool but the game forces it too much, resulting in very weak weapons and low ammo.

The 4 main campaigns are a mixed bag in quality. There are some good moments but a lot of rough or even frustrating or dull moments that just get exhausting to play. The game has a lot of QTE's and scripted sequences, which contradicts all the gameplay mechanics. A few turret/vehicle sections that also aren't very fun fill up play time.

There is a lot of variety here but again not all of it is to the game's benefit. While the game's design does get pretty generic for the time it came out, I don't find it as bad as many of it's competitors. For instance, the QTE's aren't any more frequent that RE4/5 for the most part. It's no where near the frequency of Tomb Raider 2013, Uncharted, etc. and it's better integrated into the gameplay.

It's the scripted sequences that get a bit annoying. There are MANY sections of the game where all you have to do is wait for an invisible timer to elapse and combat is optional. Or bosses that you only need to shoot a few times in a specific spot/timing but the overall battle is long and drawn out with numerous scripted encounters that gets frustrating to deal with. (many villains just won't die...)

Anyway, all that being said the core gameplay, when pitted against regular enemies is pretty fun. It is all the other additions and distractions that get in the way. So is the game worth playing? I think so. I think it's entertaining enough to play at least once even for RE fans, but one should go in with low expectations and playing with a friend will help a lot, the game doesn't seem all that well balanced for single player, partner AI is very unreliable.

I will say this though, only pick this game up at a hefty discount. About $5 to $10 USD is the most one should pay for this, though it does come with a lot of content. Also worth mentioning that the Mercenaries mini-game here is great, with many maps, characters and costumes, it may be the best implementation of the mini-game in the series. Almost worth buying the game just for Mercenaries.

Having spent quite a bit of time back on the PS3, this game is ironically one of my favorites of the series. I really like the enhanced movement control options and various features such as the quick shot, melee combat and countering capabilities; however, while the story was neatly layed out from different perspectives, the game lacked everything associated with its survival horror roots.

The lack of weapon customization that was featured in RE4 and 5 was a let down, but was more than compensated with various melee combat options and countering capabilities. The little customization that the player has is in setting up eight different triplets of skill slots that they purchase and upgrade skills throughout multiple runs of the game. These were nice, but I wish there was room for just one more due to the difficulty in escaping from various enemy grab attacks. As far as weapons go, each story includes various weapons that are acquired throughout the first playthrough and remain unlocked after that. The use of grenades has also been mapped much better to quickly and efficiently get to and use than in the other games. Another great enhancement is the dying status being upgraded from the way it was in RE5, that allows the player to defend and escape death without aid, though at a disadvantage.

The overall presentation of the game was very well done and had very good graphics. The levels were in some cases less enjoyable the way they trapped you in a smaller section at a time and blocked the ability to backtrack. One of the most annoying aspects of the game was the interactive movie events or at least some of them that wants to cause great wear and tear to the controller to pull off in the limited time. The last complaint would be in the numerous achievements that are attached to the various verses modes that few likely played to begin with, given that Resident Evil has always been a single-player/ co-op game.

Overall the game is stylish and fun and the PC port seems to run perfectly fine. The gameplay is more action oriented and less survival horror, but the movement and combat options are in my opinion the best this franchise has ever featured in any of their games. If you like these games, then you will likely enjoy this one for the game it is; however, if it must be survival horror, then you may be let down by this one.

RESIDENT EVIL 6 REVIEW 

Its very well known to anyone who is interested in this game and the Resident Evil series that this game is the most controversial entry, being more action-packed than survival horror. In my opinion this game is great, the story to me is very Resident Evil, though there a lot of action moments that seem to feel out of place, but if you dont mind those type of things then this game is for you.

GAMEPLAY 
Compared to Resident Evil 4 and 5 this game has a lot of controls, a lot of buttons to press and many more, shooting in this game is in my opinion less satisfying than previous entries, weapon upgrades dont exist in this game but there power ups for damage and aiming, when it comes to aiming you are given 2 choices the regular crosshair or the RE4 staple lasersight which can be changed to different colors. To me the biggest problem is the camera, it takes time getting used to it but i was hard at first, being that the camera is so close to the character itself.

OVERALL
 
The game is great for RE fans but know that it is not really a very scary game like the other entries, as a game this is great, it works well but as an RE game maybe not so much. Overall great game has a good and solid story and is pretty enjoyable. I highly suggest this to anyone who is into Resident Evil or just a casual player.

An enormous waste of time and money, this "ultimate horror entertainment" experience is the sad result of what happens when you mismanage and misdirect a gigantic, nearly unlimited amount of funding. 

The result is something that desperately wants to be "cool" and "flashy" and even more desperately wants to be Call of Duty, but lacks the necessary mechanics and ends up being drawn out, boring, repetitive, clunky and just a massive slog to play through, with a story that somehow manages to be even more primitive and, plainly stated, stupid than ever.

Avoid at all costs, RE6 has been universally panned and prompted a full series reboot for a good reason.

This game is consistently maligned by most RE fans, and I get it. At the time, it represented the bloated action approach that really took the game far away from what most loved about the original RE. That said, today, with those "expectations" taken out of the equation, I personally think it's a flawed kind of awesome. I love this game. 

I played it on the PS3 years ago when it came out and enjoyed the hell out of it then, too, so after finishing the decent RE 8, I was feeling nostalgic and interested to see how this held up on PC, and I plowed through the entire game again. And once again, I had a great time. 

The creatures/monsters in this game are just fantastic from a design perspective. Some of the best, most varied in the entire series. Truly creative work done here, and it keeps things constantly fresh. The graphics still hold up in 2021 for the most part. Textures are generally crisp and beautiful and it was such a huge step up to play this in 4K from what I remembered on the PS3. 

The four interwoven campaigns was a really interesting approach, and it worked well for the most part, although there were certainly times where it didn't. But the voice acting was generally great (even though the script was not), the action was nonstop (which I know some don't want in a RE game), and the combat was addictive, at least for me. The Leon campaign was especially fun with it's zombie apocalypse setting, but once you get to China and fight those bastards, that was great as well. And watching Ada Wong crawl through tiny corridors on all fours in tight leather pants? Well done, Capcom. Well done. 

I appreciate games that fail because they try too hard vs. games that fail because devs are lazy or greedy or just plain incompetent, and this game is definitely the former. They put an incredible amount of effort into this game to really take the franchise to another level. Sometimes they succeeded wildly. Other times, they failed miserably. 

The skill tree system, for example, is terrible. It takes a ridiculous amount of skill points to level up certain areas, like firearms or defense, so I spent the entire playthrough just concentrating on accumulating enough skill points to raise those. If you were going to play through the campaign multiple times, I guess the system would allow you to explore other skills, but I had no interest in doing that, despite enjoying myself immensely. 

The cover system is also horrible and incredibly awkward. If the could've gotten that down, it would've added a lot to the gameplay, especially in the Chris and Ada campaigns. I did like the new inventory system as far as health tablets go. But the inventory system when changing weapons was terrible. You just have to scroll through your weapons cache, and it's time-consuming and frustrating during a fight. There should've been ways to map certain weapons to specific buttons on the controller. The co-op AI is a step up from RE5, but still not good. I play this single-player, so I was very happy when the Ada Wong campaign allowed me to not have to rely on an AI partner who basically does nothing to really  help you. 

All that said, though, something about this game still manages to really shine through and just be a fun, fun game overall. There's a lot of variety, too, from turret sections to car chases, helicopter battles, fighter jet attacks on an aircraft carrier, etc. I loved it. 

So, despite the flaws, I think this game is a strong entry in the RE collection. It's not going to unseat RE4 for me or even the recent RE2 remake, but I'd put it right alongside, and probably a bit above, RE5 as my third favorite in the franchise after the first. It's really a remarkable achievement in many, many ways. A balls-out approach to game-making where the devs took a ton of chances, some of which failed, but many of which succeeded wildly. Absolutely does not deserve its bad reputation.

This game is a lot better than I thought it would be. Based on what I heard other Resident Evil fans saying over the years, I thought this game would be awful. But I have to say that I enjoyed RE6 more than RE5.

The most pleasant surprise was the length of the game. I thought each campaign would be a lot shorter, but all 4 campaigns are lengthy. However, the game's long length can also be counted as a downside simply because the game has inconsistent quality. Some portions of the game were very memorable and fun, while some portions were quite dull. The game really shined when it wasn't just all about running, having something explode, having the ground fall out from under you, etc. And while there are elements in this game that fans of the classic RE games should enjoy, they feel more like greatest hits being performed by a cover band.

I do prefer the atmosphere and pace of classic Resident Evil games, where you have a lot of slower pace areas to build tension - which results in bigger payoffs when you reach the action-packed sequences. I always loved the relief I felt when I reached a save room with it's calming yet melancholic music. And while those save rooms offered relief, players would also feel dread about what was to come after they left the save room. That feeling is gone in games like RE5 and RE6. 

I do have to give two big thumbs up to the combat in RE6. I wasn't even aware how good it actually was until about 10 hours into the game (due to the lack of tutorials). Not only can we finally move while shooting, but we can do quick-shots, and dodge rolls where we can either choose to stay on our feet or lay on the ground and fire at enemies from there.

You can definitely tell the parts of the game where they cut corners and rushed. The game has plenty of janky crap going on, with numerous cheap deaths and such. And Capcom simply didn't offer enough of what Resident Evil fans like me really enjoy, which are challenging puzzles and environments that are fun to explore and interact with. Instead, the majority of this game consists of one corridor after another without much exploring to be done or interactive elements to be found.

The story is forgettable. I liked Jake and Sherry's campaign the most, because I thought that their characters had great chemistry. [spoiler]Although Wesker having a son sounds like some dumb fan fiction type stuff. And I find the story of Ben making a clone of Ada to be ridiculous and pathetic.[/spoiler]

I could tell that this would have been a much more fun experience if I had a co-op partner to play with. And the Agent Hunt mode sounds really fun too. But alas, I was only able to play solo on the campaigns and the Mercenaries mode. But at least they improved on the AI partner system from RE5 by simply making it so that you don't have to worry about your AI partner dying.

Overall, I would give this game a solid 7 out of 10.

Furthermore, the tone of this game doesn't make a shred of sense. It tries to take itself seriously while simultaneously relying on absurdity as shown in the use of excessive cutscenes with vehicles and biohazards. There are a lot of anticlimactic moments and punchlines that don't land, but what really seals the nail in the coffin for this game is the gameplay. First of all the camera tricks the player into a false sense of security. You may think you have full control over the camera's movement for a while, that is until you unknowingly initiate a "cinematic" sequence that will subsequently make the camera turn in directions against your will. Combine this with the camera shifting from the typical over the shoulder perspective of your character to a myriad of arbitrary camera angles against your will and you get a migraine-inducing mechanical mess. 

Second of all, inventory management. There are no attaché cases that progressively increase in size as you get further in the game like in Resident Evil 4 or a passive inventory with 54 slots in addition to an active inventory with 9 slots like in Resident Evil 5. Instead there's a single active inventory with a meagre 9 slots to work with. Nothing is upgradable and the only thing you can buy are skill points which could have been an interesting concept, except there's a caveat in that no more than 3 of them can be equipped at any time. With the number of total skills being around 15x that amount, along with the cost/prevalence ratio of skill points in missions, it's a statistical improbability for the player to ever use the vast majority of these. Picking up too many items will inevitably lead to a situation with no other choice but to discard items as you cannot sell anything in this game either. 

Lastly there are sections where you are forced to walk at a snail's pace like in chapter 1 of Leon's campaign. Moreover there are sections where nothing is happening and you simply have to wait until the game decides enough time has passed by. There are no ways to speed these up or skip them and it practically kills all remaining replay value that potentially could have lingered within this blight. 

Final verdict: atrocious dumpster fire / 10

Resident Evil 6 is an over the top mess, Everything explodes, there's over the top action sequences, turret sections, chase sequences, all the stuff that makes an early 2010's action game. With that being said, there's absolutely fun to be had here. 

If you're like me and was playing this for the Resident Evil story of it, you'll likely be disapointed. There's nothing here that really effects the overall story of any other games and has quite a few one-off characters. But as a game, this is a really fun time for *MOST* of the playtime. 

Leon's Campaign: 

Leon's Campaign is the most resembilant of past Resident Evil titles, relating to RE 4 & RE 5. Helena is a pretty good character but getting stringed along by her in the beginning is pretty frustrating. The action sequences are pretty well done and his combat is great. The hand to hand combat was super fun and intuiative, and helped me save ammo. The boss battles are pretty good and don't drag on. Hunnigan returning is also super fun. Overall this was my favorite campaign

Chris's Campaign:

Chris's campaign is the most action heavy one, but ironically I had the most fun with this one. All the characters in this campaign are super likable and the combat is once again well done. All the different weapons are pretty good too. Some sections of this campaign drag on a bit, such as the car turret section. The boss battles are pretty good too and Piers is a super likable character. Overall this was my second favorite.

Jake's Campaign:

While Jake's campaign doesn't have the most action seqments, it has the worst ones imo. Having to replay sections from Chris and Leon's campaigns was annoying as hell and the snow mobile section is just bad. Jake as a character is unlikable at the beginning but slowly becomes better. Also Sherry being back after so long is really cool. She's great in this. Overall my third favorite. 

Ada's Capmaign:

I didn't play the full campaign. I played the first two chapters and was bored as hell and took to YouTube to finish the story and watch the cutscenes. My part of this campaign was boring as ♥♥♥♥ and so slow compared to the "go go go" fast nature of the other campaigns. Overall my least favorite. 

Overall, there's fun to be had here, but 20% of this game could've easily been cut. The combat system is so fun. but sadly is under used. 

Don't play this as your first Resident Evil. It's the only of its kind and is very different than the rest of the series. Fun as a guilty pleasure.

I tried my best to like this game. Despite the glaring flaws, I almost recommended this one, but the downsides just kept coming. 

Gameplay wise, RE6 is a pretty big improvement over the last one. This is the part that’s confusing to me, as RE5 gets better reviews overall compared to RE6. [h1] Review[/h1] 
I really liked the original survival horror trilogy of resident evil. The reason why the 6th instalment of the franchise has nothing to do anymore with the original is because the classic survival horror genre just isn’t popular anymore. The most popular genre are shooter. So capcom tried to be more like one in 4 and 5, which worked so they went with resident evil 6 the complete third person shooter route and I strangely found it totally working.

[u]Gameplay[/u]
Assuming you played RE5, the controls will be completely unfamiliar. I found the game to be working very well with mouse in keyboard, albeit some buttons for the menu or moves are weird.  In order to dodge as an example(which is quite a necessity) you need to press y(qwertz keyboard) or c But those aren’t that much better on the controller either. After some time I really got used to it and I found the gameplay to be rather fun.

A lot of the fun in the combat is now focused on the melee moves you can do. Every character has their own melee moves, which change depending which angle you do them or how you have stunned an enemy as that’s mostly the only way you can do any techniques.

The game is split into 4 campaigns and a mandatory tutorial which is rather annoying as its not skippable. The whole game is playable in coop, even the single player campaign with Ada is, albeit not really made for it as the coop partner cannot interact with anything.

Those campaigns are supposed to have their focus and playstyle and theme on something different, but altogether its rather all the same. Over the top action. I had a blast playing this game with a friend, every situation to the next is a rollercoaster ride. Literally, on one sequence you will do a mine tunnel cart ride and in the next you beat up a literal tyrant with your bare fists. The whole game is also pretty long for a story campaign, it will take you around 20 hours to finish. Which is rather impressive because there is so much variety in the game. There are even fully fledged driving and rail shooter sequences.

Its also nice to see how every character interacts which each other albeit the main protagonist is really Ada and the rest are just there to pad gameplay time.

I do recommend  getting this game solely with a friend, as there are lots of situations where the situation changes depending on which character you play.

I dislike tough that they removed the treasure hunt and upgrade system from 5 as this gave I a lot of replay value and added a fun reward structure. The only thing added is a rather ignorable upgrade system that is rather unbalanced and quite grindy.

Mercenary mode is back and with the improved combat it makes more fun than it ever did.

Obviously, the whole game is now a far cry from what the series originally meant. The whole atmosphere is gone and its “just” over the top action.

Also worth to note that the game can be somewhat buggy. Game will kick out the other player every time at a specific section in chris campaign or enemies that got knocked to the ground teleport away in mercenary mode. Weird stuff, nothing completely gamebreaking but sad to see that they are still in the game even tough release was so long ago.

[u]Story[/u]
Pretty awful I must say so. The story is told from different perspectives, playing trough all of them and finally Ada at last will puzzle the story and what’s going on quite well together. The thing is 5 had a good atmosphere and a situation that is rarely seen in videogames. Despite it already being not really a horror game anymore. It additionally had one of the best antagonist in the whole series. Wesker made that game to something unique, just by being so blatantly edgy. 

This time the antagonist is some random person that is the basic archetype of “does bad thing to do bad things”. There was no satisfaction in beating him or discovering really what’s going on. 

[u]Sound[/u]
The previous instalments always had a great soundtrack, although sometimes weird, sometimes even so bad its good, but mostly unique and worth listening to.

I remember not a single track in this game, probably because all of it sounds like royalty free action movie OST. Something you hear in every crappy action flick.

[u]Graphics[/u]
I don’t know why but the game somehow looks worse than Resident Evil 5. Not all of it, but some things are weird. There is a discrepancy between character models and objects. Textures sometimes look good then you see a character which texture doesn’t fit with the lighting or generally just looks washed out and weird. It’s hard to explain and I really would like to know why that is the case.

[u]Conclusion/TL;DR[/u]
The whole game is a very long rollercoaster ride of action that goes nonstop. The atmosphere isn’t great, nor are the graphics or soundtrack that are somehow worse than its predecessor but man the combat and variety in this game is just so good making it one of the best coop games I have ever played.

To preface, I am a fan of classic RE. I've been playing it since I was seven years old (24 now), starting on my friend's Sega Saturn. I can't tell you how many times I've played that original bunch of games; probably numbers in the hundreds, and across many copies and platforms. So, as you would expect, like many I used to loathe Resident Evil 6. It was only good to me as a part of my collection. And I thought that this would never change, and that the resentment I held toward it would only grow with time. But, it didn't. Maybe it's because RE has finally started to return to its roots in recent years or perhaps I'm no longer the cynical teenager that I once was or both, but I can honestly say that I have grown fond of RE6 over time, to the point where it's one of the games I reach for when I'm having a bad day. It's by no means one of my favorite entries in the series and it still has plenty of issues, but I choose more often than not to see the good in RE6 now rather than the bad. As a guy who finds Resident Evils 4 and 5 relatively boring affairs past a certain point, RE6 always manages to keep me entertained for hours on end. Yes, it's loud, bombastic, ridiculous and downright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in places, but that's all stuff I've come to expect from this franchise at this point and I can't say I'm ever bored when playing it. No campaign overstays its welcome and they provide enough variety from each other to warrant multiple playthroughs. And say what you will about the gameplay, but I think RE6 may provide some of the best characterization in the whole series. This game is also quite beautiful for 2012, and runs rather smoothly as well. I guess what I'm trying to say is this: If you are expecting Resident Evil 6 to deliver the same chills and thrills as the originals, you'll be disappointed. But if you can appreciate this game for what it is for just a moment, I think you'll have a quite a bit of fun with it. Especially if you bring a friend a long.

--Sincerely, a fellow fan.

I'm gonna have to ramble here because I hate this game too much to write my thoughts out coherently. It is honestly astonishing how a game can be so incredibly action-packed and so mind-numbingly boring at the same time. This whole game is just explosive setpiece after explosive setpiece with hordes of enemies between them, and absolutely nothing noteworthy happens during gameplay. I've heard some people compare this steaming pile of ♥♥♥♥ to the timeless masterpiece that was Resident Evil 4, despite the fact that the only thing these games share is a heavier focus on action. RE4 is the perfect example of action-horror, since the game restricts your movement and enemies are genuinely threatening and creepy, surrounding you and outmaneuvering you to make you feel helpless. The action is balanced by the incredible tension-building, which creates a thoroughly engaging gameplay loop. RE6, on the other hand, abandons the horror and resorts to pure stupid action. Enemies are numerous and pose very little individual threat, and movement is so unrestricted that maneuvering around them is comically easy. It's honestly kind of challenging to feel tense or scared while playing RE6, and the only thing that the enemies have going for them is their numbers. The gunplay doesn't feel satisfying, the guns sound and feel weak, and the moment-to-moment gameplay pretty much feels like third-person Left 4 Dead. Unlike RE4, this game doesn't understand the concept of downtime or any sort of breaks in the action. It just keeps throwing enemies at you nonstop without a single moment to collect yourself or reflect on anything. Also for some reason, they just don't give you ammo. I was literally softlocked at the end of Chris's campaign because I had zero bullets and healing items in my inventory for a boss fight, and I had to cheat in order to finish the game since he was unkillable otherwise.

Moments that should feel like highlights of the experience fall flat because they're typically done through repetitive QTE button mashing segments, and there's such little context for why things are happening that it's just confusing and downright stupid all the time. People just teleport from place to place between chapters, the game feels totally disconnected and the story is unengaging as a result. It's just a B-movie action plot with boring and depressing versions of once-beloved characters, throwing so many nonsensical plot threads at the player that it's impossible to avoid becoming completely detached from it all. That's not even mentioning the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane cutscenes which rival MGS Twin Snakes in their sheer stupidity, like the zombie shark or Jake's final boss fight or any of the vehicle sections. And worst of all, failing a QTE in a cutscene is almost always guaranteed death, which is such an eyerolling way to get hit with a game over screen. 

I'd say that the biggest problem is the game's insane length. It's the longest game in the series, with four entire campaigns wrapped into one, each campaign worse than the last. There's so much artificial padding as well, with the game stopping you to find a bunch of keycards or explore a big arena for hidden items when you just want to wrap things up already. Once you've sunk a few hours in, the combat feels like mind-melting mush and it just throws so much repetitive slop at you that you're practically begging for it to end. But it doesn't end. It just keeps going, and going, and going. Resident Evil 6 makes you feel bored and miserable from start to finish, draining your energy like some kind of digital parasite, and you walk away from the play session wishing you spent your time doing literally anything else. I urge everyone alive to avoid this game like the plague.
