RE6 follows in the footsteps of its more action-oriented predecessors and turns the dial to hyper stupid. Every character is a damn meme and the zombie apocalypse seems to be a rainy day at the office to our beloved BSAA agents. This game seems more like something designed by Platinum Games than Konami. Every sequence between the levels is a damn madhouse, where the most ridiculous thing that can happen *will* happen.

What's good?
Controls are intuitive, fluid and fun, and I'm playing on mouse and keyboard. Guns function as they are supposed to and different varieties of zombies require you to adapt to different situations. When you're playing this with a friend, every situation has something in store for unintentional comedy. I hear a lot of complaints that this game is a bunch of QTEs, but if anything, their relevance, difficulty and importance has been toned down.

What's not so good - or bad?

To sum it up, RE6 could have benefitted from some basic polishing. 

Let's start with the fact that zombies can move and attack you during cutscenes e.g., when you've cranked a lever to solve a puzzle, and sometimes cutscenes happen to just one of the players. Once it's over, your character will receive an inevitable slap from a nearby zombie.

Every level is a corridor. There are some secrets here and there; but due to infinitely spawning zombies, exploration seems more like a chore rather than a chance to unwind in the silent moment, unless you want to risk your health and ammo for a secret emblem find.

I do not see myself playing this solo. If anything, it's painfully obvious that this game was intended as a co-op experience. It's fun and all, but a lot of things are more fun with friends, like butt-love. That leaves the single-player experience a lackluster novelty with idiot AI. Finally, due to the simplistic and straightforward level design, there is no sense of adventure or exploration, which is found in other RE games.

In reality it's not far off from RE4 and RE5, and many of the things people complain about here... combat focus, linearity, lack of puzzles, silly story, QTEs... also apply to those games, which have much better reputations.

That said, RE6 is a bit worse mostly because of small annoyances that add up quickly. Enemies are super tanky, your partner AI will often fight when it should run or help you, endless waves of enemies become tedious and weird level design can often confuse or lead to ambushes of trial and error death. The Leon campaign is by far the best and has the least of these issues, to the point where I'd roughly compare it to RE5, but the others suffer so many cuts they bleed out into annoyance way more than fun.

That said, if you're a big RE fan and really loved RE4 and RE5 then I'd say you'll probably enjoy this more than people say you would. The Leon campaign has a decent story that doesn't truly need the others to make sense, and it has the best gameplay. If you're into the series you should at least play that.

For a general audience in 2021 though, this is not a good game and should be ignored.

Two Wongs don't make it white but that does not keep Capcom from trying. The first story is that of Leon and Helena. Leon helps Helena through her sister complex by helping her kill her sister. The second story is about Chris Redfield a gay military man who reminisces about his past loves while chasing that elusive disappearing snake. When he finds his true love Piers, his partner and is ready to give up the disappearing snake, Piers dies on an underwater base. I am not sure what type of metaphor Capcom was going for there. The third story was Jake and Sherry. Sherry helps Jake beat his heroin addiction by forcing him to run from mutants and people that are trying to shoot him. This unorthodox method works as at the end of the story he is doing what most former junkies do. Ride a motorcycle at top speed down a desert highway. The last story is Ada. Ada is a twenty something Caucasian cos-player who thinks she is the international Chinese spy Ada Wong from the Resident Evil movies and games. Of course she looks too young and white but that doesn't stop her from being obnoxious and having a whole bunch of people shoot at her. I think the real Ada Wong cos-plays as the cos-player and gets her killed at some point. This plot point was too meta for the west so it was left unexplained by Capcom.

Now let me start out by saying for the longest time I was a massive RE6 hater without ever even playing it. I think it stemmed from trying Operation Raccoon City on the 360 which I thought was awful and then just assumed RE6 was the same kind of garbage. Well Im writing this review to say that I was mostly wrong. 

I finally decided to buy the game after so long and give it a chance to speak for itself instead of just blindly hating on it. I just (not even 60 seconds ago) finished the final campaign after completing the rest in the order of Leon, Chris, Jake, and finally Ada and I must say I am pleasantly surprised at how much I enjoyed it. Maybe its because I went in with such low expectations or something but I couldnt stop playing the game for the past week. I'll now go through and do a little reviews of each campaign in the order I played them *SPOILERS AHEAD*

Leon and Helena: I think this one has the closest feel to a "textbook" Resident Evil game. It almost gave me RE Outbreak vibes at least towards the beginning so I enjoyed that. It started to kinda take a dive towards the last few chapters when it just feels like back to back boss fights with the main antagonist. It also really felt like I was playing the video game version of RE: Damnation, the animated RE movie, also the only one I've seen so I almost compared it to that instead of other RE games. This may sound stupid but it makes sense in my head. All in all though I really enjoyed this chapter and it was a good start to the game. 8.5/10 

Chris and Piers: Oh boy. This one was rough, at least the gameplay was. Without a doubt Chris and Piers' chapter has the weakest gameplay in my opinion. Almost zero variation in enemies and lack of creative boss fights compared to the other characters. Although the story was really well put together and is an emotional roller coaster so it made it worth playing through for the cutscenes alone. This whole chapter is basically what I expected the whole game to be; enemies with guns and rocket launchers, lots of explosions and annoying QTE's, basic boss battles (though the invisible snake was cool), etc. And while every chapter had SOME of those things sprinkled in Chris' got it the worst no doubt. 4/10

Jake and Sherry: After Chris and Piers' chapter this was a GIANT breath of fresh air and ended up being my absolute favorite chapter even though I thought it would be pretty hard to top Leons. This one has everything: chase sequences, crazy mutations, big ♥♥♥♥♥♥ that stops at nothing to tear you limb from limb the whole game, awesome story, awesome characters, and the list goes on. I know a lot of people hate Jakes character and I really did at first too but towards the end he (kinda) stops being such an edge lord and becomes an actual person so its a really nice arc. But beyond that the interactions between him and Sherry are always welcome and since I was playing solo it didnt feel as much that I was dragging a lifeless bot around but instead Sherry being her own character. I could keep going but we still have a whole last chapter to go through so I'll end it here. 9/10

Ada: This one was cool. Nothing special really but it was neat. Felt like I was playing a bonus chapter kinda like "Separate Ways" from RE4. Ada just doing her own ♥♥♥♥ in the background and having her own story that kinda intersects with the other characters was pretty cool to see and play. I have always loved Ada's cutthroat personality in the series and it doesnt lack here whatsoever. Shes just as awesome as always and it almost feels like your playing a James Bond game for some of the sections (in a good way) because of all the ninja ♥♥♥♥ she does. Theres some corny stealth sections throughout but they're mostly, to my surprise, done pretty well and not forced upon the player. Her boss battle is also pretty horrific and quite honestly Ada's whole campaign is probably the closest thing to horror out of all of the other chapters. 7.5/10

So now that thats all out of the way I'll do a final ranking of all the chapters from best to worst:

Jake & Sherry - Best
Leon & Helena
Ada
Chris & Piers - Weakest

TL;DR Not as bad as people make it out to be. Still far from the best the franchise has to offer but its no slouch. Give it a try when its on sale.

So we came to the last campaign, Adas. While the three before where storywise all teams (Leon & Helena  /  Chris & Piers  /  Jake & Sherry) you had no problem playing in coop through them. Now heres Ada, whos all alone. And the devs just slapped a random Soldier Bodyguard onto her. I had the pleasure of playing this Bodyguard of hers. And while I say pleasure & playing Im blatantly lying in your face. In the campaigns before it didnt really matter which character you picked. The only difference were the weapons and sometimes you had to split from your partner for 50 meters and walk on a different path. As Adas Bodyguard the only thing you can do is shoot. You cant open doors, you cant pick up quest related items or trigger cutscenes. Ada can use a grappling hook on certain portion of the map. As the bodyguard you just stand there and wait on your partner to swing and then be teleported after them. I have no idea what they were thinking or if they even playtested the coop campaign.

All in all, not a bad game at all. Weaker entry in the series, but you get quite a bit of content for what you pay for these days. It's not all great, but it ain't as bad as everyone remembers.

The whole premise is Chris has temporary memory loss since he let his teammates die to [spoiler]the fake Ada replica that Simmons made using his wifes body. Y'know, the usual foe.[/spoiler] Anyways, they all die and he represses the memory. Piers rolls up, calls him a wuss, and basically drags him back to the military still with memory loss. He retains his physical memory and just brings a damn pistol and knife. PIERS RUNS A MACHINE GUN AND [b] ANTI-MATERIAL THERMAL SNIPER RIFLE.[/b] Anyway, his team dies again and Chris remembers. The entire rest of the time he seeks revenge, even at the loss of the remainder of his team. Piers just joins him around, making sure he doesn't get himself killed doing stupid things. And they do MANY stupid things. Anyways, they're story is meh, the combat is meh, the ammo drop is CRUEL. It's perhaps one of the more annoying stories, but it's not all bad honestly. 
[b] Ada and Agent.[/b] Here, however, on the other end of the spectrum we have the assitry. People screamed joyously about there being online co-op and then pointed an accusatory finger at Ada's campaign that was strictly solo. It might not be the most well-received game of the series but it's still a fun co-op shooter at its core. By default, the game comes a load of content: four campaigns, Mercenaries, and PvP--each of which could easily net you a couple hours of enjoyment. Whether you like it or not, this is hands down the most mechanically polished with each character having a fairly large set of melee attacks and weapons in their respective campaigns. There's honestly nothing more satisfying then sliding into an enemy to stagger him, shoot him in the head for a stun, and finishing your combo by throwing him into his friends.

Now lets get into the main content of the game, the campaigns. I would say each of the four range from just okay to pretty good. Leon and Helena have a vaguely classic Resi feel with many of their levels consisting of puzzles, tight corridors, zombies, and dark spaces. Chris and Piers are the military shooter duo packing heavy firepower and easily reaching the highest body count together in the game. Jake and Sherry is very much an action-adventure since a lot of the major set pieces tend to feature a different style of gameplay and location (driving, non-linear exploration, platforming). And Ada, appropriate for the mysterious femme fatale is a stealth-action styled campaign that has her sneaking around behind-the-scenes and subtly helping the other protagonists in various ways.

With a good variety of different flavors, you and your dedicated co-op partner should easily be able to find at least one favorite amongst those four. As long as you keep in mind this is a balls-to-the-wall action game you will get a lot of enjoyment out of it. But if you miss the suspenseful atmosphere and horror of the older titles then it's best you stay away. At the very least, it's a nice way to kick ass as some of our favorite characters of the franchise once more.

What can I say about this game? I bought it very recently, and went to play it, but from the beginning I wasn't really happy with the game. The game was obviously made for a console controller, and with the combination of keyboard and mouse I wasn't a happy bunny. But I take clunky controls as another obstacle towards finishing the game, so it took me a bit of time to make an acceptable setup for me.

Beyond clunky controls and not so great camera control, lies a pretty decent game. It has a solid story about some virus on the loose. That story is very familiar with what is going on in the real world right now, so I kinda enjoyed it. Also the viruses are always a part of the main story in RE games so this was not a surprise at all.

Most of the game is fighting the enemy, or pressing the specific key at the specific moment in order to go forward. In between are cut scenes. The game is linear, but that is to be expected. When I look at the whole game, I would kinda be neutral about recommending it, but since this is not an option I would say it was like 52 - 48 for recommending it, so there it is.

I remember the reviews for this game when it originally came out. I wasn't a fan of RE 5 when I played it with a friend, and the reviews made this game sound truly awful. It's actually not too bad. It definitely has flaws. A ton of them. I wouldn't recommend this as a game to start the series with either. Heck even if you are looking for a multiplayer RE game look at 5 or the Revelations series. This game doesn't deserve the hate it gets though, and it's worth a play through if you're a fan of the bonkers plot.

The biggest flaw in this game is the game play. If you ever played RE 4 or RE 5 and thought to yourself that you would love to play a version that has all of the slow bits taken out and just have combat (sometimes infinitely spawning enemy closet combat) you'll be right at home. There are barely any puzzles in this game. Even when they do show up it would be generous to call them a puzzle. More like momentary diversions before getting back to the shooty shooty bits. Really Ada's play through it the only one I can think of that had puzzles that took more than two minutes. Personally I really missed better puzzles and needing to plan where items need to be used. Those are some of my favorite parts of RE games and it gets kind of exhausting without them. The combat in the game isn't bad. It's very similar to playing RE 5. On higher difficulties it will push you and it would be good to get a human friend to help. On lower difficulties the AI partners are okay enough. The guns all act differently, but only kind of. I mostly just used the same one until I ran out, switched to the next, and just kept repeating that until stuff died. 

The other big thing with this is that it is an ugly game. Really ugly in fact. A lot of the background textures look like old PS3 assets. The movies look good, but the second you are back in a game play section you know. I played on the highest graphics settings and it still looked bad. The environments are so boring that there were a good amount of times I got turned around for no reason. Every angle pretty much looked the same so I just kept running back to the same place over an over again. Pretty annoying. On top of that most of the chapters are stupid long. I could literally clear one of the original PS1 RE games in the time it takes to beat the average RE 6 chapter. There's quite a bit that could be cut from the levels and if some genius modder figures out a way to cut the fluff from this game I bet it would be 1,000% better.

In the long run though the biggest flaw here is the scope they tried to reach with this game. One of those Icarus reaching for the sun kinds of things. I appreciate what they were trying to do here. They were trying to tell an interconnected story like they did with RE2. It almost works. The problem is that they didn't seem to have the time to really flesh it out and having to make SO many separate environments probably set them back a bit too much. I would guess that is why the environments are so ugly and the game play is so stripped down. They just stretched themselves too thin. If they had more time or cut down two of the stories to focus on the main ones it probably would have been much better for it. 

Here I am recommending a game and I've done nothing but whine about it. Here's the thing, I have been playing RE games since '96-'97. I remember the days when RE1 had a very poorly acted live action intro. When the voice acting was barely passable. I loved that stuff. It was SO cheesy that it made this series one of my favorite video game series. When this game came out I remember seeing and reading a bunch of reviews that complained about the plot. It's like people forgot that this is a series where a slug queen hive convinces itself that it is the 80 year old creator of the T virus. A series where the captain of a special forces cop team is also some how a mad scientist as a side gig and just happens to be really into doing all the evil. When I look at the plot of this game next to those things it's really fun. I can see why people don't like it, but really if you just sit back and enjoy it for the shlocky horror/sci-fi/spy weirdness that it is the plot of this game is pretty fun.

If you are a fan of the series this can be worth it. I would wait for a major sale. It's probably the longest game in the series, but full price is still a bit much. If it is ever on sale for like $10-$15 I would say it is worth it. If you don't have patience for weird plots and janky backgrounds maybe give this one a pass and just look up the plot on YouTube or something. I'm glad I played this. It probably sounds like I'm not, but I am.

Best way to describe this game is that it's like playing a mashup between RE:4 and RE:5 with incredibly low brightness on your monitor. Combine sheer darkness with a camera that doesn't know where it is supposed to be looking, and you'll be playing a game where you can't see what the bleedin' hell is going on. Mix in an obtuse user interface and you have a recipe for frustration.

It's even more action than horror - or any exploration and adventuring at this point. This has been a progression of the series with has now reached it's nadir. You just have to try and shoot as many zombies as you can and then just go toe-to-toe with the rest! It just looks very silly. The story has huge problems with pacing - essentially it's non-stop balls-to-the-wall action. There's no real horror of which to speak because the game can't find time to slow down and build anticipation. It tries too hard to jump-scare you every minute, and when it's not doing that the vehicle or elevator the players are in are guaranteed to explode. It doesn't take long until you more or less are expecting something to go wrong at every corner - and you won't be wrong either. Comparisons of "Call of Duty - but you have to pick up ammo" are accurate.

Unlike most survival games, there's zero reason to conserve ammo. Dead zombies give you more - you just have to pick it up. Out of ammo? Just kick them all to bits! The game is marred with many quicktime events until the game becomes a mere test of your reactions. Very little thought or strategy is needed to work your way through the very linearly designed levels, party because it's an experience of pure chaos in near darkness. It couldn't be more further removed and dumbed down from the adventuring and puzzle solving of the very early Resident Evil games. To top it all off, it doesn't even save the game properly between checkpoints and you have to often retread earlier sections.

If a manic over-the-top action movie with zombie elements is your thing then you might like it. There's four campaigns so there is actually loads of content. However, I was pretty much over it from the first few levels. It just gets more comical the more you play into it. It's only saving grace is the mercenaries mode - which is unashamedly a survival mode with an annoying timer - and is pretty fun once you get into it. Playing with a friend could be fun. It's just not enough to save the whole game from my thumbs down.

The years have been kind to "Resident Evil 6". At the time of its release, the game got savaged because of its many issues - which I'll comment about here. But with time, as the game got cheaper and more people where whiling to buy it despite the bad reviews, many players felt that it had positive aspects that weren't appreciated enough at its release. The question then becomes: do its positive aspects compensate for its issues?

After "Resident Evil 5" moved the focus of the franchise from horror to action, Capcom developers wanted the next game to double-down on action, while also having some sober horror elements to apparently appease fans of previous "RE" games - a way maybe to keep some of the franchise's identity in there. They also wanted the game to feel like an epic, with multiple campaigns, and focusing on several franchise favourites like Leon S. Kennedy, Chris Redfield and Ada Wong. It is a game that feels very much like it wanted to be the most "definitive" game in the franchise.

But the final result is an uneven game that can go from pleasant to frustrating very quickly. It's a game that can be clumsy in its attempts to menage both its horror and action elements, and as a consequence, its horror is no longer scary, being more of a restrain on the action. My suggestion is that "Resident Evil 6" should have been an action game all along, scrapping all of its horror elements that just don't click with the overall vibe.

The game has four campaigns: Leon and Helena, Chris and Pears, Jake and Sherry, and then Ada. One thing I really liked about the game is the notion of the stories being interlinked: characters will find each other in their stories and influence them. By playing the game, you'll notice it has a strong focus on the idea of co-op - with the exception of Ada's campaign, all the campaigns can be played by two players. So much so that, like in "Dark Souls", the pause menu doesn't actually pause the game, which is common for online games. But of course you can play the game alone, as your partner will then be controlled by a very competent AI, who can manage itself against enemies and is quick to rescue you when you're down.

Leon's campaign is the most irregular. It starts off as a horror campaign, but it doesn't take long before it picks up and becomes more oriented to action. It has moments when it's not sure what it wants to be, and only at the end it becomes good. Chris' campaign is the most action-grounded of them all: you're a soldier fighting armed zombies. There'll be some annoying bosses, but his campaign overall is actually pretty good. Jake's campaign... I'll just say it's hilarious. Jake is such an edgy character that it feels like a parody of edgy troupes. He feels like a character out of a cartoon; he's just so out there. And what makes it all more fascinating is that it's all taken serious: he wasn't meant to be funny. But anyway, his campaign is actually pretty decent, except at some moments when you have to control vehicles (more on that in a bit). Then there's Ada's campaign, which may be the best - it's the only one properly meant for single-player. Not too frustrating, and with enough action for a good time.

You acquire skill points during the game, which curiously, are not gifted automatically to you as you kill zombies, but you have to manually collect them as drops. With these points, you can unlock new skills for your characters, making things easier. You're never truly lost or confused in the levels, since they tend to be very linear, and even when they're more open-ended, you have this device (the Q key) which will point you where to go next. So the level designs are actually well made. Even key fetching don't feel so annoying due to that.

During the stories, the characters are required to do different things at key moments. Their functions are not interchangeable, tough: what the game delegates to Sherry cannot be done by Jake, for example. At some points the game tries to variate, and to introduce players with different challenges. The issue however is that these challenges can be incredibly annoying: going to the subject of vehicles, you are sometimes asked to pilot something. In Jake's campaign, it is this snowmobile that is incredibly clunky at first, and then there's a motorbike section because, hey, there's gotta be one somewhere. In Chris' campaign, it's a VTOL, but if you're playing with Pears, it becomes much easier, since all you have to do is shoot. In Ada's campaign, it's a helicopter, which is actually decent enough. All of this is to bring some variety to the game, which is understandable, but it doesn't always work.

The main grip I have with the game, however, is the combat. Once again, the game tries to balance between horror and action, and as such, it implements many survivor horror elements that don't work with the action, such as inventory management, bad aiming, fatigue, and being throw out of balance. The game tries to focus on melee combat, which would be a way for players to save up ammo. But you can't just go around kicking enemies since there's so much fatigue you have. Besides, being grabed by zombies can sap your health pretty hard, so maybe it's best to keep your distance.

Each character has its own set of initial guns, and as you progress, you'll also find new guns. But their ammo occupies space in your inventory, and too much items means you won't have room to essential ones: namely healing herbs, which have this disgracefully complicated way to be accessed (apparently, you have to first convert the herbs in your inventory into pills, and then put them in your character). Again, this was all meant for a horror game, but they feel out of place in an action game. There are also numerous QTEs that are just overly present in the game: if we were talking about well placed events, that would be acceptable, but they're just overwhelming as they are.

The bosses are actually tricky, because you don't know when to just fill them with lead and when there's a specific action to do. The zombies come in different shapes and sizes, and at one point you'll face the so-called J'avos: zombies that get an extra mutation when they're harmed. And some of these mutations are incredibly hard to deal with (the swarm of bees being the worst of them all). This is all for the sake of combat variation, so you won't feel like you're fighting the same enemies over and over again.

The four campaigns took me nearly 27 hours to complete, but maybe the game should have been a bit shorter, as it was filled with unnecessary moments. On harder difficulties, it becomes unfairly hard, so swallow your pride and complete the game on normal: it becomes more balanced. Besides, once you beat all campaigns, you'll have the option of infinite ammo, which will make some moments much more pleasant, and will allow you to play at harder difficulties without much issues (but the hardest difficulty lacks the infinite ammo option).

"Resident Evil 6" justifies much of its criticism. But it also justifies much of its praise. You play it and you immediately understand why it's not universally beloved. Once again, developers should have focused more on making an action game, but overall, for all its flaws, it's still a decent game that could have been so much better with so little changes.

[b]TL;DR[/b] If you want co-op Resident Evil, play 5. If you're new to the franchise, feel free to skip this one as it will likely never be referenced to. If you want a fast-paced action shooter, play Doom or Vanquish. The only ones who have any business playing this are foolish, die-hard fans of the franchise who are willing to wade through garbage for the sake of completion. Like me.

Such a poorly designed game from the ground up. Any fun that may have been extracted from the combat system is trashed because of constant QTEs and set pieces interrupting the flow of gameplay. There are literally sections where you can't take 5 steps without the game wrenching control away from you to focus on something completely asinine.

The gunplay feels awful because most enemies just don't react to shots until they die. The inventory is terrible because you're forced to carry your entire arsenal on you at once. You're constantly at max capacity and constantly have to drop grenades or ammo to make room for an herb that you're just going to combine anyway. Previous Resident Evils solved this problem by letting you combine even when the inventory is full, but we're not talking about a good game here.

Navigating through that arsenal is a pain because you can only cycle from left to right, and you'll have to do it constantly to adjust for the aforementioned constantly-full inventory. The game would've benefited greatly form something like a weapon wheel. Or even just no inventory system at all since it's apparently desperate to be Call of Duty. 

The big thing people tout in regards to the gameplay is the melee combat. And yeah, that can be fun... when it works. So often your attacks whiff or you don't get to attack at all because you need to be standing the exact right spot in order to get the prompt, and half the time the enemies will just get back up before you can do anything.

The enemies themselves are so unfun to fight. They take so much damage even on normal and rarely stagger from your shots. Plus so many of them have attacks that will completely drain your health bar in what feels like unavoidable situations. There's also many instances where the game just spawns wave after wave of enemies in what feels like (and sometimes is) infinite amounts.

Nothing beyond the gameplay is worth talking about. The story is nonsensical and pointless. The level design is anti-fun. The campaigns are a slog to push through. And to top it off it doesn't even have the good graces to be short.

I consider the argument that "it's a fun action game, just a bad Resident Evil" to be thoroughly delusional. I've played many a great shooter, I've seen what Capcom can pull off with an action-focused game. This fails on all counts.

I can't recommend this game. The main reason for that is because it does a lot of things wrong which Resident Evil 5 did right. RE games are not narrative masterpieces by any stretch of the imagination but RE5 provided nontheless a fun third person coop experience. RE6 doesn't.

The main issues compared to RE5 are:
1) Terrible camera perspectives during action sequences and quick time events: The camera focuses on being cinematic but this often means you don't even see where you are going with your character. Sometimes you don't even see your own character while you are supposed to move around and evade dangers
2) Clumsy inventory interface: I don't understand what was wrong with the previous interation. But in this game inventory management is poorly implemented at least for a PC game. Hotkey assignment are impossible. You have to scroll through inventory through combination of button presses and mousewheel. You also can't choose your weapon layout anymore, meaning you will block a significact amount of your inventory space with ammunition wether you want to or not.
3) The progression system is unengaging. Instead of upgrading weapons you pick a set of three perks which you can upgrade from level one to three. Consequently you have very little meaningful choice. While in RE5 you could chosse from a variety of weapons and upgrade them, most perks in RE6 are only useful in niche circumstances. Generally you pick firearm damage, melee damage and health because they are always useful, reducing the effective amount of player choice to practically nothing.
4) No item swapping in coop. 
5) No shared progression in coop. If you find emblems or collectibles every coop partner has to pick them up seperatly for some unknown reason
6) Areas are extremly cramped with doors requiring both players interact carefully gating the players from area to area. These "two players doors" are extremly ubiquitous. A coop game has to do something like that in order to keep players from straying too far. RE6 is just extremly uncreative when it comes to accomplishing that goal. This gives the game an "on-the-rails" feeling that is only seldomly interrupted by open areas.

None of these issues are by themselves gamebreaking. However, in combination they make for a frustrating and lackluster experience. I can't give an impression on the multiplayer since I only played the main campaigns in coop. If you are looking for a coop game I suggest you try RE5 first. In addition to the aformentioned issues you should also have a high tolerance for quick time events, since they are pretty much everywhere.

It's funny, because on my first playthrough I hated Resident Evil 6 so much I uninstalled it and I wasn't even half way through Leon Chapter 1. After sitting down and be patient enough to finish all the campaigns, my opinions changed: It's a damn fine co-op action game. I went in expecting a Resident Evil game which I shouldn't have, that was probably why I despised it a lot in the first place.

[u][b]Things that Resident Evil 6 did well[/b][/u]

• [b]Well paced for an action game.[/b] After fights you get room to breathe before facing other waves of enemies.
• [b]The story is decent.[/b] This may be controversial but I quite enjoyed the story despise the criticism it has. It might not be as good as other Resident Evil games but still pretty fun on its own.
• [b]The characters.[/b] After finishing the game I appreciate so much more of Leon, Chris and Ada. The new characters such as Jake and grown-up Sherry are pretty interesting as well (except for Helena, she's kinda meh but I don't hate her). I feel like they've done a really good job writing them in this game.
• [b]You can finally run![/b] No more of that Resident Evil 4 and 5 trotting.
• [b]Level design is pretty well done for an action game.[/b] It's easy to follow and there are extra stuffs to find along the way as well.
• [b]The game's length.[/b] Resident Evil 6 is the longest game of the franchise, so if you enjoy games that run for more than 20 hours, this is for you.
• [b]Co-op is fun with friends.[/b] Remember to bring some friends with you, because randoms might try to friendly fire you (this happened to me, yup).

[u][b]Things that Resident Evil 6 did not so well[/b][/u]

• [b]Inventory management.[/b] This is the biggest con of Resident Evil 6 for me. Inventory feels clunky, you can basically see it as non-existent. It's just downright horrendous, even Resident Evil 5 did a better job with this.
• [b]Identity.[/b] The developers tried so hard to please every fans that they ended up disappointing everyone. It clearly does not feel like a Resident Evil game, and the horror that I loved in the older titles was never found in this title.
• [b]The atrocity of quick time events made its return![/b] They really prove time and time again that QTEs are really the worst thing that ever happened to this franchise. Thankfully this game has more tolerable QTEs than RE4 or RE5 but everytime you come across one you just wanna rip your head out.
• [b]Sudden camera angle changes in some segments.[/b] You cannot believe how many times I have died because this game decides to bring back fixed camera angle during tense moments?? It's a really annoying and pesky feature, and it's frequent enough to drive you mad.

[u][b]Every Resident Evil 6's campaign[/b][/u]

You can skip this part if you don't want any spoilers.

• [b]Leon's campaign[/b] is targeted to the zombie fans and the likes. This is supposed to please the Resident Evil fans who love the older titles but it was done rather... poorly. Zombies can use weapons and it looks goofy as hell. Generally, this campaign is okay and the final chapter is kinda epic. 
• [b]Chris' campaign[/b] is for Resident Evil 5 lovers. They feature the same-ish enemies from RE5 (called the J'avo). The combat/melee attacks feel really satisfying with Chris (don't know if it's the same for Piers but it probably is). Overall, I like the story side better than the gameplay side, but it's a decent campaign.
• [b]Jake's campaign[/b] is kinda a mix of Leon and Chris? It's hard to explain, but apparently Jake can do really good melee attacks (I didn't know, I was playing as Sherry). But otherwise, the story and the gameplay is fine on this one.
• [b]Ada's campaign[/b] is for the puzzle suckers from the older RE games. Features plenty of puzzle, and you get the choice of doing the campaign alone or multiplayer which is pretty cool. Ada's coolness is on point, the gameplay and plot is pretty a-okay as well.

[b]Resident Evil 6 is like what others said, a good action game but a terrible Resident Evil game.[/b] Luckily, this marks the end of the 4-5-6 trilogy and the series would turn back to its original horror roots with Resident Evil 7. Although an end to quite a controversial era, Resident Evil 6 is still a fun game, even more fun if you have friends to play it with. It's a pretty cheap time-killing game when it's on sale, and you get to dive more into the Resident Evil universe.

Edit: After finishing the game, I can say without a doubt the following about Resident Evil 6:
1. The gameplay is horrible and it backtracks on everything that made RE4 and RE5 fun.
2. The story is nonsensical, poorly executed and explained even worse.
3. The voice acting ranges from alright at best to atrocious at worst.
4. The game is CONSTANTLY interrupted by quicktime events and cutscenes. I would honestly wager that I spent about half my time playing this game in either a quicktime or a cutscene instead of controlling my character.
5. There is no semblance of difficulty even on the hardest setting, No Hope, which only marginally reduces the amount of ammo you get.
6. The pacing of the game is some of the worse I have ever experienced.
7. The game overall is a total ♥♥♥♥-show packed with terrible action movie tropes that would make Michael Bay blush.
8. The game is incredibly glitchy and broken. Enemies are constantly teleporting around, appearing and disappearing, and the collision of the game areas are generally subpar at best.
9. The music is bland and forgettable.
10. And finally, the controls. The controls in RE6 are some of the most obtuse, unresponsive and actively unfun I have ever had the displeasure of experiencing in a video game. The camera jitters rapidly and uncontrollably while running if you try to change directions with the mouse, to the point of inducing motion sickness. The game also is CONSTANTLY ripping control of your camera away from you to show you something inconsequential, which destroys whatever semblance of flow was left after the constant quicktime events and cutscenes. Your character enters a lengthy, uncontrollable falling animation that lasts about 6 seconds after being shot more than once, which also makes trying to play agonizing and constantly disrupts gameplay.

Overall I have no idea how or why this game was made. It's so universally bad by every metric that me and my brother had numerous moments of gut-busting laughter at the absurdity and general atrociousness of the game, so I guess it has that going for it. Play it with a friend for giggles, or don't play it at all.

Despite being a main entry in the Resident Evil franchise, Resident Evil 6 is noticeably different compared to its predecessors. It's even more action-oriented, to the point that many fans, myself included, said it's more like a shooter game with scary enemies compared to horror. Like RE5, this game is co-op friendly, where every mission is playable with a partner. There are 4 separate campaigns which sometimes intersect, and the playable characters are Leon/Helena, Chris/Piers, Jake/Sherry, and Ada. You can co-op on Ada's campaign, a non-canon character named Agent will appear during gameplay, but disappear in cutscenes.

Combat gameplay is similar, but also has a lot of new features. The most noticeable and important for me was the ability to move around while aiming, something RE4 and 5 doesn't have. There's also the ability to slide, roll, dodge, and quickshot. While RE6 has a lot more combat moves, honestly I prefer RE5's simpler combat. There's a lot more action scenes, like where you run away while being chased or the place falling apart, and quite plenty vehicle driving/combat scenarios. To be honest I'm not a fan of the amount of running scenes, there's just to many. And outside the helicopter combat moments, which is fun and still feels "in tone" with the game, vehicle scenes just feels jarring and very unlike a RE game.

Due to having 4 campaigns, RE6's story is quite long, it can be 5-7 hours each. Each campaign explores different areas, so it's not repeating the same levels 4 times. Although some levels use the same map or with minor differences, usually story intersection levels. All campaigns (except Ada) explore one character's relationship with their partner, giving a lot of time for development. They also have unique weapons and melee finisher moves. With many playable characters and their unique combat strategies, gameplay becomes a lot more fun and varied. It's actually a strong point for this game, like Separate Ways in RE4. It also has a Mercenaries mode, score attack levels like the ones in RE4 and 5, and Mercenaries No Mercy, a crossover with Left 4 Dead featuring characters from there and weaker, but more numerous zombies.

Remember how I said RE6 is really action-oriented and co-op friendly? It is also a major weakness for menu and inventory management. The in-game menu (Esc) where you can change settings and controls, are made in-game. That means you cannot open the menu in combat since you'll get attacked. I know it's preferable for co-op, but not everyone has friends or motivation to play that way. If you play offline there is a pause button, but you still cannot view the menu while the game pauses. Opening inventory also plays in real-time, making combining items or switching weapons difficult and stressful especially when you're in a pinch. You also cannot trade items or use your partner's inventory as an extra storage like in RE5, and the inventory is quite small. In short, it's way too co-op friendly, even if you play alone.

Despite the action direction the story takes, lore-wise I think it still makes sense. Since the use of bioweapons became more prevalent, it makes sense that zombies and the creatures here appear, and in large numbers. And of course the virus can be modified by scientists, creating the gun-using zombies who still have some intelligence. Resident Evil 6 is a good game, but comparing it to other titles it makes this game feel weird and out of place. However, with the return of many likeable characters, horror RE fans still should play this game despite the large difference in its tone and atmosphere. If you're new to the franchise, however, do not use this game as your first entry, get RE2 remake instead.

Resident Evil 6 felt like a true declining point in the franchise. It just felt... complacent. Sure, it will play out as a good 7/10 co-op game. A friend or random stranger will beat native AI, which flips a coin as to whether it will choose to revive you when you're downed. It brings the game down to that 5-6/10 level for me, where the level of the game's direction and absurdity is not exceeded or even matched in earlier games. You can skip it if you're hoping for something other than new environment - everything else feels gimped or same-y. 

Levels are short enough to play in bursts with a friend, and the level design itself is as atmospheric as other instalments in Resident Evil. But, gun selection feels pretty limited in terms of unique guns and quantity. However, they did a good overhaul on combat movement when it comes to melee fighting, which might be more important to know when ammo becomes scarce at higher difficulties. Upgrades that you purchase with points do very little in building up your character. In fact, they are quite easy to forget about in your playthrough, because you're not really prompted to spend your points at intervals that were more frequent in 4 and 5. They have toned down a lot of the quick time events (QTE), and they ported them over with the proper frame rates so that you don't need to switch between a keyboard and a controller. 

However, I do like the style in which they presented the stories the characters have found themselves in. It's a mix of canon and non-canon so that new co-op players didn't need to understand the previous story to play along. But, if they did... they might feel a little lost in the absurdity. The franchise was never known for true character development - just insane action. Unfortunately, their attempt to capture 4 unique stories leads to four very convoluted short plots that may have made more sense to the player if they were able to switch between characters. Now, the onus is on the player to essentially play the game four different times for context that they may or may not want. I guess that would have made the game feel even longer than it already played out, and as a result of this fragmented approach to telling Resident Evil's story I'm able to uninstall the game after finishing Leon's story. From there, I feel no guilt about trying to piece in frivolous parts of the story that were already touched upon in one campaign. But, if you care about that character's appearance in the first storyline you take on, then you're free to revisit it from that perspective. There's just not enough there from a combat/story perspective for me to want to do so.

Part of me also just feels spoiled at this point - they have a great action/horror formula that does work. However, I think I'm just at the point where it gets tiresome. The wheel is never invented. The same boss will follow you around for half of the game, where just when you think you have it it finds some way to be unkillable for a few levels more. It fails to be substantive anymore. 

I should have just stopped at 5. If you're at that crossroad, please heed my long-winded advice.

Ugly, tedious, and bloated. The motivation for the changes made to Resident Evil 7 make so much more sense once you've experienced this game. 

The original RE games were, in my opinion, confusing, frustrating, and clunky. I was 12 when it was genre defining and it was too hard and complicated for me then - I had no particular love for the 'traditional' formula and no reason to care about where the series went. But at least then the Resident Evil games were a unique property - something that did what they did better than the imitators around them. So where RE 4 hit a precious middle-ground in increasing the pace of the action without losing sight of what made the series enjoyable (a lucky shot that could just have easily missed the mark), RE 5 began emitting the whiff of corporate mandating as pilfered gameplay elements from other properties and genres began to creep into the series to draw in a larger player base. 

In Resident Evil 6 we see the natural end-point of swapping creative design for profit-motive. This game reeks of gimmicky excess standing in for a desperate lack of inspiration - the kind of creative bankruptcy that stained so many games of the 20-teens and rendered them utterly forgettable amongst the quagmire of conceptual plagiarism they all engaged in as they scrabbled for shreds of consumer attention like rats in a dumpster. 

If you want a bombastic 3rd-person shooter made in Japan play Binary Domain. It shares many frustrations with RE 6, but is better than you expect it to be. At least that game throws itself entirely in the direction it's leaning rather than trying to keep one foot in two worlds that are diametrically opposed in terms of tone and pace. RE 6 wants to be a high-octane action shooter while also forcing dated and annoying gameplay mechanics onto the player to simulate tension it can't organically manufacture when the narrative arc is 'kill zombie' and the entire game can be played by pressing one button at a time. 

I don't have any great investment in the series' creative direction. Who gives a sh*t what a game does mechanically if it does it well? But they say that if a book doesn't grab you in the opening chapter, then it hasn't earned your time. Resident Evil 6 throws a lot at you in its opening chapter and like so many that tried this same tactic, it fails to pull it off better than the games its aping. It's enjoyed something of a critical resurgence as expectations have boiled down and while I can appreciate that it's some mindless, functional fun with a solid amount of content on offer, I've played far too many milquetoast rip-offs trying to snatch some of Gears of War's success to endure this without a very stale taste in my mouth. 

Resident Evil 6 is the point a creative, innovative property truly buckled and became a cowed plagiarist desperate for attention. Capcom came around and closed the circle with its 7th release, but I cannot imagine a scenario in which 4 separate campaigns built on the paltry foundations of this game can provide something worth the time it would take to explore them.

I wouldn’t recommend RE6. I bought it specifically to play with a friend, but we lost motivation halfway through the final character campaign. It wasn’t even much fun, because the second player was a dispensable mob character with no bearing on the RE universe. RE5 gets a bad rap, but aside from its terrible camera, the game is a blast in co-op. Thus, I will compare the two and discuss key points that come to mind.

Bugs. RE6 seemed buggy and not well-coded. There were a couple time times in which events simply wouldn't trigger even though we figured out what we had to do in order to progress a boss fight or checkpoint.

Gameplay. Fewer puzzles than RE5, more standard objectives like survive within a time limit, kill all enemies, etc. They also removed shared inventory. Overall, there is less of a feeling that you need to depend on your partner to survive. I did not like this. However, I enjoyed the skill tree system in which you upgrade your hero (not the weapons themselves, as was the case in RE5).

Camera angles. I died more to the sudden irreversible changes in camera angles than to final bosses. After a cutscene ends and a chase + QTE sequence begins, you may have to hold backward to go forward. The timing is tight, so one of us would frequently get caught and killed. It was really frustrating to see our score go down because of this. You didn't have to worry about this in RE5.

Gamma. Holy hera! The gamma calibration was so off in comparison to other RE games. At first, I followed the instructions to turn it down until you could barely see the symbol. However, I literally could not see anything around my character. I was constantly stumbling into things and getting attacked from my periphery. The game was not remotely enjoyable until I cranked gamma up to 20.

QTEs. Strict timing like in RE5, but manageable. There were actually fewer QTEs during cutscenes than I would have liked. It was a bit boring to sit through them, because I don't know anyone who actually watches RE cutscenes for the story. A plus is that the QTE inputs were more consistent, whereas RE5 gave me PTSD by switching it up between left + right, action button, and crouch.

Driving sequences. These were the death of me.  I never want to see a snowmobile ever again. I crashed and died 10-11 times each time we had to navigate a vehicle. You have to drive so fast that you can’t even see the obstacles, but you can’t slow down either. Otherwise, you’ll get caught by enemies from behind, or the target you’re chasing gets away and you fail the checkpoint.

I've seen a lot of people say that Resident Evil 6 is a terrible game that nobody should play. I believe these are people who have jumped on the "mindlessly hate something" bandwagon and refused to give the game a fair shot. While the game doesn't live up to some of the highlights of the series like RE2 and RE4, it's still a pretty fun shooter game, whether you play solo or with a friend.

The good:
- Lots of returning beloved characters in the RE universe
- Great value; includes 4 full story campaigns to choose from (takes about 4-8 hours to complete each [I've played two so far] ), plus extra modes
- Interesting enemy designs and distinct enough campaigns to warrant playing all of them
- Entertaining (but not perfect) story, good for any fan of the RE universe
- Co-op; probably very fun to play with a friend (I played it solo)
- Some very flashy and satisfying melee attacks

The bad:
- Wonky controls and mechanics (specifically in the movement and HUD systems) that take some getting used to. You might want to play on a controller to save yourself from a headache.
- Story can be a bit weird at times due to the inclusion of co-op and so many main characters.
- Not as well balanced as RE4 and RE5, with some "what do I do" moments. I also found myself running out of ammo a lot more often than in those games.

It's not a perfect game. It might even be my least favorite in the series, but it's still pretty enjoyable and has great value if you can find it on sale.

RE6 is a body horror action adventure game that hits all the spots you would expect from a big title. Enemy variety is extensive and the bosses are creative, almost puzzle-like. The three most commendable aspects of the game are the detailed environments and enemy designs, as well as the impressive amount of content it has to offer. The enemies' animations are impressively realistic for the time, all the while looking great. Some of the environments, like the chinese shantytown are so thoroughly detailed, they were the highlights of RE6 for me. As for the extensive amount of content, RE6 offers four campaigns with interwoven stories, which all work off of each other beautifully.

The gunplay and the co-op multiplayer are top-notch, the story can be a bit hard to follow, but once you finish all four campaigns, everything will fall into place. The enemy variety and replay value are commendable, all the characters are lovable. The music is forgettable.

The game suffers from some issues however, the main culprit being the chase segments. Often times the game will put you through a chase scene where you have to dash, while avoiding enemy attacks with QTE based moves, or by shooting at the enemy. This can get very confusing, as often times the logical thing is not what the developers thought you should do and you inevitably die because you were supposed to run away when you stood your ground, or vice versa.  Another detriment is the character control in tight spaces. The guy you control pivots like you are driving a car, which can get annoying in corridors.

Despite the faults, Resident Evil 6 is a surprisingly solid experience all around.

I have mixed feelings about the series all the way to this installation. Though in the end, I still somehow had fun with this game.

First of all starting from Resident evil 4-ish, 5, 6 feel like a different genre than the first few games. More action, less horror. Don't get me wrong they are pretty fun action games, but if you are waiting to be scared, on the edge of your seat, then you might not expect what you're looking for especially in this game.

Resident Evil 6 is mostly all action except for the very beginning. There are four chapters to this game. Leon, Chris, Jake, Ada, and also a Prelude which is a tutorial I'm pretty sure. I'll describe them in a few sentences.
[list]
[*]Leon's campaign starts off on a somewhat horror-ish atmosphere, but later on gets pretty action-y in the ending levels.

[*]Chris's campaign is all gun's blazing, no horror in any of his levels whatsoever.

[*]Jake's campaign is a pretty interesting one compared to the others. Action with more emphasis on hand-to-hand combat, enhanced human abilities, and a somewhat character development between the two characters. No horror.

[*]Ada's campaign has action, but with some stealth mixed into it. Personally my favorite campaign because she is solo, so there are no partners in her story except if you're playing coop with a friend. And no horror of course.
[/list]

People dislike RE6 because it changes too much; I dislike RE6 because it is like the whole RE series, feeling totally clumsy in terms of fighting.

Obviously in RE6, players are expected to play and replay through a chapter to earn points that are used to unlock abilities. While highest difficulty certainly demands these abilities, it is fine without them at normal difficulty. But the issue comes from the game-play, not the point system.

To collect the points, one can't just evade every zombie like the series used to encourage; but the fighting system, is a mess. It has two major defaults that makes the game much lesser than it could have achieved.

Issue one is the CQC. In general play, one will see about half the attack from the character coming from the CQC. However, considering how the game picks the over-the-shoulder camera, CQC is inconvenient. The camera is too close to the character, close enough to cover too much screen space to allow easy loss of track of your target, which is worsened by the very low brightness the game promotes, which is actually a universal issue of the whole RE series. CAPCOM seems to expect everyone in the world to have an HDR capable monitor. After that comes the CQC attack itself. Well, it lacks "aim-assist", by which means it should auto-lock onto the target within range, and slightly pulls the character forward to allow a hit. But this game doesn't. With all of these issues putting together, the result is an extremely broken experience that the character initiates attacks on a zombie then quickly miss all the CQC attacks, taking time to aim again like using a gun to be able to hit. It is terrible.

Issue two, ironically, comes from the fact that there are too many weapons - more weapon types is good, but not when the character takes them all at once in every battle. Swapping to the correct weapon is tedious, ammo types dropped in a game is scripted so any weapons that you won't get ammo drops in a chapter are nothing but slot occupiers with one magazine to shoot. It should have allow the player to pick which weapon to bring before a chapter, and let the in-chapter ammo drops following the choice.

And the universal problem of RE series: the game expects the player to memorize the map. In RE6, this takes the form of extremely frequent map events all of which is a scripted kill if not reacted correctly. From the perspective of game design, map memorization should be an option that boosts the gameplay experience if done, not a source of punishment if not done. RE has always chosen the latter, and it is not the right option.

If the two (or three) issues are not there, I would say RE6 is a game of very high quality with very good gameplay. Unfortunately, it is an "if", not how it is.

Resident Evil 6 is not good. nut it souldn't have been this way. On paper, this should've been the slam-dunk and the magnum opus of the action RE games. The problem is, the game is a bloated, ugly and unfocused mess. 

The story of the game s broken up into four separate campaigns, where you play as different characters in different places. Each of the campaigns tells it's own story, but fits into larger narrative and each serve as a piece of the puzzle that connects the main mystery of the game. You can play any campaign in any order you want, but to actually understand the story as a whole, you have to play them all.
The story of the game is very convoluted and bloated beyond any strectch. Not only you have to follow 7 different characters in their own stories, the game itself is full of filler, while not even explaining what the hell is going on. The gameplay is just constantly interrupted with cutscenes of people talking what they need to do to poceed, which annoying, and most of the cutscenes you can't even skip. 
There are some good moments in tehre, but there are two main issues. First, the game takes itself way too seriously, constantly talking about how fate of the entire world is on the line. There is not a trace of some kind of jokiness and lighthearted fun in any situation, everyone is super-serious and doesn't want to make or take jokes at all. Second, the characters are actually unbearable, they are either stupid, act like a-holes, or bland and boring as a piece of wood. leon most of the game just follows around and does what everyone else tells him to do. Chris was completely butchered, erasing progress of his character from RE5 completely, and making him petty whiny b*tch. Jake, while being the son of one the most charismatic characters in the series, acts like an ididot, a-hole and he is bland uninteresting all at the same time. 
And at the same time, the ideas presented here are worth explorring. it is definetely interesting to explore Chris' inner psyche after so much war and fighting, because he probably would suffer from some kind of PTSD. Jake and Sherry beign kids of the biological war are actually worth talking about in the context of RE, two characters who's parents were responsible for so much horror and tragedy, using their gifts to fight for the good of the world is intriguing. But why in this game? Why Jake has to be the most awful character written in RE series? Why Chris has to suffer right after the game he got his closure with Jill and Wesker?  Why Leon does nothing but simping over Ada?

Then there are graphivs. The game actually looks ugly. There is this blue/grey filter over everything at all times. The textures are low-resolution and blurry, it's like they took 144p picture and streched into FullHD. The particle effects look cheap. The game actually looks like a remaster of a PS2 title. the only good part of the games visuals are character modles. There is certainly a lot of love and care put into them But there rest of the game is just unpleasant to look at. 

But how the game actually plays? Well, RE6 tries to be this action game, with big and crazy setpieces, loud combat and cool moves. The blueprint of RE4 is here, third-person camera, manual aiming and shooting, butnow movement is no longer tank-control based, characters can freely strafe around and even move while aiming. The game also borrows a lot of the mechanics from it's contemporaries, like cover system, sprinting and dodge-rolls. The game tries to blend RE stuff, with something like Uncharted, maybe a little bit of Call of Duty Modern Warfare, it tries to be as much of spectacle as possible, while provifing tight gameplay in combat.
But everything feels sloppy and weird. The movement has so much lag. Incredible combat of Re4 is gone, because there is no actual combat sandbox, the game just throws enemies at you and you just shoot them. new melee moves look cool, but rely too muvh on context sensitive inputs and require you tyo manage this new stamina gauge, which is probably was put there for you to not abuse powerful melee attacks, but in the end just punishes you for having fun. There is this weird new quick-shot mechanic, whioch probably should be used to interrupt attacks and stagger enemies, but sometimes enemies can decide to not react to it at all. 
Also, what is worng with this UI? Instead of classic grid based inventory, you get this weird wheel that looks different on each character. In older games you just pick the grid you want and do whatever you want with it. Here you have to actaully sroll to the thing you want to use, and then press a button to use it. The herbs are reworked that now they act as some sort of pills, and if you mix herbs you just get more pills that you can swallow. and tose pills have their own separate space when stored. so there is no reason to hold your herbs and they waste space in your inventory until you find red herb to mis them with. There is also problem with ammo. The game either showers you with it so much you don'e know what to do with it, or doesn't give you any at all, instead giving you new points for the awful skill system.
the skill system should be a replacement for buying new weapons and upgrades. Some skills give you more damage, some improve you defence, some can even spice up your gameplay with something unique. But the price on those skills are just outrageous. You would have to grind hard until you get skills you want leveled up. The game is long, but even then, at the end you would have only a couple of skills leveled up to maximum. 
But the biggest problem with the game is how much it tislef stops you from laying. The game constatly eitehr stuns you, you shakes the cameera around, or locks you into a QTE section, or just straight up takes control away from you, especially in sequences where you have to run in the crumbling facility and sking ships, where there is an earthquake every 30 seconds that shakes everything and doesn't let you control anything until it decides to stop. The game relies so hard on QTEs, that everything you do would be a QTE. Brreak away from enemy, turn a valve, press a button, hit an enemy. Everything is QTE., and the kind of QTE that people bullied so hard it was deleted from gaming last console generation. 
And there is still forced co-op even if you play solo. Thankfully, unlike RE5, now your AI companion is invincible, has unlimited ammo, and you don't need to manage it's inventory. The only function it has is to assist you in scritpted sequences and help you get up after you lose all of your HP. But now you can't even pause the game. Even if you disconnect from the internet, you can not stop it.Just why you would fix one thing and then completely break the other?

All of this piles up into very annoying and unpleasant experience. I know there are still people that enjoy this game and it's own brand of action. it's now in thephase where people can even nostalgic about it. But it should've ben a lot better. The series desrves better, the fans deserve better. As big blockbuster action game, it severely lacks polish of AAA game and is too clunky to be a glorious action experience it wants to give you. Even budge ttitle such as Devil May Cry 4, despite reusing assets and having troubled development from the same company, just focused on what matters and made the game really good. And that is probably what RE6 lacks the most, focus. It tries to be too many things at once, trying to please fans and new comers, trying to be both RE and not RE. This is a failure that could put any other franchise into the grave. Good thing Re is an everchanging frachise at this point. And it always deserved a second chance.

Enemy placement is just irritating (like placing an enemy on top of you when you can't aim straight upwards, or spawning an enemy with a gun shooting your face when your char calmly finishes climbing a ladder where you couldn't see upwards), enemies are boring (you fight enemies with guns 80% of the game, wich makes the game looks a generic shooter, and enemy design itself it not attractive), zombie mutations makes it look like you're playing L2D (wich makes the game lose it's identity and looks like a generic zombie game), and some boss fights have so terrible and ridiculous fighting scenes that will make you miss Chris punching a boulder.

I can barely call it a game, actually, seem fanmade stuff far better than this, actual players wouldn't do this crap. Vertical Sync doens't work.

That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.

After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.

Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.

Being a fan of the series, it is painful to write a negative review of this game. Allow me to preface it by saying that a lot of things can be forgiven, if it's played with other players in co-op mode. The single-player walkthrough, however, is a painful experience.

So much of the game sounds amazing on paper: several story campaigns with returning fan-favorite and original characters spanning all over the globe, a few dozen of unique enemy types, improved combat mechanics with proper abilities to take cover and dodge attacks etc. But any improvement from previous games is coupled with severe signs that the game was rushed and ran out of budget: clunky controls, inconsistent level design (pacing is all over the place), terrible graphics (worse than Resident Evil 5 and some textures and models are straight from the 90s) and the story that relies a lot on re-used levels and assets.

Speaking of the story, it is horrendous. Without revealing spoilers, while actors try their best with terrible dialogue, the main story is a combination of things that we have seen before, but dialed to 11. If you thought Leon being a Secret Service agent saving the President's daughter in Spain was cheesy in RE4, you should be scared of how pulpy the story becomes in 6, but only this time it is not charming, but exhausting. Another power-hungry villain who comes out of nowhere with character depth of a shallow pond, even more crashing helicopters, exploding vehicles, bike chases and a non-ending stream of cheesy one-liners that would make Arnold proud. It is an absolute opposite of the first three games, and if 4 and 5 were a signal for you that the series was going the wrong way, Resident Evil 6 is an exclamation point to that idea, gleefully embracing its own stupidity and proudly flaunting its well-deserved label of being the worst game of the series.

P.S. This game is so bad, Capcom soft-rebooted the entire franchise after this.

RE6 is a weird one in the franchise—polarizing, loud, and all over the place—but despite all that, I genuinely enjoyed it. The best thing about RE6 is how it offers multiple campaigns with completely different tones and gameplay styles. Leon’s campaign leans toward classic horror vibes, Chris’ feels like a military action thriller, Jake’s mixes hand-to-hand chaos with tension, and Ada rounds everything out with a more stealth-focused approach.

The amount of content is huge, and the pacing constantly shifts, which keeps things interesting. Is it subtle? No. Is it occasionally ridiculous? Absolutely. But that unpredictability is part of its charm. The combat system is surprisingly deep and fluid once you get used to it, making encounters feel dynamic rather than repetitive.

Co-op also elevates the experience. Playing with a friend makes even the wildest or most absurd moments fun instead of frustrating. While it’s far from the pure survival horror tone of earlier entries, it embraces its identity as a chaotic action-horror rollercoaster.

It’s not perfect and definitely not what everyone wants from Resident Evil, but for me, it delivers a memorable and enjoyable experience packed with variety and replay value.

I've played 1 - 6 and Code Veronica X and I gotta say that this one is my favorite of the bunch. I really don't understand the hate that this game historically had. It's true that out of the series that this is the Michael Bay Resident Evil, but that's what makes it so fun. The fact that when it came out (and had the player base to support it) you could have intersecting campaigns online and play with two other people across the net in real time was amazing. I've played this one the most out of all of them (5 being a close second) and it's just fun. I didn't really like the original trilogy, for me they were a chore I had to power through to get the story I needed to play 5 and 6. I will say that Code Veronica X for me was a far more enjoyable experience than 1 - 3. I have not played 0 or 7 or the Revelations games.  Maybe in the future or if 0 gets a PC port. I think all of the negativity this game got was unfair and undue and exposed how toxic the gaming community can be sometimes. The bad reviews were completely unjustified. The fact that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like TLOU 2 can get overwhelmingly positive scores and this blockbuster blast of a game can be so widely panned just shows that the gaming media is not only clueless, but possibly even corrupt.

That being said, there are some issues. Some of the dialog is corny, some of the decisions made by characters in the game make absolutely no sense, and there are still some bugs that require a restart from time to time. There are times where it is completely over the top (perhaps even exceeding punching boulders) but I maintain that this is a personal preference and not an aspect of the game to be critiqued. I myself am a fan of machismo, actions movies, and 80s tough guys (for all three, check out Far Cry Blood Dragon, an incredible homage to the era) so boulder punching for me isn't lame or silly, it's something to get pumped over.

If you enjoy fun shoot em ups, like the Resident Evil universe, or just want a good time with friends, I highly recommend it. These days more than ever we could use a fun popcorn flick (or game) to distract us from all of the silliness in the world, and I think RE6 fits the bill.

RESUMEN GENERAL DE CAMPAÑAS.
Como antes mencione el promedio. El juego tiene una durabilidad de 20 horas aproximadamente. 5 horas por campaña.

Leon / Helena
Es la historia más parecida a la de un Resident Evil.

Chris / Piers
La historia es como si fuera esa tipica pelicula SUPER EXAGERADA de Acción.

Jake / Sherry
Pasa algo similar como con la de Chris y Piers. Es como si fuera tipica pelicula en la cual aparecen los mismos 2 protagonistas y el mismo antagonista de principio a fin.

Ada / Agent
Es la más complicadas en cuanto a introducción. Luego se vuelve más sencillo pero aun asi sigue siendo complicada.

•Multiple Historias

•Sistema de habilidades (Puede ayudar dependiendo tu manera de jugar pero no te genera un GRAAN cambio)

I did not get that. You only have one gun of each type per campaign (down from the 5 of each type in RE 5). Your inventory is a mess, and the controls are terribly convoluted even for a PC port. I found myself accidentally using things all the time since the use item button and the kick the zombie in the face button are the same button for some reason.

The real no no is how choppy and disjointed the boss fights are. There is a stupid amount of quicktime events in this game. The boss fights are literally 5-10 seconds of game play and 20 seconds of cutscenes. Some of the bosses we killed by letting the AI kill them we didn't even touch them.

On top of that the game has this annoying thing with zombies playing dead, corpses you know are zombies but the game renders them invincible till you get close enough for them to grab you. If you aren't aiming at the thing you have zero chance of avoiding it. We also noticed that for some reason the zombies seem to exclusively target player 1 and almost entirely ignore player 2. Unless they had no actual path to attack me, they never attacked my friend. We could have ten of them there and they would dog pile me and just totally ignore player 2. This is especially bad when you do Chris's story because most of the enemies have guns. In the first mission I'd been downed four times (we played on professional) and I'd used every single healing item we both had. My buddy was in front of me for half the mission. He was shot once. One time. The entire mission. I was lit up like a christmas tree hiding behind a wall and he's just walking around behind the zombies shooting them all to death while they hyper focus on killing me.

Then you have the skill system that replaced the shop in RE 5. This system is bad. What's the point in having a billion skills if you can only use three? Who is going to take "increased melee damage" over "take 75% less damage"? Who would take "Reduced recoil" over "Do more damage with ALL guns?". Basically every skill set turns into "more damage with guns" "reduced damage taken" and then "extra damage to (insert primary enemy type of the mode here)." With no reason to ever change it.
