I recommend RE6 but not if you’re looking for a classic RE experience.

There is an entertaining and decent story in this RE entry, there is even some praiseworthy character development, but some of what happens is so over-the-top silly you’ll find yourself laughing. I’m laughing right now just thinking about it. However, if you’re able to set aside the absurdity and not take those parts seriously you’ll enjoy this game.

This is not survival horror. This is action horror; and there is a lot of it. Good controls, music is thrilling, and graphics are great. There is a generous amount of content. Four different campaigns that each could be half a Triple A game (it’s like getting two full games in one). You can still have a great time playing the game on your own, but this was certainly intended for people to have fun playing the various modes online in co-op with their friends or others.

Gameplay does get tiresome, though it is not overly repetitive. Plays well on KB+M. Hand-to-hand combat is a great addition and there is variety in enemies. Inventory management is attempted (you get a limit on what you can carry) but it seems out-of-place for a game like this. Unable to assign hotkeys to weapons. In-game points are collected to ‘purchase’ Skills to obtain advantages (stronger weapons, improved defense, etc.), and while this mechanic seems interesting at first it becomes less rewarding over time. I find most, not all, QTEs annoying and distracting from cutscenes. Not many tension-building moments. It’s clear the developers put in a lot of hard work and tried to make this fun to play. Overall, I’d say it’s a great game with some ridiculous story moments and a few poor mechanics choices. 

RE6 gets a heavy amount of criticism because it strays very far from its predecessors. The detractors have a point, you expect some level of survival horror from a Resident Evil title. However, it’s as I said above, if you’re able to set expectations aside and try to enjoy the game for what it is, I think you’ll like it.

[h1]Story[/h1]
As it's name suggest, this is the sixth installment of the RE series. It's a 3rd person view. It offers players 4 campaign and each campaign has 5 chapters. It comes in 5 difficulty levels: Amateur, Normal, Veteran, Professional and No Hope.

    [*]One woman's crazy out of this world, hell bent revenge story - Made RE 6

Upon completion of a chapter, players are rewarded with Experience points which will be used to purchase skills for your character. You can only equip up to 3 skills in a slot. Resident Evil 6 takes the spot as my 2nd favorite in the series for the campaign focused games. My 1st still goes to Resident Evil 4, the game which introduced me to the series. I played the Play station 2 version. Which funny enough, many years later, I find out was the worst edition of the game you could play. 

Resident Evil 6 takes the best of everything in the series and mashes it together, while sprinkling some modern and mainstream elements to appeal to a larger audience. The main focus in this title isn't multiplayer, but with the sheer amount of content and amazing combat, it has the same feeling of endless replay-ability that multiplayer tries achieve. Starting with 4 different campaigns, all following their own set of characters with their own themes and styles that intertwine like a spider web. ( Very nice foreshadowing done with the artwork. ) There are some hiccups that take getting used to, but once you work a bit with those this becomes an easy 10 / 10 for me.

( + Positive ) 4 unique and themed campaigns. 

- Campaign 1 follows Leon and Helena with RE2 / RE3 Vibes. With it's city, underground labs, and horror themes, this campaign feels the most like a taste of the originals. But faster paced and way more action packed than you'd expect. 

- Campaign 2 Follows Chris and Piers in foreign places with RE5 vibes. Seemingly the most soldier fantasy of the bunch, it involves a lot of run and gun / cover shooting action. This was the weakest campaign in my opinion because it's style and map design doesn't entice you to play differently at all, unlike the other 3. 

- Campaign 3 Follows Jake and Sherry, in a RE4 / RE3 style. There is a lot more emphasis on counter attacks and melee in this campaign, and I love it. Jake has a really cool melee fighting style that's easy to learn, but hard to master. And a bad-ass snarky personality to match it. You'll be pursued a lot through this campaign by an enemy in a similar sense to RE3's Nemesis. 

- Campaign 4 Follows Ada and Agent ( Agent only appears in multiplayer. ) This is very unique as it's the only campaign originally without a partner, and introduces some stealth sequences. Nothing super deep and hardcore, which is fine as it keeps the game still interesting and playable for people who aren't into that.

( + Positive ) - Combat is extremely satisfying. You have gun play that entices you to slow down to aim, opening up possibilities for getting overwhelmed. Various weapons have weaknesses like pump / bolt action that reward you for proper positioning. Others reward you for being able to control their spread and recoil, most commonly on the automatics. There is a weapon that looks like an AK with a bayonet that has ridiculous recoil in my opinion. You'll see when you get it. Melee combat uses a stamina system that limits the amount of punches and kicks you can do fairly. These attacks also animation lock you, forcing commitment and decision making on when to do them. This also applies to enemies as well, you can use this against them and do timed counter attacks to often instant kill them in satisfying ways.

( + Positive ) - There never seems like enough ammo, which works great. You can carry all the weapons you find in a Doom style. Ammo problems force you to constantly swap weapons and mix melee into your fighting for even more interesting engagements.

( + Positive ) - Massive enemy variety that puts RPG's to shame. Lots of enemies will mutate when injured and gain various abilities like armor or long tentacle arms that can grab you out of cover. As if the combat wasn't already awesome and dynamic enough, this adds another layer of fun.

( + Positive ) - Map design is amazing, there are lots of boxes to break for items, chests that look like a part of the environment, and even doors that lead to secret rooms of goodies. Various maps offer fun environmental ways to kill enemies as well, such as cliffs, explosive barrels, and even putting a severed hand in a microwave. Paths always seem straight forward and easy to navigate with side rooms to check out. If you get lost, you can at any time press Q to tell you where to go.

( + Positive ) - Lots of titles, name cards, and level progression. You can collect points to purchases skills in a shop, 3 of which you are allowed to use at a time in campaign and 1 at a time in the special modes. There are costumes you can unlock in the special modes as well by playing and participating in events on https://www.residentevil.net/en/p1712106.html which are still active to this day.

( + Positive ) - There are an abundance of quick time events to test your reflexes and see how well you're paying attention. I have seen a lot of complaints about them, but did you know there's an option in the settings to turn them off? Turning this on maps it impossible to fail majority of the events. There are a few that you will still have to do, but their the simple tap the button a few times kind. You aren't under much pressure in these situations. 

( + Positive ) -  Another huge complaint I've seen that I'm also going to list as a positive is the action. We are talking movie levels of action and it's epic to play through. I get where this complaint is coming from if you're getting into 6 from the previous titles. But this is a new age, a new generation. While I can appreciate the fun of a slow paced survival horror game, every single survival horror game does not need to be like that. RE Village / 8 is nearly as action packed as 6 but you don't see people throwing up a storm the way they did for this game.

( - Negative ) - For as much as this game offers replay-ability, some cut scenes are unskippable and certain sections that force you to walk get extremely tedious. There are also some area's that force you to look at something while you're in the middle of something else. Not really a major issue, but it can be annoying at times.

( - Negative ) - Too many skills are not balanced well or too situational, meaning you'll be defaulting to a handful of them.

( - Negative ) - The inventory is pretty janky, even once you get used to it. The ammo stack limits are extremely questionable as well. You can hold 150 handgun bullets in 1 slot, but only 60 assault rifle rounds in 1 slot. If this ever gets a remake, I'd really want to see it redone in the Remakes / Resistance style. For whatever reason it slows you down to walking speed when switching weapons, and you are able to rapid fire pump shotguns and bolt action snipers by rapidly swapping back and forth between them to skip the animation.

Resident Evil 6 was released in 2012 as part of the long-running Resident Evil franchise.  The series has varied between campy B-movie survival horror to campy B-movie action game-ish survival horror to campy B-movie action game and anything inbetween. RE6 is what happens when someone decides to mix all that together with flavour du jours, design by committee, and mix it in a blender.  The end result is a mildly unexpected crackpot of flavours, both good and bad.

RE6 gameplay follows up from its recent predecessors.  It keeps up mostly RE4\5-ish gameplay while improving certain aspects: smoother control, being able to strafe as opposed to tank controls in 3D, more variable interactions (and downsides of single key for everything) and essentially minor quality of life changes rather than stiff, fixed aspects that were present in 4 and 5.  It is perhaps the first modern RE game where control feels slightly more practical.  Depending how well one utilises new functions one can do at will as opposed to forced QTEs, the game can feel rather easy without being as arbitrary as previous entries.  And speaking of QTEs, there are plenty of press X not to die -moments so it is another tradition they certainly kept alive here.

RE6 has four campaigns in total, all featuring differing styles and overlapping story made of spaghetti.  You have Leon's campaign which is just slightly more in line with traditional, zombie style RE with 0.1% more focus on avoiding enemies and not nuking everything in sight, Chris' campaign which is akin to cheerful bastard child of so-called modern military shooter and B-film quadruple cheeseburger where you want to nuke everything in sight, Jake's campaign takes minor inspiration from generic stealth section elements where the AI wants to nuke you as much as possible, and finally there is Ada's campaign which combines every campaign into one giant overflowing pasta dish.  Every single campaign is available from the beginning, but would I recommend playing them in order as the game is frequently keen to outdo itself in true Ed Wood fashion.  Just get someone to play the game with and enjoy the rollercoaster of spaghetti outbreak.

Why? The creme of the crop that truly cultivates RE6 is the general plot and structure.  Over its lifespan the series went from medical company going for super soldiers to other convoluted masterplans to plans to take over a country to common bioterrorism and how to handle it with maybe tint of politics thrown to the mix.  Yet enter RE6 where it is as comprehensive as the efforts of few kids in kindergarten end up making epic story where armoured T-Rex swoops in with helicopters from the Moon to save the day from giant rats and sharks while Captain Boulder rolls down the hill through radiation and they all enjoy a sandwich at the end in a tea party on Mars except space raptors interrupted the tea party and sent them back to Earth so they can continue their nefarious plans by telling raptors had feathers so they would fly to space and avoid extinction.  Then someone pitched it to be produced and backed by serious budget and production values by passionate team.  Thus RE6 is bent in trying to outdo itself constantly to the point is beyond ridiculous.  Combine this with masterfully campy and serious B-movie atmosphere, functional and action-packed gameplay that has enough explosions to rival average Michael Bay film, and suddenly it is one of the most bafflingly entertaining, confusing, nonsensical, yet weirdly functional mishmash that can only happen by happy accident.  Or under influence.  Or having absolutely no idea what they were doing.  Or all combined.

I am not sure if calling the game the most entertaining trainwreck ever made even makes justice.  Ironic novelty or not, between functional gameplay with sometimes more inventory management puzzles than the old games combined and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane plot and presentation, it certainly is something amazing and all I can still say is, play it with a friend and enjoy the even more amazing experience of what the ♥♥♥♥ is even going on anymore.

The game's strength is it's story, which is made up of 4 interwoven campaigns. The best of these are Chris and Jake's campaign. Which stay interesting all the way through. New characters introduced to the series in these campaigns are also interesting, especially Jake and Piers, who maintain a strained allied relationship with Chris through out, both of them building up towards emotional conclusions in their relations to Chris. Chris, who's arguably the central character of the entire franchise, also has an interesting new angle added to his character in this game, bridging his character between 5 and 7, but not in a way that can be guessed from either game. Sherry Birkin, the little girl from Resident Evil 2 makes a comeback as an adult as well, which at first promised to be interesting, but was less so than expected. While she was still a likable and fairly interesting character, she tended to be overshadowed by other characters, making her the most forgettable character of both Chris and Jake's campaigns.

The reason Sherry isn't the most forgettable character is because of Leon's sidekick during his campaign, Helena. I'm honestly not totally sure what she added to the narrative. While chapter 2 of Leon's story built her up to have an emotional revenge plot, I feel like this was simply forgotten the absolute next chapter in favor of just letting Leon punch stuff for the next three hours. From the end of Chapter 2 to the end of the game, Helena is a boring, passive character.

Leon's story as a whole is pretty boring and unfocused throughout, which is a surprise considering Leon is the one fighting the villain of this game, a discount Albert Wesker who also ends up as pretty forgettable. The only thing that saves either this campaign or this villain is Ada's campaign. While it starts out weak, it ties up a lot of the loose ends throughout the three other campaigns, and ends up being pretty strong, as well as hinting at a more emotional side of Ada than we've seen in any other games.

I'm personally a fan of the interwoven storyline, but I know not everyone was. While each character only makes a few brief cameos in the other characters campaign, they all revolve a central plot that ties them together, and brings together many of the characters from the first two RE games. It's sorta like Pulp Fiction or Babel in that way.

Combat is also kinda hit or miss throughout the game. As a third person shooter like 4 and 5, there's an action focus to it, with the added feature of being able to walk while aiming for the first time in the series, as well as having a much stronger focus on melee combat than any other game. This encourages movement, but the game rarely gives you space to move. You run out of both ammo and stamina too quickly in this game, often leaving you totally defenseless. Also, the lack of any aim assist with a controller makes shooting much more clumsy than it should be. Despite all of these drawbacks, combat can at times still end up being fun, and in these moments, it's really fun. Couldn't tell you why lol

More often than not, both combat and puzzle solving is just tedious in this game. Puzzles are either so simple that they can't really be called puzzles, or so devoid of any sort of clue that you have no idea how to possibly solve them. This makes the game annoying and longer than it has to be.

This is honestly all that stuck out to me.

TL;DR: Chris story good, Jake story good, Leon story bad, Ada story okay. Combat and puzzles boring, sometimes good.

[h1] Intro [/h1]
Resident Evil 6 is a game that blends both action and horror but fails in both departments. It was an anticipated sequel back in 2012. However, It failed as both a sequel to Resident Evil 5 and as a game on its own. The game is disappointing in many aspects, including gameplay, story, characters, and mechanics. This game is probably one of the worst Resident Evil titles that I have played. I will detail below all the issues the game has, and why I can't recommend this game to anyone unless you want some mindless co-op fun because outside of that, the game offers nothing of what you expect from a Resident Evil title.



[h1] Gameplay & Mechanics [/h1]
The gameplay and shooting mechanics in Resident Evil 6 are quite similar to RE5, so there isn't much difference in this department. RE6 continues with the same co-op element from RE5. You have four campaigns, and each campaign has two characters. You get to choose to play with one of the characters while an A.I or an online player can play with the other character. I never played this game with an A.I partner, so I can't comment on how good or bad It is. The game is extremely over the top to the point of ridiculousness. Enemies aren't fun to fight and are there only to annoy you as they continue to mutate when you kill them and have to waste a lot of time and resources to kill them. They aren't fun to face or even challenging; they're just there to timegate you as much as possible. There are certain areas and missions where you can't even avoid them. You have to kill all the enemies you see to progress through the story. This mechanic goes against most of the previous RE games, where you were able to avoid enemies most of the time to conserve ammo and resources. I also want to point out that the Ada campaign doesn't really do co-op properly as it's meant to be played solo, they give you the option to play with a partner. Still, that partner is basically invisible and has no role in the story. He's just there to tag along with Ada and shoot enemies. Still, he can't interact with anything, which is quite disappointing.

The menu system in this game is quite terrible and convoluted. I have no idea why it was designed this way because It's tough to navigate through. Similarly, the item management menu is also a mess and isn't as good or as user friendly as the previous RE titles. You also get various weapons in the game, but sadly all four campaigns share most of the same weapons, so you don't get many unique weapons with each of the different campaigns. Everything ends up feeling similar and familiar as you play through them, and the only thing that will be different is the characters and some of the locales. 

The boss battles in RE6, to say the very least, are mostly all bad and are annoying to face as you face them numerous times throughout each of the campaigns. Each campaign has its own boss, but you fight them so often that It gets tiring and boring to face them for the fourth or fifth time. There isn't much variety or challenge when facing them. 

The game is also extremely padded because, throughout the campaigns, the main characters meet each other at specific points in the game, and help each other throughout the mission. You have to redo all these missions when you play the other campaigns. I feel that these missions are there just to pad the game and add length, as they bring nothing to the table other than making you go through the same level but with different characters. It's Capcom's way of cutting corners and making the game feel artificially longer, which is just disappointing.

[h1] Story [/h1]
The story in RE6 is disappointing as well. I'm not going to pretend that the previous titles of Resident Evil were amazing masterpieces when it comes to story, but at least they were good enough to fit their own narrative. However, with RE6, the game's story is ridiculous and is way over the top that you can't help but laugh at how the story unravels and how the characters react to what's going on. There are so many pointless over the top action cutscenes that make you roll your eyes and ridicule their absurdity. The story has crossovers with each of the characters in all of the campaigns. Still, these crossovers are mostly pointless and do nothing to improve the story or narrative, as the characters only meet briefly and then never meet each other again.

The characters in RE6 are also as bland as the story. Many of the characters are either dumbed down or just outright generic that almost none of them shine. Even returning characters like Leon or Chris don't feel like their previous incarnations and are dumbed down to fit the plot. The story, in general, is a major snoozefest.

[h1] Graphics & Sound [/h1]
For a 2012 game, Resident Evil 6 doesn't look bad at all. I think the graphics are quite good for its time as I have played Deadspace 3 recently, and the game was released in 2013 and looked worse than RE6 in the graphics and texture department. I will also point out that the monster mutations and animations are pretty well done and are unique. So I can praise RE6 on this one.

The sound design is nothing special, nor is it atmospheric, there is not much to talk about when it comes to sound design. It's just okay.


 [h1] The Good Parts [/h1]
The only good part about this game was the co-op. It does co-op pretty well, and for a co-op game, it was entertaining. The game also made me laugh many times at its ridiculousness, I don't know if you'd consider this as a positive, but hey gotta give the game something. 

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
Resident Evil 6 is a disappointing game. There's not much to say. The game fails in almost everything that it offers. The only thing that works well is the co-op component. 

My overall rating for this game is a 5/10. I can only recommend this game if you have a friend and want to play a mindless third-person shooter co-op game, then this game could be fun for you. However, if you're expecting something great or at least something as good as the previous Resident Evil titles, then I suggest avoiding playing this game altogether.

Melee in this game is a chore because of the stamina meter and because the range of your attacks is so pitifully small it's worthless. Enemies take multiple stomps on the ground which wouldn't normally matter but because there's a stamina meter it limits your ability to eliminate crawling or grounded enemies. Also you spend more time in end lag on missed melee attacks than the attacks are actually active. This is especially frustrating in Jake's campaign because he has a separate melee system and a majority of his attacks don't land or are interrupted by gunshots and enemy melee.

The game will put you into a cutscene of some exciting ♥♥♥♥, let you walk forward for a few feet, collect supplies and then shove you right back into another cutscene. There are invisible walls everywhere and there are a few times where it says you can perform an action but you actually can't. In the prelude, there's a section where no matter what direction you try to move in, it forces you to move forward and then turn to the right as if the game genuinely just expects you to only press those and hoped you wouldn't notice. A section involving a motorcycle says you have a brake button but if you press it while driving it does nothing. CONCLUSION:

There are many things wrong with this game, one being the story. It's really dumb and I hate it. Which is the case for a lot of video games I like because hey, you can skip a bad story, but you can't skip bad gameplay. But in the case of RE6 there are tons of unskippable mini cutscenes. Deal some damage to a boss. Unskippable cutscene of the boss recoiling. To some more damage to a boss, unskippable cutscene of it transforming. Oh and another thing about boss battles, they never end. They really stretch out these encounters that aren't fun in the first place, there's a part where you fight a snake boss, pretty standard for a RE game, but every time you deal a certain amount of damage to it it moves to a new room, and this process repeats five or six times and it's just so mindnumbingly boring. The combat is fine, you suplex zombies which while being incredibly dumb is pretty fun. I try to use as little ammo as possible and just punch everyone to death which is effective and indeed fun. [h1][b]A BROAD, UNEVEN ENTRY FOR THE SERIES' ENTHUSIASTS[/b][/h1]

Resident Evil 6 is ambitious in scope and temperament: multiple protagonists, shifting tones, and an attempt to blend frantic action with survival-horror beats. Played piecemeal, the game can be entertaining; played as a single, canonical statement within the franchise, it often feels disjointed. I purchased the game during the Summer Sale 2020 for €7, which colours my final recommendation, this is more often a bargain-hunt purchase than a must-buy at full price.

[h1][b]WHAT IT IS AND HOW IT WORKS[/b][/h1]
[quote]
[list]

[*][h2][b]STORY: 3/5[/b][/h2]
◾️ [b]Structure and clarity[/b]
The narrative is sprawling and deliberately fragmented: several campaigns present overlapping events from different viewpoints. For newcomers this structure can be confusing, and the coherence that longtime fans expect from the series is sometimes lacking. Playing through every campaign reveals a fuller picture, but the piecemeal approach will not suit everyone.

◾️ [b]Social play and pacing[/b]
Co-operative play makes some segments markedly more enjoyable, the multiplayer element can turn thin exposition into shared, kinetic fun. Even so, the story would have benefited from clearer signposting and tighter pacing.

[*][h2][b]GRAPHICS: 4/5[/b][/h2]
◾️ [b]Visual fidelity[/b]
The game remains visually impressive. Environments are richly detailed and the overall atmosphere is suitably bleak, matching the franchise’s aesthetic. Character models retain a solid level of quality and key scenes are well staged.

◾️ [b]Performance notes[/b]
There are occasional frame-rate dips in demanding sections, but these are generally sporadic and do not consistently undermine the experience. On balance the presentation holds up well.

[*][h2][b]SOUNDTRACK: 3.5/5[/b][/h2]
◾️ [b]Function over memorability[/b]
The score supports set pieces effectively, building tension when required. However, it rarely produces truly memorable themes on the scale of the series’ best work. The soundtrack does its job, but it seldom distinguishes itself.

[*][h2][b]CHARACTERS: 3/5[/b][/h2]
◾️ [b]Roster and development[/b]
The cast mixes familiar faces (Leon, Chris) with new leads, giving the game variety. Unfortunately several characters feel underwritten and some portrayals stray from earlier, better-defined incarnations, in particular, the handling of Ada Wong in one chapter may feel jarring to long-term fans.

◾️ [b]Variety versus depth[/b]
The breadth of perspectives is interesting, but it comes at the expense of deeper character work. Moments of genuine characterization exist, yet they are not consistently realised.

[*][h2][b]GAMEPLAY MECHANICS: 4/5[/b][/h2]
◾️ [b]Range and solidity[/b]
Mechanically the game is robust: it offers a wide variety of playstyles, from frenetic gunplay to more considered survival sections. The survival modes and cooperative systems add replayable challenge.

◾️ [b]Balance issues[/b]
Some sequences can become repetitive, and a small number of encounters disrupt the overall pacing. The core mechanics themselves remain solid, however.

[*][h2][b]COMPATIBILITY AND COHERENCE WITH OTHER ENTRIES: 2/5[/b][/h2]
◾️ [b]Tonality and continuity[/b]
Resident Evil 6 departs noticeably from previous entries in both tone and narrative focus. Fans looking for tight continuity may be disappointed: the story sometimes reads as disconnected from the series’ established throughline.

◾️ [b]Appreciating it on its own terms[/b]
If approached as a stand-alone chapter rather than a strict continuation, the game can be judged more kindly. Evaluated against earlier, more cohesive titles, it falls short.

[/list]

[b]BOUGHT DURING THE SUMMER SALE 2020 FOR €7[/b]

If you find it on sale, it still deserves a look from series devotees and listeners interested in military-themed plots.
[/quote]

[h1][b]WHAT ISN'T WORKING OUT?[/b][/h1]
[quote]
◾️ The fragmented narrative makes the game a poor entry point, newcomers will miss many of the emotional beats that rely on prior knowledge.

◾️ Several chapters favour spectacle or pleasant moments over meaningful dramatic payoff; some endings feel understated or anticlimactic.

◾️ Characterisation is uneven: a handful of portrayals depart from past iterations in ways that may irritate long-time fans.

◾️ Occasional performance dips and minor design repetitions interrupt immersion. These are not fatal, but they are noticeable.
[/quote]

[h1][b]JUDGEMENT[/b][/h1]
[quote]
[b]Resident Evil 6 is an uneven but sometimes rewarding experiment, broad in ambition, uneven in execution.[/b] It offers impressive visuals and a wide array of mechanics, and cooperative play can make many encounters genuinely fun. Yet its fragmented storytelling and inconsistent character work mean it rarely attains the narrative cohesion of the series’ best entries.

Good if you are a devoted series fan seeking varied gameplay and spectacle, and if you can appreciate the game as a collection of episodes rather than a single, unified statement. Not recommended as a first Resident Evil experience.

Purchase if you find it at a significant discount and you enjoy the idea of multiple playable campaigns. If you are uncertain, prefer to wait for a sale.
[/quote]

I had always been led to believe that Resident Evil 6 was the weakest of the mainline instalments for the Resident Evil franchise. Generally, the points brought up were that it had drifted too far from survival horror and was primarily a ridiculous action game.

While it is true that it is a ridiculous action game, the game is really fun. I like that there's a semi-complicated system for clearing zombies without using much ammo (hint: quickscope and melee, and if you run out of energy, flip onto your back and wait for it to recharge quickly), and I like that the body horror and gruesomeness is considerably more pronounced in this game than others, particularly the cocoons. Whoever came up with that design -- human beings frozen in their dying moments only to undergo a transformation like a caterpillar becoming the world's largest and grossest butterfly -- deserves a raise. Inspired.

If you're looking specifically for survival horror, while the game isn't as steeped in the genre as the most recent RE2 and RE3 remakes, Leon's section is thrilling and is definitely a form of survival horror. Maybe not the same kind as the games that spawned the franchise, but if it were under a different name, it would be as fondly remembered as Dead Space.

Anyway the game looks and sounds great, and the interlocking narrative structure, while a bit confusing, isn't badly done. I would do as I did and follow a guide for which chapters of which campaigns to do in which order.

In summary, get this game as a standalone action-horror experience even if you don't like Resident Evil (or perhaps especially if you're turned off by the serious stress of the most recent iterations). It's damn good fun.

After more than 21 hours playing this and just loosing every last bit of patience I had for it in the Ada campaign, I just gotta go and say it: this game f***** sucks. Oh man, where to begin uh? I knew Capcom had a fallout around this time and the RE franchise was one of its victims. If the franchise jumped the shark with its fifth entry then it completely touched rock bottom with this one. The game is full on 2010's action, and while its not true that it doesn't have horror elements, much more than 5 actually, its more of the first than the latter. The best way to talk about the plot is to analyze each campaing on its own, as Capcom tried to appeal to everybody while not appealing to anybody at all and, at the same time, further alienating their fanbase, but first, the gameplay.

Oh man, the gameplay. This continues with the co-op mechanics of the previous one. Make no mistake, this is a co-op online type game they tried to create here, and to a certain extent, they succeeded, but gone are the old isolated and terryfying atmospheres that made the originals, so if you are looking for that then you are gonna hate this more than I did. Luckily, they changed the controls in order to suit better for this type of game, you can move the camera around freely, the ridiculous meelee attacks are back, and you can even walk while aiming or firing, all of which changes the dynamic of the game itself. BUT, they locked on the camera while running, which is annoying and plain idiotic for all the quicktime events going on. Did I mention those? Yes, this game has so many quicktime events that it should be renamed "RE Interactive Movie" and by god I hate any kind of game interrupting when I'm playing. But that's not all, not only the running sections are awful, but every interaction you have with the enviroment is designed to annoy you at best. Your character will trip by just walking over a corpse, hell, Leon will trip into an open grave in Chapter 3 (I think) if you do so much as to go near it. Every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemy launches at you and triggers some sort of stupid event that just plain interrupts your movement to punch some damn combination with the pad, even bullets will make you fall down on your back. Speaking of which, this is an action game, so you are bound to spend your time shooting but the game is really stingy with the ammo. For some reason, the developers though it was a good idea to keep the low ammunition mechanic from previous games, unfortunately, you need the damn thing to make your way in it, so I ended up most of the time running around boss fights non the less, leaving the AI alone to do the job while I might hit it with the knife once or twice for 30 f***** min. And I know this is probably for the co-op mechanic, but if I'm going solo, give me the damn bullets. Most of the time all your going to find in the crates are those stupid points for the stupid points system, don't even get me started on that. Did I said previously that the controls were ok? Well, I'm sorry to contradict myself but, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, some things make absolutely no sense. The developers decided unexplicably to have two different "action buttons" (perhaps to enhance the QTE), so now you have one to reload and pick items up, and one for running and every other interaction, and that's a problem: if you try to sprint and your character is close to anything that can be interacted with (stairs, crate, table, whatever) you're gonna have a seisure. 600 people participated in the development! How can you f*** something so simple as that so badly?! I have tons of other complaits like the terrible cover system, the changing HUDS, the melee attacks only working whenever they feel like, the items selection screen, the fact that there's NO WAY TO PAUSE THE GAME, not even in single player, the un-remapable controls or the fact that you have to scroll up and down for your weapons inventory, which gets really impossible when you are in a tight situation. F*** I even experienced times when an unconveniently placed cutscene left me completely exposed to enemies attacks and died; I could go on and on but this will never finish. On to the story:

LEON: Ok this episode literally starts with a bang and never stops from there, both characters survive such a ridiculous array of things (bus crashing, helicopter crashing, freaking PLANE CRASH LANDING IN CHINA) that you are gonna be asking to yourself "who wrote this?" more times than necessary. It's RE: Left For Dead because that's exactly how it feels. Leon is as dumb as he'll ever be, constantly approaching danger as if he was a complete rookie, we also take control of Helena or whoever she is, I don't care, she's just a dumb mix of Hollywood clichés. The story is filled with lame one liners and the zombies just lounge at you like kamikazes, which of course, triggers an automatic QTE. If you are quick enough you can dodge them, but other wise it takes like a full damn clip of your gun to stop them. The final boss comes back 5 times, I'm not even kidding, you are gonna be begging to please stop for all the wrong reasons.

CHRIS: Or Call of Duty: Resident Evil, because if Activision was taking a part in the whole zombie deal why not do it opposite also right? This one gotta be the worst in gameplay terms. Chris is now a terribly cliched alcoholic who comes back to his military job for one last mission, after which, of course, we get our obligatory flashback in Estonia or some made up Eastern Europe country (cause the Middle East was unavailable I guess) with full on bio-terrorism plotline ala RE 5. He's teamed up with generic McGuffin' who only seems to talk in full military man macho hollywood lines, although pretty much every male characters seems to be doing some sort of wang measuring when they talk to each other, that's the quality of the dialogue here. I definitively did  not enjoy this. Specially the end with that camera switching running sequence, did I mention the camera locks when you sprint? Well, imagine trying to control that while the angle keeps changing while trying to run away from a gigantic beast (which like many enemies in the game, don't feel like they belong).

JAKE: I admit I did enjoy this one a little better, but it might as well been because I already was tired (the game is overstuffed to the max). This time we take control of Wesker's Son and the girl from RE 2, who now grew to become an obnoxiuos Wolverine like superhero (really). She is a crybaby and he is the typical sarcastic unimaginative antihero, both victims of poor writing, but I did like the chemistry between them if it's worth anything. They are hounded by this absurd "Wrong Turn" like beast who never dies no matter what you do. The final confrontation takes place in a lava filled facility, which only confirms the fact that even at that time, Capcom still had no idea how lava works. He falls into it, yet manages to come back, W-T-F?!?!?!? Even worse, Jake takes him on barehanded... Yeah people, the boulder punching was only the beginning (Chris even stops a full steel door with his arms at one point...)

ADA: Or RE: Arkham Asylum. And you can already see the problem here. THIS IS NOT A STEALTH GAME. So yeah, I got so fed up with this one after being cornered by a bunch of armored zombies with nothing but a damn crossbow, that I just decided to call it quits. This is as far as I go. I am simply not enjoying it.

So yeah, it does has some decent gameplay in between, specially if you play it co-op, but RE 6 is a crummy overbloated badly designed game, not just for the franchise but as a standalone product as well. If it's worth anything, the game does have it's moments of joy, but they are scarce as you are going to be constantly cussing, cursing and screaming to the wind when you get interrupted by its terrible mechanics. All I can say after venting this out is: THANK GOD CAPCOM WENT BACK TO ITS ROOTS AFTER THIS, AND THAT THIS GENERATION OF GAMING IS FINALLY OVER.

...I'd read the reviews. I knew RE6 hadn't been warmly received by its fanbase. There was a sale, and I'd enjoyed RE4 and... Kind of enjoyed RE5.

It is really amazing how many bad decisions went into this game. A game that refuses to actually pause for things like graphics and keymapping, even when you're playing offline in single-player. A horrifically awkward inventory system. Sequences that are happy to repeatedly kill you (often with drawn-out animations) with zero feedback as to how you might avoid death your next run. Timed chase sequences that throw awkward camera angles and change the direction of control, apparently just for cinematic effect. Basic gunplay that's subject to randomization and hampered by a skills system. Sequences that you WILL not pass without sufficient ammunition, combined with sometimes must-be-cleared enemies who soak up ammunition like a sponge, combined with very little apparent sense on the part of the game as to how much ammunition the player has left.

And just... Zero sense of restraint. I mean, yes, RE has always been over the top. But around the point an enemy has been run over by a train and dropped off of a building into a fire and STILL comes back for another encore, the idea that you're affecting the tide by peppering the thing with 9mm ammunition becomes completely farcical. The feeling is that the game will move on when IT'S good and ready, and the player's input is almost disdained in the process- damn it, you want to be mashing buttons?! I have CUT-SCENES to show you!

MANY, MANY CUTSCENES! Some of which will play out MULTIPLE TIMES as you are forced to replay!

I will say, for the money, that there's an awful LOT of game to this game, and the production values are nice even if the story is B-movie at best. But having now completed two of the four sequences, I think the game has eaten enough of my patience. It's tedious and frustrating, but not fun and not scary. No wonder they had to go back to the drawing board for RE7.

I completed every campaign on co-op with a friend. If I was playing alone I would have probably uninstalled this game a few hours in. It is not a good game. We played in order of the campaigns on the list so that meant we played Leon's first which was by far the best campaign, however that is not a high bar.

Combat is OK, there is a nice range of guns and the ammo is just sparse enough that you are encouraged to mix up your style by swapping between weapons, using melee attacks. You also find yourself changing tactics with the different enemy types. One exception is the wasp/fly enemy which is just completely ridiculous which does far too much damage with no obvious counter play. Boss combat is a different matter entirely as there is almost no feedback on whether or not you're making progress and  it just feels like you're waiting an arbitrary time until the next cutscene happens.

The level design is atrocious. The camera angle can swap mid-way through combat and running which also changes your character's direction. There are poorly executed 'variety' stages in each campaign which include; chase sequences, swimming, car driving, helicopter driving, invulnerable boss stages (despite having killed an enemy of the same type just seconds before), stealth, mazes etc... Almost all of these have an artificial level of difficulty where your deaths don't feel fair. This game wasn't particularly scary but the most horrifying part was knowing you'd be seeing these stages again because of the intertwined campaigns which felt like a form of PTSD.

The story was mediocre and playing through it once would have been OK. Playing through it four times with some chapters being basically a cut and paste from a different campaign was boring and felt cheap. However there were chapters which gave you a completely different perspective on a previous stage which was interesting.

This game was full of technical difficulties including random crashes which would cause my co-op session to end and my partner not being able to rejoin mid session resulting in a large loss of progress.

With the re-release of RE2 and 3, I figured I'd go through the series again. It could have been a really good game but Capcom dropped the ball on this one. Feel free to read it, I'm not putting any spoilers for the game (even if it's pretty old now). I'll try to resume the things I liked and hate about this game. It's subjective to my own tastes, so take it with a grain of salt.

Here's the pros:
- Graphics still stands to this day, it's not jaw dropping but it still looks decent.
- Several campaigns with a pair of Characters that include old and new  characters and inter twining stories.
- Replayability value if you really want to unlock all the skills or want to go through the extra content.
- Campaign Matchmaking allows you to chose what kind of game you want to focus on (have fun, story, gather collectables). I, however, haven't meet any other players during my playthrough.
- Improved AI partner, the partner no longer requires you to give away your precious ammo in order to be "useful"
- Chinese market levels look pretty good, a lot of confined claustrophobic environment.

I was thinking of putting it in the cons but some people may actually enjoy it.
- I found the story to be cheesed to a sad point. The RE series were always like that but this one was almost cringy at some points. The motivations of the main villain were disappointing to avoid any spoilers.

Cons:
- Despite the improvements, the AI partners are still dumb as bricks. I often found myself having to either backtrack or try to push them out of door frames.
- Enemy AI can still take you down during an in game cinematic. Which leaves you either waiting to be revived or killed in instants after regaining control.
- Quick Time Events are for EVERYTHING! They took everything from 4 and 5 but cranked it to 11. Fighting off an enemy, during cutscenes, opening doors, boss fights, you name it. Some of you may be okay with it, I found it to be a major irritant.
- Keyboard and Mouse controls, this was clearly a console game that was ported to PC. I feel a lot of the controls feel extremely clunky (especially the rotating QTE) in some levels with vehicle chases. I often had to move back and forth in some directions to orient the character in a specific direction, to interact with something.
- Enemies often reloaded in checkpoints despite the room being empty. Often lost some health before I could realise what happened. 


Overall Capcom seems to have listen to some of the complaints from the older games but failed in many other aspects. The QTE and controls were what broke the deal for me. These two broke the immersion for me. Based on my own tastes, I wouldn't recommend it. But if you feel like you can still deal with the cons, by all means, get the game when it's on sale. At least just for the story and the overall RE Universe timeline.

Resident Evil 6 is a game I've never got to play until now, though I've always been hearing bad opinions about it. 

I remember having some mixed feelings watching some gameplay videos years ago, but in the end, it was surprisingly good. As someone who really enjoyed Resident Evil 5, Resident Evil 6 is a worthy continuation to the series.

The gameplay felt very innovative, unique in its genre. I really liked the "freedom of movement" in this title, whereas in RE4 and RE5 movement felt slower but also unique in their genre and more likely to fit in a horror game. RE5 doesn't have an "horror" campaign for me, but the Lost In Nightmare DLC make it up, the combination with its gameplay was great. You can then tell that Resident Evil 6 is more action-oriented than the previous titles, if not the most. It was honestly hard for me to get into those new remakes (RE2R, RE3R), without all that action, and by that I mean the "Finishers moves" that I like a lot. You get me, combat feels very satisfying once you get used to it, I think Capcom made it right and I insist on "unique". For example, the "Counters", the "Finishers", sliding... All those little things RE6 came with made the game very enjoyable. 

The only thing I didn't like, and that RE5 made better, is the HUD. It was very difficult for me to get used to it, combine herbs, get rid of items, the inventory getting full fast without any idea on how much space you have left. The HUD-Phone was a really good concept though, I liked that you could get a new "HUD"/"Phone" for each campaign.
 
Another thing that I missed and that was in the two previous titles was the "merchant"/"store", the ability to buy/sell guns, upgrade them. In RE6, each character begins with a unique set of guns, you find the rest in the campaign. The positive aspect I see to this feature is the replayability. 

RE6 is also a very fun game to play co-op. We had a lot of fun trying to "sabotage" each other, make the other one being killed to see the "death scenes". About "death scenes", there are lot of them, which are very humilating, but funny and gruesome at the same time. I still remember my poor Helena getting squeezed into a mixer by a creature ! That QTE was hard. Good job Capcom.

Storywise, everything made sense to me (except the absence of Jill which is left unexplained, no references to Sheva). Time goes on, the virus gets better, so are the infected. It's all I can say, without debating on what Capcom should or shouldn't have done with the "zombies". There are 4 campaigns, and it took me over 30 hours to complete them on professional. It's almost thrice the time I spent on the RE5 campaign ! Another thing, I did notice the "texture" downgrade compared to RE5, but it is excusable due to the huge content the game has to offer. I really liked Chris and Piers campaign, it really did add more depth to Chris' character which lacked in the previous titles. Another campaign I enjoyed was Jake and Sherry, their campaign felt refreshing and connected well with the universe. However, I felt like Leon & Helena, and Ada's campaign didn't add much to the story, though it was okay to play. I'm not sure what to think about Leon's character development, but he seemed very bland in RE6, whereas in RE4 he had a more funny and distinct personnality. Other than that, the many small references to the previous titles that only the hardcore fans can recognize were very well put. 

To conclude, I really enjoyed Resident Evil 6. It is very unique compared to the two previous titles. However, I am afraid we won't see another action-oriented Resident Evil game like this for a while now.

The gunplay itself doesn't buck this trend, moving from absolutely horrific, to the best the over the shoulder shooter genre has ever got. I'm here to defend this game. At least a part of it, because it does have problems, but I still ended up enjoying it. First of all, the game looks nice and works well, I had no problems. It's not really survival or even horror, it's not scary at all, it's mostly action, but I think it is enjoyable if you accept that. Basically, what I mean by that, it's not ok as a Resi game, but it's ok as a game. Sometimes the action gets a bit too much, though, like there is a ridiculous amount of QTEs in some scenes. There are also scenes like car chasing and such. The controls are ok, the characters are mostly likeable. 
Now, the plot... The game has 4 different campaigns with different storylines that cross each other sometimes and end up being one big plot if you play them all, because they explain each other. I finished all of them and I think the story is actually pretty good... But not all campaigns are good. I played them in order and I really liked when the characters met each other and had to do things together. The game can be played in co-op, but I played it solo and I can confirm that the partner AI works well. I never had any problems with them.
First campaign, Leon & Helena: I played as Leon. Helena is ok, but she's nothing special, her personal backstory didn't interest me that much. I'm not going to lie: I'm pretty sure everyone started this campaign first and ended up hating the game because of it without actually finishing it. The first half of this campaign was so bad that I was laughing at it so much and I thought I was going to have to give it a negative review. The enemy AI is terrible. The true horror was that I could stand right next to a zombie and it didn't notice me. This was where the way too many QTEs are, Leon forgot what zombies are, the locations are horrible cliches (graveyard because fighting zombies in the city isn't exciting anymore), the puzzles are too easy. There was a cabin fight with random companions where I was literally standing in the corner wondering if I should actually do something or am I just in the way, because they were doing perfectly well without Leon's fabulous hairstyle. But I have the patience of a saint, so I continued and the second half of the campaign was pretty good and I liked it much more. It became exciting, fun and it even surprised me around the end. I kind of had enough of the main boss, though, because one thing this game does bad in each campaign is that they all have their 1 big boss, and it makes you fight that same boss like 8 times.
Second campaign, Chris & Piers. I played as Chris, but Piers ended up being likeable, too. This one has zero puzzles, it's not survival, it's not horror, it's just pure action. I was used to it at this point. It was alright, the characters are fine, the plotline is ok and it really adds more to the first one. I hated the last boss fight, though.
Third campaign, Jake & Sherry: I played as Jake, because I don't care about Sherry and I have to say, this is the worst plotline. There is a horribly done romance for whatever reason, the story is awful, Jake as a character is fine, but the plot armor is strong with him. This campaign's also mostly action, but barely has anything to offer and the connection between this and the others is paper thin. Leon's and Ada's not yet existing love child has a bigger role in this game than these two characters. I seriously wouldn't have missed anything if this campaign didn't exist. It was simply boring and awful. 
Fourth campaign, Ada & Her Iron Will That Stops Her From Finally Kissing Leon: The only one where there is no partner AI that you can kick in the face. I liked this one, too, it also has a few puzzles, an interesting plot and cool moments. At least it doesn't make you fight 1 boss a hundred times. This one wants to introduce stealth, but since I could stand next to zombies without them noticing me, I didn't really think the game understood stealth. 
All in all, the game is not pure perfection, but I think it's far from being horrible. I think the story is pretty good and the gameplay was mostly enjoyable, even if there were stupid moments. If you have the mindset to accept that this is not a survival horror game (yes, I know it should be), but an action game, then you might enjoy it. If you want the older RE style, you probably won't like it and it's better to just avoid it.

Not a bad RE game and an improvement over RE5, but it's still a game that shows that Capcom made the right move with RE7 and the RE2 and RE3 remakes, as the action-oriented formula for RE6 was definitely not working for the series.

You have four campaigns to play - Leon/Helena, Chris/Piers, Jake/Sherry and Ada. The story is actually pretty interesting and each campaign fits into the other campaigns, so events from other campaigns are explained. Jake's introduction is very poorly done, with some of the other characters recognizing him but never explaining why, but Jake as a character turns out to be actually believable and interesting to a certain degree.

It also helps that the dialogue and voice acting in the game is decently well made, with no "jill sandwich" or "master of lockpicking" moments in the dialogue. There are, however, still some silly moments in the game, like two characters talking to each other when they're trying to hide from a monster.

Gameplay-wise, it's similar to previous games but with a few differences, one being that the character can dodge and shoot from the ground and the other being that weapons are no longer modified, but instead you acquire skill points by defeating enemies and picking up treasures, which you can then use to buy and upgrade certain skills to improve gun damage, melee damage, defense, proficiency with a specific weapon, damage against a specific type of enemy, among plenty of other things.

So far it all sounds like it's a great game, but that's where the drawbacks start to show up. Inventory system is, somehow, even worse than it was in RE5, with an inventory that can barely hold anything at all - between ammo for all the different weapons, grenades and consumables, the inventory is constantly full. Even using healing items was somehow messed up in the game: aid sprays can be used as normal consumables, but herbs have to be first added to the character's herb count then used individually, with each of them healing 1 of the 6 health bars the character has. Mixing herbs together increases the count that is added to the character, but it's still a needlessly complicated system involving an inventory that already barely holds anything.

The controls are not good - they work for the most part, but some things are just incredibly counterintuitive and confusing.

Enemies are a problem - until you have purchased certain skills to make the character stronger, most enemies just feel like bullet sponges. Playing Leon's campaign for the first time with no skills equipped often means never having enough ammo for anything. Even aiming for the head, enemies can take countless shots before dying. Melee can be used to some extent to save on ammo, but it can only be used for as long as the character has combat meter bars to use.

The game has some great moments, but it also has some highly frustrating and badly designed ones. Right on Leon's campaign, there is a moment where you have to fight waves of enemies alongside Helena and other NPCs, all inside of a small store, moving from room to room while countless zombies are coming inside. It even gets to the point where the game makes you fight a fat zombie inside of a tiny room where there's barely any space to maneuver. And that's not to mention certain parts of the game that require you to perform certain actions but barely give you any time to do so. By the time you realize what you need to do, you're already looking at a death animation.

While the skills are interesting, the game only allows 3 to be equipped on the main campaign. It's understandable that they didn't want to make characters too overpowered, but being able to only equip 3 skills is WAY too limited.

The game has some stealth sections, but they're one of the worst parts of the game - not because they're stealth sections, but because they're very poorly done. Enemies are seemingly deaf and unable to hear loud footsteps two feet away from them, but if they spot you for even half a second, you'll be swarmed with countless enemies. There isn't even any way to run, hide and wait until they stop looking for you - the only options are either reset from last checkpoint or fight until the enemies stop coming. One stealth section even has instant death fail states if you don't hide in time. Stealth has no room in this game and should have been only implemented as an alternative to combat, not as entire sections.

Even leaving the issues aside, the game is way too action-oriented for a horror game. It just doesn't feel tense or scary like a horror game should feel like.

If they took the RE name out of the game and improved some of these issues, this could have been a really good game. But as a RE game and with these issues, it's just what it is - good, but not great. The story and the characters are what keep the game from going down to a 6/10.

Recommended during a sale or if you're a huge fan of RE games. And even then, I'd still suggest waiting for a sale.

[b] GAMEPLAY [/b]

Gameplaywise, the game has the best combat in the series by far, and that's a huge positive, since the game is heavily focused on action sections and they become way more enjoyable when the game has proper mechanics to support those sections, the best way to play this is definitely with a friend, since the AI is not too good, but it is still playable by yourself.

[b]The story is an intended mess.[/b]
The campaigns are needlessly intertwined, to give the impression of a multifaceted story.
Many details from the three main campaigns are left unexplained on purpose. Only for them to be tidied up neatly (at least in theory) in the secret fourth campaign. Which fails almost completely, because that last campaign raises more questionable plot points. The worst offender, when it comes to story, is that big plot revelations are spoiled across campaigns, due to shared cutscenes.

[b]The presentation is a cinematic mess.[/b]
The control over the characters is almost constantly being taken away, for the purpose of forcing set pieces and already obvious ways of progression into the player's view.
Which at best simply annoys you by changing the angle of the third person camera while you are still in control over your character.
But at worst demands you to suddenly look through a completely different camera, only to show your character standing in front of an opening door, which has an active enemy behind it, that then attacks you while you are unable to move.

[b]The gameplay is a satisfying mess.[/b]
After too many hours of playing, the combination of running, dodging, doing melee combos and finisher moves on enemies, feels good.
The weapons, gunplay and enemy feedback is serviceable.
What mostly ruins the gameplay, is the lack of control (as described above) and the lack of ammunition. "[i]But it's a survival horror game and therefore you are not supposed to have much ammo![/i]"

[b]Everything described below, also proves that Resident Evil 6 is not a survival horror game:[/b]

This game has an overabundance of "skill point" drops, which replaces possible ammo and health drops. These skill points are used, outside of the campaign, to buy and equip up to three skills per set, which can also be upgraded with ridiculously high prices. That seems to be a very deliberate choice, to encourage the grinding of skill points in modes that are completely separate from the campaigns. Modes which are paid DLCs. 

[b]The online components are just a mess.[/b]
Online coop works mostly as it should, unless the game makes you and your friend wait for 60 seconds between loading areas for no discernible reason.
The ability to skip cutscenes, if both parties agree to it, is appreciated.
The later inclusion of a second playable character in the fourth (previously singleplayer-only) campaign is also appreciated, but it was implemented in a way that is reminiscent of a fan-made mod.

This game features a Dark Souls-esque invasion mechanic, which can be disabled and should be ignored.
If a player joins your campaign as an enemy, they will randomly spawn as a standard or special enemy, most of which are  terrible to play as. Invaders with infinite health, due to hacking, are not a rarity.

Probably the most hated RE in history and the most misunderstood. The first time I played this I thought it was the clunkiest RE to date, but after watching some videos on YouTube about combat mechanics it became a whole another world. If only Capcom had taken a moment to make a tutorial for all these mechanics, I'm sure RE6 would be regarded as the most polished action experience in the whole franchise, because it is. Just look it up and see for yourself how fun this game can be. Mercenaries mode is amazing.

Some of the criticism is well deserved of course, the camera gets hijacked many times and you really really want to make sure you max your FOV in your options if you don't want headaches. Level design is more detailed than in earlier entries but also dumbed down. Coop could be better.

Now, there's also many people that like to ♥♥♥♥ on this game parroting the same hypocritical points over and over, pointing out stuff that has been present in the franchise for a long time, making RE6 look like the only ever offender. Without looking too far, somebody else right here is defending QTEs in RE4 and condemning them in RE6... Seriously.

Bad story? Yes, but that wasn't RE's forte ever. If anything, it still has that B movie feeling that has always been a constant in RE. No musical variety? Just try to remember a track from any game that isn't from the original trilogy and its not from a saveroom. Too much of a departure of survival horror? Completely true, but we already said goodbye to horror with RE4, if you consider drunk spaniards and crackhead midgets scary... well... you might as well consider Luigi's Mansion a horror title :^)

All in all, this is a great game; and no, it's not a "good game but a bad Resident Evil", it's just different. If you like action and love the characters of RE, give it a chance, it might surprise you.

Capcom, in an interview before RE6's release, said that they wanted to create a more action-oriented RE title because action games like Call of Duty at that time (the early 2010s) were popular. What we got is an "action" title that defies every genre convention in the worst ways possible. It's like Capcom's game designers have never ever played an action game in their lives.

The biggest problem with this game is its horrendous camera. It will legitimately give you a massive headache. Unlike other third-person action games like say, Uncharted (which came out years before RE6), the camera's trajectory and distance behind your character is wildly inconsistent. Sometimes the camera's FOV will zoom in excessively as you are performing a dash, which messes with your spatial awareness and orientation when you are trying to run past some zombies or dash down a narrow corridor. Other times, like in Chris's boss battle against the final boss, the camera will suddenly switch to a different perspective altogether, forcing you to play with classic-RE-series tank controls. This is done with zero warning and at a critical moment of the game where one wrong turn will lead to your death.

RE6 is also incredibly obsessed with quick-time events. In RE4, the QTEs were used sparingly and only during important set-piece moments, which created some positive tension — the QTEs felt fair and there was always an anticipated build-up to them. In RE6, they are freaking everywhere. During one absolute joke of a boss fight, 95% of the fight is about mashing QTEs. It's pointless and contrary to what an "action" game should be. QTEs should complement the action, not take over everything.

This might not be the best RE game, heck it's far from being good in "most RE fans' eyes". However, it is no doubt one of the most entertaining RE games to play casually.

- The combat is upgraded from 4&5 and it's definitely the strong point of this game. You can slide, roll, counter, lie down while fighting at the same time, do 180 spin after rolling or sliding forward. Reload/shoot while walking! 

This game gives you maybe the most options and freedom in term of character control, not just in RE but in any 3rd person style game at all. Not to mention you can actually kick your friend around with "Attack Reaction" on. Bonus point.

Boss fight in this game is pretty good. Most RE games' boss fight consist of you just walking back, aiming guns at the boss and hold/tab shoot button until it ends. It's not as simple in this game which I like.

- Plot-wise, I see people claim this game has bad story or the worst story in RE, but is that true?
RE series as a whole has amazing plot sure, but as a separate title? It's not that complicated, judging RE6 to have worst story is really unfair since other games have straight forward story as well (take RE4 for example).

I see people hating this game for not being so much horror. But considering the plot in the franchise, at this point the casts are fighting against terrorism and not helpless survival from monsters anymore. So I think it's fair that the game becomes more action-based at this point.

Some people also said this game has a lot of cheesy dialogue and what not, but that has always been the trait of the series tho. If you don't get what I mean, how about play the original RE1 to begin with.

- This game also has tons of content for nowadays standard. You get 4 campaign which easily is longer than 5-6 hours each plus Mercenaries mode which is the BEST thing about this game imo. Fun music with fun gameplay, especially when playing with friends.

Extra DLC modes is not worth it at all, so don't bother if you ask me.

- Now, the game does feel sloppy in many parts yes. F.E. Leon's story does have cut-scene that interrupt your gameplay quite a bit during the first few chapter. Plus on harder difficulty that could end up killing you outright, I'm not gonna protect that. 
Some parts might look buggy.
Some terrain and details not looking as good compared to RE5 and other games around that time.

- Oh yeah, and did I mention QTE? This game has a lot of QTE and they are not much different from RE4 and 5. Some are easy and some are really quite BS. Good thing they added the option to let the game perform QTE for you, so there's that.

This is one of, if not my top favorite, game of all time. The depth of the story and characters is beyond any other RE game out there, and tells a tale of how friendship and love can save the entire world, with the assistance of guns, explosions, and badass zombie and BOW demolishing of course.

Each route is unique and offers a different experience for every kind of resident evil fan. 
-Leon's Route is a homage to the original games, with puzzles, zombies, horror, family, and political drama. Also plenty of that Leon/Ada tension.
-Chris' route offers a fast past run and gun scenario with military drama and a deep bond between broken men fighting to keep each other alive. In tune with RE 5 in terms of action and explosions.
-Jake's route is a perfect marriage of the two previous routes, featuring new characters and those returning from childhood, now all grown up. In constant pursuit by a "Mr. X" type villain, Jake finds his way through horror and action scenarios, all while dealing with uncovering his shrouded family past, and learning to become his own person with the help of friendship, and possibly even blossoming romance?
-Ada's route is an unlockable fourth route once finished with the main three campaigns, and can still be played with a friend, or alone. Ada's route offers the behind the scenes eye that a secret agent would have, and reveals the last of the secrets about the overarching story.

I could not recommend this game /harder/. I hope those of you reading this take a chance on this game that was once poorly received, and find the depth and beauty in it that I do.

Not Recommended — Resident Evil 6

I played Resident Evil 5 before this, and right after finishing it, we jumped into RE6 purely for the coop aspect. I remember enjoying this game on console years ago because the coop system felt revolutionary at the time — and honestly, that is (and always was) the only positive aspect of this game.

Graphics & Camera:
The graphics look shockingly bad — even worse than Resident Evil 5 — which I didn’t think was possible. The camera angles are terrible, constantly getting in the way and making movement awkward.

Performance vs. Gameplay:
Even with a rock-solid 120 FPS on PC, the gameplay feels weirdly sluggish and unresponsive. Everything from movement to aiming feels heavy, almost like the game is fighting against you. The level designs feel sluggish and rushed, not creative at all - unlike its predecessors.

Story:
The story feels forced, messy, and thrown together without care. Instead of a coherent narrative, it feels like a bunch of disconnected ideas rushed into one game.

In short: aside from the coop system (which was great back in the day), everything else is painfully weak. If you’re coming from RE5, especially for coop, don’t expect an improvement — this is a major step backward.

Resident Evil Six has been sitting on my game's list ever since I played it for two hours and stopped, so I decided to go through each of the four campaign each way you could play the game as a sort of challenge before REmake 3 came out.  The following played in order with all on Normal, Leon (Leon Single Player Only), Chris (Chris Co-Op only), Jake (Sherry, Local Co-Op), and Ada (All intersections done in full Co-Op).

Leon:  It's not Survival Horror that's for sure, this campaign attempts to emulate RE4 but falls quite flat, from the Prelude that starts out with a first person dragging section that actually is not faithful to what you do in the campaign when you return to that section, to a hold out inside of a store in the first chapter.  Technically the slowest paced campaign of the lot, by the end you will be as powerful as Chris 'boulder punching' Redfield, so any attempt of suspense ends up lost inbetween the plane crash, the bus crash, the helicopter crash... how is Leon still alive?

         The Single Player AI is fine, it dose what it needs to do and can be buffed with two Skills that can help it in rezing you or increase their firepower slightly, but you should forgo those and get Firepower and increased item pickup instead, because the game loves to starve you for items if you don't.  If you want to put it in your third skill slot you could, but I personally preferred the skill that made my cursor actually accurate instead of being a suggestion due to that wild green dot that aims instead of the actual cursor..

Chris:  This Campaign is bang bang shoot shooty soldier man, not much else to say, this is the CoD section of this game where you fight against enemies with guns.  The enemies sometimes grow separate parts depending on where you shoot them, or maybe it's programmed to pop the same and there were so many enemies I couldn't tell.  You can take cover, but it is so awkward to do so I just skipped it and stood out in the open shooting at anything in my sight.

          The Online Co-Op is good, and even this late in the cycle there is always someone willing to jump in and play a round or two even if it might take a little bit of a wait if you play during non prime time hours.  You don't share drops with your online partner, so you usually have enough to get by, and besides them not being invincible like the AI you end up feeling a sense of togetherness when you pull each other out of a hard spot and feed them a healing tic-tac.  I'm tempted to play the other half of all the campaigns in online co-op in fact because it was such an enjoyable experience playing with randos.

Jake: So me and my brother played through Jake's campaign, and it was the worst of two experiences and not because of any ineptitude on my brother's part.  Jake's campaign is nothing but boss fights, hold out sequences, Stealth areas that do not have a tutorial for them, and chase sequences.  Respawning enemies litter this campaign and after playing all the chapters in my personal opinion this is the worst.  Besides the fact that Jake and Sherry are traveling together because Jake has speshul bluud they still feel like second bananas to every other campaign with their more unique bosses and better game play sections.

          Local Co-Op is garbage, the weird split screen I would be able to handle if the entire game wasn't darker than the Abyss, but in addition to that you and your co-op partner must share the sparse Ammo and healing items that the game drops by default, and due to the awful inventory one person gets regulated to having one big block of ammo while the other gets none.  I need to apologize to my sibling and play RE5 with them instead to make up for what I put his through

Ada:  Bescides the first chapter and the awful boat boss that somehow tanked the FPS of my brand new gaming laptop during it's chase section, this campaign actually felt nice.  There is no AI partner if you don't match make making me feel like I was playing a real RE game, and during Intersections I felt like a bad ass swooping into someone else campaign to lend a helping hand in defeating their enemies.  Ada's section makes me feel like a super spy, and her unique weapon, the crossbow, was powerful with Firearms 2 and eventually even more so with 3.

          Intersections are the best and worst part of this game.  Seriously if there is any other game where you can invade other people's completely separate campaigns and help them out for a while let me know in the comments, because this is a feature I absolutely adore, and find it the best part of the game.  On the other hand whoever decided to include a one minute timer for someone who is meaningfully trying to do these intersections is now my mortal enemy.  If you are online and set your join settings to don't allow you still have the timer as if you were playing online Co-Op, and the timer doesn't start again if you restart from checkpoint.  To get the timer to come back you have to quit out and hammer A until you start another session, and that wouldn't be so bad if the community wasn't slow.  I had to watch this one minute timer so many times, skip a cutscene, sometimes wait through an unskippable cutscene, and mash A so many times that it probrobly took up about five hours of my play time just mashing A and skipping cutscenes.  This is all because someone didn't think ahead to allow someone to wait for the next available intersection without a timer

I also played Agent Hunt, it's stupid, dumb fun that unlocks when you beat a campaign.  You become an enemy and try and kill the player, probably die, and come back to try it again.  You also drop a health spray on occasion so know that.  Also never, EVER allow infinite ammo in your settings, the Magnum Spam is real.

In finishing this review what can I say about the game?  Besides how dark it is even on full brightness, the one hit Kos that several enemies have, all the instant fail QTEs that plague the game, the fact none of it feels like a Resident Evil Game should?  Seriously the amount of times something fell on me from out of my view and instant murdered me was five times too many.  I would recommend the Intersections if it wasn't hell to attempt to get working now that it isn't launch day.
