Things I like about this game:

[list]
[*]Faster pace of gameplay. From the faster run speed to the on-command combat rolls to the weapons, everything requires you to be at the top of your game and right on the money with every keystroke and click. I especially enjoy the one-click-one-shot behavior of pistols where the only limit to your rate of fire is how accurate you want to be.

[*]The multi-perspective story. It's something we rarely see in a Resident Evil, and certainly not to this level. Playing each campaign has its own challenges, weapons, and perspectives on events witnessed by different characters. Getting through all of them rewards the players by revealing secrets and plot points that didn't make sense in a different campaign. There are some real head-scratchers, and only by finishing every playthrough--including the solo bonus campaign--does it all come together. As a storyteller myself, I appreciate the depth and interconnectedness of it all.
[/list]

Things I hate about this game:

[list]
[*]The dubious reliability of the movement system. There is little more annoying when you're trying to run away from a mob/boss with a ton of cover around and you keep vaulting over the same piece every half second because you're panicking and spamming the sprint key.

[*] Lack of customization. RE5 was the first entry in the series I ever played, and that introduced me to the gloriousness that was the merchant system of RE4/5. This system allowed you to customize your loadout to fit just about anything, whether that was a close-quarters focus, means of keeping enemies as far as possible, or a jack-of-all-trades. This game has...some of that, with each campaign giving you a bevy of weapon types to choose from, including each character's unique weapon and animations (every one of them is worth mastering, by the way, except maybe Chris; not really sure what his unique weapon is except the cannons he calls biceps). However, the difference between the weapons in each class is apparent from one campaign to the next, whether that's Chris' SpecOps rifle vs Jake's Bear Commander or the more powerful AK-type in Leon's campaign.

The fact that you're limited to just one model dependent on the campaign is a letdown for me, and the fact that you can't upgrade them is disappointing. Instead, you get a skill point system that takes endless hours of grinding to level up and is infinitely more useful with mouse and keyboard than controller, since the F1-8 keys allow you to switch between skill loadouts on the fly instead of having to go into the esc. menu (which doesn't pause the game because co-op--which I hate; they did it better in RE5 for sure). Also, no alternate costumes outside the extra modes?

[b] UnPlAyAbLe [/b]

[*]The inventory system. It's functional and simplified like RE5's was, and I think that's my biggest issue with it. The devs tried too hard to cater to co-op and sacrificed functionality for speed, which is something that annoyed me about RE5 and annoys me here. Yes, you spend a little more time than I'd like managing inventory in RE4, so maybe not that deep, but the smoother sailing of the RE engine make this game's inventory look like a plastic lunchbox with metal paint instead of a tin frame...this metaphor got away from me. Anyway, the inventory slots fit one item each, with each campaign having dedicated slots for their unique weapons. Everything else has to fit in the one-size-fits-all spaces, including auxiliary items like first aid spray, grenades, and remote bombs.

I don't think I'd have such a big problem with this if the AR ammo had bigger stacks. Like, seriously? 60 rounds per slot? You have any idea how fast I burn through that going full-auto? Besides which, once you find your AR of choice, ammo for it is pretty plentiful, so your inventory can fill up fast if you aren't careful, stopping you from picking up critical first aid or herbs when you need them. By comparison, the ammo for handguns/MPs goes in stacks of 150--seriously, 60 rounds for an AR vs a pistol that relies on headshots to kill reliably and I go through maybe a mag every three fights? Tsk tsk.
[/list]

Things I [b] LOVE [/b] about this game:

[list]
[*]Renewed focus on close-quarters combat. Whether it's using follow-ups to push back a crowd after you shoot a zombie in the head or using the environment to one-shot a stunned J'avo, the hand-to-hand system in this game is easily one of my favorites in a TPS. The counter system alone is a gold mine of mechanics, and not just with garden-variety zombies either. Even the tougher enemy types that are usually bullet sponges and do tons of damage can be dispatched fairly easily if you've mastered the counter system. Melee combat gives you more options and flexibility in how you want to handle each fight while doing a ton of damage and saving you ammo that's particularly precious in the early levels.

You are massively rewarded for mastering the CQC system. For perhaps the first time in the entire Resident Evil series, when you walk into a room, YOU are the boss. I know that might seem like a cheap gimmick and a massive departure for longtime fans of the series (and it is a departure, to be sure), but look at who the characters are: Leon S. "I can tank Tyrant punches to my forearms" Kennedy, Chris "I punched a boulder and it ran away" Redfield, and Sherry "G-Virus turned me into Wolverine" Birkin. Every one of them is a verified badass with years of experience and training under their belts, and this is a time period when the world has been dealing with the reality of superhuman monsters for well over a decade. Of [i] course [/i] most of the old garden-variety are going to be pushovers.

Not to say you can't die easily if you're reckless. You can. The health system is an...interesting innovation that I don't think works as well as it should. Certain attacks take one or two pips of health regardless of the endurance upgrades you get in the skill shop. There are some areas of the game that will make you want to rip your hair out, especially in Chris' campaign. The sheer amount of gunfire and RPGs that fly your way sometimes...it's a bit of a nightmare, which is one reason why I've never played his campaign on anything higher than normal.

[*]The boss fights. Some are much weaker than others, and I'm talking about the impact/drama, not the bosses themselves. Most are pretty tough the first time through unless you stockpile magnum ammo and spam weak points, and even then it usually takes some environmental wizardry to finish them off. But we see the return of the big, bad bullet sponges, as well as more subtle foes whose difficulty is based on quality of shots instead of quantity. A particular recurring boss in Jake and Sherry's campaign is my personal favorite for reasons. Basically, it's Nemesis from RE3, minus the slow movement and the incessant "STAAAARS" chanting. The final fight with him is, in my opinion, easily one of the most satisfying moments of the game, but only if you're playing as Jake. I'll leave you to find out why.

[*]How muthaflippin' ANIME this bish is. This is probably the main reason I love this game so much while a lot of hardcore RE fans hated it. It's big, it's loud, it's over-the-top. It takes the fantastical scale of moments from 4 and 5 and cranks the dial up to 11. Does that rob it of the majority of its horror? With the exception of some of Leon's campaign, absolutely. But like I said before, this is a time period in the RE-verse when the world has had it up to here with BOWs, and the professionals who have been honing their skills throughout the series finally have room to show their chops. It's not a good reflection of the franchise. It [i] is [/i] a good reflection of the world's evolution.
[/list]

1) Basic gameplay description
Resident Evil 6 is an arcade Third Person Shooter with minimal need for using covers. 
Instead you should focus on a dodge, counter attacks, melee combat and dashing (each does cost stamina).
Inventory management is a bit downgraded when comparing to Resident Evil 4 and 5 but at least you still have herb mixing, limited slots and item management.
There are small puzzles here and there, some fun, some boring. Nothing head breaking, mostly brain-dead.  
There is a lot of QTE's in Resident Evil 6 tho but I found them quite easy and fun to perform.

There are 4 story campaigns that intertwine each other and all of them can be played both solo (with AI partner) or with another player (you can play online or in splitscreen). 
You can play them in any order but for a story and gameplay reasons it's the best to play them in chronological order as they are in main menu:
Leon->Chris->Jake->Ada.



2) Skill system
During a campaign there is no weapon upgrading but you can buy (and some of them upgrade up to level 3) skills with collected points and you can select up to 3 skills.
Sadly, there are is total 43 skills and 39 of them are useless.
Here is why:

>8 "infinite ammo for X weapon" (those won't even work if game host disabled them in lobby settings so useless)

>9 "increase power of X weapon" (too weak when comparing to Firearm skill so useless)

>6 "more pick ups for X type of ammo" (do you like using the same gun over and over again? No? So it's useless)

>3 "only usable in single player mode" (so for coop only players like me - useless)

>2 "increases strength of attacks against X type of enemies" (Firearm skill have way better damage bonus so useless)

>"accuracy" and "recoil" (that are basically steadiness of your hand before and after shot - useless)

>"easier QTE's" (considering how already easy and fun those QTE's are to do - useless)

>"more damage but removes laser/crosshair" (interesting but not fun to use for anything other than shotgun so useless)

>"more stamina" (in a game where you already have ton of stamina? Useless)

>"melee damage" skill (melee damage is already high enough and the player should not focus on using it very often so useless)

>"faster recovery time when down" (useless considering that your partner should be next to you for the whole time)

>"extra sniper zoom" (useless considering how small the areas are)

>"piercing bullets" (when enemies are not group up together most of the time? Useless)

>"quick reload" (when reloading from any gun takes like a second? Useless)

>"last shot" (increase strength of your final bullet. At the end, Firearm skill is still way better so useless)



So we are down to 4 only good skills (Firearm, Defense, Item Drop Increase, Critical Hit) that a player should care about in this order:
1. Buy Item Drop Increase that increase by 40% chance for an item drop, including more points,
2. Buy Critical Hit which allow you to save time, health and bullets with instant killing headshots,
3. Buy Defense to loose as little health from range attacks as possible,
4. Upgrade both Critical Hit and Defense to level 3
5. Buy Firearm (because it's increase damage by a LOT and allows you to save ammo) and swap it with Item Drop Increase,
6. Upgrade Firearm to level 3,
Done! No need to change that unless you want to experiment.



3) Plot
All of your favourite heroes (and Ada) goes to solve another bioweapon issue (this time it's a Coronavirus outbreak in China) and then your typical Resident Evil shenanigans happen.
Basically this game is Super Smash Bros Ultimate but with Resident Evil characters.
It's the simplest plot out of all main Resident Evil games. 
The story has both serious and funny moments with a bit dose of cheesiness, corniness and action, just like every other Resident Evil game.
Is that makes it bad? No. 
Does it still feels like a Resident Evil plot? Yes. 
Did I like it? A lot.



4) Story campaigns
>Leon's campaign
This campaign is the most Resident Evil thing you will experience out of all of them.
Creepy atmosphere? Civilian casualties? Zombies? 
Animal type monsters? Good puzzles? Cheese one-liners?
Spooky locations? Action packed cutscenes? Entire classic weapon loadout? 
Laboratory section? Over the top amazing final boss fight? Finishing it off with Rocket Launcher? 
Check, check and check.
How was the final chapter? Simple amazing!
Leon gets an easy 5/5. 

>Chris's campaign
This one has definitely the most variety of different action sections including but not limiting to: 5 completely different areas (Edonia, Poisawan, Lanshiang, Carrier and Laboratory),
driving a car, piloting an aircraft, run away sections and fighting a lot of unique bosses.
What only grinds my gears only is that chapter 1 takes time in the present, chapter 2 is what happen 6 months ago and chapter 3-5 are what happen after chapter 1.
Why it's like that?  
Why not put everything from chapter 2 first in the story and then slap "6 months later" text at the beginning of what happen in chapter 1? 
Is it that hard those days to make a chronological order in story without relying on stupid flashbacks? 
What's up with Resident Evil games doing that crap?
How was the final chapter? Great!
Chris gets 4/5. 

>Jake's campaign
There was not as much variety as with Chris campaign but those few moments was really memorable such as driving a snowmobile during a cool sequence (pun intended),
a bit of stealth in pretty looking ice cave, driving a bike and exploring secret laboratories.
The main feature of this campaign is a nemesis type enemy - Ustanak.
How was the final chapter? Awesome with very satisfying ending.
Jake gets 4/5. 

>Ada's campaign
In short: a simple clusterf*ck. 
Awkward crossbow in use, tons of reused rooms and enemies, no interesting new encounters, way too many infuriating and cheap instant kills or failures, 
clunky stealth sections and hands down the worst in-game puzzles.
The entire point of this campaign is to give you that one answer about specific character at the end (a plot twist that you could see miles away in each other campaign if you knew who Ada Wong is from previous Resident Evil games) that is so underwhelming and stupidly nonsensical even for Resident Evil standards.
Overall this campaign is not only really bad but also really boring. 
Also it is horrible to play in coop because Agent cannot open boxes, doors, help with puzzles and teleports instantly when Ada uses hookshot. 
The only good thing about this campaign was that very short helicopter section.
How was the final chapter? Terrible dull with no proper final boss fight and unsatisfying ending.
Ada gets 1/5. 



5) Other free gamemodes
>Mercenary mode - horde mode (available with coop)
>Agent Hunt - invade a campaign of other people as a monster. Basically Dark Souls invasion.



6) Paid DLC gamemodes
>Survivors - 6 player deathmatch and killed human players will turn into monsters.
>Onslaught  - 2 player Mercenary mode but instead of coop its PVP. The better you play the worse it gets for enemy player.
>Predator - 5 players against a 6th player who is randomly chosen to be Ustanak. 
>Siege -  3 human players are defending VIP when 3 other are trying to kill him as monsters.

7) Summary
Resident Evil 6 does focus more on pure action than typical survival horror but to be honest - only a fool would complain about that.
Since Resident Evil 4 majority of both main and spin-off RE games does focus in majority on action and not only RE6 does that great but it also have a great designed coop mode. 

After playing a failure that was Operation Raccoon City, RE 6 is a warm breath of fresh air and proper game development.

One more thing: just as with RE5 - don't bother with RE6 if you are gonna play it solo. 
5 and 6 definitely are not fun games to play in solo due utter hot garbage AI partner.
The only way to play and enjoy those kind of games is doing it with a friend on Steam/Discord call.

The most polarizing game of all Resident Evils, well, outside of the REEEEEE'ing from RE5 when everyone took offense to the main characters shooting at colored people. Which was stupid, I mean the game takes place in Africa, you expecting a lot of white people there? The location is named Kijuju, an entirely fictional place btw. 

As for RE6, you either love this game, or hate it. No in between, it's that polarizing and for very odd reasons.

Anyways, this game had extremely mixed reviews when it first came out. The main point of everyone's argument was that it has too much action. Comparing this game to RE4 and RE5, they're not that different when it comes to that. Again, very confusing argument to say the least. This is probably the most hated RE game in the entire franchise and I cannot understand why. 

Another argument was bad level design and QTEs. I personally have never had a problem with QTEs. I agree with the level design flaws to an extent. There's a few instances where this is true. The chopper fight in Chris' campaign comes to mind (on harder difficulties) and the part when Chris and Piers are being chased by a helicopter at the docks. Some of the chases are pretty bad. Other than those few spots, I didn't think the level design is as bad as people make it out to be. There are no troubles to be had in the other 3 campaigns, smooth sailing.

This game made a ton of improvements from RE5.
Better AI partner (smarter, reacts faster, isn't constantly in trouble as they cannot be killed by enemies). If you fail a chase sequence/QTE, that's the only time you'll ever see them die. It's random, it essentially randomly chooses who to show die if you fail in certain scenarios.

Better mechanics (shooting and moving). Better sprint control, quick shots, the ability to shoot while laying down, can take cover on a ton of things, can slide, can side roll, the ability to shoot while sliding and jumping backward, alternate firing options for certain weapons, etc.

Better control (more options). There is a sticking problem with mantling but you get used to it once you figure out how touchy it is. The problem with mantling, climbing, and dropping down is that the range of activation is massive. You can be facing forward trying to run, and you'll turn around and sometimes mantle things or drop down. The only negative when it comes to control. This port handles much better in comparison to both RE4 and RE5 when it comes to camera movement and aiming.

Better combat (reversals, melees, sprinting attacks, finishing moves, environmental attacks etc) Tons of options here, play how you want to play. You're not stuck only shooting or only melee'ing. Groups of enemies can be handled how you want.

AI partner no longer hogs ammo and health, no need to keep them stocked up either

Less inventory restrictions compared to RE5. Go ahead you loot addicts, go crazy.

This game on a combat level, is imo the best in the series. Being able to dodge, counter enemies attacks, slide through enemies, jump kick, melee, pistol whip, insta kill finishers, etc. feels great and works well. 

The campaigns are great in that there are 4 unique campaigns, that are pretty lengthy, with returning flagship characters and a couple of new ones. Leon's is the best campaign to play imo. Not saying the others are bad, I just think his campaign is more interesting and the gritty environment hits home as a classic RE fan. Ada's is a bit of a bore, which is a shame, she also has a less than stellar weapon pool. I think her campaign is the easiest of the 4. Chris' campaign is "COD esque" but if you choose Piers, he has that beloved Anti Material Rifle, a .50 cal basically which wrecks shop. Sherry and Jake's campaign is ok. Jake has the best hand to hand combat, while Sherry has arguably the best starting pistol in the game. Their story is ok and the boss in that campaign is a bit like Nemesis.

Graphically, this game was made for the Xbox 360 and PS3 so they're nothing to write home about. Character models are done well, unfortunately the texturing in a lot of areas leaves a lot to be desired. I'm not a stickler on that though, I don't expect them to be any better on PC. As long as the game plays well, which it definitely does, the graphics don't need to be amazing.

The thing that kept me playing for hours, and years past its prime, was the Mercenaries mode. This mode in this game is phenomenal. By far the best Mercenaries mode out of any RE game. You get a selection of the main characters to choose from, and an alternate version with different loadouts and costumes. Plenty of replayability here. I remember logging a ton of hours into this on my 360. I played the mode in the other games, but they never stuck to me. For example, once I got the best grades for all characters, I stopped playing the RE4 Mercs mode. This one though, I just seemingly kept playing it to see how high of a score I could get with each character. Even after I stopped playing as much, I still found myself having a few beers every now and again, and throwing this game mode on.
EDIT: Currently have 53 hours on, roughly 40 hours of that has been in Mercs.

It was tough for me to hit the recommend button for this game, and there are basically only three reasons why I am recommending it.

1 : It does offer a lot of content. This has four normal sized campaigns with multi-linear rich  stories, even if some of them have a couple of interlapping scenes, it will offer you plenty of hours of playing.

2 : Some good co-op friends this game can be extremely pleasing. People give these modern RE's a hard time because of the less survival horror, or the fact that they are co-op, but I think co-op is actually one of the series biggests strenghts now. In a world with very few co-op games, this game is a fun time if you have some good friends to play it with. I highly recommend playing on the higher difficulties to feel the extreme tense.

3 : It's the Resident Evil universe. It's more of an already cool universe with favorable monsters and enjoyable characters. Yeah it's not perfect but it's still more RE compared to RE7 HAHAHAHAHA.

Now what do I not like about this game? The controls take awhile to get used to, I don't know why, but they just feel more awkward than even the older titles. I think pair that with the extremely tight corridors in some of the campaigns and it just makes it feel extremely sloppy, play with joystick to have a better experience.

Whilst the stories aren't bad, I felt there wasn't a good protagonist on the level of Wesker. I did like Chris's target for the first half, but although there was build up it did not end the way you would expect.

Leon's story I felt had the most boring / easy monsters, as well as the least inspired easy boss fights. I feel like Chris's campaign was just better over all.

I think what disappointed me the most is that RE5( despite of its multiplayer issue)  was basically a better game in every way. The only thing RE6 had going for it was length, but length is not important when RE5 just has more replay value. I think because I enjoyed RE5 so much more as a co-op game I will always just feel RE6 was one of the biggest let downs in the series. 
Don't get me wrong I still enjoyed it enough to recommend it.

Not your typical Resident Evil game, more action-pact, more shooting and killing. Not too many QTE but it's still present, manual dodging or QTE counter. Still has sexy female characters!



[h1]The gameplay[/h1]
No more QTE to dodge, you're doing all the dodging now! Only QTE are to counter enemy attacks which require precise timing and position. There is some QTE here and there, but none in actual cutscenes, yay!

Movement has majorly improved, allowing you to manually dodge, and not have your character be bound to the camera. Although the movement has been expanded upon, there are some moments where sometimes your character does wide turns and swings missing key points, objectives, and actions causing you to fail. With the new dodging mechanics, the gameplay could go in-depth and you can pull off some amazing moves!

Camera settings have FOV so definitely set that to your liking before starting a campaign.

The mercenaries is something very fun and enjoyable, with friends or alone. The new mechanics make everything look extremely flashy, from coup de grace, new dodging mechanics, the BGM/OST, and the additional costumes. There are also different online game modes that are playable, I think they are DLC. I believe up to 4 or 6 players could play in some of these game modes, very entertaining. Has unique character animations! (Like RE5).

A few dislikes, there are some parts of the game where it's not in your control and you have to rush or else you fail, the AI partner could sometimes be completely useless or have no sense of urgency/priority. They either take their sweet time, occasionally block doorways, or sometimes won't prioritize the right enemies that are obviously a problem to the player. (Mashing the R button for a QTE sequence when there's snipers shooting at you). Lastly, some parts of the campaign is tedious, tiresome to do. Feels like a chore.



[h1]The story, playable characters[/h1]
There's 4 different campaigns, 3 which has 2 selectable characters, and one completely solo. In Leon's campaign, there's Leon S Kennedy, and Helena Harper. In Chris's campaign there's Chris Redfield, and Piers Nivans. In Sherry's campaign, there's Sherry Birkin, and Jake Muller. Lastly, there's Ada Wong. Their campaigns can be played split screen, on co-op or intersect and up to 4 players can play together on these intersections, which is very fun and unique from the other Resident Evil games.

Unlockable characters in Mercenaries, up to 8 characters.

Personally, I find the story interesting but I also highly disliked it, too many cliche events that happen, [spoiler]Jake Muller being Albert Wesker's son,[/spoiler] no mention of Jill Valentine or Sheva Alomar.



[h1]Overall thoughts and conclusion[/h1]
Fantastic "Resident Evil," game, looks like they're trying something different in RE6! Filled with flashy action, and sexy female characters, a must own and play! Sexy female characters/10, would recommend.

RE 4-6 are sort of their own breed; so I manage my expectations quite differently for them. 4 was fantastic, 5 was fun but had a stupid story, and 6... was atrocious. 

I played through all 4 of the campaigns and the best way I could describe it is that it's like a really awful Michael Bay movie. There are tons of plot holes, cringy lines, and mind-numbingly awful dialog/hooks peppered throughout the experience. It's also a completely linear experience, fragmented into multiple perspectives of characters you almost certainly won't care about. 

They even manage to make the experience of playing RE vets like Chris, Leon, and Sherry (who isn't actually a vet, but we'll give her the title for her role in RE2) a boring affair with basically no development aside from the implication that this is all taking place in the future from previous games, and they're just doing this because that's what they do---they make Chris equally moronic as he was in 5, but whatever... and you'd think someone like Leon who's had exposure to the G-Virus and a plaga in his body would be less cavalier about something like the C-Virus... which christ, the C-Virus itself is a joke. 

I imagine the storyboard conference involved a couple of people making frenetic hand gestures and emphasizing the necessity for explosions and then finally someone chimed in with, "What's the actual dilemma/threat?" And someone speaks up with, "C-Virus?" Then someone else with equally frenetic hand gestures says that it's like a plaga with T-Virus-y bits and Ourborous-y bits!! I'd be fine with it, if they just gave this notion the TLC it needs to be even remotely convincing and not seem like someone's fan fiction.

The gameplay sucks... I played it on keyboard/mouse; and recognize that it wasn't designed for that, but my alternatives simply were unplayable (Steam and PS4 controller). 

The QTEs in 6 inspire a lot of eye-rolling after about 2 hours of playing. 

The camera... well, the character you play occupies about 25% of the screen, the HUD if you use it occupies another 20% of the screen, so your visibility is tremendously hampered and the camera shakes like crazy for every little thing---I'm not prone to motion sickness, but I bet I would've experienced it had I been. 

I gave this game about 25 hours and I deeply regret it. Save yourself the time/money, just read a summary of the story if you're curious about canon--spoiler, there's not much there, so you could probably even skip the summary.

I will explain at toward the end why I recommend this game, but first, I need to get the negatives out of the way! 

Resident Evil 6, what can I say about it.. When I finally got to play it on PS3, I was kinda disappointed by the gameplay.. Yeah, i understand they tried to implement some cool melee sequences, but it felt unnecessary.. I played thru the story campaigns, and when I completed them, I never played the game again. That was back sometime in late 2013 or 2014. This time around, I decided to buy it again for PC (since I've been into gaming on PC for almost a year now due to getting a gaming laptop), because it was on sale for cheap, and give it another chance. It was by playing through it again that I remembered why I never picked it up again back then: The gameplay did not seem as smooth as RE4 and 5 were, and while it helped to be able to shoot WHILE moving (something that wasn't present in RE4 and 5), it seemed the shooting was less consistent. 

I DID see that you could buy skills that could help with aiming, but I personally don't care for the kind of upgrade system Capcom implemented in the game! The upgrade system for weapons in 4 and 5 was MUCH better compared to 6! Not to mention, I think they totally overdid the quick time events in 6! You could be in the middle of a fight with a boss, and it goes to a scripted QTE, and when you complete one, another one pops up 2-3 seconds after, when you're not expecting one to pop up, making you totally miss the timing of the QTE and you get a game over screen! It's quite frustrating at times! The story campaigns are decent, but still leave you with questions!

This game may turn off some fans of the series, This is another game in the series I don't have a lot of hours here but played the ♥♥♥♥ out of on PS3.  the phrase Guilty Pleasure comes to mind.  Story-wise (on paper) the plot is no more or less outrageous than other games in the series but what hurt it was how we experience it in a style that emulates films like "Vantage Point" or "Hero" in which we experience the same story from different perspectives.  Seems cool on paper but you might find it becomes repetitive or tiresome as you play a lot of the same overlapping segments through the different campaigns.  You might be saying that's like every RE game but previous entries usually only had one or 2 additional characters to play through, this has like 4.

Action-wise I loved this game, You're more mobile than you've ever been in the games.  While there was some questionable features like a half-baked cover system that you rarely use (I mean, you fight zombies that pretty much walk toward you no matter what) with practice you can use the dive and slide mechanics to feel like an invincible savior against the zombie tide.  If I recall I milked this games mercenaries mode to earn money (which carries over between the game modes), if you love melee Chris is as beast as ever with a Rambo knife, picking up zombies over his head and throwing them so damn hard their head explodes on the ground, Jake... well, plays like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Wesker, meaning you might be reticent to use firearms because his fists will obliterate zombies into a bloody mess (especially if you know/ remember the special moves).

The UI might also hang up people, while some mobility mechanics (ducking and diving) felt initially awkward to me I got really used to them and was soon using them pretty naturally.  Shooting was fine and you can even aim and move this time around.  What hung me up was the menu system. you have a clunky pseudo phone thing that you use to manage inventory system.  While you can hold more items than you could in RE5, it suffers from an inefficient UI where you have a linear bar to cycle through EVERYTHING (namely your weapons, ammo, health, explosives).  It really hurts the game especially since time doesn't slow down or stop when you open it.  You also keep every weapon you pick up (no storage) so you may find you need to manage or dump ammo (which of course disappears when you dump it) in order to say... pick up a herb you need to badly to mix for health.

Despite it's short-comings I still have fun with this game, while it may feel like a survival game directed by Michael Bay (Cheesy action/'splosions/dialogue) there is still something redeemable about that stuff in a superficial level.  If this goes on sale or when you see it packaged in a sale I'd definitely recommend picking this title up for a try.  It did crash on me a few times though, so be warned.

Resident Evil 6 is the point where the series went down the hill most people may say since the game was originally a survival horror experience and then around 4-6 the game became less about zombies and horror and more about action. Now to a degree games can benifit from a change in franchise tone but the question here is does it work for the resident evil series. I will be reviewing the game in a pro/ con style and end with my conclusion.

Pro:
     Zombies are back. Well sort of back. They are only back for only 1/4 of the game but it is nice to fight zombies that walk slow and look rotten. This only exists mainly in leon's story which makes leon's campaign the best in the game in my honest opinion. 

      Combat is better designed. For starters you can aim and move at the same time. In previous games you could not do that which felt a little unnatural in a 3rd person shooter. To add on to that there is a stamina bar under the health bar which is used for combat actions like kicking and punching. It is another method of dispaching enemies than using guns and knifes which I appreciate since this game is more action orientated.

      The game looks nice. Each character, cutscene, and level looks really nice with great lighting and detail. It is nice to look at the level of detail the developers put into games graphics.

Con:
      Levels can last a while. Each chapter can take about an hour long to playthrough which adds longevity to the game but some levels you feel go on for too long, over staying its welcome. It does not help that the game has some rare bugs that happen like some loading doors not working properly. This happens in coop sessions.

        Skills/ skill points are useless. Skills are useless since you can only equip just 3 from a list of 30+. Mainly a person will pick the unlimited ammo skills and quick reload skill. This really makes this skill mechanic pointless since the benefits are negligable at best and artifically rewarding the player for playing. The skill points are aquired so slowly that the skills are overpriced for the average skill points earned in the game. This makes for a very tedius grind to get all skills for those who want to play around with the variety of skills or getting the skills you want. To make this short the skill system is pointless.

      The game is QTE heavy. Since the game is more action orientated that means that everything either needs to feel like a micheal bay movie with explosions or insane action scenes. In video games when you have these insane action stuff they are normally tied with QTE. They can be ok in small doses but this game has a bunch of them. Mainly in the other campaigns like chris and jake. Sometimes the game can catch you off guard by putting a qte in the intro cutscene to a chapter.

         Cover based combat in resident evil is not a good idea. Again since the game went action heavy in design they made the other 2 campaigns (chis and jake) a bit more cover based then it should. Unlike zombies the enemies that they face often times have guns so if you dont want to kiss a chunk of hp bye then you should hide behind cover. This mechanic works in other games like gears of war or spec ops the line because the game has good cover to cover mechanics. Here before you go into cover you need to aim your gun and hit the action button. It does not sound bad but in practice it becomes an annoyance to think about in action. Normally i just go to cover and drop on my back to be hidden behind the cover which is not really a good compromise.

Conclusion:
        Resident evil 6 has to the be the weakest in the series for all of it's massive flaws mainly tied to how action packed it was trying to be but not living up to the previous titles or failing to capture what made action games good. It is pretty average of a game with nothing that really stands out in any aspect like character development or story since it is trying to tell one story by 4 different perspectives bringing new plot to the table. If your looking for a resident evil game that is not very scare but are better than this game try out the 4th or 5th game, both are playable but the 4th is the fan favorite. If you want a scary resident evil game play the other games like 0, 1, or 2. I can not recommend this game since even doing coop was pretty bland, the only good parts were making fun of the plot or not taking the game seriously.

This game is amazing value for co-op players, you get 3 campaigns, a bonus one after the first three are finished. On top of that, you get the Mercenaries mode, complete with all the characters from Left 4 Dead 1 and 2 as a PC exclusive, multiplayer and you can invade other people's games as a random enemy.

The game leans heavily into action, even more so than Resident Evil 5, (There's a moment in the Jake/Sherry campaign near the end that gets real close to rivalling the infamous Chris VS Boulder scene in 5), but it does action really well. You're incredibly agile in this game, able to dive, roll, crawl along the floor on your back while continuing to shoot, plus melee has gotten an upgrade. This game being more actiony is always going to be a sore point for people who prefer the older survival horror style, but I think this game is absolutely worth a play at least once. The amount of content more than justifies the price and playing through with a good friend and laughing at all the cheesy over-the-top action scenes is a fun time!

Each of the campaigns do try to target a different category of action, so there's hopefully something for everyone. Chris/Piers campaign goes for a more tactical RE5-style action. Leon/Helena tries to capture a RE2/RE4 fell with a combination of zombies and freaky monsters and locales. Jake/Sherry is a mixture of the Chris campaign with a little sprinkling of an attempt at Nemesis 2.0 with a few stealth sections thrown in. The bonus campaign runs across all three, revealing more of the story and showing events not seen in the other three campaigns. The last one is shorter but still worth a play and you'll be coming in with the co-op already patched in since it originally was a single player only thing. (A really dumb oversight imo, this game thrives on co-op.)

Resident Evil 6 is a pretty good game.  There are 4 campaigns with 5 chapters each.  The first 3 campaigns can be played by two different characters each.  You start with different weapons depending upon who your character is.  I chose the default characters, but replayed a couple chapters to get a weapons achievement.  Some of the cinematics change depending upon your character.  As you play through the campaigns, you'll revisit some previous locations, however your character has a different experience so it's not just a repeat.

The graphics are dated but still look decent.  Sometimes the camera can be a problem and in certain situations it is fixed.  The game runs smoothly and I didn't encounter many issues except with Alt+Tabbing between programs a couple of times.  Sometimes when I tabbed back I'd find the game unresponsive and the screen black.

There are a couple of issues I have with the game.  First if you lose all of your health you get knocked down.  Your AI partner or second player can revive you or you have to wait for a bar to fill.  There's no way to restart the checkpoint during this time.  It can be annoying, especially when you know that you're going to die.  You can shoot during this time but you can't switch weapons.  If enemies don't kill you right away, the time spent waiting until you can reload is annoying.  Another thing are some of the long death sequences.  There's no way to skip them, you have to watch them repeatedly and you can't load a checkpoint until they are finished.  Some of the checkpoints are awkwardly placed and you'll find yourself rewatching some cinematics over and over.  You can skip the cinematics between chapters and sometimes between different story points, however if you're fighting a boss and there's a mid-battle animation, that can't be skipped.

The game is good for what it is, but it's starting to show it's age.  I found there's an "AI Trainer" mod that you can use to play Mercenaries with AI to help you get a few more achievements.  I'm not sure what the online community looks like at this point, I didn't check.

It's understandable why many RE fans hated this game at release, considering Capcom's plan for RE to never be survival horror again. But with that no longer being the case, we can finally sit back, relax, and enjoy one of the most ludicrously fun action games you can find on PC. Resident Evil 6 can best be described as Mission Impossible: Anime Edition. There are a couple points in the game where I was actually humming the MI theme without even realizing just because it fit so perfectly. Each of the four campaign takes you through varied and frenetic action set pieces that almost never take agency from the player except for what you could consider interactive cutscenes that are a stupendously stupid joy to behold, all wrapped up in the best third-person shooter combat system on the market and a surprisingly touching story with genuinely funny and dramatic moments among the unendingly likable cast.

Getting to know the surprisingly complex controls takes time, but Leon's campaign acclimates you to the different combat possibilities slowly, acting as the perfect starter for when you first get the game. The shooting works very well, but it's the melee combat system seamlessly integrated into the shooting that makes the game as fun as it is. Every one of the staggering amount of unique melee animations is animated fluidly and reflects the character's personality well. Once you take down four zombies with one baseball bat or roundhouse kick, you'll be completely addicted. Not every segment in the campaigns are perfect, with a couple real stinkers thrown in there, but these are all brief and don't mean much in a game this surprisingly long.

Excellent voice acting, always entertaining cutscenes, and deep but ludicrously fun combat makes RE 6 one of the most fun action games of the last generation, and a joy to play even all these years on. Pick up the complete pack and blast the Mission Impossible 2 guitar theme for the rip roaring zombie ride of a lifetime!

RE6 is one my favourite games, which breaks my heart because I know for a fact this game is perceived as the worst RE game in the series. That's fair, RE6 fully abandoned the survival horror genre that the series was at the time in favour of a "dramatic horror" (actual words it uses on the store page) which polarised the old and new generation of players; the veterans found themselves loathing the game for how far it had strayed from its original premise of a survival horror while the new generation found themselves in love with its combat system. I've heard from a lot of people that the amount of QTEs in the game are disgusting, which is fair also; there's a LOT of QTE cutscenes that overstay their welcome very quickly.

However, I'm not here to talk about the story, QTE cutscenes, and bugs; I'm here to talk about the combat system. Resident Evil peaked in terms of combat with RE6's combat system: you can move while aiming, you can dodge roll and you can counter, three features that previous entries didn't have. It offered something fresh and new on top of the established system as well as opening up new possibilities on what you could do in a given situation. If done well correctly, you end up becoming completely untouchable, drilling through zombies and j'avo alike. Things get even better if you bring a friend!

In short: If you are looking for an intricate combat system letting you style on enemies akin to Devil May Cry, this is the game for you. If you want to play through all the campaigns fully, though, I would recommend going through them in the order of: Jake -> Chris -> Leon -> Ada

I understand the negative reviews for this game. i agree, this is the worst resident evil game on PC ever. however that only means worse in the series, not a bad game at all if judged only by itself. It is in fact super fun. the campaign is non stop action with a lot of variety in gameplay, It is basically a third person shooter like Resident evil 5 but some parts you have to do a little tower defense, sometimes racing or flying a plane and using plane weapons based on locking-on targets, lots of fun quick time events that tests your reactions, thrilling chase sequences, some stealth based sections, launching missiles from a helicopter and taking down other helicopters, taking down giant snakes, constantly fighting a never dying boss similar to Nemesis from Resident Evil 3, carrying a giant arsenal of different and fun weapons to use (such as crossbow, elephant hunter, anti-material rifle, hydra shotgun, remote bombs, shock baton, bear commander and a lot more), stabbing a giant housefly in the eye with a lightning rod during a night storm with obviously a lot of lightning strikes, weird -but not annoying- puzzles and a lot more! if you like action games you should definitely not miss this one.

Apart from the lengthy campaign with 7 different characters to choose from, there is also a game mode called Mercenaries, in which you fight waves of enemies until a timer runs out. A lot of people are crazy about this mode and I'm pretty sure majority of players enjoy it, even though it is not my thing (i rather prefer Raid Modes introduced in Resident Evil Revelations series).

The reason this game has more negative reviews than other Resident Evil games is: It isn't a Survival Horror! All Resident Evil players, who played all the games in the series, mainly played it for being survival horror games, where atmosphere, simpler but a lot more creepier enemies, spooky and dark environments, ammo and healing item management take place. This one is just an action game instead, but as I stated, a great action game at least, not your typical zombie shooter where you run through corridors destroying same stupid zombies. There are a lot of different enemies, even simple enemies can mutate to something else quite often and become something completely different that requires a different strategy, dodging around and a more suitable weapon to be dealt with.

Game also introduces RPG-like elements, of course, I am not saying it is an RPG. When you kill enemies they drop some amount of experience points depending on how difficult the enemy is, also there are there are some secret chests in the game where you can find a tremendous amount of those experience points too. With experience points you can buy a whole bunch of different skills, such as damage reduction, item drop increase, faster recovery, being able to carry more ammo for specific weapon, dealing more damage to specific enemies, increasing stamina, increased melee or firearm damage and many more. This adds some depth to the game and make it much more enjoyable.

I finished the game in both Normal and Veteran difficulties without infinite ammo and I didn't notice any differences. I played professional difficulty a little bit, not really a lot so I can't really make a comment with a lot of accuracy but it felt like there wasn't like any difference in that one either. But 'No Hope' difficulty, oh boy. That is one real difficulty setting if challenge is what you are looking for.

Does the game have any cons? It surely has. The biggest one is not being be able to bind your different weapons to keyboard buttons. So it is not like you can press 2 to switch to shotgun, or 5 to grenade launcher. Instead you have to use mouse wheel to switch through them. And boy that is such a pita, considering you have a lot of different weapons and you have to switch a lot of times because when enemies mutate you must almost always have to switch to some other weapon suited to the weakness of that enemy. I really don't know what they had in mind when they decided to design it this way.

Another one is.. the story. It is simply horrible. I am not expecting a James Joyce story when playing a video game but boy, this is so cliche and generic. I must admit that it had some dramatic moments, but only some, in fact, i guess only two. Other than that it is simply crap.

I think I could add more, but that's all that I can think of right now. I highly recommend playing this game if you like action games. Very fun game.

Continuing my casual rampage through the Resident Evil series, once again I was not entirely disappointed by what I found when I dove into each of the four separate campaigns that followed each group of survivors, all of which starred at least one well known name in the franchise...Leon, Chris, Sherry and of course Ada. It was nice to see them all jammed together into what essentially turns out to be one huge campaign, just shown from different perspectives, and more so that they all crossed paths at some point in the timeline. Unfortunately I wasn't able to experience any of this with anyone else other than AI due to literally no one else playing online which I suppose is understandable for a game that came out in late 2012. People move on, play other games, whatever. This also meant that I couldn't really get to play some of the bonus content but honestly as long as I got to play the campaign I can deal with that.

[h1] An action packed, cinematic experience [/h1]

Unlike the previous titles of which I have most recently been playing through, this made me feel like I was watching a movie that had the added bonus of interactivity as opposed to just playing a game. I easily found myself snapping multiple screenshots over the course of all four campaigns due to how photogenic the cinematography was.

[h1] The story and voice actors [/h1]

Pretty entertaining I have to admit, it kept on moving so as to prevent it becoming stale or samey. Again, it felt like I was in a movie with how it was directed and flowed, everything felt impactful. I can only give huge praise to the voice acting as well, it sounded like they really cared and put effort into conveying real human emotion for whatever scene was currently playing out...from Chris barking at Leon as they point guns at one another, or how Helena screamed out to her sister as they dragged her away, they weren't just reading a few lines on a page, they were projecting exactly what they were aiming for you to feel in these moments.

[h1] Final notes [/h1]

All in all I had a great time with RE6 and can happily say that's another of the series in the bag, now I can move onto the next one! I understand the negative reviews for this game. i agree, this is the worst resident evil game on PC ever. however that only means worse in the series, not a bad game at all if judged only by itself. It is in fact super fun. the campaign is non stop action with a lot of variety in gameplay, It is basically a third person shooter like Resident evil 5 but some parts you have to do a little tower defense, sometimes racing or flying a plane and using plane weapons based on locking-on targets, lots of fun quick time events that tests your reactions, thrilling chase sequences, some stealth based sections, launching missiles from a helicopter and taking down other helicopters, taking down giant snakes, constantly fighting a never dying boss similar to Nemesis from Resident Evil 3, carrying a giant arsenal of different and fun weapons to use (such as crossbow, elephant hunter, anti-material rifle, hydra shotgun, remote bombs, shock baton, bear commander and a lot more), stabbing a giant housefly in the eye with a lightning rod during a night storm with obviously a lot of lightning strikes, weird -but not annoying- puzzles and a lot more! if you like action games you should definitely not miss this one.

Apart from the lengthy campaign with 7 different characters to choose from, there is also a game mode called Mercenaries, in which you fight waves of enemies until a timer runs out. A lot of people are crazy about this mode and I'm pretty sure majority of players enjoy it, even though it is not my thing (i rather prefer Raid Modes introduced in Resident Evil Revelations series).

The reason this game has more negative reviews than other Resident Evil games is: It isn't a Survival Horror! All Resident Evil players, who played all the games in the series, mainly played it for being survival horror games, where atmosphere, simpler but a lot more creepier enemies, spooky and dark environments, ammo and healing item management take place. This one is just an action game instead, but as I stated, a great action game at least, not your typical zombie shooter where you run through corridors destroying same stupid zombies. There are a lot of different enemies, even simple enemies can mutate to something else quite often and become something completely different that requires a different strategy, dodging around and a more suitable weapon to be dealt with. 

Game also introduces RPG-like elements, of course, I am not saying it is an RPG. When you kill enemies they drop some amount of experience points depending on how difficult the enemy is, also there are there are some secret chests in the game where you can find a tremendous amount of those experience points too. With experience points you can buy a whole bunch of different skills, such as damage reduction, item drop increase, faster recovery, being able to carry more ammo for specific weapon, dealing more damage to specific enemies, increasing stamina, increased melee or firearm damage and many more. This adds some depth to the game and make it much more enjoyable.

I finished the game in both Normal and Veteran difficulties without infinite ammo and I didn't notice any differences. I played professional difficulty a little bit, not really a lot so I can't really make a comment with a lot of accuracy but it felt like there wasn't like any difference in that one either. But 'No Hope' difficulty, oh boy. That is one real difficulty setting if challenge is what you are looking for. 

Does the game have any cons? It surely has. The biggest one is not being be able to bind your different weapons to keyboard buttons. So it is not like you can press 2 to switch to shotgun, or 5 to grenade launcher. Instead you have to use mouse wheel to switch through them. And boy that is such a pita, considering you have a lot of different weapons and you have to switch a lot of times because when enemies mutate you must almost always have to switch to some other weapon suited to the weakness of that enemy. I really don't know what they had in mind when they decided to design it this way.

Another one is.. the story. It is simply horrible. I am not expecting a James Joyce story when playing a video game but boy, this is so cliche and generic. I must admit that it had some dramatic moments, but only some, in fact, i guess only two. Other than that it is simply crap.

I think I could add more, but that's all that I can think of right now. I highly recommend playing this game if you like action games. Very fun game.

Honestly, I'm a big fan of Resident Evil games, but ... as for this part, even if I had a triple in my vein, I wouldn't be able to finish this game and remember it fondly. Why am I so critical?

[b]...The story?[/b]

Resident Evil 6 follows the story of several characters from the Resident Evil world: Leon, Helena, Jake, Sherry, Ada, Chris and one more I don't know. This part is supposed to expand the horizons of the whole series and therefore somehow end or tie the series in several timelines, but the way CAPCOM handled this story is unexpectedly bad, as a concept of the game itself it is not bad and it doesn't sound bad at all, but their conversion from paper reality is shocking, the story itself doesn't know what it's talking about and the storytelling itself is so confused that at one point you say to yourself "What the hell is this and what am I actually playing?!" There is no point in discussing the individual stories here, because first of all it would make this review very long and at the same time you would have to read this review about 3 times to at least grasp what I am telling you, just say that the story of RE6 is really complicated and you don't even know what timeline it takes place in.

[b]Luxurious gameplay.. at least something[/b]

One thing I have to admit to this part is that its Gameplay mechanics are really great and from the parts of the RE series it is really very good, the combination of weapons, along with Melee attacks and the ability to tear apart a zombie is really good, combining known plants from which you then have healing has also improved a bit and I think it has really good mechanics, I'm not sure what caused such good gameplay along with a no sense story. But the main thing is that you have a lot of options to play the game, moving around the maps and the areas you are in is really important, and I have to say that the environment and the mechanics themselves are worked out to the letter, but when you switch weapons, it is confusing at times since you have an "inventory" as a cross that is superimposed over itself and it can get confusing at times. Along with the fact that the cartridges for the two weapons look almost identical. However, if you play the game for an hour (if you survive it) you will start to get used to it and it will not feel like a burden, but rather like a sophisticated part of the game.

[b]Is it going?[/b]

To be honest, this game has been around for a year now, but sometimes some errors can occur, for example, when Alt+Tab and returning to the game again, your FPS may drop for a little while, but it's nothing serious, but as usual with Capcom games , so the optimization and technical side of the game is in excellent condition and there is nothing to complain about.

[b]So... now what?[/b]

This game throws a really bad story in your face along with cruel mechanics, Devil May Cry style, but the way this story is handled doesn't really make the game easier for you and rather makes you stop playing or uninstall the game itself, if you're a Resident Evil player you know what I'm talking about I'm talking, but if you've never played an RE game and jumped into it, then it's up to you how you perceive the story itself, but I have to say that I can't imagine it from the perspective of someone who has never played an RE game and just jumps into it. For me, I can't recommend this game for solo play, maybe it's fun in co-op, but even after I finished playing with my partner, I still didn't enjoy this game that much, maybe if you take some Devil's straw or a shot of something strong, then you might enjoy it, but I can't recommend this game for you, if you want to try it, go for it, Refund exists on Steam.

I knew of the tales, I knew it wasn't going to be as pleasantly viewed as some of the other games in the franchise. But holy god, this game was just outright awful. It's every bit as bad as a bad action movie. The story is ... I'm gonna go ahead and say it's non-existent. It's basically "Bargain bin RE5", which wasn't exactly famous for its deep story. The first and in my view the most important aspect of a video game is therefore replaced by nothing.

Let's get to gameplay. The game ditches the survival horror roots of the franchise and turns it into a shooting gallery. That's not a bad thing in of itself, I love action games. The bad thing is that it doesn't do the action well. Resident Evil 5 was also a (mostly) action game, and I loved it despite it being a rather stupid game (personal opinion). However, in RE6, the enemies aren't fun to shoot at, they're ridiculous, and for the most part, annoying.

The environments aren't memorable. This is a game breaking mistake of "Operation Raccoon City" proportions.

It's really saying something when you have to actively try not to hate the protagonist as whom you play, even beloved characters like Ada, Leon and Chris.

One other thing that just ticks me off is the fact that there are no special weapons available. RE4 had the matilda, the infinite launcher, the handcannon, the PRL412 and the chicago typewriter. Even if you had to do some pretty insane things to get them, you COULD get them. RE4 provided the annoyingly persistent player with the perfect arsenal of weapons. RE5 had the gattling gun, the long bow, the Hydra, the M93R pistol, and the S&W M500 magnum. While they weren't necessarily perfect (no PRL412), they did reward the player with something. RE6 has nothing. There's nothing "Special" to get, a point that stands for the other aspects of the game as well.

The dialogue is outright laughable, in a "They actually paid people to write, speak, and animate this line" way.

The price of the game is too high. I bought it for around $5 when it was on sale not too long ago. I wouldn't recommend anyone paying full price for this.

Resident Evil 6 is a mixed bag for many people.
Some people hate it, others love it. Most people just don't know how they feel about it and it all boils down to how much it strays from the typical RE formula.

It tells a good story but the gameplay rarely feels like something you'd expect in a Resident Evil game, especially during the Chris and Piers campaign.

The 3 main campaigns feature different playstyles.
Leon's campaign is the standard "horror" campaign. You face off against hordes of zombies in a series of attacks that strike the US and China. I found it to be a rather good campaign aside from the final boss.

Sherry's campaign is the "chase" campaign. It's highly reminiscing of RE3:Nemesis. You follow Sherry as she attempts to acquire a VIP that can potentially terminate the current bio-terror threat all the while being pursued by a hulking abomination named Ustanak. Again, a very good campaign except for certain segments in the final chapter.

Chris' campaign is the "action" campaign. I believe this is what most people have a problem with. You play as either Chris or Piers Nivans, a new addition, as they combat bio-terror across the world with the BSAA. While I appreciate the role of the BSAA in the RE universe it just doesn't feel like you're playing RE aside from the enemy being BOW's. Truth be told I did enjoy this campaign but the action was just too much at times.

There is a 4th campaign and that is the Ada Wong campaign.
It exists mostly to tie everything together and to provide some backstory to some characters that you meet and events that occur during the campaigns. Very satisfying. It is my favorite campaign.

At the end of the day I found RE6 to be a good addition to the series even with its shortcomings.

If you have played the other Resident Evils before this, especially 5 since it was CO-OP, then after playing this game you'll agree it is not very good...

To start off, the gunplay is bad in this game. Enemies do not seem react at all when being shot. The gun sway is also annoying at range. The gunplay felt better in the previous games.

The campaigns have lots of situations that just do not make plan sense at all. Out of all the Resident Evils, this game seems like it does this the worst. But that if anything isn't what is really wrong with this game.

The enemies you encounter are whatever. Where are the OG enemies at, like the Chainsaw Man, the executioner, etc?

The character development, for the most part, is awful. Especially Leon's. Leon is just a disappointment in this game. Where is the cool Leon from RE4 at?

The story development also is terrible. There is no meaning to anything. Nothing really is explained. You'll be quite confused a lot when playing through the game.

I personally preferred the inventory system from RE5. Also why is it that you and your partner have the same weapons? Why isn't it different / unique like RE5? And why can I not drop stuff like ammo and herbs like in RE5?

The bosses in this game are nothing like ones in the previous. They have no mechanics at all (different move sets) and, therefore, are easy to defeat. One of the most annoying things in this game is the boss fight against Simmons, who is considered the main boss of the game. First of all, he just isn't a very good villain compared to Wesker. But most importantly, his "transformation" into the "boss" are just stupid. He becomes "this" then you think you killed him, but nope. He comes back as something else. Think you killed him again? LUL. He comes back again as something else. After like the fourth time or whatever, it just becomes a freaking annoyance at this point and you just want it to end. And the game does not give you any ammo barely up to when fighting him every time, so you will always run out. Why?

And his transformations btw? They are awfully stupid. They make plan no sense at all. At one point he turns basically into a T-Rex and then at another point a huge bug. And then back into a human in front of your eyes. Like wtf?...

And I played this game at the highest difficulty, and Simmons was a complete meme to defeat. No challenge at all. He just became irritating to fight as he did the same boring stuff over and over again and you just get tired of killing him.

The game also feels more action and cliche rather than a horror game, like how Resident Evil is SUPPOSED to be. Which is just depressing. Now yes RE5 was action horror but it did it a lot better. The game campaign / story development made sense, the character development was good, and the enemies / bosses were good too. 

If you're desperate for CO-OP experience, then buy the game. I played it CO-OP and that is the only reason why I played it.

If not, do not bother. Unless the game is cheap af atm.

Quite an enjoyable game. This game is also valuable in another way as it is arguably the best game you can travel the famous but now demolished slum, Kowloon Wall City in Hong Kong. Some previous games depicted this location, such as Kowloon's Gate (PS1) and Shenmue 2 (DC/Xbox), but neither's graphic reached the authenticity and quality of RE6. Aside from the subpar texture quality, it perfectly recreated some environment and the feel of the location. A lot of locations in the game can be seen in the book of "City of Darkness" by Ian Lambot, and the great photography books of "The Last of Kowloon / Saigo No Kowloon Johsai" by Shintaro Nakamura. Japanese people are known for their ardent love in the Kowloon Walled City and the feature the location in numerous of mangas (for example, GetBackers) and animes (Ghost in the Shell 2.0). If you have read those books and played this game, you can easily feel such kind of love the programmers and artists poured into this game to recreate it. I finished this game on PS4, sold the game, and then repurchase it on Steam for the solely purpose that one day I would like to visit the virtual Kowloon again.

[h1]Quick Summary[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 is an action/horror third person shooter game with co-op, puzzle, and story elements. It takes away the focus from horror and emphasizes the action and story compared to older RE games, while providing around 20 hours of campaign. 

[h1]Pros[/h1]
-Lots of content. There are 4 separate campaigns that can be played fully in co-op or alone, with cutscenes and multiple action sequences. 
-Intricate storyline with intertwining story arcs from the various characters. 
-Cutscenes and dialogue. They are all pretty good quality with good voice actors. 
-Overall fun gameplay with lots of different guns depending on the campaign and character you play.
-Each campaign is pretty varied from the other ones, with different melee animations, guns, locations, bosses, and even common enemies. This keeps each playthrough feeling fresh and new.

[h1]Cons[/h1]
-The primary con in my opinion is the forced “fixed camera angle” segments in the games. They often take place during boss battles or forced flight sequences, throwing in unnecessary awkwardness into gameplay. I do understand that this was a staple of the original titles, but as a newcomer to the series it felt very unfair and annoying to have to adjust everything I knew just for certain parts of the game, when the tension was already high enough. While playing co-op with my wife, we died so many times just during these parts where the camera was locked a certain way or made you run backwards for example, never during the actual combat. 
- You can’t skip the credits at the end of each campaign. 

[h1]Neutral[/h1]
-Less horror; more action. This depends on your preference. I thought the focus on action was pretty fun especially when you played as soldiers in Chris Redfield’s campaign. You’re able to kill zombies with powerful melee hits, many different firearms, grenades, and environmental tools. Not only that but you are able to dodge hits, roll, slide, and shoot while in cover or on the ground. This gives you many options for taking down enemies. However, this takes away some of the tension of previous games by eliminating the need for really conserving ammo or choosing your battles. 

[h1]Story Quality[/h1]
For the most part, Resident Evil 6 presents an interesting but somewhat predictable story. I did really enjoy how side characters in one campaign were playable in the next, so you got to see everything that happens in between. 

[h1]Technical Analysis[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 ran with no bugs or crashes in all 4 campaigns, so it runs great from a technical standpoint. I will say the user interface is different in each campaign and uses symbols instead of text, so it is not intuitive on which part of the menu is what you need. It uses a glaring, almost neon colored UI that I really did not enjoy. It also is quite different from previous games so it’s hard to get used to it, at least initially. Figuring out how to combine items or change ammo type in weapons was also not easy to figure out.
Resident Evil 6 is a bit older, so optimization was no issue. The textures were pretty blurry at times, but this is also a 6 year old game so I don’t feel I can complain too much. 

[h1]Price…is it worth it?[/h1]
I bought the game on sale at $7.49. At that price, I think it’s easily worth it and a no-brainer if you like Resident Evil games or even just want to shoot up some zombies for a few hours. It’s base price of $29.99 seems a bit high since it is older, so I would recommend if you are interested in this game, to buy it on sale. 

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 makes some bold moves in the franchise by taking away some of the tension, item management and horror of previous titles. However, as an action and story-driven game I believe it’s quite fun and especially enjoyable in co-op. I do recommend picking it up on sale though, as it’s a bit older and not a mind-blowing story.

This is the first game in the series left I hadn't yet played, and is also the worst.   Damn shame,  as I was very much looking forward to it. NOTE: Campaign play only!

THE GOOD:
[list]
[*]4 Campaigns with crossovers
[*]FANTASTIC animation
[*]The action gets your blood pumping in the first few moments
[/list]
THE BAD:
[list]
[*]The action is all there is.  There's no exploration, no reward for being extra diligent beyond the typical out-of-play extras.  [*]It makes the action lose all meaning
[*]THE CAMERA. GOD, THE CAMERA.  It feels like an old PS1 game. 
[*]You see how in the promo video characters sometimes move around in circles to do something?  That's not a nifty dodge.  It's how you move.  The movement controls are kind of hit and miss. 
[*]The key mapping, by default, is nothing like the previous games.   This makes sense only in as much as neither are the controls.  Remember tabbing into your inventory to pause the action?  NOPE.   You'll be holding ALT and scrolling with your mouse, or hitting a key that brings up an item menu with NO CLUE how to use it.   I know, you're thinking, "ti's just an inventory", but imagine playing old Zelda and having to hold the Select key white twisting the controller sideways and holding A plus the directional pad to select the flute. 
[*]The QTEs are back and man are they awkward.   You're either rolling WASD keys in order or rapidly tapping the key you mapped to actions.
[*]Back to that inventory.  Not only is there no pause, but you have to seelct every item previous to the one you want to get to the one you want. 
[*] The HUD is confusing; it resembles old arcade rifle shooters, with a bullet count in little  bullet icons and a number indicating all of the shells in your inventory.   Health is a large series of blocks, while combat energy is in a little bar. 
[*] Gone are the onscreen prompts like blood around the edges to tll you that our health is low.  Your only indicator is your nearly transparent HUD. 
[*] Herbs shake into pills, and pills only restore one point of health.  Found a red herb?  Mix it to get 5 green pills basically.  
[*] Bosses often lack visible weak spots and the "difficulty" is bullet sponge elimination. 
[*]You can't carry ammo for every weapons, and ive found no inventory expansion item
[*] The level design is atrocious.   You're often running or driving in scripted events and the controls are sluggish and bad.  The developers appear to have looked up "levels players hate" because you WILL have sewer levels and there IS an underwater level where you have to hunt air pockets like Sonic the Hedgehog. Unfortunately, you can't see most of the things you need to save your life or to avoid getting killed until they've killed you already. 
[*]NOTHING is scary about this, other than the damage it does tot he franchise.  The constant threats completely eliminate the sense of tension and foreboding that made the games great
[*] Companion AI always gets the easy job while you're stuck with your back to the wall, no ammo, no health items. 
[*] Those health items are so rare they are almost pointless
[*] Prior games rewarded identifying a sleeping zombie and killing it.  In this game, unless a script has run to make it attack you AND it's been put on its feet, bullets *pass through* the target, so you have to piss it off and risk injury to kill it. 
[*] You MUST master the dodge mechanic, because once a zombie begins its attack, it is invincible until it lands it.
[*] Campaigns spoil each other due to them not being in chronological  order. 
[*] Most bosses are killed by a scripted event, and some you may as well not even shoot. 
[*] Companions can't share loot
[*] Game is so totally on rails that if you see a place to explore, it's really just where it was going to send you next. 
[*] Even a successful QTE can be ignored and you'll get hurt anyway
[*] Some QTEs chain in a way that if you fail the first, the next one coming up will hurt you
[*] Most of the time, running from zombies isn't an option.   You absolutely must kill everyone on the field. 
[/list]

Edit: Since my last attempt, i tried playing the game again, but with a setting that ostensibly disables the QTEs.  It doesn't, actually, except for certain QTEs that would prevent you from watching the story unfold because you have to do the QTE to not die.  However, this did make enough of a difference to enjoy it, and I happily played through Leon's campaign and started into the others.   I'll update this list as I go, but here's what to expect:

[Prologue] - Easy peasy.   Just shoot zombies when you see them, though one or two can be evaded.   

[Leon Campaign] - The nerfed QTEs from the setting toggle helped a lot here.   I enjoyed most of the playthrough, and most enemies were zombies, as one might expect from a zombie game. 

[Chris Campaign] - Chris's campaign starts out more militaristic, but play focused a lot more on weak point discovery.  This had more "first run traps", such as a hall where if you go for ammo before you chase off an invisible snake monster, it will yank you up into the vents and you get a game over screen.  I ran out of ammunition more often here, but Chris is a dynamo with a combat knife.   Unfortunately, this campaign also introduced the dreaded "running in reverse" that no gamer enjoys, where you have to run toward the screen from something that kills you if you slow down or stop at all, but also have to climb or slide under things as if you were playing Crash Bandicoot backward.   The final boss for the campaign even has this feature, with the camera angle becoming your worst enemy as it flips around and messes with your running direction. 

[Jake Campaign] - This campaign has been hell so far.   It starts with some passable combat moments and story tension, but whoever designed these levels thinks that turning the environment against the player in a Nintendohard fashion is fun, especially combined with the 'Ustanak'. That word means "uprising", but in this case, it's Nemesis from RE:3 but without random appearance, with a multipurpose arm that seems to change function as easily as MegaMan selecting a weapon.  He's in every mission so far that doesn't involve you driving a sluggish snowmobile at breakneck speeds to escape an avalanche, and im stuck on the ultimate crap combo: a stealth mission where if you step on ice or shoot a gun or otherwise make noise, Ustanak busts through a wall and kills you almost instantly.   If your'e seen by his pet fireflies, he does it as well.  Then, you have to use bombs to distract him while your partner gets a card key, and then do ->8<- QTEs in rapid succession using the movement keys or again, instant death.   You have to run between those QTEs as well, so if you happen to hit a movement button as the QTE finishes, you lose half a second and die to the Ustanak. 
[Ada Campaign] let you know after I finish the Jake campaign....if I can stomach it.

I know what my major issue is.   if you've ever played D&D or another tabletop game with a bad DM, that's how this feels.   Innovation isn't rewarded.  You aren't allowed to outsmart the design, but instead must follow tightly on the rails. QTEs arefrequent and sometimes even success equates to failure.   Particularly in the Jake campaign, I feel less like I'm playing a game and more like I'm going through  level design that was put together specifically to make sure players ragequit.
