The game that killed classic Resident Evil. Perhaps unfair to lay entirely at its feet as a lot of the bad ideas here have root in RE5 and to a degree 4, but this games takes them and runs with it.

It's got cool ideas on occasion. The scene where there's a gas attack, the initial escape from the infected college campus, many of the set pieces, really, have basically good ideas at their core. But everything about the execution is so haphazard and messy and dull that it kills any joy from watching Leon play Keifer Sutherland, or Ada and her inexplicable best pal Gas-mask Bob, the most disposable man ever designed.

It's a game where you can tell the team was just out of ideas. There's a nemesis who's really big and tougher than original flavour nemesis, because the kids, they loved nemesis. The parasite Zombos from 4 and 5 are back but they're sharing the space with more traditional T-virus-y zeds because why not. You fight a T-rex monster who somehow is able to store his entire bulk inside of a single man's body despite being A FULL SIZED, SEVERAL METRE TALL TYRANNOSAURUS REX-SCORPION-ZOMBIE-FLESH-MONSTER-THING. Chris has a buddy. A young woman is escorted by Troy Baker, as is tradition. Most of the cast from previous entries doesn't warrant a mention because I guess they're doing other stuff in the middle of the world ending again. It all feels very, very tired.

It's also a game that has some spots that look really, really good, the rain effects are pretty nice for 2013 in a "wet-coat" kind of way. the characters look pretty solid. But then, at the same time as fancy, well rendered, grizzled leon and his stalwart lady sidekick are doing something, the environmental textures look like they're straight out of the dreamcast days. It's a really weird gap in quality.

It's something of a relief the series went a fresh direction and also managed to find something new to do with the classic characters. Being able to come back from a slump and do two entirely different takes on the same franchise and have them BOTH land with the audience is a notable achievement and Capcom should get some serious props for that.

Resident Evil 6, however, is debatably as low as the series has ever gotten.

Resident Evil 6 has given me a new appreciation for Resident Evil 5. That game wasn't good, but this game takes it to a whole new level of awful.

Since RE6 is one of those entries in a well-established series that deviates significantly from nearly everything that was enjoyable about the best entries in the series, it is fashionable to say things like "it may not be a good RESIDENT EVIL game, but it is a good ACTION game." No. Absolutely not. This piece of garbage wishes that its only problem was not being Resident Evil enough. This game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks for more reasons than I am likely to remember, but I will do my best.

In the interest of fairness, let's start with the positives:

[list]
[*]It runs at a rock solid 120fps (capped). Even RE5 had the ocassional dips in gameplay. This game does not.
[*]You can move while shooting.
[*]There is a lot of it. This is probably a plus if you actually enjoy this game for some reason. It is not short.
[/list]

Now, let's talk about why this game is god-awful.

[list]
[*]Terrible character controller. Of course this game features that special kind of overwrought third person character controller with an excess of animation frames and a minimum of control. Most of the time, any attempt to change directions will result in the character slowly moving in an awkward arc. I actually felt more in control with old school tank controls and they were more responsive.

[*]Over-reliance on incredibly generous grab attacks. This becomes apparent very quickly in Leon's campaign, because they ALSO drastically overuse the "zombie play dead and then attack you" cliche (of course, you can't shoot them until they activate). The majority of the damage I took in this game was probably from grabs that I had no real chance of dodging and from the sniper enemies (which of course are feature in tiny indoor environments, because that's how snipers work).

[*]The "new melee system." Well, in theory this is an improvement, but with the terrible movement, it's mostly a pain. Watching your character do a lap around the enemy while you try to line up the head stomp or pressing the attack button just slightly out of range for the context sensitive finisher and just throwing out a regular attack that does nothing.

[*]Aggressively hyper linear levels with tons silly invisible walls. So, here's my experience with Resident Evil 6.  TL;DR : it's basically a faster paced RE 5.

When I first bought it during the summer on 2017, I really hated it.  It was basically went the complete opposite way I expected this opus of the serie to go : I was expecting the story to be about 12-15 hours long (like the previous entries in the serie), it was actually 25h ; I was expecting the controls to be a bit stiff and slower paced like the ones in RE 5, RE 6 was actually very fast paced ; I was expecting a heavy emphasis towards coop between the players (akin to RE 5 in which you need to exchange ammunitions, grenades, herbs, etc.), there is actually no real insentives to cooperate except to open/unlock some doors ; amongst other things.  So since it was nothing like I expected it to be, I felt a bit disoriented and frustrated with the game.  Especially since I wanted to finish it fast so I could then move on to RE: Operation Raccoon City.  What was also very frustrating to me was that I never knew where to go or what to do (especially since sometimes, the clue is simply "Figure out the puzzle"...) So as soon as I finished it, I ended up immediatly uninstalling it and telling myself I would never touch it ever again.

After about one year, I decided to give RE 6 another chance, since I'm an achivements ♥♥♥♥♥ and the ones in RE games are often easy to acquire.  And maybe it wasn't as bad as I remembered it. So I installed it again, despite what I was thinking a year prior.  This time, I knew what to expect from the game.  I had a clearer idea of what the devoloppers were trying to do.  RE 6 is essentially like RE 5, but without the stiff and sometimes clunky control, shooting and inventory management mechanics.  For example, you have access to every weapons you find it each campaigns (unlike RE 5 in which you need to select which ones you are going to use and want to upgrade).

And since it was supposed to be the last entry in the RE saga, there's a little recap of every previous entries with each campaigns.  The Leon and Helena campaign has stuff from RE 2 (Leon driving a cop car) in it, with bit's of RE: Code Veronica (Deborah boss fight) ; Chris and Piers campaign has vibes of RE 1 (City Hall part being similar to the Spencer manor) and RE 5 (Chris losing his partners) ; Jake and Sherry campaign has vibes of RE 3 (with Ustanak following you everywhere akin to the Nemesis) ; Ada's campaign has RE 4 vibes (being a double agent you are never sure you can fully trust and always teasing Leon) ; etc.

This second playthrough ended up being a lot more enjoyable than I ever thought it would be, all because I took the time to better understand what the game was.  The only lackluster thing RE 6 has is a lack of polishing.  The graphics and voice acting in most language are often laughable and sometimes even pathetic, especially for minor characters (the teacher/director in the first part of the first mission in Leon and Helena's campaign comes to mind...)  But overall, I'd say it's a pretty fun coop game that I definitely recommend.

Upon its completion, I found far less faults with Resident Evil 6 than I was expecting. On its own, this is still a somewhat-flawed-yet-fun action game, and I believe I can explain the backlash from fans and critics. 

Since the release of Resident Evil 4, the series has gradually stepped away from its survival-horror and adventure roots. Level design in RE4, 5 and 6 was more of a straight path rather than the intricately-built puzzle boxes of the first games. Puzzles are nearly nonexistent, and the ones that appear are elementary. Ammunition is plentiful, making the games reward fight instead of flight. What we’re left with in RE6 is a (mostly) competent action romp that still  contains a ton of value. There’s a lot of game here, and action horror fans would still do well to pick this one up on sale.
It's not bad

[i]Resident Evil 6 (RE6)[/i] is a crossover between a third-person shooter, an action adventure game and a survival horror game. Like its predecessor, RE6 was designed for co-op play, but you can play it solo with an AI-controlled partner, too. And to start off this review on a positive note: the AI is a lot less annoying this time, mainly because they made the AI partners immortal. 

The Resident Evil games started out as survival horror games, and while this installment in the series still shows its roots in the survival horror genre, the focus has shifted almost entirely to combat action.

Compared to RE5 and to both Resident Evil Revelations (RER) games, which were also shooter games rather than survival horror games, RE6 has some striking flaws. But since RE6 offers a story set in the ever-fascinating Resident Evil universe, some creepy settings and opponents, tense shooting action, high replayability and just overall decently exciting gameplay, I came to the conclusion I'll recommend RE6, albeit not with the greatest enthousiasm. As an action adventure game it's a no-brainer: recommended! As a Resident Evil game, though… let's say I understand why RE6 gets so much hate, especially from longtime fans of the series.


[h1]Story[/h1]

Biotechnological viruses are deployed in both the US and China, and the protagonists of the four campaigns will do their part to put a stop to both outbreaks. Yes, the story of RE6 is split up into four campaigns (Leon/Rebecca, Chris/Piers, Jake/Sherry and Ada Wong), each containing five chapters. The campaigns are interwoven but they don't play out chronologically, which makes the story confusing. It also makes the game a bit repetitive, as about two chapters of each of the campaigns you play after the first one are set in the same place and during the same events you've witnessed before. RE6's story is by far the weakest of the Resident Evil games I've played. Also, the main antagonist of the game is one of the least interesting characters ever in the RE universe.


[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

RE6 plays like a regular third-person shooter game in a 3D environment. But sometimes, the camera is your worst opponent, forcing you to look in one direction while there's action going on all around you. 

As has become customary in Resident Evil games, you'll have to deal with Quick-Time Events (QTE) in RE6. If you hate QTE even half as much as I do, you'll draw from your entire arsenal of swearwords while playing RE6, especially during Leon's campaign, which doesn't only throw a ton of QTE at you during cutscenes and parcours sections, but also every time a 'zombie' manages to grab you.

Too often, the game restricts your freedom of movement, especially during Leon's campaign. Or you find yourself in the middle of a large fight when the camera suddenly points towards something going on in the distance two or three times, which makes the pacing of some fights awful and frustrating.

When you start the second campaign, Chris' campaign, you get the feeling you're playing a run-of-the-mill shooter. Later on, you'll encounter several timed parcours segments with awkward controls and camera angles. And in between, you find yourself playing a racing game, driving a vehicle and having to learn the obstacles and curves of the track by trial and error in order to complete it succesfully. Events like that aren't the main part of the game, but they're numerous enough to sometimes make you feel like checking if you've actually fired up a Resident Evil game.

One of my biggest gripes with RE6 is that there are no weapon upgrades at all, despite the game being so gun-action focused. Instead, there is a skill system but it's just there for form's sake. You can only ever have three skills active, so early on in the game you'll have selected your three or four favorite skills, which you'll be able to fully upgrade in the course of the first few levels, and that's it for 'character customization'. 

There isn't any form of a reward system like RE4, RE5, RER & RER2 had to unlock weapons, weapon upgrades or skills beyond the first part of the game. RE6 is a very linear game and there are no secrets to discover. The only lootable objects in the game are ammo and healing items. So there's no more treasure to loot like in RE4 and RE5, and there are no more collectibles to find (except for the emblems, which do make a return but have no tangible reward tied to them), so there is no reason for exploration in this game. New weapons are clearly marked on your screen, and if you still manage to miss one, it's handed to you at the end of the chapter.

There are very little puzzles and they're child's play. Gameplay is mostly shooter action, alternated with some parcours sections and a few racing segments. 

I think it's clear I'm not praising RE6 to the sky. As far as Resident Evil games go, it's the misfit of the family. Still, in the whole of games out there, RE6 definitely has some fun parts and even though I considered quitting RE6 a few times, it did manage to make me want to play through all the campaigns once, at least (you can play three of the four campaigns as the other character of the duo, which makes for a slightly different experience, adding replayability). If a game manages to make me want to finish it, it deserves a recommendation, but RE6 definitely doesn't come [i]highly[/i] recommended in my book.


[h1]Mercenaries and DLC[/h1]

I never played the Mercenaries game mode in RE4. I loved the version RER and especially RER 2 had, but not so much RE6's version. The challenge isn't to survive or to manage your resources to complete a level, but to create a chain of 50 kills within a time frame, preferably using melee attacks because these increase your alotted time. Not my kind of fun, but to each his own. Also, the reward system is practically non-existent as you just get more skill points, which you'll have plenty of anyway by playing the campaign.

The DLCs just add a few online modes to the game. Since RE6's online activity is pretty much dead and the DLC are fairly expensive, I gave them a miss.


[h1]Graphics and sound[/h1]

Considering RE6 is 6 years old, its graphics look very nice. Sure, they won't compare favourably to a triple-A game released last year, but the environments' textures look sharp and sometimes genuinely beautiful, and since you want to avoid being up close and personal to any 'zombie' or other mutant, they look adequately scary from a regular distance.

RE6 is a very dark game, though, especially compared to RE5 which was set in sunny Africa. The darkness adds to the spooky atmosphere, of course, but it doesn't do justice to the game world, which looks very nice but is mostly covered in darkness and shadows.

The user interface (UI) looks fancy, modern and stylish BUT the slick design results in a very user-unfriendly UI. Function over design, dear devs, not the other way around!

I usually write a few words about the music of each game I review, but for RE6, I can't. The music didn't leave one bit of a lasting impression on me. On the one hand, that means the score wasn't terribly impressive, but on the other hand, it means it wasn't annoying, either.

The voice acting is the best in the main series so far (I haven't played RE7 or the remake of RE2 yet). There is almost no character development in the narrative, so the voice actors didn't have decent enough scripts to draw a lot from, but they still managed to add some credible emotions to each of the characters.


[h1]On Steam's extra features[/h1]

RE6 has 8 Steam Trading Cards. You'll get 4 while running the game.

The 70 Steam Achievements are varied. RE6 is a game that's very hard to 100%. Some achievements are time-consuming because they require a significant amount of grinding. Others can only be unlocked through online play, which is pretty much dead now, and most of them require purchasing the DLC to boot.

RE6 has been frequently ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on for being nothing like RE and being more of an action game that almost killed the franchise. Before playing this game with a friend, I saw it as another action game that could have potential to be *a good* action game. However it isn't like that. Not only is this game an insult towards the rest of the RE games, it's just not a good game to begin with, for the most part at least. The game has 4 campaigns, and the order you should go in is how it's presented. Finish Leon's then go Chris's, then Jake's, then Ada's (iirc lol). The game has a weird line of quality. Leon's campaign at the start was laughable, in terms of writing and level design and just general dialogue. Then later on in his campaign it gets a bit better (or more bearable rather) then it's over. The first thing you'll notice is that RE's signature tank controls are gone, and it's more like your normal action shooter's movement system. This is one of the main things that make it *not* an RE game. [b]Resident Evil 6[/b] completely ditches the "survival horror" part, now it's an over the top action game. After completing a short prologue mission as Leon. You get to choose, who you want to play as. The game features 4 distinct campaigns: Leon, Chris, Jake and Ada. All of them take place around the same time, so you will run into other characters and you'll have to complete each of the campaigns to get the full picture. 

In Leon's campaign you fight zombies, that are similar to the ones from the original trilogy. Except now they are faster, they can jump at you and avoid your aim. To compensate for it, you can now move while shooting, do some cool melee attacks and jump around like Max Payne. What I liked about this game, that it's actually hard and in order to complete it, you're gonna need to learn how to avoid enemy attacks and use melee properly, because finding ammo is almost as hard as in previous RE games. 

The game changes drastically when you launch Chris's campaign. It becomes a cover based shooter with one of the worst cover systems. Enemies now have guns and can shoot at you, so you'd better find some cover. There are some complications hovewer, when you shoot an enemy, it might mutate and turn into something, that can't shoot, but will charge at you with great speed. So staying at the cover for a long time wouldn't work. But when you're not in cover, the bullets will be flying at you. It feels a bit unbalaced, though if you use jumping mechanics right you can avoid most of the enemy attacks.

Each campaign features an epic bossfight and is filled with breathtaking set pieces. The game feels like a very highbudget blockbuster, graphics look great and voice acting is better than in every other RE game. A lot of money went into the game, so it's understandable why the devs made it more action than survival, it was an attempt to gain new audience, while also bringing back most of the characters from previous games.

[Scoring Breakdown] (0/1  = 0pts, 2/3 = 1pt, 4/5 = 2pts)

=Graphics (5/5)

1. Appropriate - Yes
2. Readable - Yes, mostly.
3. Level of Detail - Things are slightly oversized at times for gameplay purposes, otherwise good details.
4. Effects and Shaders - Sure, a bit much at times but the whole game is a bit much.
5. Consistency - Yes, the game is consistent in graphics across the board.

=Audio (5/5)

1. Appropriate - Yes
2. Readable - Yes, mostly.
3. Quality - Voice acting was surprisingly good in this game after all I heard about it. guns had punch and blood squelched nicely.
4. Volume balance - Audio balance is really good, music got loud at times but the characters weren't talking or saying anything important.
5. Consistent - Yeah, for the most part audio was consistent.

=Gameplay (3/5)

1. Direction - The game is a series of set-pieces, but if you expect that going in, it's all pretty well paced.
2. Controls - THE CONTROLS CAN KISS MY ASS, OH MY GOD THEY ARE BAD!
3. Concepts - the mechanics and gameplay are pretty much what you would expect from a more cinematic Resident Evil 5
4. Appropriate - the gameplay fits the game pretty well, it just lacks polish.
5. Consistent - gameplay wasn't really consistent at all.

=Story (2/3)

1. Characters/Plot - Characters like Jake are kind of uninteresting, Chris and Leons campaigns have a lot of character stuff happening though, so i'll say yeah to it being interesting.
2. Backstory - Backstory is other games or is shown through flashbacks and cutscenes, they did an alright job with it.
3. Consistent - sure, why not... it wasn't inconsistent?

=World (2/3)

1. Lore - it's Resident Evil lore, I'll say yes, it fits together... others might say no.
2. Design - I wish there were a few more areas where you could find little secrets of extra ammo or skill points, some areas were nice and open and also support multiple playthroughs (different character paths)

This game is 90% quick time events and annoying invincible enemies. There's a skeleton of a story, and they really tried to do the 'multiple character arcs are happening at the same time' approach that RE2 did, but it mostly falls flat.

Enemies are mostly annoying. Leon's more traditional zombie enemies are probably the best of the campaigns, but even they have their frustrating moments. Sometimes, animations will glitch and result in dead enemies getting free hits in, causing frustrating deaths on harder difficulties. Bosses range between 'shoot the spot' and 'you can't actually kill them, you're on a timer, but we're not going to tell you so you'll waste bullets.'

The controls are annoying as hell. It's very obvious that this game is a console port. If you're not the kind of person who remaps their keys, you're going to have a bad time.

Set designs run the range of standard survival horror environments. However, many times you'll find yourself asking why, exactly, there are ancient ruins full of ancient traps powered by ancient zombies. There's no story behind it; a level designer just plopped it in there because he or she thought it would be fun. This thoughtlessness is often repeated.

The extras are the only excellent part of this game. Mercenaries mode is as fun as ever. Multiplayer was also fairly entertaining, but good luck finding anyone to play with that isn't on your friends list.

If it's on sale for 75% off, and you really just want to play resident evil, go for it. Otherwise, move on to the remastered 2, the excellent 4, or the shiny new 7.

I did not have fun playing RE6. I loved RE4 and RE5. But not this. I'll keep it simple:
1. Terrible inventory UI - took me forever to figure it out. 28hrs into the game I found out you could press H to have all herbs converted to tablets.
2. QTEs that instantly kill you unless you've memorized the game - not fun for first time plays lets be real here. Yeah you can turn it off but it should come that way since failing to press the right button combo (Space + R wth?) results in instantly dying and lowering your completion score.
3. Enemies have guns. The issue here is the game was designed for slower paced aiming. Now that enemies have guns you realize that the speed is important and you don't have that. Not only that level design also becomes a problem since having something in between you and the enemy is key to not being shot. To add to this, the cover mechanics in this game are absolute trash. You'll be aiming around a corner and instantly hug the wall, completely ruining your aim and your time. Get too close to a wall = automatically hug it. Games like Uncharted, Gears of War and Division make you press a button if you want to take cover. This game thinks you always do. Really really annoying.
4. Enemies have guns. Again. That's how bad it is. If you get shot. Your character will fall to the ground. Completely breaking any momentum you had with its 'faster' gameplay. Extremely frustrating. Especially if you were going to finish someone off with a melee attack but now you're on the floor licking the ground cuz you got shot.
5. Terrible running sequences. These should be removed entirely and never put in a game again unless it was like some time-attack mode or something. There's a bug on PC where you're doing Chris' campaign and jumping from boat to boat and right at the end you fall into the water and instantly drown. Took me 9 deaths to realize something was totally off. The only way you can actually not auto-die is if you and your AI partner are right beside each other when you do the last jump. If he's ahead of you - just kill yourself. If you're ahead of him - he'll just kill himself.
6. Enemies and their lack of response to your actions. Basically, you can unload all your ammo and have an enemy standing there with you being confused as to why he's not dead. There is no visual indication or sound indication that you're "hitting them where it hurts". For instance, the final boss in Chris' campaign, I was destroying him. Then after 15 minutes of destroying him I became concerned as to why he's not dead yet. Turns out when he's knocked down you have a brief moment to go up to him and do some melee damage. How was I supposed to know that I had to go up and kiss him? 

Honestly, game desperately needs polish. Both graphically (some textures literally look like puke) and gameplay wise. Cover shooting should be removed entirely with greater focus on FOV and better level design.

RE6 is a continuation of the downwards trend Resident Evil 5 has started for the genre (and I'm only considering canons here). A franchise built on survival and moderately-paced, tactical gameplay turned into a fast-paced, "action," third-person shooter.

Admittedly, the AI, my greatest qualms with RE5, has improved from the previous game, but it remains a reminder that the entire concept of this game is built around a lousy co-op concept. An annoying fad that has plagued gaming industry in the late 2000s ~ early 2010s. For a single player run, it is no uncommon to find yourself pressing B (or whatever you have it mapped for) to trigger a teamwork activity and just sit there, twiddling your thumbs, waiting for your "partner" to show up.

This coop idiocy continues the stupid "dying" mechanics inherited from RE5 and somehow manages to make it worse. It is not uncommon to find yourself sent to a dying state by one enemy, only to have another ready to finish you off. Some don’t need help at all. The armoured "Napads" tend to keep pushing towards a downed player, priming their AI to finish off the player a few moments after they send them to the downed state. And with their movement speed greater than the crawling speed of a downed player, escaping this fate becomes practically impossible. While one might argue that this makes sense to make it possible for a player to die, I argue that if the player often is going to die regardless, why waste their time at all? 

Of course, complaining about RE6 (and any of the second RE trilogy) isn’t complete without nagging about the widely-hated, Quick-Time Events. I keep wondering whether anyone at Capcom ever bothered going online during the development of this game. With all the ire QTE has gotten, they still implemented them to a greater degree than RE5. Not a second goes by without a zombie/J'avo jumping on your back and prompting you to circle the hell out of your joysticks to escape. Boss fights become a stress test for a gamepad's durability, and no 5 minutes can go by without reducing the expected lifespan of your X or A buttons by half.

And let's not even start about difficulties levels, with the entire concept falling down to "less ammo, stronger enemies." While this formula may have worked in the first three Resident Evils, limiting an ammo supply to a game turned purely an action, third person shooter that often puts players in a "kill all to advance" is beyond me.

But perhaps the most idiotic of all this game's shortcomings is the game flow. In their attempts to go "cinematic" RE6 employs what I like to call "camera hijacking." The player is forced to "look" at something, sometimes while movement is possible, others not. But often, often the game AI remains in action. The result? While the game is forcing you to watch that unskippable sequence where some bridge slowly lowers, two enemies have cut that 50 meters between them and the player and readied their melee jab, landing a perfect, practically unavoidable hit once the player regains control. The game devs’ desire to "force" the player to see every bloody lever being dropped and every door being opened makes this mess too frequent an occurrence.

This is true for actions' animations as well. Climbing ladders -for example-is no controllable action. Pressing A at the bottom of that ladder means committing to climbing it the entire way up. Now if one enemy was waiting on top, the -unskippable- period between the player's character getting up on the platform and regaining control is more than enough for that melee j'avo to shish kebab the bloody hell out of your -character's- gut. Scratch this as simply "badly unbalanced AI," if you want.

But at least you don't get a “Game Over” every five seconds because your AI partner developed an appetite for mutated bone-blades any more...

RE6 is a horrible game. It's annoying, frustrating and hardly ever rewarding. The short "campaigns" style leaves little space for developing gameplay and stories (mind you, stories aren't exactly what I -personally- sign up for when I fire up a Japanese game), the less-than-stellar graphics and mediocre animations leave much to be desired, and the overall flawed gameplay sprinkled with forced implementation of cliched mechanics (Ada’s campaign stealth mini-objectives *rolls eyes*) makes the whole experience an excruciating exercise in self-torture. 

Capcom may have "fixed" Resident Evil with RE7, but RE6 (and other horrible non-canons a la Operation Raccoon City) will forever remain a stain that can never be washed, a reminder that no matter how much you can expect a big game house to ruin a title, they'll somehow manage to exceed your expectations!

As a long time Resident Evil fan / lore freak, I despise RE6. Period. Its poor sob story, paired with over the top action straight out of Bollywood, reached new hights of disbelief. Even as I write this, trying to maintain a modicum of sanity, all sense of coherent thought evades me, as I hoplessly try to grasp anything real just outside the lines of reason.

Right off the bat, you'll notice the soundtrack does not fit the theme of the Resident Evil universe at all. It feels like you're listening to a 'Dark Knight Rises' soundtrack when all is quiet, and then during action sequences it borrows from Star Wars. But that's just the start.

The game doesn't let you in on the main menu when you start. They made such deep changes in the mechanic that the abysmal QTE tutorial section is mandatory before all else, and you quickly understand why. The game made such a departure from what Resident Evil was and what it stood for, in mechanics, themes and gameplay design, it became unrecognizable. It deconstructed itself, to be rebuilt into a terrifying, hideous thing. The way it destroys the established lore is amazing. It's just laughable how they created the situations we see in the "story", just to make these characters come together. 

Just pathethic. The narrative is aking to something you'd see in an 'Expandables' movie. It's just hilariosity through and through. Everybody always need to be either related or son or daughter or friend or rival of everybody else, that it makes it feel like a cheap soap opera. Yes. There would be no sequels after this. This was the Resident Evil to end all Resident Evils. An unreckonable force which brought down a primordial creator in the gaming cosmos, a franchise which defined horror gaming, and then again, decades later, redefined how we understood action gaming. It prompted Capcom to go back to the drawing board when developing RE7, and then to go on to reboot the entire series. And just like that, a recently deceased infected franchise awaits it's inevitable ressurection. Bigger. Better. Stronger. Evolved. This is arguably the only redeemable quality of Resident Evil 6.

Resident Evil 6 completely fails as a Resident Evil title. It isn’t even an enjoyable game in and of itself. Jerky unpleasant character movement, terrible aiming mechanics, tons of cheap shots by enemies, enemy actions and movements that make you go “lol, wut?”, messy story direction, and of course QTEs. It’s like Capcom took every hated game mechanic from every RE title and decided to cram it into one game and cranked up the annoyance factor to eleven.

This is a travesty of design that is only barely functional as a comedy piece when it attempts to stumble through its laughable attempt character drama. 

Some of the time it functions as a solid enough 4/10 action co-op game and I long for those glorious high points during every tedious vehicle, stealth, quicktime, railshooter, exploration or 'story'  section. Relative to Resident Evil 5 this game fails at every level of cooperative play from the ground up. No interaction in inventory, resourses, enemy control, or specialized loadouts. The inability to remove guns from your loadout combined with ammo distribution that heavily favours empty weapons means you are forced to waste inventory on ammo for weapons you are not interested in using as discarding it will starve you of ammo for weapons that are more important or enjoyable. 

The game conveys intention terribly with many enemies appearing entirely impervious but requiring combat to proceed and others telegraph effective damage taken purely to waste ammo while actually being impervious. Enemy animations are full of poorly concieved invulnerability frames while in alternate animation stats such as transitioning to new levels of mutation or as simple as while they are playing dead. 

None of this comes close to how unplayable the forced camera, sloppy sprinting controls, and multi-bound key functions render many sections of the game. The challenge is undesigned, you run around with infinite ammo and more grendes than you can possibly hold but still encounter entirely unfair sudden death frequently. The higher difficulties don't add any meaninful agency or skill expression they merely seek to waste more time.

Whoooo boy, talk about conflicting views. This game is...different from a lot of the other Resident Evil titles I've played. Somehow, it manages to remind me of the firestorm that was Operation: Raccoon City; explosions every few seconds and automatic gunfire shredding through zombies.
The gameplay as a whole feels very smooth most of the time. Granted, there are some areas that feel clunky or bizarre, but they pale in comparison to three very, very annoying segments. In the Chris/Piers and Jake/Sherry campaigns, you will encounter driving segments. While it's more prominent in the former, and it only happens in one area, it's still a significant annoyance that drove me to look up what was wrong. But I digress. The biggest problem this game has going for it gameplay-wise is that the mouse/keyboard controls are extremely awkward. So warning: you will need to use a controller to play this game effectively.
The story is what really separates it from the RES-E universe, though. The overall story is separated into four individual segments following a pair of characters with some tie to the prior titles. Each campaign is tied to the others in some way, usually intersecting multiple times throughout each playthrough. The main problem that most people (including me for some parts) have is that it feels like...well, the only example I can use is comparing the original Alien to its Cameron-directed sequel Aliens. In the earlier titles, it mostly used suspense and buildup, giving the player a sense of claustrophobia. This one is more fire and explosions; crazy-looking mutations that look like they were drawn by a seriously disturbed art student. The characters are admittedly the main turn-off though. While the dialogue in the older titles had cheesy voice-acting, it still conveyed the story. In this game, it still tries to convey the story but usually relies on character-stereotypes and one-liners for filler. For example, Leon mostly says one-liners and variations of "you're gonna give me answers." While at the same time, his partner Helena, who didn't exist before this title, has dialogue stating revenge or "I'll give you answers when we get here; you won't believe me otherwise." Overall, the story has an interesting premise and poor execution.
In short, I can give this game a flat 7.5. It's got some charm to it, and doesn't lack in the zombie-killing, head-crushing action. It just doesn't have what made the old games what they are. Thankfully 7 rectified that.

Half bat s h i t, half brilliant, Resident Evil 6 is a game that tries to do everything and be everything to everyone. It attempts an old school horror experience for RE veterans (well, at least Leon's campaign tries that for a bit), it amps up the "military guys versus zombies" vibe of RE5 on acid, it has weird forced shipping between the little girl from RE2 who's grown up and hot now and Wesker's son, who is an annoying emo boy, and it even has the best video game interpretation of a city based on Hong Kong that I've ever seen.

It doesn't succeed on all of these ambitions, and is frankly kind of a mess at times, which is why it got mixed reviews upon release and split the fanbase. But by jove, it sure does TRY, and its sheer ambition to be the best game for everyone is hard to not appreciate at times. Give it a go if you've played other titles in the series. 

Quick campaign breakdown for your convenience: 
Leon: Starts out in a remixed Racoon City that is cool. Ends with Leon running through China as everything blows up and a zombie T-Rex chases him. Pulpy as heck, I dug it.
Chris: Military PTSD dude re-learns how to be a soldier again thanks to sidekick. Probably has the best storytelling Resident Evil has ever seen. Most people think this campaign is the best.
Jake: A weird experimental mess with bad stealth segments that try to make you feel like how Nemesis made ya feel in RE3 but fail. Play as Sherry instead since she's a cutie pie.
Ada: Awful and an example of why Ada Wong has almost no personality aside from being a hot spy that Leon has Yellow Fever for.

While the game has problems (and a lot of those problems are obnoxious,) the game still manages to remain fun even after 400+ hours of playing the damn thing. 
Is the story good? No. It has it character moments that are well done and interesting, but outside of that there is nothing worth noting.
Are the controls good? Yes, actually. Movement is a lot more fluid than previous games and this shines in higher difficulties when the need to use such movement (rolling, dodging, etc) comes into play.
That brings me onto my main point: the combat. The combat in this game is actually really fun and it's the main reason I still play the game. There are so many different ways to dispatch enemies, from environment kills, to finishing the enemy off with that particular character's finishing move (Coup De Grace.) Virtually every enemy in the game can be countered by pressing a button at the precise moment. It's a small QTE in a way, but it doesn't FEEL like it. It's extremely satisfying to pull these off and rewards the player in different ways.
I get why the game wasn't received well.  It's about as far from Resident Evil as you can get, but the developers stiill managed to make a somewhat decent action game.

Resident Evil 6 is another game in Third Person Shooter Action series that started with Resident Evil 4. And pretty much the last, aside from Revelations 2. And yep, this one is designed for Coop fun. And yep, it got hated by a lot of people on release, it seems. But hey, it's Capcom's own fault for calling it as "ultimate horror experience" in interviews.
Another funny thing is that I remember reading, back when I actually read game magazine, that they were actually moving the release date forward, saying that they can't wait to make fans happy. Heh, most devs prefer to delay instead.

And well, I don't feel like writing out the mechanics of third person shooter once again. Only say that it threw away "limitations as design" of RE4 and RE5, as you can move freely while shooting now. Kinda like in Revelations, yes. But you can also melee anytime, effectively, I must say. I don't think that you can stun enemy by shooting at their legs anymore but  I think that you can do a stronger stun if you shoot while they are stunned? Or hit them with something, like sliding. To allow you to do fatal special melee. And you can do stealth instakill melee if you sneak up on them in rare moments when they don't spawn into map already aware of you.
And this time around there is an universal cover system. Mostly used for non-Leon campaign. He has to deal with zombies while others have to deal with mutating gun-wielding enemies the most. Combined with ability to slide, which you do by aiming while running. Or pressing run while aiming and holding a direction key.

And yea, there are few campaigns that open up after you are done with Prelude, which also gives you a bad impression due to being so linear and forced with QTEs. Main game is linear and has a lot of QTEs too but not to the point of allowing you to move only in one line in a big room. I recommend you to start with Leon, then do Chris and Jake, that's how I feel it goes in complexity of gameplay. Preferably do it with friend in coop. But leave the Ada for the last. When game was originally released, her campaign was unlocked only after beating others first. Furthermore, it was designed as solo at first, before some updated added a really crippled coop support. The coop partner can't even open doors! So do it last and solo.

I also am a bit disappointed with how they handled the inventory, especially in coop. There is no shop system, albeit maybe it exists on their residentevil website. You can't share inventory items with coop partner anymore. Albeit at least healing yourself nearby your partner heals them too, a bit less. Your inventory is bigger as well. And each person gets their own copy of the item in the world from the viewpoint, similar to Serious Sam games. I guess it was all done to make online multiplayer to be less painful with complete strangers, make it less griefable. Less fun with a friend than in RE5 however. I also felt that I would almost never run out of ammo.

Oh, and the game is even more like action than ever before. Funnily enough, the interaction and plot is more down to earth than RE4 and RE5 however, pretty much no one is doing Matrix BS around here. The plot is interconnected with each campaign. Too bad that you can feel that some chapters, such as the last one for Ada, were made to fit into other campaigns, not being able to stand on their own. And even worse, the amount of QTE is a bit too much. There are some QTEs that were too hard for gamepad that I hated. And they happen too often and too suddenly. I will let you know, majority of our deaths in our games with friend came not from enemies during core gameplay but due to sudden QTE or by introducing us to a new situation without letting us get ready. Such as running and sliding toward camera or suddenly getting to drive a car. I don't hate on occasional or expected or forgiving QTEs, but this one goes a dat overboard. Gameplay feels more scripted as well.

Otherwise, if it's your first walkthrough, the game's great variety and action-explosive pacing is pretty fun, it really is. As an action game by itself, it's underrated. It still delivers on the interesting combat system with enemies feedback toward your hits. It even looks great, with a lot of colors and darkness. I like this art style. Sadly, most of the music was forgettable movie-epic stuff. And hmmm, still disappointed that there were no files in-game to read. Once again, to make it more pleasant to play with random strangers online? Instead you shoot at emblems to unlock files in game's menu.

Also, online community for non-campaign modes is dead and thus DLCs are not worth it.

PS: Having a friend for coop is required to have fun, don't bother much with solo.

I had never played any resident evil game before, this game made me a big fan of the series. 

I'm talking as purely an online co-op experience though, I found it a load of fun:
-Nice but not over the top graphics.
-Excellent Michael Bay style cinematics throughout and the character interaction is even enjoyable and funny at times (whaat?).
- 4 very varied campaigns all of decent length? Hardly any game has that, just fantastic idea. Only Ada's was slightly disappointing due to her limited partner, the rest were excellent. How their stories all interlink is wonderfully unique, you're watching a cutscene and think "I remember doing that when playing as ____!".
- Lots of varied action scenes on motorbikes, cars, helicopters etc, and co-op is implemented perfectly with always one driving and the other usually shooting.
- Some puzzles which can be challenging, even if many of us would've preferred more.
- Extremely easy to connect to partners at different sub-chapters throughout each campaign, and can change difficulty at any time.
- Skills system wasn't great but it was a fairly interesting idea.

I've later gone on to play RE Remaster, and currently playing RE5 with a friend. I am disappointed how vastly inferior RE5 is compared to this, I expected something of a similar level and it is not even in the same league. Think its partly due to my high expectations after playing RE6, makes you realise that making 4 campaigns all well is very rare in a game. Play RE6 over RE5, no question.

I don't know how to describe RE6. It's almost impossible to review it. It's fitting, in a sense, because I struggled to play through it, even though I had a friend playing with me over the internet. In fact, were it not for our couch critic approach and the chance to laugh our way through it together, I would have never, ever finished this game.

Before I delve into the awful things about RE6 - and there's no shortage of those - I feel like I should say what's good about it: the monster design. It's really, really good. Also the PC port had very little technical issues - free framerate, good mouse aiming, all that jazz.

There, that's taken care of. Let's get on with this so I can finally forget about this game.

RE6 boasts four different campaigns: Leon, Chris, Jake and Ada all get their time in the spotlight. In every campaign, you have a coop buddy who ties in with the plot. Well, aside from Ada but we'll get there. Each campaign is supposedly different from one another, but ultimately it's just a zombie killfest with chase sequences every time. 

What IS different about them is the UI. For whatever reason Capcom decided that every campaign should look and feel different. Nice idea, but if I want to change my settings mid-game, I don't want to relearn my way through the menu. Now, this is just pet peeve, but on top of every other misstep, it's truly a cherry on top.

The most ridiculous thing about RE6 is the plot and dialogue, hands down. They've taken all their cues from the "Hollywood Action Films 101" handbook and it's unbearable to witness. Grumpy special ops staredowns, explosions from things that shouldn't explode, grabbing ledges with one hand, more explosions, more staredowns. I'm no stranger to Hollywood action and I can enjoy it if it's well done, but RE6 overdid it so blatantly it's embarassing to watch.

While writing this, I had to check Wikipedia, where it says, and I quote: "Critics praised the storyline." This is truly astonishing. To think that there is actually a person who has played this game, analyzed the plot and concluded that it's praiseworthy, and to think that there are SEVERAL people like that. I can (and do) enjoy tacky films with silly plots; I don't want everything to read as Dostojevski; and I most certainly didn't expect a pinnacle of storytelling when playing a Resident Evil game, but goodness gracious RE6 was all over the place. I repeat: who played this and thought: this storyline was GOOD? I reckon a single cell organism might find the story serviceable but anything beyond that is a stretch.

The pacing is all over the place. The first moment you're walking down a street taking down J'ava or whatever, the next there's an attack helicopter which prompts a quip or a one-liner from one of the characters. Oh, now we're in the sewers hunting down skull pieces of a CEO's family to gain access to a tomb and... well, you get the picture. It's a standard RE fare to hunt down emblems and rings and crests, but in RE6 they feel out of place and stick out like an army of sore thumbs.

The characters seldom have anything meaningful to say. Running and gunning makes it difficult to follow whatever the characters are talking about. I would love to go into detail, but I honestly can't remember a single thing anyone said - even if some of the scenes are repeated several times in different campaigns!

Repetition was a huge turnoff. Having to play the same levels twice would've lended itself nicely for diverse storytelling and gameplay, but most of the time you literally did the same thing you already did. This was most notable in the section in Edonia where you take down some ginormous BOW. It's literally the same thing in both Chris's and Jake's campaign. That's just lazy.

The chase sequences killed me more than anything else in the game, thanks to the clunky controls and the camera panning every which way. I've read that it's easy on a controller, but with a keyboard and mouse my character would abruptly stop dead in his tracks, turn around, bump into an invisible wall, and ultimately die because the invisible timer ran out, or my partner got too far ahead of me. It felt almost arbitrary what killed us in those sections.

Every character in the game is made of Adamantium grade plot armor, to the point where they can withstand an RPG to the face. I'm sorry, but there's only so much stupid I can take.

The gameplay was.... ok. Aiming and shooting is fine, but everything else feels like it was designed by Martians. Trying to manage the items is unintuitive, overcomplicated and frustrating and the simple task of deleting an item requires going through several motions. Even in earlier RE games where you paused to enter your inventory it wasn't this complicated. A personal pet peeve with the controls was how they were mapped originally. I can't for the life of me understand why 1 uses a health item, 2 and 3 are dodge moves, F and G scroll through weapons and items respectively. 3rd person shooters have existed for a long time and some things have been set in stone. RE6 decided to do everything its own way and it failed.

Luckily, playing with a friend was still (mostly) fun, because you can just laugh at all the stupidity. But at the same time we had to call it quits several times simply because we couldn't take it anymore. 

There are so many things I could talk about but I would go on forever and I don't feel this game deserves it. I want to end on a light note, though, so let's talk about Ada's campaign real quick.

For whatever reason, despite the fact that every other campaign had two characters that tied into the plot, Ada is coupled with "Agent." This nameless goon will not show up in any FMV's, nor does he have any dialogue. He will magically teleport right next to you if you grapple hook somewhere or go through a door. Agent cannot interact with ANYTHING; he cannot open doors or do QTE's, open briefcases or solve puzzles. My friend actually entertained the thought he might be just Ada's imaginary friend. That would've made sense, because otherwise Ada is constantly talking to herself. But no, he's there as a placeholder character for coop, because I suppose Capcom realized at the last moment that suddenly switching into single player only is a very dumb move. So they had to have SOMEONE there.

Having Agent along for the ride however is a surefire recipe for hilarious scenes. If Ada goes through a door and closes it behind her, you can see Agent standing still with his emotionless gas-mask face as the door closes in front of him... only to magically teleport next to you when the scene is done. Very late into the game there is an elevator of sorts you have to ride on. You summon it to where you are, and sure enough, Agent is already there, with his blank stare. He appears everywhere like a ghost, even if you leave him behind. There's no getting rid of Agent, he'll appear in the chopper cockpit after an FMV and no doors or obstacles will ever hold him down. He'll be there when you go to sleep and he'll be there when you wake up. If you go on vacation and book a hotel, he'll be waiting for you there. Forget about showering alone or getting some me-time. Agent is always present with his gun and his gas-mask. And you never even learn his name. Nice.

I cannot with a good conscience recommend RE6 to anyone who wants to have an enjoyable gaming experience, a good story or memorable characters. If you absolutely have to, play it with a friend, get inebriated and do your best to ignore all the nonsense. That's the only way to enjoy this sub-standard snoozefest.

Resident Evil 6 is probably the least favorite Resident Evil among fans, for it abandoned all the iconic Resident Evil designs and embraced over-the-top blockbuster action to be an action (not horror) third-person shooter. But to me, Resident Evil 6 always has a spot in my heart for being my first Resident Evil game. To be fair, it is not regarded as a good Resident Evil, but still is a very decent third-person shooter. So far I’ve done five playthroughs (not all on Steam), two of which are done cooperatively with friends. Co-op is way more fun than playing solo. That said, solo is not bad either. It is harder, but AI is decent and would not drag you down like in Operation Raccoon City or some sessions in Resident Evil 5.

The story took a very dramatic tone to accommodate the action, which some fans dislike. The protagonists do not die no matter it is an explosion or a high falling, even people around all die or turn into zombies. These dramatic scenes are probably just slightly better than Chris “Boulder Puncher” Redfield in Resident Evil 5. I think they are too much, but I won’t bother myself picking out all the dramatic yet unreasonable stuff. Just enjoy it for what it is, it is a little cliché but still very entertaining. On the other hand, character building is pretty good though. In my regard, Ada Wong is probably the best of all, with her unspoken affection for Leon. Sherry is my second favorite with her cute voice and clumsiness as a rookie agent. Characters in this game have certain personalities and some very good moments.

As for the storytelling, this game has four storylines going on at the same time, given the event in the game is on a global scale. This approach is very unique among video games and a brave trial in the narrative. I appreciate it for being able to present a full picture of a biological terror event, from the start to the climax and to the end. On the flip side, you will experience some scenarios twice when you play different roles. Capcom tried to minimize the repetition in these scenarios by offering different viewpoints for different characters, yet I still find it somewhat redundant and uninteresting because on the gameplay side you just do the same thing again. Four storylines also have certain different play styles. Leon’s questline has more of a traditional Resident Evil vibe, Chris’s and Jade’s are full-on gun-blazing and very action-packed, while Ada’s questline has some stealth elements and puzzle-solving. It is very dynamic, to say the least, but unfortunately, none of them nail the horror apartment.

The presentation itself is not bad. Surely it is a 2013 game so it doesn’t have good textures, lighting and other visual stuff like today’s game, it is still very decent. Character models are eye candy, not only better than counterparts at that time but also many games later on. I also like its music and I still listen to some of them from time to time.

The gameplay of Resident Evil consists of shooting, action, QTE and some light puzzles. There is no inventory management or any complex map design from the classical Resident Evil. Shooting is much faster-paced than previous games, it feels good, accurate and responsive. To compensate for the fast pacing, the game introduced a fairly complex dodge mechanic, which is quite in-depth for a shooter and very useful if you can master it. Puzzle session is too few to talk about and as for QTE and action, they are not a hurdle but I hold negative opinion towards these two. 

QTE is a popular game design at that period and I hate it because it is a very lazy design trying to engage players in the current event. This game has too many, to the point it kind of exhausts you out. As for the action, this game has quite some escape sessions which themselves are not the problem. The problem is this game has a very stiff keyboard and mouse control for movement because it was transplanted from the console, and the fixed camera angle during escape made the matter worse. I remember back in 2013 when I first played the game, in the last chapter of Chris where he has to flee from the giant monster, I could not make the escape no matter how many times I tried, not until I bought an Xbox controller just for this session. Also in other escape scenes and even normal sessions, you can feel the stiffness and unresponsiveness of movement from the poor keyboard and mouse control. It can be frustrating from time to time.

To sum it up, I don’t think Resident Evil 6 is a bad game. It surely has its problem and is not a Resident Evil that fans hope for. But if you just treat it as a normal third-person shooter, you can still have some good experience.

I haven't managed to beat the second level yet. Not for difficulties sake, but through sheer annoyance at the miserable experience. 

Since the beginning, Resident Evil has been about spacing. Knowing where the enemy is, and maintaining distance through round about traversal and kiting techniques. This quintessential part was a major similarity between the original fixed camera games and the post-4 over the shoulder ones. This requires three things. 

A) Characters who control crisply.
B) Good level design.
C) Enemies having specific spawns or having a bit of warning before becoming active.

This game fails on all three. 
Capcom decided to give the characters a sort of inertia. No more spinning in place allowed. It feels awful. Not only does this break the most important part of video games - how the player controls and interfaces with the game which allows for immersion and enjoyment - this fundamentally does not work with how the series is supposed to play. It also makes the highly contextual melee mechanics nearly uncontrollable. 
The levels are messy and convoluted.
Enemies spawning in directly next to you, fully ready to attack. The zombies are colluding with LIGHTNING.

A love of stealing control. NEVER. TAKE. CONTROL. FROM. THE. PLAYER. Forced walking segments aren't "cinematic", which isn't even inherently positive. They're annoying and break up the game. If there is tension the player will slow down by themselves. That's the mark of a well put together game. If camera controls must be stolen for a pan, do a hard cut to a pan like the other RE games do. Don't stay in game-play so when I'm getting attacked it twists my head away from the zombie about to bite my face off just to tell me a stupid door has opened.

The knife has been a fundamental tool since RE2. It really sucks. I don't know why non-knife melee was implemented. It just confuses the game and makes the knife take a slot in the already cumbersome inventory. Melee also has a much shorter reach than it would seem, meaning a lot of stupid damage because Leon is unwilling to do anymore than a light 2 inch sweep with his 3+ foot legs. 

I didn't think quick time events could get worse, but RE6 has shown me. Now there are delayed quick time events that you have to wait until the right moment to press! Yes, and entire form of game play based on twitch reflexes now requires you to wait. They also have you do them for the most mundane things in this game. RE4 and RE5 had a few scattered around, but this game is inundated with them. It almost feels like a Quantic Dream game. That isn't a good thing.

The aiming is off. I don't know what it is, but coming from the previous games, I can feel something wrong. It may be how the character model is aiming. Instead of shooting straight, it always feels like the character is aiming slightly down.

The enemies have almost no hit response, even from the shotgun. All the guns feel so lacking in oomph. Going form the glorious feeling gun-play from the other games to this is baffling, since this game has more shooting than the rest combined! Gone are the days when a single bullet would stop a dog or cause a zombie to flinch. You will eat that hit.

At least the straight-edge, 80's - 90's camp is still kind of there. That's the charm that makes Resident Evil.

If you want an over the shoulder RE. seriously go play 4 again. Or 5. Or Revelations. Even Revelations 2.

My main problems with this game are the incoherent game design, the repetitive gameplay and the fixed (and very bad) camera during a lot of action sequences.

For example, a certain button is pressed for a certain type of action (i.e. opening a door) but half the time another button will have to be pressed instead. Or a certain height of objects can be jumped over, but half the time an object of exact same height cannot be jumped over. Or you should be able to add an Herb to your quick-button "Case", but you can't despite available room. These are a very few examples, but those kind of things happen ALL the time. Add to this the very poor controls of vehicle sections, and it's obvious game design was, at the very best, rushed without consideration. 

Repetitive gameplay is self-explanatory, and the camera has a very frustrating tendency to auto-lock on "important" things in the worst possible way, forcing you to avoid enemies you can't look at, or move to an interactive point without the ability to actually see the path you're walking. "Resident Evil 6" is a 3rd person, over-the-shoulder, adventure zombie shooter. The graphics are generally good and the sound is built beautifully. It's also very very long (almost 50 hours played and I'm still not sure if the thing is going to end...). Overall, I like this game a lot.

RE 6 feels exactly like a Resident Evil game in that we can play multiple characters through a variety of maps, skill upgrades are funded by collectable artifacts, boss battles are fun yet long winded, the movement system is consistently inconsistent (by now I have to wonder whether Capcom thinks poor movement makes things scarier?), and the story follows a convoluted plot about human experiments that spawn zombies. What makes it feel unlike most Resident Evil games, is the satisfying Fun of it all.

This is the most complete of the Resident Evil games, without daring to reinvent anything at all. Not quite as swift and addictive to play through as RE 5, but definitely a well built and functional adventure.

Does Resident Evil 6 have an annoying amount of flash at times? Yes, it does. And does the game not let you quit because re-starting will load a Chapter rather than a Checkpoint? Why, yes it does. But the flash can be turned off honestly and replaying chunks isn't a problem, because this action adventure's primary gameplay is so creepy, sleek, fast-paced, and thrilling that we forgive the sins. The puzzles throughout are clear and engaging, battles in general are a blast, and the skill tree can actually change things specifically for your unique gaming style. Even though the game maybe overstays its welcome because it's so darn long, I would be ashamed to complain about getting more for your buck in this day and age.

Resident Evil 6 HAD to happen in order for series to be actually good again. I don't hate it necessarily and I do have some fun playing it, but it is so far removed from anything I played RE for, it could easily be called a different name entirely.

And yes, while the game is not "scary", there is plenty of horror in this game... story/theme/general goal of the game is to tell a horror story... but it also wants to offer an action adventure, and a war story... all at once. Can you see the problem? So you play through a campaign of your choosing, let's say Jake, and it goes like this...

You start on a battlefield, lots of enemies, explosions, cool macho posturing. After 15 minutes you end up in a horror scenario locked in a warehouse with an invincible monster, then you go through a creepy blink-and-you-miss-it manequin factory, then there is a layered battle sequence against a giant angry monster, then you are shooting down helicopters and incoming rackets. END Chapter 1.

EVERY chapter does this. Every 10-15 minutes you get thrown into a different style of gameplay and the game wants you to feel something different. But NONE of it works, because everything is so over-producer and over-eager to please everyone. Nothing sticks with you. This is a horror story of epic proportions as told by Michael Bay. Lots of explosions and cleavages, lots of macho posturing, lots of slow motion and "epic" setpieces.

Gameplay:
The big issue.
There are 4 campaigsn in total the gunplay is alright no problems there.
But you almost alwyas have similar or the same weapons throughout all campaigns and the gameplay loop is the same. (only the one of Ada changes) which makes it kinda stale.

Resident Evil 6
To like or not to like? To recommend or send to hell for inifnite damnation? That I am unsure of. (this will be quite long.) 
This game recieved quite a mixed reception upon its release, both from the fans of the franchise and the general critics.
At its core, this is an action game with brilliant gunplay mechanics through and through. 
Survival? Wh... Horror? Just no. 

Let's talk about the good first. This game actually did address a lot of the complaints and issues that people had with the 5th game. 

[Tanky controls?]
Gone, fully replaced with free camera, movement, ability to sprint, slide, vault, jump over gaps (still contextual doe.), move & shoot, move & reload, directional dodges and more.
The combat itself has also recieved a nice overhaul compared to the previous games. You can open up enemies to melee takedowns by initiating a 2 hit combo to stun them. The damage dealt can also be doubled if you perform a slide into the enemy while he's stunned (called Coupe de Grace). You can also counter almost any melee attack that enemy throws at you, some of them result in you stealing their weapons and killing an extra zombie around you with it. Neat. 

[Tiny 3x3 inventory box?]
 Well.. too bad. Now it's a wheel. However.. you are no longer limited to the amount of weapons you can carry, so everything you snatch during the campaign can be carried throughout the whole game. However, the space in this stupid wheel feels just as, if not even less spacey like it was in RE5. You're still gonna be throwing out other items in exchange for more space for those herbs. (Speaking of herbs, bye bye cuz now they're pills for some reason. The glorious 1st aid spray stays though.) It takes a while to get used to it. But in a way, it's actually much faster to navigate and swap to necessary items. The case from RE4 was still the most flexible one. Shame it didn't make a return.

[Sheva! Come on! Come on!]
Might have been an issue for some. Not for me though. (Playing with a friend online or split screen is highly recommended.) But! If you wanted to breeze through the campaign solo and never liked the idea of having an AI with you all the time that wastes bullets and keeps taking hits from those bosses, this game kinda solved it in the most easiest way possible. Your partner now has an unlimited ammo, unlimited health, pretty good reactions to incoming attacks so it usually avoids most with dodges. Aaand.. doesn't really get in the way. 

Now to some generic info. The story is bananas. Bio-weapon terrorist attack happens again. Zombies everywhere, new type of virus. Leon! Chris! Sherry, Piers, Helena, Jake! (Wait, who are those 4?) Right. You get to play 3 different cam.-- 4 actually. (Recommend playing that one as a last since it's the most frustrating one and probably the most boring too.) 
Four playable campaigns with a decent lenght, all overlapping at certain points so you get to see some events take place from a different perspective. Overall, I'd say that this was executed pretty well. It'll make the story a lot more enjoyable once you see the full picture. 8 different characters with unique set of combat animations and weapon sets. 
Beautifully directed cutscenes (on every corner though. But at least, the QTEs are not in them, only during the actual gameplay.) Varied locations. (Japan, Murica, and uhhh.. I think I'll classify the rest as Eastern Europe.) Plenty of famously grotesque BOW (mutated) boss designs. And... actually, a varied gameplay. Which is a double edged sword for me, so now I'm gonna talk about the bad. 

THE  B A D.
And there's quite a lot of it. 
Let me start by saying that this game, to me at least does seem to suffer from an identity issue. 
Resident Evil 6 came at a time where the market was being oversaturated with mainly FPS titles. 
It seems to me like CAPCOM tried to compromise when developing this one and tried to make it both an action game and a horror game. And I will say that it didn't work for me. 
The survival aspect of the game is very minimal, most of the horror atmosphere that they try to create in Leon's campaign feels really cheap. Decent amount of predictable jumpscares, the game is overly dark even in places where it shouldn't be. 
It's filled with a lot of unnecessary walking sequences where the game just locks you into walking and taking the camera out of your control to either focus on something ''really'' cool or just switches into a fixed positon during the worst moments. (So much for that old school Resi throwback CAPCOM.)
The default camera FOV and positioning is also pretty bad. Luckily, you can change that in the settings, so I'd recommend doing that. 
CAPCOM also thought that it would be a brilliant idea to include a lot of driving and piloting sections. Now, that wouldn't be bad.. if they weren't, well you know. Bad. And they are. 
Chase sequences are also overused a bit too much and that constantly shifting camera perspective does not help the experience at all.
Did you like the QTEs in previous games? No? Heh. Well, this game has like twice as much of them. You can turn on some auto-QTE option on if you want. Not sure how that even works. I guess it does most of them for you. But either way. Be prepared for a lot of WSAD, Space, R and LMB/RMB mashing. 
The ability to share items with your partner while in-game is gone. Fully upgradable weapons feature was also removed, got instead replaced with the Skill system. 
(The weapon upgrading was far more in-depth, They don't even show you the stats on those Skills that you buy.) 
This means that there is no money currency either, so no treasures to find & sell and the ability to store items that you bought or found in the menu is also gone. 
Lastly, when playing online, you and your partner both have independant item drops.

[Just to end this thing]
Overall. This game is actually a pretty decent RE sequel. It has plenty of references and returning characters from the previous games. The cutscenes do set up (if not interesting or the most elaborate) then at least an entertaining plot. 
It features quite a lot of derpy silly, over the top moments and the campaign is pretty long. 
HOWEVER. That would not make me spend any more time in the game than I did, if it wasn't for one thing and one thing only.
The additonal content, The Mercenaries.
This game mode, to me is probably the most fun I had in the game. If you're a fan of those classic arcade  score elimination 
games where you try to rack up as many points by being the most stylish with all the gameplay mechanics that you use, then you won't be disappointed with this one. It's true that the previous games had this mode as well. But ask pretty much any Merc player out there and you'll know that RE6 did it the best. 
To me, Mercenaries is probably the only place where you can drop the chains and go full rambo with all the abilities the game gives you to learn and master without any scripted QTEs/cutscenes/walking segments interrupting your flow. 
And once you do learn most of the mechanics (and there's a lot more to the combat than you might think at first), then this game becomes arguably one of the most satisfying third person action zombie games that money can buy.

TL;DR: A fantastically-paced coop shooter with a silly and funny storyline, 4 interesting campaigns, great coop mechanics, very varied levels and interesting, if somewhat easy, puzzles. A fantastic game to play alone, and an absolute blast in coop. Which makes me all the more sad that Capcom decided to can this type of Resident Evil games instead of branching it out to a separate series.

The best thing about Resident Evil 5 and 6 is just how different and interesting the levels are and how well-paced everything is. You never feel bored, the game never outstays it's welcome. Every new level introduces new mechanics, new enemies, new interesting way to play, and even the silly storyline and dialogue plays an important role - since this is a coop game, it would be difficult to enjoy a good and nuanced story here. So what did the devs do? They made it so instead of telling your friend to be quite during a cutscene you will both laugh at the cutscene! And because the storyline is not intrusive it's cutscenes serve as good transitions between sections, preparing the player for the next level and it's set of mechanics. Also dialogues are surprisingly well-acted, considering the nonsense they are saying.

Combat is also great - it is fairly slow, and there can be difficulty spikes at times, but nevertheless, it keeps you on your toes with constant variety of threats and different situations, which change more often than you can adapt to be able to handle them with ease (normal difficulty is still very easy though). There are upgrades which do make a difference, and infinite ammo ones unlocked in NG+ add replay value. Four campaigns feature 7 different characters(last one was not intended for coop, I recommend to play it solo), all of them have some differences in gameplay (some are faster, some have higher mellee damage, some have less recoil, etc.) which, again contrubutes to this game's incredible variety. Not to mention that they occasionally have diverging paths , which adds to replayability.

Tradeoff for all that? Linearity. This game is entriely linear in every way. There is only ever one way to achieve a goal. But honestly with such a great variety, coop mechanics, funny plot and overall top quality 20 hours of entertainment, I will take that tradeoff any day! On top of that, the game only ever crashed once, and that was because I was alt-tabbing heavily. We  recently revisited this with a friend of mine to swap characters and play NG+ and once again I enjoyed myself a lot here. Just like in Resident Evil 5.

Resident Evil 6 takes a strange change of pace compared to the other entries in the series. A pace where enemies and gear is just thrown in your face, a linear pace where exploring isn't important anymore and the game is on rails. To put it bluntly, this game is downright boring. Aside from the occasional fun segments that are far and few between, I just keep asking myself when it will be over. The chapters just drag on and on, with far too much combat and almost no puzzles throughout the game.  Although Capcom gave us some of the things us fans have been asking for, such as being able to move and shoot, they also took away many of the things we loved. Where is the horror, the sense of urgency or hopelessness that became so profound in the earlier titles? And why do so many zombies have guns now? If you didn't like how action-centric RE5 was, you will absolutely hate this game. It went from survival horror to action shooter- and not even a good shooter for that matter, but at least your team-mate is a little more useful this time around. The story offers more questions than answers and is recycles at times in the other character campaigns. In fact, the story can be extremely frustrating as far as the decisions made. In short, if you want that classic Resident Evil vibe, go back and replay RE4. If you want a little more action and good story, go play RE5. If you want downright horror that takes you back to the good old days, play the newest entry. If you want a solid third-person shooter, I can think of several games that do it better than this one. Out of all the negative this game has to offer, I did really like the setting. Now cross this one off your list.
