TL;DR: This is a fun, cheesy co-op shooter, not a horror game. Make sure to play on No Hope with a co-op partner.

Mandatory disclaimer: This is not Resident Evil 1, 2 nor 3. I'm OK with that, since I dont like broken controls, broken camera & broken puzzles. The love the original 3 get is 90% because of nostalgia, the remaining 10% is the love for the cheese those games had.

I've played through this entire game on No Hope difficulty with a co-op partner, that is the only correct way to play this game, as it's far too easy otherwise & the AI partner is brain-dead. Just remember to spam dodge buttons after cutscenes, lest you get insta-gibbed.

RE6/BH6 is fun, over the top action with a fair bit of cheese & interesting scenarios, but it's far from a horror game. This game is about the story, the characters & the action, which I feel it mostly delivers on, although you need to finish all 4 campaigns to get the full picture.

Pros: (assumes you're playing on No Hope, the only difficulty option)
+ Ammo presevation is important, if you miss more than 1 shot per 5 enemies you'll run out of ammo, as you should.
+ A single regular enemy is a genuine threat if not taken seriously.
+ You die in 1-3 hits.
+ You want to stealth & avoid battles whenever available. (not because combat is bad, but because it's costly)
+ It contains cheese & interesting scenarios.
+ Decent weapon variety.
+ Good enemy variety.
+ Severely punishes incompitent behaviour.
+ Approximately 30 hours of content split in 4 campaigns.

Cons: (also assumes you're playing on No Hope, the only difficulty option)
- You must hold the dodge keys to dodge, they're not instant, causing a delay & lowering the skill-cieling.
- Enemies can shoot through eachother in order to hit you, so sometimes enemies you can't even see shoot you.
- It contains quick time events.
- Sometimes difficult to get co-op to run properly.
- No item trading with co-op partner.
- Getting insta-gibbed/grappled to death right after cutscenes.
- You stagger like crazy every single time you're hit or you triggered a trigger.
- Contains bad driving segments.
- The worst aiming-style is on by default, you must change to laser-only yourself.
- Some shared events from different campaigns (due to characters bumping into eachother).

Others:
+/- Easy but fun bosses.
+/- Graphics & audio are acceptable.
+/- There are 2 states between healthy & dead, one making you slower & melee useless & another one where you crawl.
+/- Pointless passive skills system. (It's not in effect in No Hope, the only difficulty option.)
+/- There are invisible (for you) duplicates of all items in the game, so both co-op partners get everything.
+/- When in-game most menus are in the style of a phone, a poorly designed phone. It's immersive, but bad.

This game doesn't play like other third person shooters, and even less like previous Resident Evil games. Instead, it's one of the most rewarding action games out there.

There's a reason why Mercenaries is unlocked from the start, because it's the best way to experience the huge variety of enemies and weapons. Make sure you practice parrying, because nearly every attack in the game can be countered. It's a fantastic risk/reward mechanic, since you're punished for doing it too early or too late, but when done right is the best way to take out most enemies, especially the bloodshots (skinless zombies).

Even though Vanquish is still my favourite third-person shooter, Resident Evil 6 fixes my two problems with that game, which are the harsh punishment for using melee moves and the lack of extra content. 

Co-op is also implemented really well, but when playing in single-player your partner is never the burden they were in RE6. They have infinite ammo and health, and you don't have to worry about their inventory either. You're capable of holding plenty of weapons and ammo, so there's no need to use your partner to hold all the stuff you aren't using.

I tried....I tried so hard to like this game but I just can't. There is just nothing resident evil about it, be it the controls, the atmosphere or every feckin time you have to hit E or V or R to conduct some way over the top move. It's just too much and played more like something you would see in a Hollywood action movie. 

If that's your thing, go for it, but I was born and raised on Resident Evil 1 on the Playstation 1, and I have kept with the games ever since despite the clear decline in standard. 

Some people will love this game. I hated it.

So, there are people who will tell you this game is unadulterated trash, and there are people who will tell you this is a great game misunderstood by those who played it on release.

As someone who is looking at this review while the game is on sale, you're likely asking yourself:

Which of these two takes should you believe?

I'm here to tell you: both.

The game looks great and terrible all at once. Character models, animations, sounds, and so on are all superb. Certain shadows looks great and crisp, while certain shadows and many textures and environment models, I would say, look like they were taken straight out of a Gamecube title.

Combat is great and terrible all at once- you're given a good assortment of weapons, and an incredible amount of options for attacking, stunning, and killing your foes, either with conventional weapons or with melee options. The problem is that a lot of the actions you perform are contextual, so the game sometimes guesses incorrectly about the exact foe you wished to target. This isn't usually a problem, but it will occur often enough that you will notice it.

The campaign is a confused mess, mostly because there isn't just one full length campaign, but four. 

Yes, you read that right: there are FOUR campaigns. Without spoiling too much for you, sometimes the game just works, and sometimes it just doesn't. Sometimes, the mechanics seem at odds with the narrative the game is trying to present, and sometimes, the narrative clashes with the gameplay. There is a perk system for singleplayer, where you choose three perks out of many to give you buffs. The problem is, a lot of these perks offer advantages that are too meager to really bother with, so your best bet is to pick perks with obvious and explicitly defined benefits, such as infinite ammo, stamina upgrades, etc. You buy them with Skill Points, which for all intents and purposes are just Pesetas/Gold renamed from RE 4/5 respectively, and this stuff is scarce. Like, you'll have enough for maybe a few decent perks, but only after you've completed FOUR. CAMPAIGNS. 

The Mercenaries mode is honestly the best part of the game, because it's where the game's combat is allowed to shine most without dumb cinematics/QTEs interrupting your fun. It's also really good for farming Skill Points.

The narrative is complex- it's also dumb and not really worth focusing on. The combat is fluid and precise- but also janky. The game looks great, but also looks bad depending on what you're looking at. One half masterpiece, another half messy, poorly paced, frustrating tedium, this game is conflicting to me even after 100+ hours played. I want to love it, but I hate it's confused design elements and tedious story sections. I want to hate it, but the engaging, fast paced combat and single-player co-op have me re-installing this game four years after I originally bought it and completed it. Did I mention this is a PC game with splitscreen coop? Yeah, you read that right. It's fun, too. Certainly makes the campaign more bearable.

This game is the result of ridiculous ambitions being tempered by lack of budget, lack of time, and lack of a focused vision. I'm shocked that this game was released at all- but unlike many who reviewed this game when it launched, I'm happy that they did. 

This game isn't a horror masterpiece a-la RE1, nor is it an action masterpiece like DMC3. So if you can curb your expectations and enjoy the game for what it is, sometimes in spite of itself, the same way you would with movies like Planet Terror or Universal Soldier: Day of Reckoning, you're bound to have a... Mostly good time.

Resident Evil 6 is a solid and powerful game that I never get tired of playing again and again, even after the three and a half years that have passed since its original release. Maybe not the perfection that Resident Evil 4 was, but Resident Evil 6 is very close to that. 

We get to play as three of our long-known and favourite characters (Leon, Chris and Ada) plus a new addition to the saga, which is Jake, Wesker's son. As an alternative, you can also play the three main campaigns (Leon, Chris and Jake) with the characters' partners (Helena, Piers and Sherry), which is recommended as the experience is very different with them. Unlike the bad partner programming in Resident Evil 5, in this game the partners never cause you problems, they have their own inventory and they come to your rescue whenever you need them. But overall the gameplay is excellent anyway; each character has their own fighting style, others are quicker (Leon, Piers) others have better melee (Helena, Sherry) or are great at going stealthy (Ada). 

There are four main difficulty levels, ranging from piece-of-cake kind of easy (Amateur) to really tough stuff (Professional) plus an additional extra hard mode (No Hope) which is basically of the Professional level, but without any perks and skills. 

The story of the game is divided in four main sub-stories, and at some point these stories intersect. As a result, there are a few stages that you have to go through more than once (ie, you have to fight the mutated Deborah with Leon and then with Ada, or the creepy Ogromen with Chris and then with Jake). This may get slightly boring after some time, and there's a possibility that these particular stages may feel like a chore. However this doesn't really take the fun away, if you think about it, because with each character you may have to apply slightly different strategies and this is very interesting and enjoyable. 

Atmosphere-wise, each campaign has a different feel: Leon's campaign is a strong reminiscent of the classic Resident Evil games, with all the zombies infesting the towns, the labs, the cemeteries and the cities and what not (there is even a police car to make your escape, and the - almost always present in zombie-themed stories - gas station in the first chapter), Chris's campaign on the other hand has a dominant feeling of war, mostly due to the overwhelming flashback, Jake's campaign is a refreshing change of pace with the two chartacters being constantly on the run and Ada's campaign is a lonely journey of our lady spy (well, unless you play co-op in which case you have a nameless and speechless soldier for partner) through most of the places that we have seen with the other characters. 

Back to the gameplay, which is particularly important in this game, everything works perfectly; however there are a couple of situations and quick-time events that may cause issues. I don't know if these are bugs or something random, but I found out that in these cases fiddling with the screen resolution and/or the FPS fixes the problem. Other than that, the game is almost flawless; each character has unique melee attacks and counter attacks and a special weapon or fighting skill, and there's decent variety in weaponry as well. There are also many moves, other attacks and finishing moves that you can perform, plus the amazing quick-shot, which can be executed in different styles and ways depending on the character you are playing with. However the game is not so generous with ammo, which makes it significantly more demanding in this light. 

There is interesting and in-depth character development, though it may not be easily appreciated on first look. The character design is gorgeous, the moves and expressions are incredibly realistic. Overall this game is great, definitely one of my favourites of the Resident Evil series.

Resident Evil 6 is a a good game, but not a great game. 

It's something I'd recommend picking up on sale, but not even for the $30 price tag it has now. Its got plenty of action, a more convenient inventory system, and has a nice look; however, the story and gameplay is what doesn't make the cut.

The run and gun is probably one of the more satisfying changes I've seen (which is apparently what some people are agonizing about). While it could be re-worked a bit to feel smoother that's not so much the issue. The problem is, how the whole experience just works out. Obnoxious falling over after being shot, the tripping over bodies, crappy cover system, and  terrible camera angles/forced aiming for the sake of a in-game 'scene' all work against the game. That's just a few of the problems which have come with the game. Each campaign (4 all together) has a problem though in their own right. Leon's is probably one of the better one reminiscing more of an old schoool Resident Evil take. The constant falling over after being shot doesn't become apparent until you hit up Chris' campaign. Then, perhaps the worst of all is Jake's campaign. Which attempts to put you into a more cat and mouse type game which just works out terribly for the run and gun gameplay. Some areas where they try and encourage stealth can be laughably avoided by just sprinting past the entirety of it.

I applaud Capcom for trying to deliver so many experiences and different play-styles into one package, but it ends up just falling short. Instead of receiving one fantastic experience, we get four different mediocre ones. 

Then comes the story. Terribly transitioned flashbacks, shallow characters and your typical 'conspiracy' stuff all show up in RE6. The story naturally requires you to play all 4 campaigns to understand it completely. Each campaign is a puzzle piece that doesn't quite make sense til you complete it. The part that really screws it over is just how they stick in details that apparently happen in the gap between RE4-5 to this. Things come up that make you say, "I don't remember that happening at all!" Which Capcom then tags in, "Oh, this happened in that 6 year gap between RE5 and 6 somewhere." The story isn't necessarily bad, but it's just okay. Since the story is split into 4 campaigns the experience is different and it shows that Capcom gave more love to one campaign vs another.



Overall, I had fun with the game. Coop is probably what became this games saving grace for me as my friend and I tackled it together. The segments of the game which have you "searching for a partner" are somewhat sad as you'll find pretty much nobody, but the AI that takes the players' place is great. The AI does their objective and they do it well without you having to babysit them. 


If you're a fan of Resident Evil I'd say pick it up on sale, or if you're new to the series pick it up on sale too. It's a fun game with friends, but not worth the current price tag. Which is why, I will not recommend this game. I paid $10 and felt I got my money's worth (still am), but would not do it for $30. Just wait for one of the many Steam sales and have your fun too.

While not a great Resident Evil game it is a good TPS, albeit a flawed one. 

I will start with the positives, first and foremost it's just a lot of fun to play as the combat is truly fantastic, apart from the cover system which is quite terrible so I never used it. There's endless ways to kill the enemy, including the always fun to execute melee finishers. The monsters take visible damage as you shoot them which I loved, bits of their body will fly off as you focus them and it just adds something to the combat which I appreciated. The game doesn't have an Oscar winning story but it keeps you interested, if you've ever played a Resident Evil game you know what's going to happen, as it always happens. The voice work is done well, although hurt by the script which isn't great at best, it's very cheesy and almost cringe-worthy at times but that's a staple of Resident Evil games at this point. Also I'll say that I had no technical issues, the game ran at a solid 60fps throughout on max settings, I know performance was an issue in the past but it's certainly not now on appropriate hardware.

As for negatives, the biggest for me was the length of the game, it truly overstayed its welcome, at 22 hours it feels very long and fatigue kicked in around the 15 hours mark. I would have enjoyed the game a lot more had they trimmed the fat and sliced off at least 5 hours, it would have been a more enjoyable game for it, I can think of a few sections that could be shortened or just removed entirely. By the end I was struggling to find motivation to finish it, and I dropped my overall rating from a 7 to a 6 as it just dragged on too much, the reduction in score was also due to the fact that Ada's campaign was poor almost throughout and as I played it last it left a sour taste in my mouth after I finished the game. Another gripe were the unskippable cutscenes, no one likes them, so please stop using them devs! Another dev favourite that we all hate are QTEs and the game is littered with them, so be prepared to die if you don't press A + X within a split second of it popping up on the screen.

Overall I did enjoy it for the most part but it definitely wore me down by the end, would I recommend it? Yes, but only when on sale and only if you feel you can endure the boring chapters as to enjoy the good ones. I should also mention the game is heavily co-op focused, you can play solo with an AI companion but the game is far more fun with a friend, or even a random online player although those are rare these days.

[*]Absolutely fantastic monster design. The cocoon idea for a lot of transformations keeps me wondering what I'm about to fight. Bosses are also super grotesque and interesting.
[/list]

[h1]NEUTRAL[/h1]
[list]
[*]Really wish the UI didn't constantly change aesthetics.
[*]Story is incredibly standard. New bad guy with ties to research for monsters trying to do something kinda evil and is evil, then more evil people pop up around him behind the scenes.
[*]Not incredibly great additons to the combat. Of course you can move and shoot now, but you also have odd dodging and crawling.

[/list]

[h1]BAD[/h1]
[list]
[*]Game focuses on spectacle rather than fun action horror that RE4 introduced.

[*]There is a bevy of terrible sequences that just made me sigh and dip my head. Here are a few: obnoxious shark bio weapon (B.O.W.) section with exploding barrels that don't always land in time, you have to redo the intro section with Leon that you played at the beginning with barely any changes, rescuing hostages from spider J'avo, highway chase scene with Chris and friend, unfortunately paced and disappointing snake fight, Ustanak hide & seek, annoying bus sequence with Ada against a chainsaw boss, and a crude sequence against some goo on a ship. The devs went into the game with one real motive: make a game jam packed with as much fanservice as possible. Returning characters facing off against each other, badass kaiju sized bioweapons that can turn into anything based on pure Rule of Cool and level entire buildings. So much danger, destruction and action setpieces are thrown at you, that you ironically don't feel like you are under any real threat. It's just a constant stream of "hey, remember when this happened in an older game? Well, here's more!"

It's not a poor game by any means, but anyone who isn't an RE fan would just comment, "why do people like Resident Evil? It's just a boring, mediocre third-person shooter with a strangely ludicrous production value". Looking back on it with the hindsight that they ultimately saved the series it's easier to accept it for what it is. Still, besides the fun movement tech, the gunplay's kinda bad.

Resident Evil 6 has a lot of content that's stretched far too thin, with woeful execution and an overall lack of direction. Playing it, I couldn't help but feel that I couldn't wait for it to be over. 

Its problems are numerous. It has multiple campaigns with recycled content across them. It makes you watch the same long cutscenes repeatedly across those campaigns. The controls are awful and inventory management is unintuitive and clunky. The game's Gears of War style cover system is broken, with enemy attacks often clipping through geometry. The melee combat is frustrating; moves are supposed to be contextual but it often just leaves you roundhouse kicking the air. The button to run is the same button to climb ladders and jump up or down ledges so you will frequently do one thing when you meant to do another. It has bad checkpointing so you'll replay tedious sections repeatedly. It's full of unnecessary and annoying quicktime events that cause instant game overs, far more than any other Resident Evil game. Ammo conservation, a cornerstone of the series is completely unbalanced, relying on RPG grinding and a pity mechanic on game over to deal with it. It also has a major bug in Jake's campaign that halts progression in coop that requires a workaround to continue progression. 

The worst part of the game is it frequently takes away control to make you look at something the game wants to tell you is important; unfortunately the enemies don't stop when this happens. As a result the game ends up being full of cheap deaths where you will be killed by an enemy that approached you and jumped on you during a cutscene. See an enemy approaching you? Well the game may decide then it wants to point the camera towards your objective, whilst the enemy continues to approach. Meanwhile you will be killed by the now unseen enemy. In this game, cutscenes in the middle of gameplay are one of the deadliest threats. 

Other places where the game takes control from you is in the game's many, many enemies that put you in grab animations if they come anywhere near you, forcing you into a quicktime event that comes with a canned animation that must play to completion. Surely then, the answer then is to use your weapons to make sure enemies don't come near you? If only that were the case; the game is balanced around making sure you need to come in close proximity with most enemies to melee and conserve ammo. Enemies also can't die during many of their canned animations - if your coop partner unloads half their gun into them it won't matter, and leads to some interesting scenarios, such as where you'll be grabbed by an enemy that goes to bite you, their head blown off by your partner, then you die because you failed the quicktime event as your character reacts to getting bitten by a now headless enemy. It also makes the weapons feel weak, with guns like the shotgun satisfyingly throwing enemies back, until they don't - if you try to use it to knockback an enemy jumping at you, sorry but their invincibility frames are in effect and you're probably going to die. 

The game is far too in love with its heavily scripted sequences, but even then they're just so poorly constructed. You will encounter enemies that can only be hurt during specific sequences, where you can use half your ammo in a game that relies on ammo conservation as a mechanic on an enemy, before realising that you weren't able to damage him because you hadn't reached some arbitrary checkpoint. You will run into basic enemies lying on the ground numerous times that you know are obvious threats. You can shoot them but your bullets will have no impact. Even though you know they're a threat, you have to walk past them where they will stand up and are only then able to be damaged. There's tons of instances where the game just arbitrarily decides it's not going to let you do something you should be able to, such as opening a door, because the game wants an event to happen first or for an NPC to do it for you. 

Overall, the coop is poor compared to Resident Evil 5 or other coop games. There is no resource sharing, so if your partner runs out of ammo and you have a ton, that person is just going to have to go on a punching spree until they find some more. You can't give first aid kits or medical supplies to your partner either, although you can use them on them. This is such a basic feature and it was important in Resident Evil 5, so its omission here is glaring. 

Resident Evil 6 doesn't play like a survival horror game. I don't have any problem with that in itself, but the game is trying to be this mix of action game and horror and fails at even achieving a basic level of competence at either. Like many Japanese games being developed in its time, its attempts to emulate Western games like Gears of War and Call of Duty is horribly misguided. The lack of player agency as the game constantly wrests control from you is infuriating and leads to a game that isn't just unfun, but one that makes you angry to play it as it treats the player as unnecessary. Unfortunately there's little redeeming this game; it's terrible and should be avoided.

HANDS-DOWN, ONE OF THE MOST ABOMINABLE OPENINGS TO A VIDEO GAME...EVER.  
 
   I mean, I do appreciate that some Resident Evil fans actually prefer a zombie-kickboxing simulator to a more atmospheric gaming experience, but seriously, does ANYONE out there actually like all this mechanics-breaking, quick-time-in-lieu-of-a-cutscene ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥?!  Okay, so maybe The Walking Dead games get away with some degree of it...but if the Resident Evil games are now aspiring to the level of immersion and emotional depth that THOSE games achieve, they may want to start paying some attention to concepts like themes, storytelling, and characterisation, don'tcha think?

   The opening sequence of this game is sooooo painful, they even give you an Achievement for getting through it, appropriately entitled "The Longest Night".  They even have the gall to call it a "tutorial", when it teaches you precious little other than how to die repeatedly because you don't understand the poorly-explained on-screen instructions of how to RUN...in a SINGLE DIRECTION...and then force you to watch the same ten-second snatch of cutscene OVER AND OVER AND OVER AGAIN to atone for your aforementioned sins.  Next time, Capcom, just hawk up a great big loogie and spit it straight in my face, eh?
 
   Things then start to look a TINY bit more hopeful, as Leon and some chick we've never seen before make their slow, moody way through a super-darkened government building, which is seemingly full of spooky noises but no actual undead. It isn't long, however, before we're spin-kicking and pile-driving zombies, and trying to work out just how the hell you even switch from guns to grenades or use health items (all adventures in their own rights, believe me)!  On the whole, there's really nothing terribly intuitive here...not the controls, not trying to estimate how close you can get to a zombie with your flyin' feet before they can get at YOU...the early part of the game is a constant struggle, or at least it was for me, and I played this straight off the back of Resident Evils 4 and 5, and all the DLCS and "bonus episodes" attached to those (undeniably superior) games. 
 
   Overall, there's really not much respect given to long-term fans: this may as well be a big-budget rival company's rip-off of the RE franchise for all the continuity it serves up, both tonally and mechanically.  It's far from the worst game ever made...but it's definitely one of the weakest Resident Evil games, period.  (And I've even played obscure, long-forgotten ♥♥♥♥ like Dead Aim, the Outbreak series, and the Survivor series, for what it's worth.)
 
    For much of its length, this is barely even a horror game.  It's an action game with unfeasibly dark lighting and horror undertones.  Hell, as zombie-action games go, it's a long way from bad - even slightly "thrilling" upon occasion - but it's hardly honest-to-God HORROR, at least seventy-five per cent of the time.  And for all its attempted surliness, its "grit" never surpasses that of a Michael Bay movie (nice stubble, Leon, but you still have pretty-boy hair); and when all is said and done, it's still every bit as corny as a farmer's field in Summer ("Mr President, please don't make me do this!" blubbers Leon, unwilling to shoot the prez, even though he's clearly turned into a FREAKING ZOMBIE)!
 
   A message to the developers of Resident Evil 7: stop catering to the undiscerning fans of those awful Milla Jovavich movies, and stop pandering to whatever is de rigueur in video games right at this very micro-second in time.  Multiplayer and/or A.I. partners DO NOT MAKE GAMES SCARY.  Quick-time events DO NOT MAKE GAMES SCARY.  Endless kickboxing moves DO NOT MAKE GAMES SCARY.  And making parts of your games so visually dark that you can't even tell what the hell just wounded you, IS JUST FRUSTRATING, NOT SCARY.  

   Pretty pretty please, let's do a little better next time, eh? This series is still pretty good...but it used to be GREAT.  The Revelations games seem to be heading in the right direction...how about lifting the game of the MAIN series, whad'ya say?
 
Verdict: 7.5/10.  
 
(Oh, and PS to the devs: there's this thing they invented a while back, called "save points", and you shouldn't feel obliged to limit yourselves to only one every half-hour or so of gameplay.  Just sayin'...)

Hi there! I might not have a lot of hours at the time of writing this, but I've both watched and played the game by now. And I definitely recommend this game, particularly so with a friend! Warning, a bit long below I'm sorry.

First, I'll name off all the bad points, so we can get those pesky buggers out of the way!

The Camera hates you. You have to play with the options a bit - I definitely recomend cranking that field and aiming point of view as high as you can go - and sometimes it's just outright dumb. I think I died around 16 times on Amateur, the easy mode, in Chris' route. It was basically a run away from thing and they kept changing the friggin' camera angle twenty times, inverting the controls each friggin' time. JEEZ. It's my #1 beef of the game. 

What's Inventory space? Your inventory space is well... very small. Unless you're like me, constantly needing herbs because you keep getting hurt, or you use up all your ammo because you're dumb at shooters and you miss all the time, you're probably going to be fighting for space in your inventory. One solution is to just not pick up any gun you don't really like to use - like say you're running melee, you don't need the sniper rifle dude - but honestly what kind of solution is that? So prepare to try to figure out what guns you're going to keep ammo for.

Stagger times are real. So if you get hit by a zombie, it takes eight years to get back up, and that's really frustrating when you have like five of them that manage to get right in front of you and eat your face. Or when some stupid little robot explodes, and it takes your forever to get back up and you're on limited time. I mean, it could be worse, but sometimes it's very sluggish to react, and that makes it difficult to enjoy the combat often enough.

So we're done with the bad! Onwards with the good!

I love, love, love the storyline. Playing one campaign will give you a general idea of the story, but so much is left in the air. As you play more campaigns, you start to understand the story more and more. And if you manage to complete all four? Well the story comes together in it's full, glorious picture. The characters are fun, for the most part - looking at you Chris - and it's actually fun to listen to them in other languages. The story has a lot of depth surprisingly enough, requiring at least a large amount of attention to catch every nuance. In fact, you'll see hints of the other campaigns in the one you're in, even in the background! Can you find where it all intersects?

Co-op. This game is CO-OP. Every campaign, you can play with a friend! And that's twice the fun! Honestly, the fact that you can co-op is really amazing with this game - in fact I even recomend to play this with someone else more then by yourself! You get to totally have fun with your friends, well most of the time, and each character has differences. For example, you'll see and do different things as Helena then you do as Leon. Sure you might be in the same campaign, but there still is individual flavours for co-op players and that's fantastic. And it actually doesn't take three years to connect to play together.

Action, Horror and Zombies. You heard me. Most people would look at me and go 'this game isn't horror' and I want to shot them down. So an undead corpse losing all their skin, transforming into a meaty beast that will lynch you and tear your body to pieces isn't horrifying? Or how about a being that regenerates and comes out of the grates and if it catches you, shoves it's tongue in your face, carving it out for it's babies? Yeah. That is bloody horrifying. It has some jumpscares, but the game isn't filled with them. And sometimes, they'll just straight up fake you out, making you think there's a jumpscare but there isn't. It's very action-oriented, I won't deny that, but to me, that's what makes it even more fun. Like each time there's a split path in the campaign? I'm scared. I'm honestly scared because sure I have guns, sure I can defend myself, but what will I encounter? What new thing will try to kill me next? I don't even have my friend with me to save me if I screw up... and that is truly, what's so horrorfying.

MELEE. The executions are top notch, and melee is actually viable. You don't have to sit there, and gun everything down - you can walk right in and spin kick them and watch them explode when you elbow drop them. It's so much fun to melee, and they even have a stamina system in place to make sure you don't abuse it - and if you go over it? you pay the consenquences. It gives you options to play the game, and that is what is very fun about the melee system. Oh, and the kickass execution cutscenes.

All the pretties. The art looks fantastic. The music is great and thematic and not super intrusive. You get wet when you enter the water. You can't run when you're in water. Water looks like water. I could go on forever, but honestly I've gone on long enough don't you think?

So basically, I love this game. It's not everyone's cup of tea, but I would definitely say at least go watch a video or two of it before buying it for yourself, make sure it's a game you want to touch. I definitely don't regret it!

[h1] I got RE6 through the recent Capcom Humble Bundle. [/h1]

RE6 is an uneven experience, lacking the input of either its masterminds (Mikami and Inafune) and relying on a "let's do it all" mentality backed by unrelenting budget, resulting a decent game buried somewhere beneath layers of sloppy execution and odd design decisions.

Pros:
- Nice graphics, varied scenery and competent art direction.
- Unobtrusive music, great sound effects and terrific voice acting.
- Workmanlike story and writing with pleasant storyline intersections.
- When it sticks to the basics, the game plays great. 
- Lengthy campaign featuring four large "acts" with multiple playable characters.
- The Mercenaries minigame can be great fun, even solo.

Cons:
- A metric ton of QTEs, some are easy, some are demanding, some are pointless and some are inhumane with insta-kill on failure.
- A metric ton of "sequences", those either rely on QTEs or on contextual actions. (tap button infinitly to do this, tap buttons in rhythm to do that, etc)
- The game often messes with the camera or strips you of control either to focus your attention on something or to show you a small, pointless cutscene. 
- Game mechanics aren't well realized: cover is useless, sliding is useless (good for breaking boxes though), dodging is almost useless, skill system is limiting at best, Combat Gauge bar needs deeper integration.
- Atrocious inventory and inventory managment: you have to fumble through weapons/items with the wheel or with prev/next hotkeys like it's 1999. Also no hotkeys for weapon slots, which is a big blemish on the otherwise thorough KB/mouse support.
- Online community is near non-existent.

I enjoyed RE5. Even though it wasn't the classic RE everyone knew, it was really a mostly good buddy action game with solid mechanics. The campaign was fun, and Mercenaries was also fun.

Although this game was also good buddy fun, there are too many flaws to recommend this game normally. And for the 6th game in such a well established series, it's pretty shocking how flawed it is. You should get this game only if:

1. You have a friend to play with whom you can enjoy a good laugh with while playing a really flawed game.
2. You're paying less than $10.

I played the majority of the game with a friend. Only when I played the last campaign did I come face to face with how bad the game really is.

Good stuff:

1. Movement Controls/Combat mechanics. They're very action oriented and can be really fluid in given situations. Honestly the best showcase for the controls is mercenary mode.

2. Pretty decent looking graphically.

3. Co-op fun for the first 3 campaigns and mercenary mode.

Bad Stuff:

1. One of the first things I noticed was the lighting in the game makes absolutely no sense. This was most noticeable in Leon's campaign. The brightness calibration test at the start is HORRIBLY miscalibrated. Both me and my buddy had to increase brightness drastically once we were in the actual game. On top of that, the game seemed absurdley dark. The light sources in the game seemed to give off no light on the surrounding environment. It looks really bad, but this is most noticeable in Leon's campaign.

2. Cover mechanics suck, despite so many other cover based shooters having existed by the time this game came out.

3. QTEs. See now, I don't hate all QTEs. I like "context sensitive" ones. Pressing RT when an enemy is stunned activates a special move. This kind of QTE is fine to me. I hate the "fill the meter to not die" and "press a random button you have no way of knowing before seeing it" kind. There are a lot of those.

4. The camera can be pretty bad, sometimes it's way too close to your character and they occupy way too much screen space. Similarly, this game has running sections where the camera orients itself classic RE style, from a set angle which you can't anticipate. This will often be the cause of many unjustified deaths.

5. The plot is pretty whatever, RE isn't really known for having a brilliant plot, despite taking itself so seriously.

6. A lot of things that happen seem to make absolutely NO sense, plot-wise AND gameplay-wise. I noticed this mostly in Ada's campaign (which I'm still playing through). There are puzzles you encounter that only make sense within the context of a video game, they have no logic to them. There was a puzzle where I needed an emblem. I walked into a room and a zombie pulls a lever which drops the big chest with the emblem through a trap door. Was he waiting here the whole time to do this? Why is he sentient enough to do this and how does he know my intentions? I killed him and I clearly needed to hold the lever down somehow so i could go through the trap door. 

So how did I do this? There are bodies hanging from the ceiling from nooses with locks on them. You're supposed to move the lever (which is on a track) near one of the bodies, shoot the lock which causes the body to drop from the noose (how?), the body gets caught on the lever and holds it down. If you shoot the body without landing on the lever, it dissolves and another one drops from the ceiling. ...WHAT. The whole premise of the puzzle makes no sense at all. There are many more like this. I can't even chalk this up to video game logic because there is no logic to this at all.

7. Ada's campaign being single player oriented. I appreciate they tried to do something different by making it a single player campaign, but it's executed in the worst way possible. You play 3 campaigns co-op. The 4th campaign can still be played co-op, but the story and gameplay is built around one player. Only Ada can interact with puzzles and exist in cutscenes. The most the second player can do is fight zombies, but there aren't nearly as many because it's built around one person playing. It really dissuades you from playing with a friend because they end up being useless, thus taking pretty much the only entertaining factor of the game away.

So yeah the game is fun with a friend, but not worth it otherwise. RE5 was a better game.

I'm a huge fan of the Resident Evil series and have prided myself in giving each game in the series a shot...so I decided to give this one a bash even after not enjoying RE5 and the absolutely abortionate Operation Raccoon City.

I regret that decision. I absolutely dispise this game.

First, the game dumps me right into the thick of it without so much as being able to map the controls, change the sensitivities and turn subtitles on, but then I actually get to shoot something- with the exact same horrible hit detection and lack of feedback that plagued ORC (And I might add that both RE4 and 5 got exactly right.) along with a lack of explaination on how melee works, a much more difficult and far less satisfying gameplay mechanic for knives and herbs, a far, far more buggy and uncertain Melee command with very little (And inaccurately late) prompting and a severe lack of ammo. All of this is evident in the first ten minutes.

Add to that the action movie scene of the entire street becoming engulfed in an explosion that you just barely escape into the helecopter, only to find the pilot inexplicably not only wounded but somehow INFECTED without any explaiantion or plausability whatsoever, who then proceeds to turn instantly and attack your partner, showing once again Capcom's lack of writing skill and thematic consistency with their own lore. 

Of course, there are QTEs and they're just as unsatisfying as RE4 and RE5, only there are EVEN MORE of them. In the 76 minutes that I managed of this game, I'd performed over 20 QTEs and was auto-attacked by so many scripted, railroaded 'enemies' that my head was spinning.

So, after the high octane Michael Bay stylings of the intro, I'm then railroaded into a slow and very predictable 'horror' gameplay sequence as Leon where I'm force-walking down a corridor for 20 minutes unable to take the prudent measure of pre-killing zombies (Something we were able to do in Dead Space, several years prior) that we can see have already turned but aren't 'activated' yet. We happen upon an infected survivor and his infected survivor daughter that Leon doesn't realise is infected despite being the literal biggest expert in Bioterrorism that the Secret Service have...and then we're force-script attacked in an elevator with four 'enemies' piling into us without ANY EXPLAINATION OF HOW MELEE WORKS IN THIS GAME!! I'm trying to shoot them in the head instead of booting them out the door like a numpty and find that ultra-close range shooting is about as accurate as Starfox Zero and about half as satisfying.

Add to that how unbearably dark the game is even with the gamma turned down and you have an absolutely miserable experience both in terms of looks and in terms of gameplay.

The voice acting seems to be of a much higher quality, but the dialogue is stiff, formal and extremely cliché at pretty much all times undermining any attempt at serious storytelling that this game pretends to- exactly like RE5 only much more braindead. Think 'Chris Redfield punching a boulder' stupid...it's that bad.

The final straw that broke my back was the scene where Leon and Helena get in a police car...I have to QTE to find the keys, then QTE accelerate and then QTE reverse to avoid some 'enemies.'

Next thing I know 'ARGH, OH NOES, DERRS STILL BAD GUYS ON MY CAARRR!!' and instead of shooting them in the head as I had done in every weapon QTE and Leon had done in most cutscenes, instead he decided to steer-flip the car, roll it over, totally trash it and then think nothing of doing so. DONE!! I'M SO DONE!! I'M SO COMPLETELY TOTALLY UTTERLY DONE WITH THIS ABSOLUTE WASTE OF MY TIME AND ENERGY!

So the gameplay is a 3 / 10.

The graphics are a 6 / 10.

The story and dialogue that I played through is a 2 / 10.

The UI and menu system is a 2 / 10.

The weapons, Inventory management (A Resident Evil staple that was completely ripped out of the heart of this game) and control feedback are a 2 / 10.

This game is at most a 3 / 10. It's exceptionally bad in terms of gameplay, hideously braindead in its storytelling, has a UI that in 2016 is a clunky mess of a thing that does not befit the series and is really only marginally better than the absolutely shambolic Operation Raccoon City- a game which I suspect this shares an engine and shares its weapon registration and hit detection with. (And I might add, beat this game as my 'Worst game of 2012' by quite a large margin- ORC is THAT bad.)

I'd love nothing more than to be able to say that I enjoyed this, but then I'd be lying.

It's a disaster. An utter disaster.

Resident Evil didn't invent the survival horror genre as we know it, that distinction belongs to 1992's Alone in the Dark, but it is the franchise that popularized the genre and as a result has become the standard bearer. Over the series 20 year history, it has evolved and changed to stay keep up with modern gameplay and mechanics; pre-rendered back drops were ditched in favor of fully 3d modeled environments. Grid based tank controls and fixed camera angles evolved into a tight over the shoulder perspective with swifter character movement and a dedicated single player experience has been replaced by co-operative gameplay. While no one can accuse the franchise of failing to evolve, it's entirely fair to criticize what it has evolved into. Starting with RE4, the series morphed into a more action game, alienating purists but ultimately appealing to a larger audience. Resident Evil 6 is Capcom's attempt to give both purists and newcomers an agreeable middle ground by splitting the game into four smaller campaings with different protagonists and gameplay styles. The problem is that Capcom's attempt to please everyone has given us a game that fully pleases no one. 

	Players take control of Leon Kennedy, Chris Redfield, Jake Muller and Ada Wong in four separate but interwoven campaigns in an effort to combat the C-Virus. It's a globe spanning whodunit, though players will have cracked the game's mysteries long before the reveal. Players will benefit from having played the other titles in the series in order to have an understanding of the backgrounds of each character. The problem with Resident Evil 6's narrative is that it attempts to be a bigger, more bombastic version of the events in previous games but it only manages to feel needlessly convoluted and dry... The narratives of previous Resident Evil titles have had a silly B movie charm while lovingly fleshing out the game's mythos with countless files and documents. The increase in scope and size ruins the B movie charm but is still too absurd to have blockbuster appeal. The characters have been written into corners and their individual narratives are so complex and independent of each other that this attempt to write these series favorites into the same chain of events is forced and clumsy. It's clear that a narrative reboot is in order for the franchise to retain the charm and quality the first games were known for.

	Gameplay has received and overhaul that moves Resident Evil further toward pure action. Characters can now aim while moving and heal with the press of a button. While these tweaks are convenient, they take away much of the tension present in previous entries to the franchise. A clunky Gears of War style cover system has also been added pushing the gameplay too far from the series' roots. Puzzles are restricted to Leon and Ada's campaign further betraying the roots of the series. In addition to these changes the game features idiotic cinematic action sequences on motorcycles, jets and snowmobiles that offer needless spectacle. The attempt to force these visually complex and flashy moments into the game cheapens the whole experience. Between the gunplay and watching your characters survive plane crashes, car crashes, helicopter crashes and surviving falls from high places a few zombies don't really pose a credible threat. With its ultra resilient characters Resident Evil 6 could be reskinned as a Justice League game with little effort. As with other action games expect an irritating amount of stick waggling and button mashing thanks to copious quick time events. A spare controller might be required. The melee system has been overhauled as well offering a number of context sensitive commands that frankly make it completely overpowered. Seriously, you can punch your way through half of the game on professional difficulty. It has never been easier to conserve ammo in a Resident Evil though it's not like the game isn't generous in that regard anyway. Speaking of conserving ammo, you will actually be spending most of your time dumping it on the ground thanks to a miserable inventory system. Your characters carry around more guns than John Matrix during the finale of Commando but it doesn't leave much room for bullets. There is also no item swapping between AI or human partners and the UI itself is atrocious. 

	Each campaign generally offers a players a different flavor and some try to recall previous games in the franchise. Leon's campaign is our favorite since it is generally the most traditional. There are a few puzzles and the environments in his campaign are among the most atmospheric in the game. Chris' campaign is pretty much an unofficial Gear of War title, emphasizing gunplay and taking players through a fictional war torn eastern European country called Edonia. It's the weakest campaign in the game as a result of it's fixation with bullets and chest high walls. Jake Muller's campaign is interesting at first since he and series darling Sherry Birkin have to face off against a Nemesis-like creature called the Ustanak. Unlike Resident Evil 3 and Resident Evil 2's scenario B featuring Tyrant, the game design telegraphs the appearance of the Ustanak killing any tension or sense of unpredictability this unstoppable beast might have otherwise provided. The Ustanak also facilitates some of the obnoxious  action set pieces that force players into watching ♥♥♥♥♥♥, bloated cinematic sequences while mashing buttons during quick time events. Since Ada takes her campaign on alone it's more about stealth and offers several puzzles. It works well enough and comes out as one of the stronger campaigns. Having several interconnecting campaigns also means that you replay the same segments with multiple characters and it's completely unnecessary and lazy. If you are not playing the same sections with different characters you can expect to experience the same gameplay gimmicks; like finding three keys in a labyrinth of hallways while being chased by unkillable regenerators. It's like waking up in Bill Murray's shoes in Groundhog Day. Only worse.

	While it may sound like this is the most awful Resident Evil game to date, the truth is that it was one of the best action games on the market when it was released. When seen as a competitor to games like Gears of War it's stumbles and inconsistencies are more forgivable. The frustrating thing is there are moments in the game that are excellent and are a sign of what could have been if this game was focused on being a Resident Evil game first and pleasing a mass audience second. We expect moody atmosphere, slower paced gameplay and tension from anything in a box that says Resident Evil. In their attempt to give everyone something to like about this game they have created a game that lacks cohesion and focus. After experiencing one of Resident Evil 6's stand out moments, it doesn't take long before the game has your trudging through more cover based shooting ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or waggling your stick like you're having a seizure. 

It's four campaigns plus Mercenaries mode equates to over 100 hours of entertainment for fans. Each campaign attempts to use some of the best aspects of previous games to give players a total package. Yet, when it all comes together the only thing that makes it feel like a Resident Evil game are the familiar faces of Chris, Ada, Leon and Sherry. In an age where we often get so little for our buck, Capcom tried to give us everything fans could want but it's so inconsistent; wasting time and effort to give players glitz and spectacle instead of tension and scares. It would seem that the survival horror genre that we fell in love with in the 90's is dead. The twitch fodder hide and seek games that are now considered survival horror are mechanically shallow. I hope that the RE2 remake will remind Capcom why the franchise was brilliant.

Would I recommend RE6  to someone? That's a half-hearted yes. I wish Steam used stars instead of a simple thumbs up or down. If you're a fan of the series and you like the characters that have grown on you over the last decade or so, then yes, RE6 is a good play. 

On the other hand, if you're really just casually into the series from a distance or haven't really been following all the games to this point, I'd say, just go ahead and watch the full videos on YouTube to get the gist and skip this purchase. 

[h1]The Good:  [/h1]A lot of people really hated on this game in strong ways, and the criticism has some validation. But let's start with the good. 

[b]Graphics -[/b] A nice improvement from previous RE games, though at times the lighting makes it hard to tell as such. There's several different campaings to go through in this game, each one has some pretty nice visuals and character design. 

[b]Gameplay -[/b] This is both in the good category, and the bad category. The good part of the gameplay is in the improved combat structure. Overall all the control scheme plays a lot more like a normal 3rd person shooter, making it easier to aim and shoot on the fly. Veterans of other games should pick up the controls fairly intuitively, and I'm glad to say that ditching the old tank-style controls from previous fames feels like quite the improvement. 

[b]Characters -[/b] We've got some old favorites coming back for long time fans, and some new characters in the form of Helena, Piers, and Jake. Helena is paired up with long time vet of the series, Leon Kennedy, and Jake Muller is paired up with Sherry Birkin, now in a starring role. Chris and Piers have an interesting dynamic as Chris has fallen into a rut, so Piers is almost the spitting image of who Chris was back in RE 1. No matter who you play as, the characters flesh out pretty much the same, but it is entertaining to see how some of the characters have either matured or fallen into disgrace, (like Chris). 

[b]Story -[/b] This is another category that's both good and bad. The good part of the story is that there's actually 4 whole campaigns to work through, almost like 4 entire resident evil games. Each one takes on an archetype: Leon's is dark and tense, Chris' is very action themed, Jake's is mostly a chase sequence, and Ada's has a lot of the classic puzzle solving and intrigue. 

[h1]The Bad [/h1]

[b]Gameplay -[/b] Man, despite all the new 3rd person changes, there are some very head banging moments due to unnecessary Quick Time Events (QTE) and bad camera angles. I died more times to stupid button pushes and a poorly rotated camera than I did to any creature in the game. Jake and Sherry's chapter was the worst offender. 

[b]Story - [/b] Oh man, where do I begin? It's fun to have 4 different interweaving tales, but the downside is that you really get to a point that you just want the game to GET TO THE POINT. You have to do several boss fights several times on several characters, which can feel very repetitive. But my main issue with the story is that I didn't feel that any of the characters really found any major progression, with the exception of newcomer duo Jake and Sherry. At the end of the game, Leon is still Leon, Ada is still a mystery woman, and Chris is reset back to where he was at the end of RE5. Nothing new gained. Jake/Sherry, Piers, and Helena change, but nothing new with returning cast members.

[b]Characters -[/b] The villains in this game needed a lot of work. A LOT. The enemy types are fantastic: tons of work went into making the J'avo and zombies in this game different and creepy from other games. The bosses and lead villains however, have very little in the way of explanations for why they are doing what they are doing it. This is pretty typical for Resident Evil in general, but I really felt the bite of it in this game. You'll find out who the mastermind is of a plot and basically shrug your shoulders and say, "but do I care?" Instead of villain development, you may just have to fight that same boss 3, 4, or 5 times, which in no way substitutes character development. At some point, players want a payoff for their hard work: they want questions answered, they want to see what makes the characters tick. Don't expect that here.

[h1] The Ugly	[/h1]

[b]Cheapness -[/b] Yep, I'm calling shenanigans. I'm a big fan of the Dead Space series, which has a few cheap tricks in the form of jump scares or regenerating bad guys that piss you off sometimes. RE6 had this in every campaign. So let me define cheap: despite your ability to annhilate waves of undead and using your nearly omnipotent hand-eye coordination, you fall victim to a boss mechanic you didn't know existed. Or, you fail to rotate the left stick fast enough, since you weren't expecting a QTE. Or, you do exactly what you were supposed to do, but the camera flips on you so instead of it being behind you, it's now in front of you and you have to change what you are doing. Yeah... cheapness.

And let's not forget my favorite: the 'protected by the plot' enemy. You're walking down a hallway full of corpses you know will probably come alive. You aim carefully for a headshot and squeeze a bullet off, which passes harmlessly through the body as if it was ethereal. Once you get close enough though, it comes after you, and now you're in a bullet spraying/melee frenzy. I find that extremely cheap. 

[b]Gun Inefficiency - [/b] I don't know what happened to firearms between RE5 and RE6, but bad guys just don't take bullets like they used to. Aiming at a hand or foot in RE4 or 5 and popping off a shot, even with your first pistol, resulted in a body lurch from the bad guy that resonated a satisfying impact from your bullet hitting their body. None of that in RE 6. I might as well have been shooting water pistols instead of a figgin' magnum. One thing I love about Dead Space as a series is that each weapon has some serious weight to it. None of the weaponry in RE6 feel like they pack a punch, with the possible exception being the grenade launchers, and even those don't have nearly the splash damage and impact you'd like. This game tries to add in more of a melee component, where you either stun a guy with bullets and then finish with a melee strike, or vice versa. To say I hated it would be an understatement. What the hell are firearms good for if I should just be slugging my way through the apocalypse with my dukes?! Even with every boost you can get for your firearm skills, expect them to feel woefully under-powered, especially during Leon and Helena's campaign. Even when you get a shotgun in that campaign you're wondering why you bothered with it.


[b]Ridiculousness - [/b] A tank chasing you through a building? Check. A sudden avalanche chasing you down a mountain while you race down it with a snow mobile... while the ground erupts earthquake style under your feet? Check. Literally, this list goes on and on. Resident Evil has always had it's moments (Zombie SHARKS?! = RE 1) but this game took it to a new extreme. There's actually a lot of good moments in this game where the action is feeling tense, but then it's broken with yet another ridiculous chase sequence, or button spamming QTE, or monster that won't die from bullets, because, REASONS.

[h1]In conclusion:[/h1] Some of the game can be pretty fun, (more than I was expecting, still frustrating at times), but there was definitely some ideas that didn't pan out in this game. Too much genre mash-up, too many QTE's. The game does have some good visuals and atmosphere at times, but if you're looking a pure survival horror experience, you'll probably want to pick up Dead Space 1, 2, or 3. If you're a fan of Resident Evil/BioHazard and want to check in with some of your old favorite characters, by all means, pick up this game, but be ready for some shenanigans.

Resident Evil 6 (or Camera Madness as it is called in Japan) is a camera hijacking simulator with some shaky zombie shooting mechanics.  Literally, you shake and vibrate like the guns are red bull incarnate, and every time you fire, your weapon forgets what you were shooting at. [b] If capcom gave this game a bit more time it would have been one of the best for it's time, and frankly the biggest thing that is sinking this game down is the Resident Evil/Biohazard license. [/b]

[b] Caution: [/b] Wall of text incoming.

The gun fight mechanics in this game are absolutely amazing, when before in 4 and 5 you can only do certain actions like dodge only when an enemy is about to hit you by using a combination of keys, now its free, you can roll anywhere, slide and you can use those mechanics together, for instance rolling and holding aim will keep you on the ground aiming instead of instantly standing up after finishing the maneuver, you can also use melee freely whenever you want, where before you could only melee someone if you stunned them by a shot to the head or the leg, and you REALLY need to use melee because if you don't you're not going to have enough ammo and you'll end up meleeing a boss and good luck with that. those great mechanics are the game's best and worst part depending on who you are, yes i prefer the old Resident Evil formula and i don't particularily like how Resident evil became more focused on action and explosions but give credit when credit is due, the mechanics in this game are amazing.

This game bit a lot more than it could chew for me, it tried to combine everything in one game by making seperate character paths that are all part of one big story and those characters collide occasionally, the concept is really clever but sadly instead of making the game unparallelled, it makes it an average experience for each character, the game needs more time and you can feel how rushed some of the things are.

Ammo is more scarce which is again, a good thing or a bad thing depending on you, Resident evil games prior to 4 were all about thinking ahead and saving ammo whenever possible, back to the matter at hand, you can remedy the lack of ammo drops with a perk that increases the drop rate for different types of ammo.


But what about the core concept of a Resident evil game, Horror? well the game doesn't deliver at all in this aspect, leon's campaign path is supposed to return to the roots with the classic flesh eating zombies instead of "las plagas" or "uroboros"etc, granted in some parts of the game it gets really classic but all in all with the exception of a few jump scares there isn't anything to be scared of.


In terms of Storyline, it's... well there, that's what it is at best, you're going to have a few emotional moments and a few really badass ones but it's cliche and you can see what's going to happen miles away, very predictable, but playing through all 4 storylines will reveal a lot of the things you didn't understand or just took for granted which is really good.

However the game can get challenging sometimes which is always good, you'll die and some enemies are really tough, and the lack of ammunition (if you don't use melee efficiently) doesn't help either.


I have a few minor gripes, for instance the graphics are great but the textures really kill it sometimes, you're walking in this amazingly lighted and detailed enviroment and you look at the floor and it looks straight out of resident evil 4 (non-hd), really needed more time here.

Playing it with a mouse has this bug, a HUGE mouse lag that makes the game unplayable, there is a fix but it hinders you a bit, you're better off with a controller for this one.


Lastly i can recommend this game if you have a friend that can play it with you, having a friend will make this game extremely fun and will use the coop nature of it to the max, if not then if you can deal with the AI (which isn't that bad) then by all means go ahead.

There are a lot of games that I wouldn't recommend playing on their own, but would recommend playing with friends. Left 4 Dead is one of these games. Resident Evil 5 is one of these games. Dead Space 3 is one of these games. Even Daikatana, despite what many believe, is one of these games. You'll notice that there's a trend in these games, in that each one is worse than the last.

You'll also notice that Resident Evil 6 is not on the list at all.

Resident Evil 6 is a game that includes 4 campaigns, starring Leon, Chris, newcomer Jake, and the formerly secret Ada campaign. These campaigns total to around 30 hours in gameplay, with each of the first 3 campaigns being nearly as long as Resident Evil 5. You may think "Wow, what a bargain!", but you're missing one key component: almost none of it is worth playing. The game takes a severe quantity over quality stance, and even when the campaigns aren't directly overlapping (which is a feature, in which you might've been able to play with other people playing different campaigns in 4-player co-op at certain points if anybody was still around to actually play this game) you'll probably feel like you're just playing the same campaign over and over. Resident Evil 6 isn't a survival horror game, but it's not an action shooter either; it's just a third person shooter with really awful, gimped controls that are only worse when brought over to the PC. The only parts of the game that are even slightly redeemable are Leon's first chapter, which is about an hour long (some people will tell you that all of Leon's campaign is good, but those people are liars - all of Leon's personality and charm has been drained and given to Jake, instead) Jake's campaign, which is the only portion of the game that I would consider actually slightly worth playing at all, and the Mercenaries mode, which is as fun as ever. The story is a convoluted mess that puts literally anything in a series full of convoluted twists to shame, to the point that it makes Wesker suddenly returning with superpowers seem like a natural character development that was planned from the start. 

Resident Evil 6 is, as a whole, just an absolute mess. A disaster. A waste of time, effort, and money. It feels like Capcom just got together 1,000 people and said "hey, make a video game" and let them each try to decide what horror is, and while Jake's campaign has an extremely noticeable increase in interesting locations and mechanics, the game as a whole just feels like a mess of ideas that don't go together at all and overall leaves the game feeling bland and mass-produced, and it's just not worth it. Even if you do play with a friend it's barely worth it, since it's not even good enough to play for the sake of laughing at since after more than an hour or two of 3 of the 4 campaigns your soul will have been stripped of the concept of laughter. Ada's campaign is bafflingly not even built for co-op in a game that spends 25 hours reminding you that co-op exists, and if you do happen to drag some poor soul into the game with you they get stuck playing as "Agent", a character with no dialogue, no background, no cutscene presence, and no physical prescence - he can shoot enemies, and that's about the extent, since he can't open doors, solve puzzles, pull levers, or generally do anything except get carted through the levels by teleportation whenever Ada uses her grappling hook.

I can't even begin to recommend this game to anyone. There are some games that I hate that I can understand other people liking, but I have yet to see any sort of defense of Resident Evil 6 that didn't absolutely baffle me. For $30, you could buy Resident Evil 6, but $30 also buys you a ton of bleach that you could drink and have a way better time.

I’d heard this game was bad, and having played the demo I decided to skip this. But then the years went on, and both critics and game developers popped their head out to say “Resident Evil 6 wasn’t that bad!”. Could there be something interesting here after all? No. No there isn’t.

Maybe it’s a matter of preference? The way games like Resident Evil Revelations 2 or The Evil Within are paced is like a rollercoaster. You have long stretches of buildup and tension before all hell breaks loose. They both do a great job at it. Neither are particularly effective as horror games, but as action games I love them. Resident Evil 6 on the other hand is more like being strapped to a rocket. There’s some anticipation at the start, but then it’s non-stop action with set pieces upon set pieces with maybe 5 seconds of breathing room between them. I only played the first chapter of Leon’s story, and I apparently killed 228 enemies during that time. That’s the kinds of numbers you’d expect out of late game Doom 2 or Serious Sam.

So all pretense of it being horror is out the window, and there’s minimal exploration and the pacing is nonexistent. This puts more strain on the combat mechanics. They better be good if it’s the only thing you’ll be doing. Unfortunately they tossed out the mechanics used in Resident Evil 4 and 5 and tried to come up with new ones. I can appreciate the thought. But what they have here is simply worse. Your guns and enemies somehow both feel weak and flimsy, yet they take more hits to kill than I’d like. When you shoot enemies with a shotgun, there’s no difference in reaction from when you shoot them with a gun. It feels like an underdeveloped system that was rushed out the door. This is especially true of tougher enemies. In the parts of the game I played there were higher evolved zombies that took loads of bullets to take down, and there were big fat ones that took the rest of my inventory to kill. None of them were intimidating or exciting to fight. All they did was add tedium because their health meant the action set piece would go on for longer than it already was. 

I didn’t enjoy playing Resident Evil 6 at all. The story starts in a laughable manner, and it doesn’t get much better after that. In fact, almost nothing happened in the 2 hours I played, as characters insisted the story would start once I reached a cathedral. But on the way there I had to go through 9 action set pieces, one more tedious than the other. On every level from characterization, pacing, tension, the feel of the weapons, the enemy designs, and the way environments were designed and lit was worse than it has ever been in the series. I’m actually glad I decided to play it properly, because now I can finally write it off completely as garbage. If you like this for some reason, fine, I have nothing against that. But I can’t understand at all what the appeal is. This isn’t mediocre, it’s absolutely horrible.

Don't let its title fool you: Resident Evil 6 is not a survival horror game, but action-shooter.

If you seek to enjoy titles similar to Resident Evil 1 and Resident Evil 2 remake, then, this game is not for you. Resident Evil 6 is more like a World War II game, more, or less.

All the Cons/Pros of the title:

Pros:
+ Great character depth and realistic personalities (Piers Nivans, Helena Harper, etc).
+ Four major campaigns (Leon's, Chris's, Jake's, and Ada's) with 5 chapters each.
+ Multiple Protagonists (over 7) for you to play, across these 4 different campaigns.
+ Partner system, like in Resident Evil 5, with the only difference that the partner in Resident Evil 6 has infinite ammo and infinite health if controlled by the AI. (Thankfully! No more notorious AI Partner deaths!)
+ Huge variety of enemies and bosses - From the classic zombies to the J'avo. (J'avo are infected humans, similar to the Las Plagas from RE4 and can carry weapons and feature many mutations)
+ Each of the 4 major campaign offers different atmosphere / theme:
++ Leon's campaign has the dark classic theme - contains zombies, dark corridors and is closest to Resident Evil 1 and 2.
++ Chris's campaign has the World-War-style acton shooting theme - the most "american" of all 4 campaigns, and is close to Resident Evil 5 in terms of action and shooting.
++ Jake's campaign has the Tyrant theme. You are being chased by a Tyrant-type of monster like in Resident Evil 3.
++ Ada's campaign... well, for this one... I leave this to you to see what it is all about.
+ Character/Story crossovers - during the story you meet some of the other protagonists, controlled by others or the AI.
+ Skill system, that allows you to influence various aspects of the gameplay.
+ Different graphical UI styles for the inventory and menus. Each of the 4 campaigns will have different visual UI style, as if you are playing a completely different game.
+ Herbs and ammo boxes are here like usual! Lets refresh our memory. 1 Green Herb + 1 Red Herb, what does it do? :)
+ Melee combat moves / Extended combat system for certain characters.
+ Dashing and running system.
+ Excellent Dodge system. With proper timing, you can dodge almost any enemy/boss attack in the game, if done right. This allows you to leave the battleS unscratched!
+ Each of the 7 protagonists have their signature weapons and moves which others cannot obtain/learn. Ada for example has her trademark weapon, the famous crossbow, when Sherry has her unique Stun Rod and Jake is skilled in the Martial Arts and can deliver great blows with his bare hands, etc.

Cons:
- Your weapons and firearms cannot be customized, upgraded or improved. The ability of upgrading your gun stats, from Resident Evil 2, 4 and 5, has been removed completely from Resident Evil 6. This means, with simple words, that, whatever weapons you may have, will stay the same forever. 
- Camera is your biggest enemy. Causes troubles at times, especially when you need it to stay on your character's back but it doesn't. Super annoying!
- During cutscenes, the player's character can die. When a cutscene plays, your character will stay frozen solid, but the enemies will not. This means, if it happens there to be enemies nearby when a cutscene triggers, they can (and will) attack your character and kill him! And, no, it is not possible to defend your character from these hostile attacks, as you will have to wait for the entire cutscene to finish playing (!) and then for the camera to return back to its position over the character's shoulder (!) before you can resume control of your character. And if you see the Game Over screen after the cutscene, it means your character got killed and that you will have to start all over again... How shameful of Capcom's part to let a such oversight in a modern-day videogame like Resident Evil 6 to happen. Trully shameful. The Game Over screens right after cutscenes shows how poor job Capcom has done with Resident Evil 6.
- Most cutscenes can be skipped, but there is a good amount of them that cannot be skipped at all when the appropriate button is pressed.
- Way too many Quick Time Events. At least x10 times more QTEs than in Resident Evil 4.
- The game is trying hard to impress the player by adopting a Hollywood-style gaming  experience, at the expense of the player's own joy and comfort. Too many explosions and destruction in the surroundings, (such as cars blowing off, etc), can get repetitive and boring... And the camera leaves your character's shoulder way too often...
- AI is very stupid and poorly written. Enemies could come for you, pass by you, and then forget about you,
- Your partner has "body mass" and thus, you cant walk through him. This often leads in him blocking your path, especially in narrow areas and corridors. The problem here is that, due to the stupidity of the AI, he wont realize that he is blocking you from passing through a door, and thus, he won't give a ♥♥♥♥ about that. For example If you want to pass through a narrow door (narrow = wide enough for just only 1 person to pass through it) and it happens that your partner is standing in the middle of that narrow door, you wont be able to pass, well, at least not right away... So, if you are in the middle of a gunfight and you want to get past a door for cover from hostile fire, your AI partner may prevent you from doing so, and thus, increasing the risk of you dying or getting hurt, especially on the higher difficulties...
- The Cover system (Cover = taking shelter behind obstacles such as fences, corners and walls to protect yourself from enemy fire) could have been better... You enter into Cover Mode even when you don't want it, all just because Capcom decided that it was very practical to have the button for the Take Cover to be merged with the button for Weapon Aiming! Yes, you read right: if you hold the Aim button to shoot at an enemy with your firearm, but your character position happens to be near a corner, a crate, a fence or an wall, you will, instead of aiming + shooting, go into Cover Mode even if this was not your intention... how frustating! Capcom, you screwed it...
- The game's story spans 3 continents (America, Europe, Asia), but it lacks any depth. It could have been better.
- Your partner, when he is controlled by the AI, will rarely use the dash ability unless it is scripted to do so. This can be a problem, especially if you are seeking to get good timing scores / planning to do a speedrun in  chapters that feature very long corridors and paths.
- Graphics could have been better. The game allows you to visit many different places, such as cities, mountains, ships, etc, but the graphics in some of these places feel really outdated...
- It is not a survival horror title, despite its name. It is an action shooter title. It seems that Capcom took Resident Evil 5 and added a tons more unecessary action to its successor, distancing Resident Evil 6 even further from the series's successful and memorable roots.
- No costumes or extra weapons unlocked once you beat the game.
