Past RE games began with a build-up of tension, then the story was gradually revealed. RE1 and 2, and RE4 spring to mind. Whereas RE6 begins with a mindless action film intro that isn't scary, just frustrating, in the middle of a confusing story; then jumps back in time to the middle of an earlier part of the confusing story, leaving you none the wiser (since now you're with someone you seem to have never met before). Instead of pulling you in it just leaves you not caring. This was just the first of many annoyances. When a game keeps drawing attention to its mechanics and flaws, that isn't a good start.

The story is full of stupidities and bizarre motivations and character inconsistencies. Monsters are carrying people on top, you’re meant to save them. You pump clips of machine gun fire into them – the monster is killed, the person unscratched. … Church people won’t let you in, saying there are too many monsters – so they ring the bells and summon more??? Then you get in, realise it is just glass windows the monsters could easily break in through (but they don’t). … A character wants revenge – decides on poetic justice tied to a virus, since they have access to bioweapons. What would you do? Inject your enemy with a virus that is painful, makes them a weak monster and kills them, but only after they’ve suffered? Not in RE6. Instead they  inject their enemy with a virus that makes them a super-powerful being that seems indestructible and will go on a rampage killing people, innocents, friends, and probably the injector themselves, with more power than ever before – right. Nothing to do with character motivations, everything to do with the designers wanting you to have multiple fights with the cartoon villain. … Oh, Leon and Helena climb a rope using their arms, but leaving their legs stuck out in frog positions – I’ve never seen anyone do that, a ridiculous method of climbing a rope. … Again and again two people do synchronised dives and jumps from explosion – too much action movie mindlessness. … Chris forgot the term bio weapons – even though he’d spent most of his adult life dealing with them. ... One character had a flashback, where I gained a new weapon – then the flashback ended and I still had the gun. Yes, in RE6 you can gain new weapons from memories. 

Oh, how I groaned at the ridiculous chances. Every time I’d go through doorway or across a bridge it seemed to collapse, forcing me to go another way. … I crashed a plane in another country – and the person I saw across the world just passed me on a train. … I throw my enemy off a skyscraper, they happen to land exactly on a spike (and they blood forms the Umbrella pattern).

You can no longer save at typewriters (or wherever you want). Instead we have a flawed checkpoint system. It isn't explained properly, and when you quit it warns you about losing progress, but doesn't give you any helpful information about when progress was last saved. So you have to try and remember back to the last time a small icon popped up on screen that meant it was saved (rather than just a mid-save checkpoint). And they are often really far apart. One time I'd played for ages, had to leave, quit - came back later, and found I'd been reset to an area from way before that I'd have to play again. So frustrating.

Controls! There's no Steam manual. The in-game tutorial misses out most of the key controls (inventory, melee and so on), so the beginning is even more confusing and you may have to look for help online. Controls, especially for QTEs, are not explained well. … Often they're unnecessarily inconsistent, e.g. sometimes you open doors with A sometimes, with B (they could have just stuck to A, interact - it could still have been a requirement for your partner, even though it's stupid that your character is sometimes too scared to open a door unless their friend is stood next to them). … The tutorial tells you to press (Y) for the inventory. Later I did that, saw a first aid spray, but the only option was to discard it, not use it; It turns out you have to access it with the D pad instead - not explained in the game. … There's a weird drift to the gamepad (at least on my PC) that I haven't come across in any other game. Every few seconds the view starts drifting to the left and slowly rotates. It feels like I am controlling a shopping trolley with a wonky wheel. The same happens in the inventory screen.

The game seems to take place all at night (or maybe that’s just the gamma). You often see less of what's going on than even in earlier RE games. Tight environments, a view from behind (partially blocked by the character), darkness: it just feels like you die because of the view, not lack of skill.

Cliches. You pass bodies that do nothing (even if you shoot them in the head) until you examine something with your back to them, then they all come to life. … Kill a boss, and they return in a “surprise” scene later, tougher. Repeat. Repeat. Then you kill it and assume it is really dead (even though you seemed to do hardly any damage) and walk away – duh! It wasn’t a surprise the third time it reappeared, why would it be a surprise the fourth?

A new aspect - every room has bodies on the floor. Even though I can see them and would step over them, you highly-trained character insists on tripping up over every single one. Then there is a 50% chance that nothing happens, 50% that it grabs you for a QTE. Oh joy.

It is so much more gamey than earlier games. Enemies and crates actually drop "skill points". WTF? Also I have no idea how to use them. I looked through menus, found a way of equipping skills but not buying any. I've now completed a chapter and still haven't come across a shop or whatever to spend them in. (Found out later – it only shows you if you complete a chapter and continue, not if you quit the game at that point – also it is available in a sub-menu when you quit out of the game.)
Bodies dissolve. Even Doom did better.

I never play online multiplayer (it would make it even less scary), but have to turn that default option off every time I continue my game, it doesn’t remember your preference; like it is nagging you to use the options the developers are pushing.

Emotions just ring hollow and twee; the dialogue is generally pretty bad. Tradition maybe, but still…
Ridiculous chest-thump recoveries. You’re on the floor, wounded. How does your partner help? They thump you on the chest. Suddenly you can stand again. What? Is there a reset button there or something?

People who like RE1, RE2, and RE4 probably do so because part of the atmosphere is from the loneliness, the danger of often being the only human surrounded by horror, with no-one you can rely on but yourself. It’s probably why I don’t really get on with RE5 and RE6, since the fighting partner means you trade that terrifying lonely immersion for one-line quips. There's no tension when you have an invincible partner to hide behind, so spend your time running in circles to save ammo during boss battles. And tension dies when you get respawned with full health when you die, meaning there's no point using healing items most of the time, you are better saving them for the wearying boss battles.

It may get better, but I seriously considered uninstalling at a few points, which is a first for RE games with me. My history is RE1, RE2, RE Nemesis, RE4, RE5. I loved them all up to RE5, which seemed average. RE6 feels like a low point.

Lest I seem purely critical – there is some RE satisfaction here. Just that the bombast and silliness overshadows much of the horror and immersion.

After loving Resident Evil 4 and having a great time with 5, I decided to give this one a fair shake, this was a grave mistake. A frustrating and tiresome slog through tight linear hallways lacking in captivating level design and populated with annoying one dimensional characters, Resident Evil 6 has virtually no appeal as far as I can observe. 

The action is as clumsy and claustrophobic as it is mindless requiring no tactical thinking beyond ‘don’t miss’ despite the game’s efforts to provide challenging enemies. This is because the game showers you with ammo and supplies. It’s pointless to try to be efficient in your combat if the rewards are negligible. 

Furthermore, the joy of cooperation has been stripped to a bare bones experience since you and your companion don’t share supplies at all, each instead getting their own private loot drops. No strategy, no “I’ll carry the grenades, you the herbs” interactions that made 5 interesting as a co-op shooter. Yet somehow, the story is an even bigger trainweck.

Instead of opting for a traditional way of storytelling, Resident Evil 6 offers you 4 different campaigns each with their own protagonists. Problem is, each campaign happens at roughly the same time in the story and they intersect at various points. Meaning you end up revisiting the same locations and events over and over with different characters but doing the same thing. It would help if the different perspectives gave you a more nuanced look into the plot but it never goes beyond "now we'll explain this thing that didnt make any sense before". The game fails to connect any meaningful revelations or interesting twists in a plot rife with spectacle creep and no substance or convincing drama whatsoever. 

There is nothing here. No characters, no story, no visceral fun or clever design. This entry is practically a walking corpse and about as appealing.

This is the game that made me never trust the "general consensus" ever again. 

It is no exaggeration when I say that I believe the hatred for this game is in fact an observable case of mass hysteria.

The only olive branch I will offer is I understand that classic RE1 fans were likely quite upset that this game is the ultimate departure from its roots, and it is likely that dissatisfaction that incandesced the bandwagon of hatred for this game.

With that out of the way, regardless of expectation it is insanity to imply that RE6 is bad, let alone terrible as most people imply, I can fully see why someone might dislike it, but I think it is impossible to call it objectively bad. 

Why am I writing this? Because I have seen so many people call this game bad, and then when I ask them what they think about the slide tackle reversal they answer: "The what?"

That's right, RE6 has probably some of most in-depth movement systems of ANY over the shoulder shooter on the market, this is a TEN year old game at the time of writing and I cannot think of a single game that comes close. And though the game doesn't teach you it, and you can beat the game without using much of it. 

You can duck, you can roll in all directions, you can slide tackle off a sprint, you can REVERSE that slide tackle to face the way you came. You can choose to stay on the ground, from which you can roll left or right, or jut back and forth, as well as crawl, you can however stand instantly instead. You can shoot while sliding, reverse sliding, while on your back.

These aren't even all the moves, there's way more, I'm not going to drone on, though, you get the point.

What matters is that this system exists, now, I know that's not enough to make a game good. That's where the: Shooting, Enemy Design, Level Design, Quick Shot and Melee come into play.

All these mechanics mentioned above are a balanced gestalt of gameplay. They complement and layer each other near flawlessly. 

The shooting is well tuned and satisfying

The enemies are interactive and varied in many ways from having objects you can shoot on(or off) them, weak spots, unique mechanics with the player/melee system/terrain and all kinda of insanity I won't spoil.

The Level Design promotes using the movement system by having hazards, shortcuts, holes you can slide trough or objects you can vault over.

Quick shot allows you to instantly fire your weapon accurately at the nearest enemy, every weapon has a unique animation for this, effectively serving as the third layer of combat.

Melee allows you to preform environment-aware attacks of opportunity to staggered or otherwise available enemies. This fourth layer of combat ties all the other mechanics together, there are so many of these. Throwing enemies off ledges, pulling their feet while you're below them so they hit their head on the edge, or dropping down on them and push their head to the ground, or slam them into a railing, or a wall. Or snap their neck from behind. Or PARRY them, take their weapon, use them against them.  FLIP a zombie that is LEAPING AT YOU and STOMP on them.

Calling RE6 just an over the shoulder shooter isn't quite enough, it's very nearly an over the shoulder shooter/fighter.

[Did I mention every single character has a unique melee moveset?]

So that's my argument for the gameplay and why you should play it.

Give it an honest try. USE the movement system, you'll not find another like it for a long time.

[b]So the short and skinny of Resident Evil 6[/b]

There are 4 campaigns to play through that intertwine with each other that can lead to a lot of similar fights and locations being revisited. This can makes the game campaigns feel slightly lazy in comparison to previous games. However, other than the final campaign mission that was offered as dlc, each campaign is approximately 4 hours long. You couple the repetitiveness of the main campaign with some very Bollywood action sequences and it really is a toss-up whether or not you will enjoy it. Personally, I had no problem with it because if you can accept monsters, mutants, and zombies then you might as well suspend disbelief on the rest as well. 

Where the game really REALLY shines is the mobility of play style and improved combat system. There is sliding, rolling, jumping onto your back, running (like really running, not just the light jog from previous games), countering attacks, and a bit more. 
 
Oh and it has [b]LOCAL COOP[/b], the fact is, if you have one friend, just one friend that will visit you to play games, Resident Evil 6 is fun. Sure, the way the split screen works is a bit funky and very poorly implemented but I personally have zero problems with it. Therefore, if you have a single friend to play games with and an extra controller I promise you, your game play experience will generally be entertaining. However, if you play Resident Evil 6 alone, the game will be a bit of a slog at times.

Despite some obvious negatives you do get your money's worth when purchasing this game.

Recommend or not recommend - it’s not easy with this game.

At a 7.50 sale-price, you get a lot of content for your money. 
But how about the quality of said content?

The parts of the game which are fun to play, thrilling and exciting are “infiltrated” by parts which are not that much fun to play and can even feel like a chore. 

Sadly, some sections seem to exist solely to fill time, to give some variety or for narrative as their implementation (controls mostly) is mediocre at best.

There are lots of quicktime-events - which is not bad per se - but some of them felt out of place, at times annoying.

Obviously the creators had a big action-flick in mind, but the lack of execution in many parts make for an inconsistent experience.

I think if you play this game with your expectations not too high - ideally in coop-mode - you might have some fun with RE6. If you’re looking for a polished, focused experience maybe not.

Recommend for 7.50 or less.

  I bought 3 RE games in a package (RE 4,5,6). I played a couple of hours on RE4...it felt a bit stale and slow. Decided to give RE6 a try. In terms of graphics and gameplay, I don't see much difference in quality between RE4 and RE6. 

A few things that get annoying really quick:

1. Cut scenes and worthless narratives:  I love a good story. Unfortunately, there's not much of a story happening here.  Shoot zombies. Go somewhere else. Shoot zombies. The pace is interupted by cut-scenes which serve no apparent purpose. Two hours into the game, I'm still unsure why I'm here and what I'm after.

2.  Linear, stale, canned environment: It's the zombie apocalypse, so every building and street is in disarray. The game creators have used piles of junk to seal off areas and make the map appear bigger than it is. But there's no consistency to the barriers. In one rooom, you might be able to jump over a bench or a table. In the next room, you can't. Or you might find that a small board blocks a hallway that, somehow, you can't smash or crawl under.  It's just a very poorly constructed environment. RE needs to go open-world!

3.  No tips/tutorials for crafting:  Herbs are a mainstay. I mixed them, I eat them, I'm healed - but there's no way to tell if I'm "doing it right".  Anyone new to the franchise would probably be confused. Find a plant. Combine the plant. Be sure to put the mixture in a vial. Then use it to heal. Not tremendously complex, but crafting in any game deserves a small tutorial or entry on the "Help" menu. What's the diffrence between red, green, etc...? It's a guessing game. So I had to take 5 minutes to restart from a save point and play around with herb combos. Worthless waste of my time. Just provide the information up front. (FC3 does FPS crafting right, CapCom should take a page from Ubi's playbook.)

4. Cheap, underhanded AI tactics: For example, I see a zombie laying on the ground. I shoot it in the head. Bullet goes right through, no damage. Just a dead body, right? I walk up and try to kick it. Still no reaction. I walk past it. The zombie comes to life and attacks me from behind. I don't mind a genuine surprise attack from the AI, but tactics like this are off-putting to the player.

After playing RE 4 and 6 for a total of about four hours, I'm calling the Resident Evil franchise broken. The linear style can't compete  with open world FPS.  The narrative is old and tired.  Even at half-price, it's still too much money.

This game. This game is what introduced me to the RE series. From the general reviews, MANY RE fan hate this game. They  said that it was a departure from the main series by a long shot, third person camera, duck and weave motions, clonky controls etc. There are many.

This game is not friendly when you boot and play it for the first time. Unskippable tutorial mission, instant death from QTEs (which some will appear without warning), mobs appearing to be bullet sponges, accidental action due to control overlap, odd camera angle adjustments etc. Some may hate this game because of it (heck many of the hardcore RE fans hate this game due to the above reasons above).

I had that feeling as well. "Why are I climbing a deck repeatedly, when I wanted to climb and then sprint?", as I thought when I died due to time running out trying to escape. However I thought "Hey, maybe instead of holding down the Space button (which is used for both sprinting and context action), why not I press it once I am far away from the prompt?" Guess what? It worked.

As I played it longer, all the above reasons were overlooked (though occasionally I still mess up the context actions). This game benefit more the longer you played it. You will know by then what will happen next, where to move, how to properly get rid of a mob etc, which will make the campaign mode less of a hassle.

In a brief overview of the campaign, it's divided into 4 parts, each are having their own backstory, atmosphere and mobs.  There is the classical campaign aka Leon's, RE 5-esque (or shall I call it, the COD bros campaign) of Chris, Jake's (or Sherry's, if you know who she is) campaign, which is a less actiony version of Chris's , and finally, the more stealth based campaign of none other than Ada Wong. Even though they ara their own campaign, in the end they overlapped which each other, with some part of the campaign even replayable on another campaign (e.g. Chris 2 with Sherry 1).

Control wise, it's not like the old RE that you know. You will get to sprint, duck, roll, strafe and slide, unlike the old RE controls, which is more limited to tank controls. Your default movement is a jogging based motion, so everything here is a bit faster paced. The cover system also returns here as well. You won't be using it much, maybe except for Chris's campaign (and to a much, much lesser extent, Sherry's). Item management wise is much simpler than RE 5 one, just press Delete if you want to remove them. However, you cannot contorl what weapon you will like to use. By default, you will wield them all.

QTEs make a return here as well (meh), though in an excessive manner. Granted you can make it automated, but this option will only appear once you have completed the game. But the biggest part of the prompt action comes in two ways:
a) Melees and c'oup de grace
b) Counters

Counter prompts appear for a brief period of time, but if you can get the timing down, you will receive 0 damage in total, in fact you may outright kill the attacker. Melee prompts appear during certain circumstances (headshots, few light melee blows) while c'oup de grace will appear when the enemies are stunned heavily (flash grenades especialy). If you can master this, the campaign will be a cakewalk, since you will be avoiding nearly all source of damages (except bullets and missiles, screw those).

After the campaign there are many other type of minigames you can play. Depending on whether you bought the DLC or not, by default, you get 3 modes:
a) A mode which is similar to L4D versus, where you invade other people's game as a monster.
b) Mercenaries make a return here from RE 5.
c) No Mercy as well.

Note that I won't cover the DLC modes, since I don't have them.

In my opinion, the true highlight of this game is not the campaign or the characters, but the Mercenaries mode. With the enhanced mobility, this mode is a must play mode of RE 6. Being surrounded by non-stop wave of enemies while keeping the time and combo counting is truly fun. No Mercy ramps it up by spawing even more mobs at you, Your whole screen will be covered by them.

Another additional highlight are the asses. There are section where you get to crawl as the female characters. My God, Ada's tight pants are to die for, though Sherry is overall the all rounded one. The trophy for the best booty, however have to go to Helena. Did I mention that all the pants the character are wearing are really, really tight? :3

Overall, I would really recommend this game. Some may not agree with me since I am a newcomer to the series, but to each their own. However, like fine wine, it will take a while for you to truly enjoy this game, since at the start, everything will always go south. Experience and memory of what will happen will help you on subsequent playthrough.

First of all, while this game has excellent graphic, the rest of the system is just abysmally horrible. The controls are severely over-complicated for PC, with multiple actions that require pressing at least three keys at once. Players are limited to using only a few and can barely touch its potential. The game has a truckload of keys to press in game, but the list is outside, in the first welcome screen instead of being accessible in the game. If you forget anything on that list while playing, then screw you. You have to quit the game to access that list in the key config. The tutorial, if you can call that pathetic excuse of a prelude one, are AWFUL and barely teach anything of the mechanics. I was hoping that the game would teach you more when you pick up things, but no. The game doesn't teach you ANY-FREAKING-THING. If you need any in-depth key combinations, you find it online. It's not even in the damn manual. This is how responsible CAPCOM has become.

The pathfinder system of your partner's AI is also god-awful. Your partner often finds yourself stuck near the edge of a door without being smart enough to walk an inch sideways and clear the obstacle. It is one of the case when artificial intelligence completely beats genuine stupidity. To make matters worse, sometimes you cannot cancel a command issued to your partner, and if the AI can't clear a door, it ends up getting stuck there forever, requiring you to restart from the check point. Makes you wonder if the AI of your partner is controlling a BSAA Agent or a chimp. A chimp might be arguably smarter.

The menu interface is also terrible. It is not intuitive and instead making things accessible in one place for easy access, it splits every bit of everything everywhere. There's a weapon in one menu, grenades and health items in another. Oh, and herbs have specific method of using them too. You have to mix them in the menu, put it in capsules, and use it outside the menu using a specific key. When you throw a grenade, if you have 10, you can't just throw 10. You have to throw one, and the game "intelligently" switch to your guns, and you have to switch the menu to grenade menu, find the grenade, select the grenades, and use another. If you want to use 10 grenades, you do that 10 times. If this is not called horrible, I don't know what is. You also have to do all this IN REAL TIME, WHILE FIGHTING.

There are over-abundance of quick-time event. One mistake, and you're dead. You also cannot skip cutscenes. NONE of them. Many of them are minutes long. If the quick-time events are specially difficult, the torture of watching the cutscenes over and over might be more of a challenge than the actual gameplay.

I certainly hope that despite all the heavy sales, this piece of crap doesn't get your money. If you want to know the story, just watch people play this game on YouTube and save yourself the frustration.

Big fan of the series since the beginning, and never have I liked a Resident Evil game so little. The combat is inconsistent, and firearms feel ineffectual and useless against enemies. The majority of the damage you take is from unavoidable "surprise" events, reducing any feeling of accomplishment or control. The game is packed with quick-time events as well, and they are poorly integrated into the flow of the action. 
I did not have the feeling that my actions or skill level, good or bad, actually had anything to do with the progression of the game. Death is hardly a failure, as dying actually gets you some life back and and a refill of ammo. When it takes between 3 and 10 shots to the head at close range to kill a standard zombie on standard difficulty, you are going to run out of ammo. I defaulted to running around zombies and using melee attacks against them, which feels clunky and unsatisfying.
 Buy this if you are a hardcore fan looking to continue the series. The story is not bad, the gameplay is poor and unsatisfying. Many other modern games have taken the old RE formula and done it better (Evil Within, Dead Space and Alan Wake come to mind).

Do you like to die?  Well, RE6 will grant your wish.  I've never played a game where it was so easy to get killed.  Not just through the typical action but from the generously peppered "reflex events" or whatever you call them where you have to mash buttons at specific times or suffer dire consequences.  The visuals and big-world feel are all there, even though you are mostly on rails the whole time from point to point.  The monsters definitely feel dangerous and the environments are classic RE, just scaled up.  The plot is decent and easy enough to follow, though neophytes to the series may be lost on who some of these people are and why they should care.  Even still, there's lots of action to be had and the ability to control your character in agile ways keeps things exciting, especially in fast paced, close-quartered combat.  And the dying again.  As frustrating as it is to get killed (which happens 1000x more when playing multiplayer) the death scenes are fairly gruesome and well done, actually worth watching.

As a Resident Evil game, though, it's TERRIBLE and because it's actually SUPPOSED to be a Resident Evil game, it deserves the negative review. The last great RE game, IMO and not counting remakes, was RE4. This game takes everything good about the older RE games and throws it out the window while taking all the bad stuff and amplifies it 100 fold. It also throws in all the garbage gaming conventions that modern AAA devs think games need that drive me crazy like QTEs, excessive cutscenes, QTEs, taking control away from the player in the middle of gameplay segments, QTEs, gamey button prompts that ruin immersion, have I mentioned QTEs? 

Let me compare the beginning of this game to a great RE game like RE2. In RE2 you had an FMV cutscene (with zero QTEs) followed by a wonderful gameplay intro that was so memorable I could paint a picture of each scene from memory. Between the end of the FMV cutscene and finding the police station, there was only one short cutscene that used the in-game engine at a gun shop. Aside from that short cutscene it was all normal gameplay allowing the player to get used to the game and immerse themself in the world. In RE6 you're being shot at by a helicopter right off the bat, but wait, you have to open the options menu because you're dropped into the game without a main menu. The heli shoots constantly without hitting anything while you mess with settings, a real immersion killer. Then you have to drag Helena away from the heli but you don't press the movement keys to do so, you mash the spacebar for a garbage QTE. Then you're in an alley for an on-rails segment where any direction you press has Leon lumber forward. Up/down/left/right all progress him down this rail. The player has extremely limited control. In the next part you're finally free to walk around but that's it. You can't check the weapon controls or even run. You can only walk. Then the game expects you to learn the weapon controls in 0.25 seconds as they throw a zombie at your face and flash QTE style prompts on the screen (although this isn't a QTE, it just has the immersion-destroying prompts as a kind of tutorial). Failing to shoot the zombie because you weren't simply allowed to play with your gun to get used to it before the zombie shows up, you die and go back to a checkpoint. As the tutorial segment continues you jump over cars as part of a QTE, you fly a helicopter as part of a QTE, you run from an explosion as part of a QTE, you shoot zombies as part of a QTE, etc... It's all very exciting gameplay... NOT. Devs, how about you let ME play the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game? 

The co-op is generic, as I said. In a Resident Evil game I expect to poke around, click on environmental stuff to read little descriptions of things, pick up files, search for ammo/herbs, solve puzzles, etc. Aside from picking up the odd ammo/herb none of that is present. Also, 90% of your items come from enemy drops so searching for environmental pickups isn't even that important. It's streamlined for co-op, in other words. Devs these days seem to think that a co-op experience has to be FAST to be playable. Can't stop to read descriptions! Can't stop to admire the scenery! Can't stop to solve puzzles! Gotta blaze through the game ASAP! You want a puzzle? How about Player A helps Player B access a co-op accessible area, and then Player B presses a button/unlocks a door/pushes a box/etc to allow Player A to follow? Great puzzle, right? There are also dual pickups meaning both players can pick up each item once meaning there's no real communication aside from "ammo/herb over here". You won't have to discuss how much ammo/herbs of each type each player has and who should get what. 

I could go on. There are many factors that make this a terrible RE game or just a sub-par generic co-op game but we'd be here all day. Overall, the game is playable. If you're playing with a friend, it's actually not bad to play through and laugh at the problems the game has so if that sounds like something you'd enjoy, I can honestly recommend picking it up on sale. For the many reasons stated, however, I feel this game falls way, way, way short of it's potential and isn't a fitting entry in the RE franchise and that's where the negative review comes from.

Final Edit: Finished the main campaign and while I have a number of new complaints, the one that really needs to be added here is the dynamic difficulty. In other games that have dynamic difficulty, after you die at the same spot a few times the game might get a little easier to help you get past that part. Here, though, you die once and it  switches to Baby Mode. You'll never die in the same place twice (unless it's due to some janky QTE). Not only is this very insulting to the player but it's also a huge flaw in game design philosphy to think that nothing in the game should take more than 2 attempts.

Score 9/10

The most misunderstood game in the series. It's a fantastic action 3rd person shooter that excells at what it's supposed to do. Fluid controls, satysfying gameplay with tons of variety, great replay value (especially with friends), beautiful and or atmosphereic level design, and TONS of content that will keep your playtime peaking in the hundreds.

Let's look at this in more depth 

[b]Gameplay[b]: 

I've been playing shooters my entire life and never have I encounterd such a game that matches the amazing controls 6 has to offer, tank controls in previous Resident Evil games are non existent, so expect to move like a butterfly and pull off some intresting tech. For instance, you can slide down through a enemy's gap between his legs, plant a bomb WHILE you're sliding in his legs, get up and watch him explode into bits. There's a ton of variety in the gameplay as you're pit up with a VAST amount of weapons, enemies and bosses to fight, melee combat is also different with each and every character you play as, without spoiling anything, expect to never get bored of what the game has to offer. 

The content this game has to offer is something else, you have bonus modes such as Mercinaries or Mercinaries No Mercy. Both of those  will easily satisfy anybody who wanted something more out of the game, you're set up on a stage and character of your choice and you have to survive, while killing the most amount of enemies in a given time, each stage has it's own set of enemies and design to give, most will give you quite a challenge. There's also Agent Hunt and other DLC content which I haven't bought yet.

Replay value in this game is huge, there's a new game plus mode everytime you beat the game, in that you get to keep the items you picked up during the campaign. There's a lot of difficulty and edits you can make to the gameplay to suit anyone's needs. If you want something where ammo is more scarce and you run the risk of dying very fast if you're not carefull, play on professional mode. I once had to KNIFE 2 enemies to death because I used up all my ammo, and I was being very carefull with them too! There's also little skills you can add to your character, such as infinite ammo, not being revived by an A.I partner, more damage with weapon x, etc.

In short, RE6 shines in a lot of areas, however the gameplay will sit just right with anyone 


[b]Story[b]:

It is what it is, without spoiling anything, expect to have a moment for everything, sad moments, happy moments, funny momemnts and everything in between. I've also found the dialogue to be amusing at times to, though it does vary.


[b]Eveything else[b]:

Soundtrack fits every moment, and expect to find a few songs catchy. As I've said before, level design is very atmospheric and well done, it ranges from very creepy to beautifull neon lights, though this isn't the prettiest game of 2013, it sure as hell makes up for it with asthetics. 

Let me know if I forgot anything, feel free to ask me anything about the game.

Resident Evil 6/ Biohazard 6 (originalní název) je third-person akční lineární střílečka, dělaná pro dva hráče.
Začal bych kampaní, za kterou bych přidal dost bodíků. Kampaň je dlouhá a dokonce rozčleněná na 5 etap a ty etapy ještě na kapitoly. Kampaň má dokupy něco kolem 30 hodin, což je víc než dostačující.
Nalezneme zde Intro, což je, jak již název napovídá, pouze jeden level kde nás hra seznámí co a jak.

Kampaně -
Leonovu kampaň. Tato kampaň je takové vaše typické moderní Resident Evil, procházíme různé lokace, střílíme klasické zombie a sem tam potkáme něco silnějšího. U mě je tato kampaň na druhém místě ze čtyř dostupných. (nepočítám intro)

Chrisovo kampaň. Hrajeme za člena BSAA Chrise Redfielda a nebo za jeho parťáka Pierse Nivanse a snažíme se ,jako každý charakter ze hry, polapit Adu Wong a zachránit svět před hromadným Bio útokem. Tahle recenze není spoiler free takže dál k tomu nic.
Avšak kdybych měl kampaň zhodnotit tak Chrisovo je asi nejhorší, stále není špatná, ale ze všech dostupných je nejhorší.

Jakeovo kampaň. Hrajeme zde za Jakea nebo Sherry a tahle kampaň má dle mě tu nejzajímavější zápletku a i levely. Jake je imunní vůči C-Viru a Sherry má zajistit aby se v bezpečí dostal do laborek a oni mohli udělat vakcínu. Avšak Ada si to nenechá líbit a pošle nezničitelného Ustanaka který ma za každou cenu zabít Jakea a donést ho k ní. A bude se snažit fakt tvrdě. Tato kampaň je jednoznačně u mě na prvním místě. 

A jako poslední tu máme kampaň Ady Wong. Která se mi zas líbí ve faktu že je dost odlišná od ostatních. Není v ní až tolik akce a v první misi se máte dokonce snažit jí projít stealth, což mě docela překvapilo na moderní Resident Evil. Ačkoliv i přesto jí mám na druhém nejhorším místě, hned za Chrisem.


Gameplay - 
Jak bylo zmiňováno na začátku, toto RE si opět zahrajeme z pohledu třetí osoby. Budeme sbírat náboje do 400 typů zbraní, hledat skill pointy a taky marně koukat po Zelených rostlinách které jaksi charakter zpracuje a pak si z nich dobijí život. To taky není žádná novinka. Ačkoliv, byl zlepšen aiming systém. A jde to vidět. Znatelně se zde líp míří než v RE5. Stále to není úplně ťip ťop ale přesto ukázka zlepšení tu je. 
Co se týče movementu, máme tu celkem dost tlačítek. Můžeme sprintovat, chodit pomalu, dodgovat dopředu i do stran a bůh ví co ještě. Takže tady je toho nejspíš dost.
Zároveň co mi přišlo dost zajímavé je to, že i přesto že hra používá milion tlačítek na různé akce, tak např. na reload a sbírání věcí je to samé tlačítko! Což mi ale nakonec přišlo docela pohodlné.

Ovládání - 
K tomuhle mám několik věcí co říct. Je to šílené, ne tak jako ARMA ale stálé ŠÍLENÉ! Je tu milion akcí na různá tlačítka a do toho i další milion kombinací. Já osobně jsem si např. změnil přehazování itemů na  3+M3 a přeházování zbraní je klasicky M3 (kolečky u myši), takže to byla ukázka.
Zároveň tu je opět i omezený system inventáře. REovsky tak omezený že často nevíte co byste radši vyměnili za ten herb. Ale tady se mi taky naskytl problem který jsem nijak neřešil takže nevím jestli je to dost vzácný problem a nebo to dokonce ani není problem jen jsem nepochopil mechaniky hry, ale občas když jsem otevřel inventář tak se mi nezobrazil kursor. Což je problem protože pak nebylo nijak možné vyhodit věci. (Teda aspoň si to myslím, klávesově jsem to nedokázal, možná byl způsob. Ani já tu hru nemam od A do Z proštudovanou.)

Grafika -
Opět pokrok od RE5, stále to není tak parádní, ale máme tu nějaké hezké efekty, osvětlení a další věcičky. O grafiku se tolik nezájímám takže to je asi vše k tomu.

Mechaniky hry - 
Tady bych vytknul jednu věc, sice jednu ale kritickou. Hra si přímo ZAKLÁDÁ na Quick time eventech. Unikni zombie tak že budeš klikat pravé a levé tlačítko myší. Odkopni zombie tak že ve správnou dobu klikneš. Mačkej zběsile R aby si otočil páčkou á však to znáte. Ale tady je to až tak šílené použito ve všem, až je to otravné. 
Skills, po kapitolách naleznete i sběratelské předměty včetně skill pointu. Což trochu zachovává replayabilitě. Sbíráte emblemy abyste si otevřeli dokumenty a "figurky" hrdinů. A taky dáváte dohromady skill pointy abyste si odemkli vylepšení pro samo sebe. Klasika ale pro spoustu lidí zábavná věc.

Bonusy -
Ve hře je kromě te 30ti hodinové kampaně dokonce DALŠÍ MOŽNOST. Když nemluvím o placených DLC tak máte i po dohrání kampaně možnost si zahrát Mercenries mod, který teda mě osobně dost baví. Je to klasický Horde mode. Zvolíte mapu, každá má své preset nepřátele, zvolíte charaktera. (A to radši pečlivě, nejen že každý jinak vypadá, ale á i jiný loadout!) Případně si najdete partnera (což doporučuji) a jedete. Drtíte zombíky tak abyste nasbírali, pokud možno s partnerovou pomocí, co největší ba-i maximalni combo. Co je na tom všem ještě lepší je fakt, že abyste odemkli další mapu či charaktera, musíte již odemknuté mapy dát na Rank A-S, což jsou ty dva nejlepší pochopitelně. Takže to je taková malá motivace abyste to zvládli. Protože nová mapa nejen že otvírá nové možnosti ale některé z nich i nové nepřátele.
A kdyby vás už i Mercenaries nebavili mužete si trochu připlatit za další bonusové mody.

Para decepción de muchos fans, esta saga dejó de ser un survival horror hace tiempo, convitiéndose en un juego de acción y disparos en tercera persona. Lo cual no es malo, y Resident Evil 6 es un ejemplo de ello. El juego no da un minuto de respiro; constantemente tienes que estar matando zombis, huyendo de monstruos o sitios que explotan, o ejecutando comandos para no morir en una emboscada o trampa. Hay una gran variedad de enemigos, cada uno con nuevas formas de matarte, y bosses enormes, espeluznantes y con bastante tendencia a no morirse aunque les estrelles un helicóptero en la cabeza. Igualmente, disponemos también de un buen arsenal de armas para despacharlos a gusto, desde porras eléctricas y cuchillos, a las clásicas escopetas y pistolas magnum. Incluso puedes desahogarte a puñetazo limpio y machacar cabezas a pisotones.

El juego contiene cuatro campañas de cinco capítulos cada una, lo que lo convierte en un juego bastante largo si quieres completarlo del todo, y cada una está protagonizada por personajes clásicos de la saga, desde Chris Redfield y Leon Kennedy, hasta Sherry Birkin (si, la niña que tanto daba la murga en el RE2). Cada campaña tiene su propio argumento, aunque todas se entremezclan en algún momento, y aunque al terminarlas te dejan con la sensación de que no te lo han contado todo, puedes ir desbloqueando los secretos del juego para ir revelando información. El nivel de dificultad no es gran cosa, pero puedes modificarlo a tu gusto si buscas un desafío mayor, y puedes probar diferentes personajes para una experiencia nueva. En mi opinión, no es mejor que los clásicos o el 4, pero supera con creces a su predecesor.

I don't even know where to start with this abomination of a game. This game seems to be a congregation of promising ideas with the most abysmal implementation known to the video game industry. Apparently no one could decide if they wanted an interactive movie or another true installment into the Resident Evil franchise and just said "♥♥♥♥ it" morphing whatever they could think of into a tangled mess of a game. Don't get me wrong Id love to like this game. Its nothing short of a neat concept to have 4 seperate stories take place all at once ultimately ending in one cohesive vision of action and suspense.

So I'll start with the positives in this game, it loads. Well...no not really on several occasions there were times when trying to join a co-op session cause the game to lag horribly unless the creator quits and restarts the lobby. And alt tabbing would inexplicably cause the framerate to lag without and indication of going back to normal.

Ok so whats wrong with the game? Everything. A barage of bullet sponge enemies acompanied with 30 second moments of action inbetween pointless cutscenes only to immediately lead into another part of the story making me wonder why the game included it as gameplay rather than just an entire cutscene. (seriously the chapters felt about as shattered as Lost Planet 2) The camera and controls were pretty pathetic, taking the gameplay many steps back instead of progressing into something refreshing. Not to mention something simple like rebinding sidemouse buttons won't work as the game doesn't even recognize them. You'll often be thrown to the ground or flung about being disorientated forcing you to trudge through parts of the game. Which would be fun if the gunplay didnt feel like shooting scarecrows. You can't be tactical or skillful in encounters. Headshots are a hit and miss for either killing the enemy or just triggering a transformation. Thus your best bet is to either unload as many clips as possible and hope you can tell when theyre dead (a health bar honestly wouldve done wonders for this game) or try to incapacitate with a single shot and use melee (which you are limited on and eventually get slowed down if you run out of stamina) and just hope the enemy doesnt land a cheap shot before youre able to thus flinging you about some more...becoming incapacitated yet again and....do you see the pattern yet?

Lets not forget the muddled story. Breaking it off into 4 segments wouldve been nice if it wasnt filled with the same chore missions/enemies throughout several campaigns instead of being done and over with it and if they had made SOME effort to bring any suspense to the story at all. 0 build up. Get guns, shoot things. Thats it, theres some garbage character development love story in one of the campaigns and nonsense drama (you killed my dad i dunno how to deal with that ok im better now we're friends lets save the world) (uhoh my evil clone is doing ♥♥♥♥ better not let anyone in on that so they all want to kill me because im mysterious and cant break character by using my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brain) 

Lets not forget that the graphics have gone NOWHERE. Given that capcom games fundamentally focus on gameplay and story I was prepared for that. However this games story and gameplay were drivel so it would've been nice if the engine had actually changed or at least looked better than the previous title. Youre left romping about an ugly world (not for the sake of atmosphere, it looks more like lack of effort) with poor contrast and an overall muddy template. 

Last but not least Id like to mention that playing number 2 to ada wong in the 4th campaign had me feeling more useless than watching someone else play solo. You magically teleport when she grapples, you cant pick anything up, you can't open doors or interact with anything, and you start with less weapons. Did I mention theres a good 5-10 minutes when youre in a helicopter doing absolutely nothing because the person playing ada is driving and you can only shoot straight ahead, which wouldve been fine if for some arbitrary reason my controls on my half of the weapons systems werent locked only to the right side, thus making it impossible to aim.

tl;dr this game is a travesty and massive blemish on the RE franchise. It shows you how to do everything wrong. I dunno how they got it funded but I had more fun writing this hateful review than playing the game. Anyways heres wonderwall

I'm not trying to send people into a rabid rage, but this is my favorite Resident Evil... by far. It's honestly one of my favorite games period. Let me explain a little.

First thing you need to know, it's not dead. You can still get into all kinds of games. I'm not the only one who enjoys this, maybe you'll understand why in a moment.

I've played all the RE's up to this one, I've only skipped SOME of the recent couple tho, but I watched them still. I still see assets and animations from this one one appearing in the new ones.

This game was so ambitious. They did not play it safe at all, they put everything into this. There is so many animations for the player, and that translates into mechanics. In a way, it honestly ruined Resident Evil for me, until they release something that surpasses this.

You have 8 (human) characters that all have unique animations and mechanics. Everyone can walk, run, sprint, slide, dodge, ram attack, take cover, quick duck, cover fire, melee, quick melee, counter, crawl, roll, parry, shoulder swap, and more. Every weapon has the whole quick shot mechanic, which does like a critical attack that auto targets the nearest enemy, and with some weapons it has unique consecutive attacks. Dual pistols with Leon is the most fun. I don't think I'm even half way done yet, or capable of doing this justice. There's all kinds of contextual attacks you can do, and every character has unique versions of the different contextual attacks. Some guns have alternate fire modes. Some characters have whole melee systems unique to them... It's actually insane.

Then there is also some light rpg mechanics on top of it.

Now, a lot of people are like, it's not horror, it's action. Play it on the hardest difficulty, reset your skills/weapons, it's hard, and nearly every enemy can one hit you. It's scary then.

Then there's the fact that it's coop. That's generally a plus, but there's also like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 6 other game modes, with also a play as zombie or tyrant modes. There's even this mechanic where two sets of coop players can encounter each other in their own campaigns just randomly. It's rare now a days, but it's just such a kool ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing.

All this make the recent games look like downgrades. In fact, it makes most games look pathetic. I could go into all the drawbacks/issues I have with of the recent ones, but I'm not hear to go into that.

Everyone loved 4 and 5, it's just like that but improved in every way. It does have kinda a greatest hits sorta feel, very self referential, and as an old fan... I love that.

I'm not gunna say it's the greatest story, but it's not the worst. It's certainly the most epic, without getting boulder punching corny. It takes itself pretty seriously, and the acting is great. Troy Baker before we realized he only had one character, and the best Leon. 

There's really so much to say about this, but to cut this short, it's just a must have.
One of my all time favorites, and really just one of the most important and ambitious games ever made. Wildly underrated, and misunderstood. I can't speak highly enough about it. Could some things be better, sure, but not much... and it really just comes down to taste.

I rather enjoyed this game; When I was young, I played Resident Evil 1, 2 and 3 and I think that's the problem here with a lot of people. People expect it to play like a game they played years ago; Completely ignoring the fact that the industry and even players have changed.

If Resident Evil #1 released these days, It would be flamed. The controls were terrible by today's standards, There's no hand-holding whatsoever and the limited inventory just don't work when compared by today's standards.

"But what about the HD Remaster?" - Well, As you well know Resident Evil is a massive franchise with fans of the old games that many developers dream of. The nostalgia alone sells copies. But don't get me wrong; It's a fantastic game - Like really, really good. But not one that would survive without the Resident Evil brand these days.

Games have to update; Change up their mechanics to fit in a world where the games today aren't the games that players were playing years ago. 

This is Capcom's attempt to introduce a new generation to the Resident Evil universe. Using characters from the old games (As well as some new additions), Capcom have updated the gameplay of the classic Resident Evil games (To be more in line with what gamers "Want") and sprinkled some innovation on top and it's a fantasic game that I highly recommened.

The reason I've mentioned all that stuff above is that a lot of negative reviews are from people who haven't realized that games HAVE to be updated mechanically as well as aesthically to stay relevant these days.

It's the exact same reason MK X doesn't play like MK 1, 2 and 3. You just can't pull something like that off anymore. The compeition is different, the customers are different and the tools that are around these days are fantastic stuff.

If you're still not convinced; Think of the freakin' Beatles. They couldn't go on making soppy pop-love songs their whole career; They had to update their image, Change their style. To fit in not only with the change of fans but with the music industry as a whole.

This is Capcom's "White Album" and I have to say it's a rather fantastic one. I noticed looking at the forums on Steam a lot of people have reported bugs; But I managed to complete the game reletively bug-free; In fact, I don't think I encountered a single bug in my 13 hours playthrough.

I hope this review has helped some people and I really do hope you give the game a go; It's definately a fun experience!

I don't often leave reviews, but when I do, it's for really disappointing games. 

For a game with this much potential, Capcom really haven't capitalised on it. 

Fair enough you can't just take a great game like RE4 and clone it, that's left for the Call of Duty series; but at least make more of an effort to produce a game as worthy as RE4 for a later sequel.  

The camera is clunky, frustrating, and just generally a nuisance. It snaps to hazards and dangers, but keeps the camera frozen there making it hard to actually react and get away from them. 

The gameplay gets a little tedious after a while, especially the endless, monotonous boss battles in the latter half of the game. I mean for one, surely there is an unwritten rule on the number of times a person can mutate and regenerate without it getting a little ridiculous? And the amount of things that would kill just about anything else and returning from them not just unscathed, but also stronger and larger? I'm talking many times your body weight in lead from bullets, explosions, fires, train collisions, drownings, falling from large heights, and being eaten by a crowd of zombies. Oh, and electrified by a thunderstorm. None of that seems to stop this boss. The boss battles in RE4 and 5 seemed a lot more, well, better in almost every way. It's almost like the concept art was drawn up for possible bosses, and the developers went, "♥♥♥♥ it, let's just use them all."

The inventory was a real pain in the arse. I think this adds to the gameplay being quite tedious and non-immersive, the fact that you have a very limited inventory space, and not even a box to store items in like the original series. You can't have an overview of all of your items like in RE4 or 5, you can only scroll through items or weapons one at a time. And the Shift + Mouse wheel to select grenades/first aid sprays was a bit weird, too. You can't customise weapons, you often find yourself dropping (well, discarding) ammo to mix your herbs. This is merely another aspect of the game which makes it rather hard to get into. The selection of items, like grenades etc., was also particularly limited in this game, when compared to the earlier instalments in the series.There is an incendiary grenade, although this is the only grenade you can get. Hand grenades make an appearance, but you can only use them in a fixed action on one of the final boss fights of the game. 

This brings me to the story. It is not immersive, there seem to very few major characters, it mostly seems like cameo appearances. RE6's story has nothing on RE4 or 5. I seemed to switch between not really knowing what was going on or why, to just not really caring. It seemed to be written quite lazily, e.g. just when your vehicle crashes, you somehow always seem to crash in the right place at the right time. This gives you the feeling of just bumbling along the game, not feeling any particular sense of reward or achievement for reaching or progressing to or from certain stages. 

The music wasn't great either, which I'm not often bothered about or pay attention to in games, but the end credits/cutscene music was particularly cringe-worthy. 

On the upside, some of the settings had a lot of potential, I liked the urban focus throughout the game, which made a nice change from the tribal/country/back of beyond style settings of RE4 and 5. 

All in all, this game had a lot of potential, but do to a lot of annoying game features, non-immersive storyline, and frequently boring gameplay this was mostly wasted. I'd only consider this as a purchase for the more die-hard Resident Evil fans looking to complete their collection. Let's hope that the next instalment in the series really does it justice. 



TL;DR: Die hard RE fans only, boring/frustrating gameplay, boring story, not as good as RE4 or RE5.

This entry has to be the biggest letdown of the franchise in terms of first impression.
I am not sure what Capcom was trying to make in  RE6 - a horrible survival terror game or merely an average 3rd person action game.
Regardless of my previous griefs... after completing all the campaigns, I am left with a mixed bag.

Controls -
RE 6 does not allow you to key bind weapons on PC. This game requires you to scroll through the weapons one by one (luckily, there are only 5 weapons per campaign).
Dodging - Apparently this is a new feature. You can press a key to dodge and stay down by holding the dodge key.
Capcom could have made a much better tutorial regarding dodge controls. All my gripes about controls previously have pretty much gone away after 15-20 hours into the game (and dying roughly 30-50 times along the way).
My biggest gripe? (And Capcom really lost me on this one) why make the action key the same as reload? **Does not apply to amateur, where players are required to press only 1 key instead of combination keys.

Inventory management is atrocious - 
1. You have to go through extra steps to put healing items in to heal yourself (can't use herbs directly from the inventory...  what???). To illustrate this:
Mixing herbs do not heal more, they give you more healing tablets (R+G = used to be full heal, but gives 6 tablets instead in this title).
To heal yourself fully, you must press 1 (by default) multiple times.
2. Grenades work on a separate line (as an "item" not a weapon). You are required to re-equip grenades after throwing one (I stockpile grenades for rough encounters, so this was stupid).
3. You will never know what your inventory limit is until you can't pick up anymore items.
However, Weapons are simplified for everyone - pistol, shotgun, assault rifle, and sniper rifle.

Visuals -
Nothing extraordinary as a console port.

Game play (update 05-23-2015)
Quick Time Events are integrated into the game... much to my displeasure.
For example in Leon's Chapter 3, considering the reload key is the same as the action key.
During the said quick time events for combo key entry, Leon ended up reloading and dying rather than performing the action to duck from an oncoming board. (I later adapted by "dodging" and staying prone).
I also hated the snowmobile event in Jake's campaign, that part alone took me 15-20 tries.
Friendly AI partner can be pretty wonky (not sure why Helena refuses to shoot a target 10m ahead...) but they have unlimited ammunition and (VERY) rarely dies.

Story
Well... it is a mixed bag, really. As far as I can tell, every vehicle in the game explodes in the most exaggerated way possible (except the final escape chopper).
there are 4 campaigns, 7 characters (2 characters per campaign, each character represents their own game play perspective, and Ada's campaign is the loner) centered around the big event of global "bio-terrorism" attack on the US and China. I don't understand why Capcom tried to put so many different spins on the same story; I think it would have been much better if they had just focused their efforts and centered the story around 1 to 4 characters.

Resident evil 6 is the 6th entry to main 'resident evil' series. I began playing 6 after completing revelations, 4 and 5. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much from this game after looking at reviews and what not. However, after playing it for a while, I found that it has strengths and flaws.

[h1]Story[/h1]
Honestly it's a mess. The story is split into 4 campaigns. In each campaign you get to experience the story through the eyes of 1 or 2 characters. The problem is that their segments happen at different points in the timeline, so if you just play one campaign you will definitely be left confused. I was able to follow the story by completing one segment of a campaign, quiting and checking cutscenes menu to see which character's campaign level came next (ultimately playing all four at once). This did somewhat disrupt the gameplay, but definitely made the plot more understandable.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Forget horror, Resident evil 6 went full on action.  To explain clearly Resident evil 6 is like getting Resident evil 5 and giving it crack and polishing. The controls are the best in series yet. You can move freely while aiming and have the ability to freely dodge at a press of a button. Movement feel fluid and not clunky. Inventory management also makes a comeback, with items stored into horizontal segments.  You have a variety of weapons available including rifles, pistols, magnums, grenades, flash bang, flame grenades and knife. You can't upgrade weapons like previous entries. Instead, before starting the next campaign segment you can select and upgrade perks. Perks include increasing damage with weapons, getting more money, health, etc. There are no stores to buy weapons, health and ammo. You have to scavenge for them in the map or corpses instead. Unlike in previous entries where close combat was a dangerous affair, Resident evil 6 allows you to easily dispatch foes via melee attacks. You face a wide range of enemies including range, melee, wolves, zombies and bosses. there is plenty of cover available for you and your enemies to use. In a sense, this makes the game feel more like a third person shooter rather than a horror game. An issue I had with this game is the number of QTE (quick time events). There are so many of them during gameplay and cutscenes that kinda ruined the emertion with the game. There is an option that allows you to succeed all QTE during cutscenes, but not for gameplay unfortunately. Another issue I had was the camera suddenly changing POV, which takes control away from the player (forcing them to look in a particular direction) and made it cumbersome to navigate areas. 

The gameplay types are somewhat split amongst the four campaigns.

Leon/Helen Campaign = Action, zombies and puzzles
Chris/Pierce = Action
Jake/Sherry = Mix of everything
Ada = Stealth and puzzles


 
[h1]Graphics[/h1]
Definitely an improvement over previous entries. Character models have good detail. The same can also be said of the environment as well.

[h1]Audio[/h1]
Audio is acceptable. Voice acting is good with no annoying characters for a change (I'm looking at you Ramon Salazar, Ashley and Irving). Weapon sound effect are good as well.

[h1]Extras[/h1]
Like many resident evil games there is extra content to find and unlock. Each level in the campaign has a set of 'serpent medallions' for you to find and shoot (similar to BSSA Badges in resi 5). For each one you shoot, you collect documents which contain background information on the various characters in the campaign. If you complete a row of them, you unlock character trophies. 

After completing one of the campaigns, you will get the option of playing "New Game +" which transfers all your weapons and items in your next playthrough. There is also a section which allows you to view the cutscenes which you have seen during the campaign.

Mercenaries mode also makes a return. If you are unfamiliar, mercenaries mode places you (with or without another player) as one of several selectable characters in a map trying to hold out until the timer runs out. Each map has unique enemies, which come at you. There are items such a healing, ammo etc scattered around the map for you to collect. Time bonuses are available to extend the time to rack up a higher score. At the end of the round you get a score. Depending on how high the score is, you may unlock a new character to play with. New stages are unlocked by completing previous ones or playing the campaign.

No mercy mode is similar to standard mercenaries. The difference is that there are more enemies present at once so you can rack up higher scores. Also you can play as Left 4 Dead 2 (L4D) characters and Face some L4D 2 monster as well.

[h1]Final Verdict[/h1]
If you are looking for a classic resident evil game with horror, stay the hell away. If you are looking for a good action game to be played with friends, this game will satisfy you.

I have no idea what to say about RESIDENT EVIL 6, really. Suppose I'll just ramble a bit.

tl;dr at the bottom

The gameplay is fairly solid and the action is exhilarating, for sure. The production values and graphics are impressive, and playing with a buddy in coop is a blast.
However, what really brings this game down for me is the ludicrous story, illogical character actions, and punishing length of the game.

Those sound like strange criticisms for a Resident Evil game, I know, but they truly transform this game into something that's not Resident Evil. The story is divided into four sections, with 3 of them following different sets of characters, and a final epilogue where everything is wrapped up neatly (that's not including the bonus add-on story mission). Though the action is always rising in pitch, it never truly felt like the story was moving along at the same pace; plot progression would be dragged back by long boss encounters and extensive action scenes where nothing is accomplished, aside from the characters receiving a couple extra scars...which is insane, since many of those sequences should have resulted in grisly death, not near-misses.

Again, seems like a strange criticism for a Resident Evil game, a series known for crazy nonsensical plot elements. But much like the film adaptations, RESIDENT EVIL 6 is an adrenaline-pounded sequel to a series that benefitted most on subtlety and horror, with only tiny slivers of its former glory tacked on.

The game is also brutally long. You'd think that more game equals better, right?
That's not the case here, unfortunately. The game is padded by extensive fight scenes, and progressing through the story feels like a drawn out chore rather than an enjoyable gauntlet. Just when you think you've reached the climax of the game, and must be close to the end, you end up playing for 3 more hours. THEN you're close to the end.
In the final chapters I just wanted the game to be over. I was tired of fighting the same boss, who would always "resurrect" himself with some new appendage or mutation. Having bosses continually come back certainly sucks the tension out of the game, when you expect that the abomination you just torched will arrive again in 10 minutes. 

RESIDENT EVIL 6 is also punishing to completionists: if you want to finish the game "100%" you'll have to go through the entire game TWICE, once as one character, then again as their partner. The play time I currently have logged is from going through the entire game (and the bonus mission) just once. I don't think I have the patience to go through the game a second time.

Also never expected to find continuity errors in a video game. Before the main game starts you have to play through a tutorial prologue that shows certain characters in peril. However, when you catch up to that point in the story in the main game things are completely different. The game lies to you right at the start, and changes certain events throughout the game as you switch between sets of characters. It's crazy.

Though it has its moments, RESIDENT EVIL 6 isn't a game I want to revisit any time soon. Unless it goes on sale for like 5 bucks or something, I'd recommend avoiding this title.

OK, let's see. Why did I say No to this game? Because I don't want Capcom to make the same mistake again. 

The game contains 4 campaign, one of which is captivating. I played Leon’s campaign repetitively, like an actual insane person. I can’t say that it has any major issues, expect the game’s general issues, which the entire game has. I know the dialogue is a little more than cheesy, and you won’t really want to listen to the character’s talk, but the rest is fine. The game (I’m speaking exclusively No Hope difficulty, the hardest mode of the game) doesn’t give you much ammo, which makes it much MUCH more survivor than Resident Evil 5, and you’ll have to do a lot of headshots combined with the following melee attack in order to get through chapters. Of course, sometimes it get pretty annoying when killing an enemy is mandatory, you’ve used your bullets judiciously, but the game is refusing to give you bullets and instead keeps showering you with skill points. 
This campaign is dark and nostalgic. I actually lived through it. I missed Raccoon city so much; I missed the atmosphere of Resident Evil 3, and this game came so close, which I’m grateful for. Thank you, Capcom. 
The bosses, as always, are needy pathetic characters you can’t grow a liking or respect for (which doesn’t count for a flaw.)
Chris’s campaign is where the bugs and issues come to life for the first time, but the campaign still feels like an actual game. Here, you will see enemies actually shooting “through” each other. While you can’t possibly shoot an enemy through another enemy (the first enemy is blocking the other one), enemies can do this. Their bullets fly right through each other and reach you.
It has ridiculous artificial intelligence. When you’re hiding behind a wall and an enemy is using a machine gun from 100 feet away to kill you, the enemy will aim at you even when you’re moving behind the wall. HOW CAN THE ENEMY SEE WHERE I’M MOVING FROM BEHIND THE WALL?
There are these round and explosive enemies who will explode when you get close to them or kick them. Piers, your partner for this session, keeps kicking them all the while, regardless of where you’re standing. If I had a cent for every time Piers killed me, I’d have a dollar. 
Then there are the headshots, which is a very crucial thing in the No Hope difficulty of the game. When you do a headshot, then enemy starts crying and pressing the wound, giving you a chance to perform a lethal melee attack. But the thing is, if you do 1000 more headshots, the enemy won’t show reaction again until he’s done crying, meaning you won’t be able to get the enemy to react again until it’s done with his first reaction. Now that’s just a big flaw.
Oh, the Camera, the Camera. Do I even want to tell you about the camera? The heroes are constantly looking around, and the camera follows their looks. When they’re done sightseeing, you’re usually attacked instantly, which is hideously annoying in No Hope difficulty, where you can actually die because of that. Sometimes a bus is following you, and you have to dash in order to escape. The character is looking at his front, but the camera only shows his back, which results in you being blocked by some crate or something, and then dying. In Chris’s campaign, luckily, there isn’t much to block your way. But in Leon’s campaign, you can be sure to die at least once. 
There are these cut scenes that you can’t skip, which will annoy you to death for two reasons. One, the enemy has the ability to move during these scene, but you’re not. And when the cut scene is finished, the enemy will attack you instantaneously, giving you null chance of defending yourself.

Now, please pay attention that I got an S (the highest score possible) on every chapter of this game without cheating or using tactics that count as cheating. So I’m not annoyed because I don’t know how to play or anything. The game is seriously flawed. 

One time, a truck ran over my partner Helena in chapter one, and she died. I’m only made responsible for my own character in this game. Why the hell does my partner die like that at times?

I don’t have much more to say about Chris’s campaign. I should add that it’s STILL worth playing. Once you get used to the bugs and flaws, you’ll really like this game. It has beautiful bosses. If you know what I mean by beautiful. Really fun to kill.

Don’t even play the third and fourth campaign. I continuously felt like I’m waiting for the game to begin. The chapters were either too short or too long. And they didn’t feel like games, they felt like prologues. 

Speaking of prologues, the prologue of the game is most boring thing ever. Helena is dying and you have to save her. The more boring thing is that you have to play that part of the game for a second and third time (as Leon, and then as Ada).

The story was beautiful. This is the only Resident Evil game with an actual storyline, with character development. It’s no longer about saving a certain somebody and escaping a certain town (which happened for five games), this one actually contain some drama. You may even cry. :D Don’t say I didn’t tell ya’. ;)

Verdict:
Do not buy this game if you’re not a Resident Evil fanatic, because you’d only be supporting a failure. You’d be rooting for another game of this type. 
There is much more I can say to dissuade you from buying this game, but I’m not gonna. This is becoming longer than I had expected.

Let's face it, Resident Evil has lost its step. It isn't the horror juggernaut it used to be. 4 and 5 made it clear that it was transitioning into a more action-esque genre which upset a lot of fans. So where does this put 6?

RE6 is by no means an amazing game, nor is it the best Resident Evil game. However, for what it provides, it's a good game. The action combat feels refined with the ability to move while you aim and shoot. Gone are the days where you had to stand still to fire a gun. This certainly makes for better action gameplay. While the quick time events are more consistent in what they ask the player to press and when, the game unfortunately throws several more at you than 5. What about the narrative?

Resident Evil 6's plot is still that silly B movie narrative that it's always had. It tries so hard to be serious and emotional, but follows so many expected tropes that it never hits the nail hard enough. However, it isn't a complete travesty and shouldn't be shunned completely. 

Overall Resident Evil 6 is a decent entry into the Resident Evil franchise. If you at least enjoyed 5, I'd reccommend picking 6 up, but only if it is on sale. This game is worth about $15 USD at most, and that's stretching it. If you didn't enjoy 5, you probably won't enjoy 6.
